## [BANK] Color Customizer App for a 3D Model (Codrops) — deep-read entry 140 (siding-windows-doors pack: `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md`)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/Tutorials/3DModelCustomizer/
- **How it looks:** A 3D product (a chair-class model) centred on a plain studio background with a row of colour swatches; clicking a swatch re-colours one named part of the model instantly — no page reload, no image swap.
- **Frame by frame:** Page load → the model slowly auto-rotates (intro spin) → visitor clicks a swatch → that part's material colour changes in the same frame → visitor drags to orbit and inspect.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Three.js r108; parts matched by name substring; each swatch click rebuilds the material for the matched part; intro spin π/60 per frame × 120 frames. The mechanic — pick a part, recolour it live — is the direct ancestor of the siding visualiser pattern (see BLK, entry 531, for the cheaper 2D SVG version).
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — real 3D toll; the bank's own visualiser recipe (R36) is library-free and under 11 KB.
- **Best for:** Product configurators where the product is genuinely 3D (doors, windows in situ); portfolio demos. For trade lead pages prefer the SVG-zone version.
- **Deep read:** `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md` (entry 140). **Code:** `animation/code-source/color-customizer-3d/`.

## [BANK] Count Up (React Bits) — deep-read entry 279 (all four packs: `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md`)
- **Reference source:** https://reactbits.dev/text-animations/count-up
- **How it looks:** A plain stat number (years, jobs, reviews) that sits at its final value in the HTML, then — when scrolled into view — sweeps up from zero to that value once, digits tabular so the width never jitters.
- **Frame by frame:** Stat scrolls into view → IntersectionObserver fires once → number eases up over 2 s → lands exactly on the printed final value and stops. No repeat on re-scroll.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Duration 2 s; easeOut cubic-bezier(0.33, 1, 0.68, 1); IO trigger, once; `tabular-nums`; the final value is in the HTML as the no-JS fallback (a counter that renders 0 without JS is a bank-flagged defect). Optional roll mode: digit cells 1.2 em tall, stagger 0.07 capped at 40%.
- **Tier:** STRONG — the bank's standard trust-stat recipe (R20 in the builder brief).
- **Best for:** Hero proof strips and stat bands (jobs done, review counts, years) on every trade page.
- **Deep read:** `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md` (entry 279). **Code:** `animation/code-source/count-up-reactbits/`.

## [BANK] CSS scroll()-driven animations (Codrops, Adam Argyle) — deep-read entry 271 (all four packs: `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md`)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2024/01/17/a-practical-introduction-to-scroll-driven-animations-with-css-scroll-and-view/
- **How it looks:** Elements fade, slide or scale purely because the page scrolled — progress bars fill, cards rise — with no JavaScript running at all; the animation is glued to the scrollbar's position.
- **Frame by frame:** Visitor scrolls → the named scroll/view timeline advances → keyframes interpolate in exact lockstep with scroll position → scrolling back reverses them perfectly.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Pure CSS: `animation-timeline: scroll()` / `view()` with named timelines; zero JS. At the time of writing Chromium-only, so the bank gates it behind `@supports` and reduced-motion rules — unsupported browsers simply see the finished state.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — elegant and free, but support-gated; never the only reveal layer.
- **Best for:** Progress indicators, subtle scroll-linked reveals on content pages; a zero-JS enhancement layer over static content.
- **Deep read:** `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md` (entry 271). **Code:** none in the packs.

## [BANK] Direction-aware reveals (GreenSock pen pojzxwZ) — deep-read entry 40 (all four packs: `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-1.md`)
- **Reference source:** None recorded (the bank records only the pen id pojzxwZ for this entry).
- **How it looks:** Sections and cards glide in from the direction the visitor is scrolling — scrolling down, content rises up into place; scrolling back up, it settles down from above. The page feels like it knows which way you are moving.
- **Frame by frame:** Element approaches the viewport → GSAP reads scroll direction → element starts offset ±100 px on the entry side, transparent → travels to rest over 1.25 s on an expo ease → `clearProps` leaves it clean. Rapid direction changes don't queue up: overwrite is set to auto.
- **Mechanism & key values:** GSAP `fromTo` with ±100 px travel, 1.25 s expo, overwrite: 'auto'; travel halved on phones. This is recipe R1 in the builder brief — the house scroll reveal, deliberately slower than the 0.4–0.8 s family because the duration IS the recipe.
- **Tier:** STRONG — a default recipe in the builder brief's stack.
- **Best for:** Section entrances on every page type; the general scroll-reveal layer.
- **Deep read:** `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-1.md` (entry 40). **Code:** `animation/code-source/pen-40-direction-reveals/`.

## [BANK] Dynamic Shape Overlays (Codrops) — deep-read entry 150 (roofing, hvac packs: `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md`)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/Development/ShapeOverlays/
- **How it looks:** Click a menu or a link and a coloured liquid shape sweeps across the whole screen in a wave — the edge bulges and ripples like fabric — covering the old page before the new one appears.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger clicked → an SVG path overlay animates its control points in sequence, the wave edge crossing the screen → screen fully covered at mid-point (content swaps underneath) → wave exits the other side → new page revealed.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Demo 1 (the lush version): 18 path points, 600 ms, delayPointsMax 300 ms, delayPerPath 100 ms; fills #413f46 / #e6e5ea / #cccccc. Demo 3 (the snappy wipe): 2 points, 600 ms, delayPerPath 200 ms — per-path easing swaps between opening and closing. Delay formula: (sin(radian + range) + 1)/2 × max.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — a page-transition effect; trade lead pages don't change pages in-file, so its home is portfolio/multi-page work.
- **Best for:** Full-screen menu opens and page transitions on portfolio sites; a signature transition between a homepage and a case study.
- **Deep read:** `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md` (entry 150). **Code:** `animation/code-source/dynamic-shape-overlays/`.

## [BANK] Fancy SVG Letter Animation (Codrops) — deep-read entry 258 (roofing, remodeling packs: `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md`)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2016/09/13/fancy-svg-letter-animation/
- **How it looks:** A word rendered as three stacked outline copies of itself — thin strokes in slightly different weights — that draw themselves on letter by letter, then the whole word springs in with an elastic settle.
- **Frame by frame:** Page/section enters → each letter's outline strokes draw on over 800 ms (easeOutQuint), delayed per path and per letter → the filled word pops in with a 900 ms elastic ease → static end state.
- **Mechanism & key values:** 3 stroke layers at 9 / 9.5 / 10 px; draw-on 800 ms easeOutQuint; delay = path × 200 ms + letter × 40 ms; entrance 900 ms easeOutElastic with elasticity 600. SVG stroke-dash technique throughout.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — decorative display type; one accent word only, never body copy.
- **Best for:** A single hero word or section-title flourish on a portfolio page; logo-type animation.
- **Deep read:** `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md` (entry 258). **Code:** `animation/code-source/fancy-svg-letter-animation/`.

## [BANK] Grid-to-Fullscreen (Codrops) — deep-read entry 48 (siding-windows-doors, remodeling packs: `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-1.md`)
- **Reference source:** tympanus.net/Tutorials/GridToFullscreenAnimations
- **How it looks:** A tidy grid of project photos; click one and that photo grows smoothly out of the grid until it fills the screen, the grid melting away around it — no page change, no jump cut.
- **Frame by frame:** Click a thumbnail → its bounds are measured at click time → a single WebGL plane takes over the image and expands it to fullscreen while the grid fades → close reverses the path back into the grid slot.
- **Mechanism & key values:** One reusable WebGL plane (not one canvas per image), 128 segments for the bend/distortion during travel, measurements taken at click. The builder brief's production version (R10) is a DOM port — same choreography, no WebGL — and phones get fade/scale instead.
- **Tier:** STRONG — a named gallery recipe (R10) with a proven DOM port.
- **Best for:** Project galleries and portfolio indexes; the "work" section's click-to-open move.
- **Deep read:** `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-1.md` (entry 48). **Code:** `animation/code-source/grid-to-fullscreen/`.

## [BANK] GSAP Marquee Text (GreenSock pen) — deep-read entry 161 (roofing, hvac packs: `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md`)
- **Reference source:** https://codepen.io/GreenSock/pen/wvZMwez
- **How it looks:** A single line of items — town names, project types, review snippets — sliding sideways in an endless, perfectly seamless loop, no visible seam where the content repeats.

- **Best for:** Areas-served strips, review tickers, project-type marquees — one per page.

## [BANK] GSAP Pin Sidebar (CodePen, akapowl) — deep-read entry 153 (roofing, hvac packs: `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md`)
- **Reference source:** https://codepen.io/akapowl/pen/poRdoLV/9b99361db3839f1169cdc0f278746ee5
- **How it looks:** A two-column process section: the left column (step titles + a progress indicator) sticks in place while the right column's step panels scroll past; the indicator ticks from step to step as each panel passes.
- **Frame by frame:** Section reaches the pin point → sidebar pins → each content panel scrolls through, its step lighting up in the indicator (0.25 s, to orange) → at each step's 75% point the state hands over → after the last panel the sidebar unpins and the page continues.
- **Mechanism & key values:** ScrollTrigger pin with end "+100% × N points"; a points timeline of 100% × N; indicator tween 0.25 s; exits keyed at i + 0.75. Bank pin rules apply: on phones it needs a stacked fallback — a pinned sidebar must never trap phone scrolling.
- **Tier:** STRONG — the pinned-process pattern, with the phone caveat attached.
- **Best for:** Numbered process sections (survey → quote → install → sign-off) on desktop; long step-through explainers.
- **Deep read:** `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md` (entry 153). **Code:** `animation/code-source/gsap-pin-sidebar/`.

- **Reference source:** https://www.powermoves.com/co-op-solar/how-it-works/
- **How it looks:** A long scrollytelling page where a sun travels across the sky on a curved path as you scroll through a solar co-op explainer — landscape, panels and copy changing scene by scene around it.

## [BANK] How to Animate SVG Shapes on Scroll (Codrops) — deep-read entry 53 (roofing, remodeling packs: `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md`)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2022/06/08/how-to-animate-svg-shapes-on-scroll/
- **How it looks:** Big soft SVG blob shapes used as section separators morph and drift as the sections scroll past — the divider between two sections is alive, swelling and settling with scroll speed.
- **Frame by frame:** Section boundary enters → the separator shape's path begins morphing, scrubbed to scroll → shape reaches its alternate form as the boundary crosses → settles as the next section locks in.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Separator viewBox 0 0 100 10, rendered 150 px tall; scrub from "top bottom" to "bottom top"; Lenis lerp 0.1 drives the scroll. Hard rule (also in the builder brief): the `d` and `data-path-to` command/point structure must match exactly or the morph garbles.
- **Tier:** STRONG — the bank's morphing-separator recipe family (R8), with its recorded production fix (the last separator's end must sit inside reachable scroll).
- **Best for:** Section separators/dividers on long pages; quiet shape interest between sections.
- **Deep read:** `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md` (entry 53). **Code:** `animation/code-source/53-onscroll-path-animations/`.

## [BANK] Infinite Marquee Along an SVG Path (Codrops) — deep-read entry 149 (roofing pack: `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md`)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2025/06/17/building-an-infinite-marquee-along-an-svg-path-with-react-motion/
- **How it looks:** Cards or words flow endlessly along a curved, looping SVG track — like a conveyor belt bent into a ribbon — instead of the usual straight marquee line.
- **Frame by frame:** Items advance along the path at constant velocity → each wraps from path end back to start invisibly → hovering slows the flow to a crawl → on resize the path is re-sampled so spacing stays even.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Demo path "M0 186.219C138.5 186.219 305.5 194.719 305.5 49.7188C305.5 -113.652 -75 186.219 484.5 186.219H587.5", viewBox 0 0 588 187; baseVelocity 20 (single-item demo), 5 in the final build (5 cards × repeat 4 = 20 items); hover factor 0.3; hover spring stiffness 100, damping 20; D3 `getPointAtLength` resampling on resize.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — a flourish; the straight marquee covers most trade uses at a fraction of the complexity.
- **Best for:** A curved logo/review ribbon on a portfolio page; playful section dividers.
- **Deep read:** `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md` (entry 149). **Code:** `animation/code-source/infinite-marquee-svg-path/`.

## [BANK] Masked Heading (React Bits) — deep-read entry 95 (roofing, remodeling packs: `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md`)
- **Reference source:** https://reactbits.dev/text-animations/masked-heading
- **How it looks:** A giant headline whose letters are filled with a moving image/video texture, and as you scroll, a soft spotlight of clarity follows across the words while the heading drifts slightly — the type itself is the visual.
- **Frame by frame:** Heading enters → words rise in one by one (1.1 s, stagger 0.09/word, power4.out) from behind their masks → a radial spotlight (radius 160) tracks across the text with scroll → the whole block parallaxes gently (26 px) and drifts (18 px) as the page moves.
- **Mechanism & key values:** fillScale 1.25 on the masked fill; parallax 26; drift 18; rise 1.1 s stagger 0.09/word power4.out; spotlightRadius 160. Reduced-motion behaviour is verified present in the source — one of the few demos that ships it.
- **Tier:** STRONG — headline craft for portfolio heroes and section titles (R2 masked-reveal family).
- **Best for:** Hero headlines and giant section titles where the words carry the design; Asiful's own portfolio tier only on prospect pages.
- **Deep read:** `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md` (entry 95). **Code:** `animation/code-source/95-masked-heading/`.

- **Reference source:** https://codepen.io/GreenSock/pen/XWoBypQ
- **How it looks:** An object (plane, dot, van icon) travels along a drawn curved route across the section, rotating to face its direction of travel like it is really driving the line.

## [BANK] Mouse-Following Square Lens (Codrops) — deep-read entry 125 (siding-windows-doors pack: `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md`)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2026/08/25/building-a-mouse-following-square-lens-effect-with-three-js-and-glsl/
- **How it looks:** A sharp square "lens" follows the cursor over an image; inside the square the image is distorted — stretched and RGB-split like looking through glass — while outside it stays normal.
- **Frame by frame:** Cursor moves → the square eases after it (pointerEase 0.1, always slightly behind) → inside the square the image warps with lens distortion and the colour channels separate at the edges → cursor leaves, the lens fades.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Three.js + GLSL; squareSize 0.4 as deployed; lensDistortion 1.5; RGB shift +0.01 / 0 / −0.01; pointerEase 0.1; ~589 KB Three.js toll. Bank verdict inside the entry: take the MASK idea, rebuild it in DOM — do not ship the WebGL weight for this effect.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — mechanism worth stealing, implementation too heavy for trade pages.
- **Best for:** Before/after or material-inspection interactions re-implemented in DOM; portfolio hero accents.
- **Deep read:** `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md` (entry 125). **Code:** `animation/code-source/125-square-lens/`.

## [BANK] Scroll-Triggered Curved Path Animations (Codrops) — deep-read entry 54 (roofing pack: `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md`)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2025/12/17/building-responsive-scroll-triggered-curved-path-animations-with-gsap/
- **How it looks:** A smooth curved line draws itself across the page as you scroll, bending around content; midway along the scroll the curve hands over from one size regime to another, so the line stays graceful on any screen width.
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll enters the section → the path's draw progress advances with scroll → control points pull the curve through its bends (multipliers 0.8 / 0.3 / 0.6 / 0.2) → at progress 0.5 the size logic switches regime → path completes at section end.
- **Mechanism & key values:** GSAP + ScrollTrigger with DrawSVG-style progress; control-point multipliers 0.8/0.3/0.6/0.2; path length caps 800 / 80 px; size split at progress 0.5; resize debounce 200 ms. Recorded gap: the original skips a reduced-motion jump-to-final — our builds must add it.
- **Tier:** STRONG — responsive path-drawing with real breakpoint behaviour.
- **Best for:** Route/journey lines, process connectors, decorative scroll-drawn curves that must survive responsive layouts.
- **Deep read:** `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md` (entry 54). **Code:** none in the packs.

## [BANK] Scrollable and Draggable Timeline with GSAP (Codrops) — deep-read entry 275 (roofing, remodeling packs: `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md`)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2022/01/03/building-a-scrollable-and-draggable-timeline-with-gsap/
- **How it looks:** A wide horizontal timeline of events that moves BOTH ways: scroll the page and it slides sideways; grab it and drag, and the page scroll follows your drag — the two inputs never fight.
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll → master tween slides the track → drag the track instead → ScrollTrigger disables during the drag, the drag maps back into page scroll position → release → scroll control resumes seamlessly.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Master tween ease 'none' (mandatory — any easing desyncs the two inputs); Draggable edgeResistance 1; drag↔scroll sync via mapRange → st.scroll(y); InertiaPlugin is Club GSAP (paid) — the bank's Mode B proves the feel without it. Over-wide nav track sizing recorded alongside: min-width max(200rem, 200%).
- **Tier:** STRONG — the scroll/drag sync pattern, with the Club-plugin caveat priced in.
- **Best for:** Timelines (company history, project journey), draggable galleries that must coexist with page scroll.
- **Deep read:** `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md` (entry 275). **Code:** none in the packs.

- **Reference source:** https://www.shopify.com/editions/winter2026
- **How it looks:** A polished product-release microsite: feature sections fade and slide in as they arrive, illustrated product scenes animate in a flat illustrated style, everything moving on one consistent, calm motion language.

- **Mechanism & key values:** A MOTION-TOKEN SYSTEM: scroll-state 0.6 s cubic-bezier(.41,.19,.13,.95); fade 0.52 s; slide 0.6 s; spring cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1); Lenis duration 1 easeOutExpo; IntersectionObserver threshold vocabulary 0 / 0.1 / 0.5. GSAP absent; Rive carries the illustration animation.
- **Tier:** STRONG — the reference for running a whole page on named motion tokens instead of scattered values.
- **Best for:** Design-system discipline on any multi-section page; product/feature announcement pages.
- **Deep read:** `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md` (entry 58). **Code:** `animation/code-source/58-shopify-editions-winter26/`.

- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2026/02/19/creating-a-smooth-horizontal-parallax-gallery-from-dom-to-webgl/
- **How it looks:** A row of large photos gliding sideways with buttery lag — each image inside its frame shifts slightly against the frame (parallax) as the row moves, so the gallery feels deep rather than flat.
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll/drag → the row's target moves, the rendered position lerps after it (0.07) → each oversized image (125% width, offset −12.5%) counter-shifts inside its frame, capped at MAX_SHIFT 10 → motion settles softly when input stops.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Two-phase build (DOM first, then the same gallery in WebGL); DOM phase: lerp 0.07, img 125% at left −12.5%, MAX_SHIFT 10. Recorded gap: touch support is an unimplemented exercise in the source — the DOM phase is the portable half.
- **Tier:** STRONG — the parallax-gallery parameter set behind R13's desktop form.

## [BANK] Sticky Grid Scroll (Codrops) — deep-read entry 94 (siding-windows-doors, remodeling packs: `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md`)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2026/03/02/sticky-grid-scroll-building-a-scroll-driven-animated-grid/
- **How it looks:** A grid of tiles sticks to the screen; as you scroll, tiles pop in one by one, then the whole grid zooms toward one centre tile until it fills the view and becomes the next section.
- **Frame by frame:** A 425 vh scroll block begins → 0–45%: tiles reveal in stagger (each 0.06, power1.inOut) → 45–90%: the grid scales up (to 2.05) toward the focal tile → 90–100%: the zoomed tile IS the next section's hero.
- **Mechanism & key values:** 425 vh pinned block; reveal phase 0–45% stagger 0.06 power1.inOut; zoom phase 45–90% to scale 2.05; Lenis lerp 0.08, wheelMultiplier 1.4; fluid sizing rem = 100vw/1440. Recorded gap: no reduced-motion handling in source — add the bank's fallback before use.
- **Tier:** STRONG — a complete grid-to-section transition system with exact phase values.
- **Best for:** Gallery-to-case-study transitions; services grid that zooms into a service detail.
- **Deep read:** `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md` (entry 94). **Code:** `animation/code-source/94-sticky-grid-scroll/`.

## [BANK] The Architecture Behind Trionn (Codrops) — deep-read entry 163 (roofing, remodeling packs: `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md`)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2026/07/15/the-architecture-behind-trionn-coordinating-gsap-three-js-lenis-and-web-audio/
- **How it looks:** An award-tier agency site where a 3D object explodes into floating cards as you scroll, headlines un-blur letter by letter, and every system (scroll, 3D, text) moves as one organism because one ticker drives all of them.
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll advances a single master progress → at 0.35 the 3D sequence starts exploding → 0.53 explosion completes → 0.56–1.0 the cards arrange → headlines reveal char by char (0.8 s, stagger 0.08 random, blur 12 px → 0).
- **Mechanism & key values:** ONE GSAP ticker drives Lenis + Three.js + ScrollTrigger (no competing clocks); a 371-frame image sequence on a single <img>; EXPLODE_START 0.35 / EXPLODE_END 0.53 / CARDS 0.56–1.0; BlurTextReveal chars 0.8 s stagger 0.08 random from blur 12 px.
- **Tier:** STRONG — as architecture doctrine (one clock for everything); the scene weight itself is portfolio-tier only.
- **Best for:** Coordinating any build where scroll, canvas and text must stay in sync; the one-ticker rule applies at every scale.
- **Deep read:** `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md` (entry 163). **Code:** `animation/code-source/trionn-architecture/`.

## [BANK] Accordion with CSS3 (Codrops) — deep-read entry 306 (all four packs: `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-5.md`)

- **Tier:** STRONG — the ancestor of the bank's zero-JS FAQ recipe.
- **Best for:** FAQ sections; any accordion that must work with JS off.

## [BANK] How to Create a Circular Progress Button (Codrops) — deep-read entry 348 (all four packs: `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-5.md`)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2014/04/09/how-to-create-a-circular-progress-button/
- **How it looks:** A wide pill button ("Send") that, on click, shrinks into a circle while a ring draws itself around it as the request runs — then the ring resolves into a drawn green tick (success) or a cross (error).
- **Frame by frame:** Hover → fill warms → click → label fades (0.15 s) → button morphs 250×70 px pill → 70 px circle → SVG ring stroke draws with real progress → success: button fills green #1ECD97 and the checkmark path draws; error: the cross draws → state resets (label returns, 0.3 s with 0.1 s delay).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Ring r = 32.5, stroke #1ECD97 width 5; check/cross stroke #fff width 4, round caps, opacity transition 0.1 s; loading state border #ddd width 5. Vanilla JS class machine (`UIProgressButton`) keyed off transitionend. The bank's form-feedback standard for quote forms — the button must reflect the REAL submit state.
- **Tier:** STRONG — the designated submit-feedback pattern for forms.
- **Best for:** Quote/contact form submit buttons; any async action needing honest progress.
- **Deep read:** `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-5.md` (entry 348). **Code:** none in the packs.

## [BANK] Inspiration for Text Input Effects (Codrops) — deep-read entry 310 (all four packs: `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-5.md`)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2015/01/08/inspiration-text-input-effects/
- **How it looks:** A set of 14 named text-field styles (Haruki, Hoshi, Kuro, Madoka…) where the label is part of the animation: focus a field and its label slides up, splits, or an SVG outline draws itself around the input.
- **Frame by frame:** Field receives focus (or is filled) → the label's ::before/::after elements transform — text lifts, borders draw (Madoka animates an SVG stroke via stroke-dashoffset) → the field reads as active; blur with content keeps the floated state.
- **Mechanism & key values:** The load-bearing detail is markup order: label sits AFTER the input (`input + label`) so :focus sibling selectors can drive it. Haruki margins 4em 1em 1em, field padding 0.4em 0.25em. Elementor form widgets cannot reproduce these label mechanics — the bank rebuilds them in an HTML widget inside the form section (the builder brief's R22 floating-label kit is the house descendant).
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — polish for form sections; use one style per form, never a medley.
- **Best for:** Quote-form styling; contact-form craft on portfolio-tier pages.
- **Deep read:** `reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-5.md` (entry 310). **Code:** none in the packs.

Scrub ladder: true ×21, .5 ×9, 1 ×4, .8/.75 also present; durations 1 ×7 / 2 ×3 / 4 ×1 (the 4s is a slow hero drift); staggers .1 ×5, {each:.03} ×1, .25 ×1; CSS bezier cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1). Reduced motion handled in CSS and JS (×10 CSS + ×2 JS + ×1 HTML) — strong for a GSAP site.
- **Best for:** The scrub-ladder pattern (ambient/chapter/lagged) and accessible premium-interiors motion: dense ScrollTrigger use that still ships reduced-motion handling.
- **Deep read:** remodeling/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-8.md (entry 516). **Code:** remodeling/design/code-source/tillberg-design/.

## [BANK] Shazam-Like Morphing Button (Codrops) — manifest pick → code-source demo + deep-read entry (hvac/MANIFEST.md, Animation 7)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2015/11/24/shazam-like-morphing-button-effect/
- **How it looks:** One round button on a plain stage. It is a real button that becomes the interface: the disc squashes and reshapes into a wide "listening" form ringed by a pulsing ripple while musical notes drift outward, then reshapes again into a player card. Content for each state (start / listen / player) fades and slides inside the morphing shape.
- **Frame by frame:** Click → the shape morphs to the listen state in 400ms on an overshoot bezier (cubic-bezier(0.8,−0.6,0.2,1) — it dips below its start before settling, the "squash" anticipation) while the start content exits upward (−25px, 0.4s) and the listen content enters from +25px → a ripple ring pulses behind it (1.2s ease-out, infinite, second ring delayed 0.6s) and up to 50 notes spawn on a 60ms cascade, each flying at constant velocity (its transition duration = 4.5ms × its distance in px, rotation jitter ±30°, fade 0.8s), recycling on transitionend → click again → after a 250ms delay the shape morphs to the player card in 450ms (cubic-bezier(0.7,0,0.3,1)) → close morphs back in 400ms (cubic-bezier(0.4,1,0.3,1)).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Snap.svg path morphing: three same-point-count SVG paths stored as strings in data-path-start / data-path-listen / data-path-player attributes on one element inside a 300×500 viewBox, interpolated directly. Content swaps are transform+opacity 0.4s transitions on per-state beziers; button opacity 0.3s; player panel opacity 0.5s. The HVAC use per the manifest: a "Call now" button that morphs into the contact card (the article carries the mobile Safari workarounds). In a single-file build, GSAP's attr:{d:…} tween replaces Snap.svg when point counts match.
- **Best for:** A call-to-contact CTA transition: one button that becomes the contact card, with the anticipation-overshoot morph as the signature.
- **Deep read:** hvac/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md (entry 255). **Code:** hvac/animation/code-source/shazam-morphing-button/.

## [BANK] Q571 · AHA — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-9.md)
- **Reference source:** https://www.aha.com.au/
- **How it looks:** A WordPress services site whose structural spine is a numbered services index — 11 services as rows with a current/total counter (01OF11 pattern) — followed by a 5-card projects grid and a second index for sectors. Motion is restrained: content blocks rise in on GSAP reveals as they enter view, scrolling is Lenis-damped. No WebGL, no shaders (0/0 Measured). Type: a display heading font + "Inclusive Sans" body (WP preset families).
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll → blocks entering the viewport (IntersectionObserver present ×18) play GSAP rises, dominant authored ease power2.out → content settles. Authored durations are sparse in the bundles (0.7, 0.5, 0.21, micro 0.05) — most reveal timing likely lives in per-block inline config not present in the three same-host bundles; logged as a gap, not filled.
- **Mechanism & key values:** WordPress block theme + GSAP **3.15.0** (version string ×3 in bundles) + Lenis (version global present). ScrollTrigger mentions: 5, with 19 `scrollTrigger` config-string hits — library internals inflate this; treat 19 as an upper bound, not a config count. Site-authored eases extracted: power2.out ×2, power2.inOut, power4, expo, none. Portable pattern: the services index as a semantic ordered list, counter generated by CSS counters (01OF11 = current/total). Reduced motion: 0 occurrences in mined CSS — ABSENT (a measured negative, upgrading the L2 "not verifiable").
- **Tier:** STRONG — WP + GSAP 3.15 + Lenis is a proven Elementor-adjacent stack; the CSS-counter services index is the portable unit. No reduced-motion support is the gap.
- **Best for:** Numbered services-index sections on trade homepages; WP builds that need one clean reveal layer.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-9.md (entry Q571). **Code:** code-source/aha-au/ (full bank — not in the packs).

## [BANK] Q236 ★ · Custom-Shaped Cursor Trail (Three.js + TSL) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-9.md)
- **Reference source:** tympanus.net/codrops/2026/09/24/custom-shaped-cursor-trail/
- **How it looks:** A fullscreen WebGPU canvas holding a word/image printed as ink on paper. Moving the pointer drags a shaped trail (circle, hatch, dots, or PNG brushes — six brushes demoed) across it: the image warps along the trail's flow field, the trail is coloured by pointer speed (red→yellow→orange ramp), and the picture relaxes back to still as the trail decays.
- **Frame by frame:** Pointer moves → per-frame velocity is deposited into a grid trail field: R/G = flow = NEGATED travel direction (looks dragged, not pushed), B = speed → the field decays frame-rate-independently (k = decay^(delta·60), applied to R,G,B every frame) → the output pass samples the source texture through UVs warped by the flow → a 3×3 Gaussian read smoothing softens the warp → at rest the field fades to zero and the un-warped still frame returns (that still frame is explicitly the reduced-motion fallback). Frame order: fade → deposit → texture.needsUpdate = true.
- **Mechanism & key values:** R3F + Three.js WebGPU renderer + TSL, MeshBasicNodeMaterial; no versions stated. Canvas frameloop "never" until renderer.init() resolves, then "always"; orthographic camera [0,0,1], one fullscreen quad — all fragment work. Trail field: CPU Float32Array(4·grid·grid) → DataTexture RGBA/FloatType, NearestFilter both (deliberate, keeps the pattern sharp); **grid 200×200** (160,000 floats). Deposit: cell index i = 4·(cx + grid·cy), loop bounded to the brush bounding box; dist from cell centre; skip if dist ≥ brushRadius; force = (1 − dist/brushRadius)^falloff; magnitude = strength·force·speed; R += magnitude·(−vx/speed), G likewise, B = min(1, B + magnitude) (the clamp stops slow scrubbing blowing out white). UV warp (core): flow = texture(trailTex, uv).rg; warpedUv = uv + flow·warpStrength, **warpStrength = uniform(1.5)** (must be uniform() — Fn() builds the graph once). Read smoothing: 3×3 Gaussian, weights centre 4 / edges 2 / corners 1, ÷16, offsets ±blurRadius. Brushes: pattern = function of normalised lx/ly (−1…1); default circle = () => 1; hatch worked example: diagonal = (lx−ly)·√½, stripe = fract(diagonal·repeat), return stripe > thickness ? 1 : 0 with **repeat 6, thickness 0.44**; flow rotatable perpendicular for swirl. Source texture: word/image rasterised to an offscreen 2D canvas → CanvasTexture mask; output mix(paper, ink, luminance(source)). GAPS (honest): brushRadius, falloff, strength, decay, blurRadius, trailIntensity are used symbolically — no numeric defaults published; tune on rebuild. Mobile: nothing stated; cursor-only (Inferred: no pointer, no trail).
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — mechanism-study only, phone-hostile; the DataTexture trail-field + decay^(delta·60) maths is the bankable part.
- **Best for:** Desktop hero-canvas experiments; the trail-field technique itself, not a trade-site effect.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-9.md (entry Q236). **Code:** none recorded (demo embedded on the article page).

## [BANK] Q239 ★ · Stylised Mouse Trails with OGL — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-9.md)
- **Reference source:** tympanus.net/codrops/2019/09/24/crafting-stylised-mouse-trails-with-ogl/
- **How it looks:** Coloured ribbon lines chase the cursor across a plain WebGL canvas, tapering to a smooth lens shape (fat in the middle, pointed at both ends). The final demo runs 5 coloured lines, each with randomised springiness, slithering behind the pointer.
- **Frame by frame:** Mouse → NDC (x = (e.x/w)·2−1, y = (e.y/h)·−2+1). Each frame the point chain updates BACKWARDS: point 0 lerps to the mouse, every other point lerps to its predecessor, factor **0.9** → geometry updates and renders. Spring variant (point 0 only): tmp = (mouse−point)·spring; vel = (vel+tmp)·friction; point += vel — with **spring 0.06, friction 0.85** the head overshoots and settles.
- **Mechanism & key values:** OGL (the author's minimal WebGL library, classes used <13kb gzipped, over half maths), ES modules via jsDelivr, plain WebGL shaders, no framework; version not recoverable. Line = duplicated point pairs pushed apart along the line NORMAL in the vertex shader: tangent = normalize(nextScreen−prevScreen) from next/prev attributes, normal = vec2(−tangent.y, tangent.x). Width work happens AFTER projection in NDC (constant screen thickness); aspect correction: multiply next/prev by aspect = vec2(res.x/res.y, 1) (uniform uResolution) before the tangent, divide the normal by aspect after. Base width normal *= 0.1 (NDC spans −1…1, so 0.1 = 10% viewport height). Final trail version discards the camera entirely; points authored in NDC. Polyline defaults: uColor #1b1b1b, uThickness 20 (dropped in the custom-shader version). Renderer dpr 2 in the intro version. Recipes: sine demo count = 100, x = (i/(count−1)−0.5)·3, y = sin(i/10.5)·0.5; circle count = 100, angle = i/(count−2)·2π; shaping demo count = 40; **animated trail = 20 points**, all init [0,0,0]. Width-shaping formulas (uv.y 0…1 along the line): triangle uv.y·0.2 · exponential pow(uv.y,2)·0.2 · zigzag abs(fract(uv.y·2)−0.5)·0.4 · wavy cos(uv.y·12.56)·0.1+0.2 · diamond (1−abs(uv.y−0.5)·2)·0.2 · **chosen final: (1−pow(abs(uv.y−0.5)·2, 2))·0.2** (smooth lens taper). Mobile/reduced-motion: none stated.
- **Tier:** STRONG — a complete, portable recipe: the NDC polyline + 0.9-lerp chain + spring 0.06/0.85 (L2 values confirmed and extended here).
- **Best for:** Custom cursor ribbons / decorative pointer trails on desktop heroes; the width-shaping formula set transfers to any line/trail rendering.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-9.md (entry Q239). **Code:** none recorded (article-level study; code excerpts in the article).

## [BANK] Q252 ★ · WebGPU Fluid Simulations — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-9.md)
- **Reference source:** tympanus.net/codrops/2025/02/26/webgpu-fluid-simulations-high-performance-real-time-rendering/
- **How it looks:** Two linked demos: WebGPU-Ocean (a real-time particle water volume; MLS-MPM and SPH solvers both implemented and toggleable; SPH appears to freeze on Mac) and WaterBall (fluid particles on a sphere, gravity pulling to the centre). Water renders as a smooth surface, not visible dots.
- **Frame by frame:** Per frame the MLS-MPM solver runs P2G (scatter particle mass/momentum to a grid) → grid update → G2P (gather velocities back to particles) — no particle–particle interaction, hence no neighbourhood search, which is the whole performance argument. Currently **2 sim steps per frame** ("a bit too large, occasionally explodes", author's words). Rendering = Screen-Space Fluid Rendering, 5 steps: render depth → render thickness (additive) → smooth both (bilateral/gaussian) → reconstruct normals from the smoothed depth → shade reflection/refraction (thickness)/specular.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Raw WebGPU compute shaders (no Three.js in the sim projects), TypeScript + Vite in the linked repos. This is an EXPLAINER, not a code tutorial — it publishes no shader code or solver constants; numbers are its stated results + two details from its own linked WebGPU-Ocean repo README (labelled). WebGPU enabler: P2G scatter via compute atomicAdd; repo detail: WebGPU atomicAdd is 32-bit-int only, so particle data is fixed-point integers decoded × a constant, e.g. **1e-7**. Performance (Measured, test GPU = iGPU of AMD Ryzen 7 5825U): SPH ~30,000 particles real-time; MLS-MPM ~100,000 on iGPU, ~300,000 on a decent discrete GPU. WaterBall renders SSFR at HALF window resolution; particle size varies with simulated density; particles stretched along velocity; edges highlighted at depth discontinuities. Mobile (Measured): WaterBall runs smoothly on a 6-year-old iPad Air 3 with the WebGPU flag on and particle count "small". Reduced-motion: none.
- **Tier:** NOT-FOR-TRADES — mechanism-study only: it documents the MLS-MPM + SSFR route and its particle budgets; nothing here ships to a trade site.
- **Best for:** Background knowledge / the feasibility ceiling for fluid effects; not a build source.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-9.md (entry Q252). **Code:** none recorded (explainer; demos at webgpu-ocean.netlify.app and waterball.netlify.app as linked in the article).

## [BANK] Q341 ★ · 3D Weather Visualization with R3F — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-9.md)
- **Reference source:** tympanus.net/codrops/2025/09/18/creating-an-immersive-3d-weather-visualization-with-react-three-fiber/
- **How it looks:** A 3D scene that renders the actual forecast: a textured sun or moon in the sky with a warm point light, volumetric-style cloud clusters, instanced rain or snow falling, occasional lightning flashes in storm mode, a star field at night — and three forecast "portal" cards, each containing its own miniature weather scene, that blend open to fullscreen.
- **Frame by frame:** Weather data loads → the condition text maps to a scene (order matters: sunny/clear→sunny; thunder/storm→stormy; cloud/overcast→cloudy; rain/drizzle→rainy; snow/blizzard→snowy; fog/mist branches; default cloudy) and the API localtime hour sets time of day (night ≥19 or ≤6; dawn 6–8; dusk 17–19; else day) → the sun sphere spins (rotation.y = elapsed·0.1) → rain instances fall (speed = rand·0.1+0.05 per frame — code does NOT multiply by delta, frame-rate dependent, noted) and reset to y = 20 at y < −1; snow adds x += sin(elapsed+i)·drift and tumble rotation → lightning: per frame, if Math.random() < 0.003 and not active, a flash fires (pointLight intensity 90, setTimeout 400ms resets to 0) → portal cards blend toward fullscreen at lerp 0.1 per frame.
- **Mechanism & key values:** R3F, drei (Clouds/Cloud, Sky, Stars, MeshPortalMaterial), maath roundedPlaneGeometry, R3F-Ultimate-Lens-Flare, postprocessing EffectComposer/Bloom, axios, WeatherAPI.com; no versions stated. Data layer: forecast.json?days=3&aqi=no&alerts=no, axios timeout 10,000ms; server cache Map key weather:{location lowercase}, CACHE_DURATION 10×60×1000 (10 min); rate limit 15 req/hour; on HTTP 429 return demo weather data instead of erroring. Sun/Moon: sphere args [2,32,32] at [0,4.5,0], MeshBasicMaterial 2k texture, child pointLight intensity 2.5, colour #FFD700, distance 25. Rain (one instancedMesh + one reused Object3D dummy + useMemo particle array): default count 1000; spawn x = (rand−0.5)·20, z same, y = rand·20+10; geometry cylinder [0.01,0.01,0.5,8]; material #87CEEB, transparent, opacity 0.6; invocation counts rainy 800, storm 1500. Snow count 400. Clouds: drei Clouds (MeshLambertMaterial), defaults intensity 0.7, speed 0.1; main cluster segments 80, bounds [12,4,4], volume 15, fade 50; overrides sunny-partly 0.5/0.1, rainy 0.8/0.15, snowy 0.6/0.05; storm cloud segments 60, #8A8A8A, fade 100, speed 0.2, opacity 0.8. Sky sunPosition dawn [100,−5,100], dusk [−100,−5,100], day [100,20,100]; inclination 0.6 transitions / 0.9 day; turbidity 8 / 2. Night: Sky skipped, bg #000000, Stars radius 100, depth 50, count 5000, factor 4, saturation 0, fade, speed 1. Forecast portals ×3: roundedPlaneGeometry [2, 2.5, 0.15], MeshPortalMaterial blur 0, resolution 256; portal data forced is_day = 1, localtime = date+T12:00. Portal-mode optimisation: Rain 100 vs 800, Snow 50 vs 400, clouds 6+→2 — all-rain total 800 + 3×100 = 1,100 particles vs 3,200 unoptimised. Lens flare: opacity 1.00, glareSize 1.68, flareSize 1.68, flareShape 0.81, starPoints 2, ghostScale 0.03, haloScale 3.88; Bloom intensity 0.3, threshold 0.9; flare only when not night and the condition text lacks overcast/rain/storm/snow. Mobile/reduced-motion: none stated.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — mechanism-study; the bankable parts are the instanced precipitation template, the condition→scene mapping, and the portal-mode particle budgets (87.5% precipitation cut).
- **Best for:** Weather/time-aware hero scenes; the instanced-particle + budget-cut pattern for any particle system.

## [BANK] Q344 ★ · Drawing With Light: Lit GPU Tubes with TSL/WebGPU — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-9.md)
- **Reference source:** tympanus.net/codrops/2026/09/07/drawing-with-light-an-exploration-of-lit-gpu-tubes-with-tsl-and-webgpu/
- **How it looks:** ~1,500 glowing light strands shaped like hands, drawn as real lit 3D tubes. Strands grow in from the fingertips in a reveal sweep (a radius gate, not a fade); ~12% of strands carry bright travelling light packets; a click sends a shockwave ring through displacement + emissive flash + core flare, all in sync from one clock; emissive-only bloom makes the strands glow.
- **Frame by frame:** Curves live as control points in a GPU storage buffer → the vertex stage builds each tube from parameter space only (progress along the curve × angle around the section) → wind/curl/pointer displacement and the click shockwave apply after the spline sample → the reveal front sweeps: radius 0 ahead of the front, full behind it, material fully opaque (no transparency sorting cost) → post: emissive-only bloom (from a G-buffer/MRT), then SMAA (renderer MSAA does nothing through a post pipeline). Pointer interaction is in screen space (strand points project to NDC; distance to cursor measured on screen, so the brush stays under the mouse from any camera); camera chase is frame-rate-independent. Per-frame CPU = a few uniform writes.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Three.js WebGPU + TSL on MeshStandardNodeMaterial (real PBR — lights, env maps, roughness/metalness and shadow passes keep working; meshline-style clip-space expansion can't, because no world normal exists there). No versions stated. Parameter space per vertex: progress 0→1, angle 0→2π, quad indices between rings; positions zeroed, normals meaningless. Project grid: **90 tubular × 3 radial segments** (triangular section — at hair thickness, lighting sells roundness before geometry). Tangent by central difference at progress ± EPS, **EPS = half a segment**; radial = N·cos(angle) + B·sin(angle); position = P + radial·radius; the radial direction IS the normal → normalNode override; radius is a function radiusFn(r, progress, angle). Gotcha: **frustumCulled = false** or the mesh culls itself. Frame problem (the article's central lesson): no stateless per-vertex frame is continuous for all tangents (hairy-ball) — branchless orthonormal basis (Duff et al.) → sign(tangent.z) flip → 180° twists (test helix crosses tangent.z = 0 exactly 4× in two turns → exactly 4 pinches); blended reference axes → cross collapses at |tangent.y| ≈ 0.93 → "glitter" slivers; least-aligned axis → never degenerates but switches at ties → "bamboo" snaps; SHIPPED: one fixed reference axis, upAxis default +Z (content runs mostly vertical; +Y would park every curve on the singularity). Authored curves: each strand **49–129 control points**, Catmull-Rom in TSL (linear interpolation explicitly rejected — derivative jumps = visible facets); ONE instanced draw for all strands. Hand authoring (CPU, once at load, cached): weld duplicate vertices → graph; one Dijkstra pass from wrist vertices → geodesic distance field whose gradient points to fingertips (local maxima ARE the fingertips, no manual markers); flow strands ~500 walks from near fingertips; wander strands ~1,000 longer walks with a coverage term; crowding baked into the buffer's 4th channel. Camera chase: **k = 1 − e^(−damping·dt)**. Click shockwave = ONE uniform age reset to 0 on click, read by three shaders. Mobile/reduced-motion: none stated.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — mechanism-study; bankable: the parameter-space tube + radial-as-normal trick, the frame-singularity decision table, the radius-gated reveal, and k = 1−e^(−damping·dt).
- **Best for:** WebGPU light-drawing heroes; the radius-gated reveal and damping formula transfer to any GPU line/tube work.

## [BANK] Q347 ★ · Pixel-to-Voxel Video Drop with Three.js + Rapier — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-9.md)
- **Reference source:** tympanus.net/codrops/2026/01/05/how-to-create-a-pixel-to-voxel-video-drop-effect-with-three-js-and-rapier/
- **How it looks:** A playing video (Shibuya Crossing footage from Pexels) shown as a grid of flat tiles. On trigger, a ripple spreads from the click point: tiles pass through glitch/RGB-shift → pixelated single-colour → full 3D voxels of varying depth; then the voxels become physics bodies and rain down, tumbling. A "BACK TO PLANE" action flies every cube back into a flat video. A dance mode and mouse-grab keep it playful.
- **Frame by frame:** Click sets the ripple centre (click UV, aspect-corrected) → a GSAP-tweened progress uniform sweeps the grid: each tile's depth grows by a smoothstep ripple with a bounce (smooth mode: valSmooth = progressSmooth + sin(progressSmooth·π)·uEffectDepth) or an elastic ripple (organic mode) → a JS mirror of the same maths decides per tile when its voxelisation completes → that tile's Rapier body wakes as Dynamic with gravityScale 0.01 and linearDamping 1.2 and drops with a random initial velocity → restore: gravity disabled for all bodies, a progress object tweens to 1 + staggerStrength over **duration 1.0**, and each body lerps/slerps back to its creation transform.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Three.js + custom GLSL + Rapier physics + GSAP control + Tweakpane GUI; no versions stated. Grid metrics derive cols/rows/count/cellSize/spacing from video w/h, camera, cameraDistance and fitMargin. One InstancedMesh with BoxGeometry(cellSize, cellSize, cellSize) — boxes from the start, flattened in the vertex shader to read as flat tiles; each instance has a matching Rapier RigidBodyDesc.fixed() + ColliderDesc.cuboid. The vertex shader recovers the cell from gl_InstanceID (col = mod(gl_InstanceID, uGridDims.x), row = floor(gl_InstanceID/uGridDims.x)) so the instanced grid samples the video as one cohesive image. Random depth: if shape = "random", Math.random() < 0.2 ? 1.0 : 1.0 + Math.random()·1.5, else 1.0. Voxel depth: baseDepth = 0.05 → targetDepth = mix(1.0, aRandomDepth, uUseRandomDepth). Progress target = maxDist + effectSpread + 0.1. Drop check: spreadThreshold = spread·0.98; drop when currentProgress − spreadThreshold − noiseOffset > 0 AND threshold² > distSq; on drop, **force = spacing·2.0**. activateBody: setBodyType(Dynamic), setGravityScale(0.01), setLinearDamping(1.2), wakeUp(), initial linear velocity (rand−0.5)·force per axis, angular velocity rand−0.5 per axis. Rapier step() is called directly in rAF — deliberately NO fixed-timestep accumulator; the author flags CPU intensity and advises reducing the GUI "Column" value; Rapier's contact-pair cache persists across restores so a second drop feels slightly less intense. GAPS: uEffectSpread default, currentDamp, and the GSAP tween duration/easing for uVoxelateProgress are not published. Mobile/reduced-motion: none stated.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — mechanism-study; bankable: the shader/CPU mirror-maths pattern for GPU-timed physics triggers, baseDepth 0.05 → depth ripple, and the gravityScale 0.01 + linearDamping 1.2 drop recipe.
- **Best for:** Video/image voxelisation showpieces; physics-drop transitions (desktop only).

- **Reference source:** tympanus.net/codrops/2023/12/19/creating-audio-reactive-visuals-with-dynamic-particles-in-three-js/
- **How it looks:** A cloud of shader particles forming procedural shapes (boxes/cylinders) that breathes and distorts with music: high frequencies push the curl-noise amplitude, mids drive a z-offset gain, lows set the time speed; on each detected beat the particle system pulses (GSAP animates scale/position/rotation).
- **Frame by frame:** First user click starts the audio (scene init deferred to first click — autoplay policy) → the analyser splits frequency data into low/mid/high bands → each frame the bands remap into uniforms: amplitude = 0.8 + mapLinear(high, 0, 0.6, −0.1, 0.2); offsetGain = mid·0.6; time step t = mapLinear(low, 0.6, 1, 0.2, 0.5), then time += clamp(t, 0.2, 0.5) → the vertex shader displaces particles toward a curl-noise target by pow(d, 4) → beats dispatch on setInterval(60000/bpm) → particles.onBPMBeat().
- **Mechanism & key values:** Plain WebGLRenderer (built for a music site). Camera PerspectiveCamera(70, aspect, 0.1, 10000). Audio pipeline: AudioLoader loads a Spotify preview URL; AudioAnalyser frequency data; bin index = floor(freqHz · bufferLength / sampleRate); lowFrequency = 10; band averages normalised 0–1; BPM via web-audio-beat-detector guess(audioBuffer). Particles: THREE.Points over procedural geometry — BoxGeometry(1,1,1, w/h/d segments) and cylinders with randomised segments. ShaderMaterial {side: DoubleSide, transparent: true}, uniform size = 2. Vertex: target = position + normal·0.1 + curl(newpos · frequency) · amplitude; d = length(newpos − target) / maxDistance; newpos = mix(position, target, pow(d, 4.)); newpos.z += sin(time) · (0.1 · offsetGain); gl_PointSize = size + (pow(d, 3.) · offsetSize) · (1 / −mvPosition.z). Fragment: circle mask circle(uv, 1.); color = mix(startColor, endColor, vDistance); alpha = circ.r · vDistance. Techniques credited in the article: FBO + curl noise (Akella/Yuri Artiukh), Ashima WebGL noise, Book of Shaders circle function. GAPS: demo URL not captured this pass (the demo is linked from the article page — not asserted). Mobile/reduced-motion: none mentioned. (This entry is the full version of L2 chunk-3 #62, logged there as a duplicate of the chunk-3 #232 article — queue treats 62 as the promoted original.)
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — mechanism-study; the band→uniform mapping table and the pow(d,4) curl-displacement vertex recipe are the bankable units.

## [BANK] Q224 ★ · Distort Image Using Fragment Shader (CodePen, marksunming) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-9.md)
- **Reference source:** CodePen pen JjELdyK by marksunming (uniquely identified: exact-title search returned exactly one pen; full HTML/CSS/JS + both shaders captured from the pen embed).
- **How it looks:** A single photograph (an Unsplash photo, w=800&q=80) on a sky-blue page that melts sideways as a progress value rises: the image's Y is pulled by a displacement texture and the red/green/blue channels separate by increasing amounts, so the picture smears into RGB-split streaks.
- **Frame by frame:** In the pen, a dat.GUI slider is the ONLY driver — gui.add(settings, "progress", 0, 1, 0.01), default 0; no tween, no pointer. Each frame, material.uniforms.progress.value = settings.progress → the fragment shader samples the displacement texture with swizzled .yx coordinates, offsets displacedUV.y toward displacement.r − 0.1 by progress, then re-samples per channel with Y-offsets scaled by progress. On a real site, drive progress with a GSAP ScrollTrigger scrub or hover tween instead of the GUI slider.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Three.js **0.117.0** (OrbitControls from unpkg three@0.117.0 examples/jsm); dat.GUI progress slider; displacement texture imported from another of the author's pens. WebGLRenderer({antialias: true}), clear colour 0x87cefa, outputEncoding sRGBEncoding. Camera PerspectiveCamera(70, aspect, 0.001, 1000) at (0,0,1) + OrbitControls. Geometry PlaneBufferGeometry(1,1,1,1) — ONE segment: all distortion is fragment-side, the cheapest possible form of this effect. ShaderMaterial {side: DoubleSide, transparent: true}, derivatives extension enabled. Fragment (complete): displacement = texture2D(disp, vUv.yx) — note the SWIZZLED .yx sample; displacedUV.y = mix(displacedUV.y, displacement.r − 0.1, progress) — Y only; per-channel RGB shift re-samples with Y-offsets scaled by progress: **r 5.0·0.005 = 0.025, g 5.0·0.01 = 0.05, b 5.0·0.02 = 0.1**. Dead code logged honestly: the loop does time += 0.05 per frame but the time uniform is never written back to the material; the resolution (v4) uniform is declared but NEVER populated. Mobile/reduced-motion: none in pen.
- **Tier:** STRONG — complete and tiny; the .yx swizzle + asymmetric RGB offsets (0.025/0.05/0.1) are the exact values to bank.
- **Best for:** Hover/scroll image-distortion accents on hero or gallery images (swap the GUI slider for a tween).

- **Reference source:** tympanus.net/codrops/2026/08/12/creating-an-interactive-3d-cluster-with-three-js-tsl-and-three-start/
- **How it looks:** A faceted 3D blob — an icosahedron whose faces are extruded into prisms — slowly spinning, its surface breathing with noise. Hovering swells the faces near the cursor and mixes in a yellow matcap; a Sobel edge pass + Bayer dither gives the render a printed, graphic finish.
- **Frame by frame:** The cluster spins (rotation.y += dt · speed; instance used Spin, −0.4; default parameter 1) → noise continuously inflates/deflates faces (scale remapped 0.15–0.75) → the pointer raycasts an INVISIBLE inner mesh (BackSide + flatShading, final state colorWrite: false, depthWrite: false — kept ONLY as the raycast target) → the hover point tweens to the hit point (duration 0.5, ease power2.out, overwrite: true) while effectStrength rises →1 in 0.5s and falls →0 in 0.2s → faces near the hover point scale up (up to +0.45) and blend toward the matcap → post: Sobel operator on the scene depth texture, .step(0.01); output = scene colour + sobel; then bayerDither(result).
- **Mechanism & key values:** three + three-start + gsap (pnpm); imports from three/webgpu and three/tsl; three-start scaffolds loop/renderer/camera/resize. Camera position.z = 4. No version numbers stated. Base mesh: IcosahedronGeometry(1, 1). Face extrusion via BatchedMesh(numFaces, numVertices·6, numVertices·6, ClusterMaterial), numFaces = numVertices / 9; per face: geometry recentred on its centroid, instance matrix = translation to centroid; extrusion: 3 extra vertices offset along the face normal by **faceExtrusion = 0.45** → a 24-vertex prism per face; one face's winding swapped to fix normals. Position node (TSL): centroid = positionLocal − attribute('position'); t = time · 0.5; noise = mx_noise_float(centroid.yz + t) remapped −1..1 → **scaleMin 0.15 / scaleMax 0.75**; return centroid + centered · noise. Colour: colorA vec3(0.8), colorB vec3(0); dotRemapped = dot(normalWorld, toOrigin).remap(−1, 1, 0, 1); colour = mix(colorB, colorA, smoothstep(0.35, 0.95, dotRemapped)). Hover: raycast via GSAP Observer (type pointer) against the invisible inner mesh; uniforms hoverPointWS vec3(0), effectStrength 0; hoverEffect(p) = distance(p, hoverPointWS).clamp(0,1).smoothstep(0.8, 0.2) · effectStrength; scaleByHover = hover.remap(0, 1, 0, 0.45) added to the noise scale. Matcap: "Yellow 18" from /yellow-18.png, SRGBColorSpace; placeholder 1×1 DataTexture([0,0,0,0]) in the exported map uniform; final colour mixes colorA → matcap by hover amount. Mobile/reduced-motion: none stated; pointer-based (touch arrives via the same pointer events — Inferred).
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — mechanism-study; bankable: the invisible-raycast-proxy pattern, hover falloff smoothstep(0.8, 0.2), asymmetric strength tweens (in 0.5 / out 0.2).

## [BANK] Q230 ★ · High-Speed Light Trails in Three.js ("Infinite Lights") — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-9.md)
- **Reference source:** tympanus.net/codrops/2019/11/13/high-speed-light-trails-in-three-js/
- **How it looks:** A night highway from a low camera: two roads of streaming light trails — red (0xff102a) on the left, white (0xfafafa) on the right — bending through a distorted landscape. Holding the mouse down speeds the traffic up and widens the camera's FOV until it feels like acceleration.
- **Frame by frame:** Trails loop endlessly: zOffset = len − mod(uTime·uSpeed + aOffset.z, uTravelLength) (the mod-loop) → mousedown raises speedUpTarget to 0.1 (0 on up/out), eased by a helper lerp (speed 0.1, limit 0.001) with the frame-rate-independent form lerpT = exp(−coefficient · delta) — the old 0.1@60fps coefficient converts as −60 · log2(1 − 0.1) → timeOffset += speedUp · delta → FOV target swings **90 → 140** on mousedown (camera.fov += fovChange · delta · 6, then updateProjectionMatrix()) → road and lights bend through the distortion function as they travel.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Three.js, ShaderMaterial + InstancedBufferGeometry, distortion injected via onBeforeCompile (string-replacing a #include <getdistortion_vertex> placeholder). Road (Measured): PlaneBufferGeometry(width, length, 20, 200), uColor 0x101012, rotation.x = −π/2, position.z = −length/2. Camera (0, 7, −4). Light geometry: base curve LineCurve3((0,0,0), (0,0,−1)); TubeBufferGeometry(curve, 25, 1, 8, false) — unit length/radius, scaled per instance in shader; InstancedBufferGeometry, maxInstancedCount = nPairs · 2, FrontSide for performance. aOffset (vec3): lane section = i % 3; carWidth = 0.5 · sectionWidth; offsetX = 0.5 · random(); offsetY = radius · 1.3; pair pushed at sectionX ∓ carWidth/2 + offsetX, same −offsetZ. aMetrics (vec2): radius = random·0.1 + 0.1; length = random·length·0.08 + length·0.02. Vertex: transformed.xy *= radius; transformed.z *= len; then offset applied. Two roads: meshes offset x = ∓(roadWidth/2 + islandWidth/2). Distortion module: uniforms uDistortionX Vector2(80, 3), uDistortionY Vector2(−40, 2.5) (amplitude, frequency); nsin(v) = sin(v)·0.5 + 0.5; getDistortion(progress) = (xAmp · nsin(progress·π·xFreq − π/2), yAmp · nsin(progress·π·yFreq − π/2), 0), progress clamped 0..1; lights use progress = abs(transformed.z / uTravelLength); road uses progress = (y + uTravelLength/2) / uTravelLength and applies distortion.y to transformed.z (pre-rotation axes). GAP (honest): the article body does NOT state the global option values (roadWidth / roadSections / islandWidth / length / nPairs) — they live in the linked CodeSandbox demos; none invented here. Mobile/reduced-motion: none mentioned.
- **Tier:** STRONG — bankable: instanced tube trails with per-instance aOffset/aMetrics, the mod-loop travel formula, and the frame-rate-independent lerp conversion −60·log2(1−0.1).
- **Best for:** Night-drive / speed-themed hero backgrounds; the mod-loop + lerp-conversion maths transfers to any looping instanced motion.

- **Reference source:** Codrops tutorial "Interactive Particles with Three.js" by Bruno Imbrizi — the article URL was not surfaced by the logged searches (route log in the entry: two site-scoped searches did not surface it; older tutorial, not blocked); parameters below are repo-Measured from the author's own repo github.com/brunoimbrizi/interactive-particles, which the repo itself states was created as the tutorial accompanying the Codrops article.
- **How it looks:** A photograph rebuilt as tens of thousands of tiny round particles — one per visible pixel. Moving the pointer over it pushes a soft circular dent through the particle field: particles swell, scatter in Z and slide radially where the touch passes, then settle back as the touch fades over ~2 seconds.
- **Frame by frame:** Image loads → pixels with **red channel ≤ 34 (hex #22) are discarded**; one instanced billboard quad per surviving pixel → pointer raycasts an invisible hitArea plane → the intersection UV paints a stamp into a 64×64 off-screen canvas (TouchTexture) whose intensity fades in over the first 0.3 of its life and out over the rest → the vertex shader samples uTouch at the particle's UV and displaces it (strength 20.0, direction from a per-particle random angle, scaled by a noise-driven rndz) → show(): uSize 0.5 → 1.5, uRandom → 2.0, uDepth 40.0 → 4.0 over time · 1.5; hide(): uRandom → 5.0, uDepth → −20.0 with Quad.easeIn, uSize → 0 over time · 0.8.
- **Mechanism & key values:** three **r98**; GSAP **v2** (TweenLite/TimelineLite); glslify + glsl-noise (2D simplex snoise); controlkit GUI; stats.js; domready; browser-detect (switches passive touch vs mouse listeners — the mobile note); Webpack 4 + Babel. RawShaderMaterial + InstancedBufferGeometry. Core mechanism: GPU-side interaction via the off-screen 2D canvas uploaded as texture uTouch — no per-particle CPU updates. Per-instance attributes: pindex (flat pixel index), offset = (i % width, floor(i / width), 0), angle = random · π. TouchTexture constants (Measured): canvas **64×64**; **maxAge = 120 frames** (~2s at 60fps); base **radius = 0.15 of size** (= 9.6px at full intensity); force = min(dd · 10000, 1), dd = squared UV distance from the previous point; radial gradient inner stop at radius · 0.25 with rgba(255,255,255,0.2), outer rgba(0,0,0,0); canvas cleared to black and repainted every frame, texture.needsUpdate = true. Vertex displacement: luminance grey = colA.r·0.21 + colA.g·0.71 + colA.b·0.07 (BT.601); XY scatter (random(pindex) − 0.5, random(offset.x + pindex) − 0.5) · uRandom, random() = fract(sin(n) · 43758.5453123); Z noise rndz = random(pindex) + snoise(vec2(pindex·0.1, uTime·0.1)); touch: displaced.z += t · 20.0 · rndz; displaced.x += cos(angle) · t · 20.0 · rndz; displaced.y += sin(angle) · t · 20.0 · rndz. Size: psize = (snoise(vec2(uTime, pindex) · 0.5) + 2.0) · max(grey, 0.2) · uSize; billboard in view space. Fragment: greyscale from the source texture; circular alpha mask dist = 0.5 − distance(uv, vec2(0.5)), alpha = smoothstep(0.0, 0.3, dist). Uniform defaults uTime 0, uRandom 1.0, uDepth 2.0, uSize 0.0; depthTest: false, transparent: true. Honesty note: the L2 figures (57,600 points from a 320×180 image) are CONSISTENT with the repo mechanism (one instance per visible pixel; 320×180 = 57,600 max before culling) but the exact image dimensions were not re-verified this pass — 320×180 / 57,600 stay **Inferred-from-bank**; the red ≤ 34 cull is repo-Measured. Reduced-motion: none.
- **Tier:** STRONG — bankable: the touch-texture pattern (64×64 canvas, maxAge 120, radius 0.15, force min(dd·10000, 1)) lets thousands of particles react to a pointer with zero per-particle CPU work; the dark-pixel cull (red ≤ 34) is the image→particles conversion rule.

- **How it looks:** A line of Cinzel text (sand colour #ECCFA3 on near-black #111111) that dissolves over 5 seconds: a Perlin threshold eats the glyphs away, the colour desaturating to grey as it goes, while dust motes and red/white petals spawn inside the text's bounds, drift on wind (−1,0,0), wobble and tumble away. Selective bloom makes text, petals and dust glow at different intensities; a fixed control bar (200px, clip-path corner-cut buttons) sits at the bottom.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger → ONE shared uProgress tweens 0→1 (**gsap.to(uProgress, {value: 1, duration: 5, ease: "linear"})** — an earlier draft used duration 4; 5s is final) → dissolve = step(uProgress, perlinRemap) with the Perlin field remapped 0.4–0.87 (before this remap the text had fully dissolved by progress 0.7) → colour #ECCFA3 → #5E5E5E via smoothstep(0, uDesatComplete = 0.45, uProgress) → meanwhile two repeating GSAP spawn tweens (dust interval 0.125s, petal interval 0.05s, repeat −1, onRepeat) emit particles at random positions inside the text bounds for the whole run → dust (life 4s) scales in over the first 5% of life and fades out over the last 20%; petals (life 6s) bend and spin as they rise → reset snaps value to 0 instantly and kills both spawn tweens; retrigger blocked while a run is active.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Vite; three from three/webgpu + TSL from three/tsl — GAP: the exact three version string was obscured in extraction, none asserted; three-msdf-text-utils@^1.2.1; GSAP; Tweakpane-style debug class. Renderer: WebGPURenderer({antialias: true}), shadowMap off, ACESFilmicToneMapping, clear 0x111111 alpha 1, setPixelRatio(min(dpr, 2)). Camera fov 45, near 0.1, far 25, position (0,0,5); resize keeps HORIZONTAL fov constant at 45°. MSDF text: font generated with msdf-bmfont from Cinzel-Regular.ttf (--font-size 64 --distance-range 16 --texture-padding 8 --border 2 --smart-size); MSDFTextGeometry {width: 1000, align: "center"}; alphaTest = 0.1; text scaled so line height = **targetLineHeight 0.3** world units — DISCREPANCY flagged in the source: the article's prose elsewhere says 0.4; the code value 0.3 governs. Dissolve UVs: customUv = center·0.05 + glyphUv·0.75 (uCenterScale 0.05, uGlyphScale 0.75); perlinRemap = clamp((perlin − 0.4) / (0.87 − 0.4), 0, 1); opacity = msdfOpacity · dissolve. Dust: **MAX_DUST = 100**; PlaneGeometry(0.02, 0.02); InstancedMesh; packed instanced attribute aBirthLifeSeedScale (birth = performance.now()·0.001, **life = 4s**, seed = random, scale = random·0.5 + 0.5); ring buffer wraps index to 0; colour #8A8A8A × dust-texture alpha; wind uWindDirection (−1,0,0) normalised, uWindStrength 0.3, uRiseSpeed 0.1; turbulence uNoiseScale 30.0, uNoiseSpeed 0.015, uWobbleAmp 0.6. Petals: **MAX_PETAL = 400**; geometry from GLB /models/petal.glb, object "PetalV2", pre-scaled **0.15**; **life = 6s**; uBendAmount 2.5, uBendSpeed 1.0, bendWeight = pow(uv.y, 3.0); uSpinSpeed 2.0, uSpinAmp 0.45; colour uRedColor #9B0000, uWhiteColor #EEEEEE, petalColor = mix(red, white, instanceIndex.mod(3).equal(0)) — one third white; fake lighting: facing = clamp(abs(dot(normal, lightDirection)), 0.4, 1). Selective bloom via MRT: bloomPass = bloom(outputPass · bloomIntensityPass, **0.8**); per-material MRT bloom intensities: text 0.4 · dissolve, petals 0.7 · fadingOut, dust 0.5 · fadingOut. Textures: perlin (RepeatWrapping), dust particle, Cinzel atlas — all NoColorSpace, LinearFilter, no mipmaps. Mobile/reduced-motion: none mentioned; requires WebGPU.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — mechanism-study; bankable: one shared uProgress driving dissolve + two coupled particle systems + per-material MRT bloom intensities, the remapped-step dissolve (0.4–0.87), and the packed birth/life/seed/scale instanced attribute.
- **Best for:** Headline dissolve showpieces (WebGPU); the shared-progress orchestrator pattern for multi-system effects.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-9.md (entry Q235). **Code:** none recorded (the article links a demo repo whose commits match the tutorial sections; repo URL not captured verbatim — not invented).

### — Slice 1: live-site source passes + L2-Measured pen/tutorial entries (queue 3–49) —

## [BANK] Q3 · Ronin161 portfolio — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-1.md)
- **Reference source:** ronin161.com
- **How it looks:** A cel-shaded (toon) 3D character rendered with a custom toon material (gradient-map quantised lighting) sits in a fixed WebGL canvas; page content itself is conventional DOM over the canvas. The deeper you scroll, the more the character's image is distorted.
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll progress is divided into bands → one ScrollTrigger per effect band writes its progress into a post-processing uniform → the effects run in sequence, not stacked — vignette, RGB shift, bulge/pinch, a fluid-sim pass and datamoshing-style smear — so the character distorts progressively more the deeper you scroll.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Nuxt + Prismic + Three.js (three 0.161) + GSAP 3.12.5 (L2-Measured via the Codrops case study). Source pass: same-host bundles mined, but ScrollTrigger references 0 in same-host JS — the motion code ships in the Nuxt payload/CDN chunks, so parameters are article-stated. The transferable core is the *scroll→uniform binding pattern*: one ScrollTrigger per effect band, progress written into a shader uniform, effects sequenced not stacked. The character itself (model + toon rig) is a multi-day asset build; the full post stack (5 chained passes = GPU cost per frame) would not survive copying to phones.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — the scroll→uniform banding pattern (LIB) transfers to a single hero canvas (e.g. a roof/house illustration that subtly distorts), desktop accent only; the character pipeline does not.
- **Best for:** Scroll-sequenced shader accents on a single hero canvas.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-1.md (entry Q3). **Code:** code-source/ronin161/ (full bank — not in the packs).

## [BANK] Q4 · Ragged Edge — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-1.md)
- **Reference source:** raggededge.com
- **How it looks:** A conventional-scroll agency site whose motion is almost entirely content reveals in service of proof: metric-led case cards (large valuation/store-count numbers as the headline of each card, not the client name), staggered card entrances, linear-scrubbed elements where progress itself is the message. Structure: hero claim → case cards led by the metric → services → team → contact. No pinning theatre, no WebGL.
- **Frame by frame:** Case cards stagger in on power2.out reveals (rebuild values: 0.4–0.6s durations, cards stagger ~0.08–0.1); scrubbed elements move linearly with scroll.
- **Mechanism & key values:** GSAP + ScrollTrigger mined in same-host JS (12 refs, 38 ST configs), IntersectionObserver ×6, rAF ×60 (custom loop code). Eases mined: linear ×12, power2.out ×6, power2.in ×2, power4 ×2. This is a structure recipe, not an effects recipe (LIB: case-card structure + reveal set — power2.out, 0.4–0.6s). Nothing technical fails to survive copying — the risk is content: metrics must be real.
- **Tier:** STRONG — the default agency skeleton (banked for Asiful's own site, dentivax.com); metric-first case cards port directly.
- **Best for:** Proof-led case-study sections on agency and trade sites.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-1.md (entry Q4). **Code:** code-source/ragged-edge/ (full bank — not in the packs).

## [BANK] Q6 · Joffrey Spitzer — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-1.md)
- **Reference source:** joffreyspitzer.com
- **How it looks:** A portfolio where page changes feel continuous: click a project link and its title flies from its list position/size into the detail-page hero — the title never visually "jumps". A slider↔grid toggle re-layouts the same cards as a morph, not a reload. Headings enter with a global SplitText diagonal "clipTitle" reveal.
- **Frame by frame:** Click a project link → Flip.getState captures the title element → the Swup page swap happens → Flip.from animates the title from list geometry into the hero. Toggle the view → Flip.getState → class change → Flip.from morphs every card between slider and grid layouts. L2 caveat stands: the preloader (steps(14)) stuck at 100 in the browser pass — do not copy the preloader.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Astro + vanilla JS + GSAP (ScrollTrigger ×6, SplitText ×2, Flip) + Lenis ×1 + Three.js + Swup + Tailwind + Prismic (Mined + L2); 1 cross-host asset skipped. Flip transitions need stable element identity across views; in Elementor terms this maps to a shared hero title block reused across page templates. LIB: Flip.getState/Flip.from transition recipe. Swup itself doesn't transfer (WordPress routing differs).

Segment travel + long repeatDelay is the tasteful version of path animation; full-path continuous loops read cheap.
- **Mechanism & key values:** GSAP MotionPathPlugin; L2-Measured from pen JS. LIB: segment 0.25→0.80, autoRotate, repeatDelay 5.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — a dotted-route divider animation (van/plane along a route) at segment 0.25–0.80, repeatDelay ≥4–5.
- **Best for:** Route/journey divider accents.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-1.md (entry Q36). **Code:** none (L2-Measured values only; pen source account-gated).

## [BANK] Q40 · Direction-aware reveals (GreenSock pen pojzxwZ) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-1.md)
- **Reference source:** GreenSock pen pojzxwZ (the bank records only the pen id for this entry; fullpage source curled and verified 26 Oct).
- **How it looks:** Section content enters FROM the direction of scroll: scroll down and elements rise in from +100px below, fading in; reverse and scroll up and the next elements drop in from −100px above — content always arrives from where the user is heading.
- **Frame by frame:** ScrollTrigger onToggle/onEnter/onEnterBack fires → self.direction is checked → a fromTo tween sets y to +100px when scrolling down, −100px when scrolling up, with **autoAlpha 0→1, duration 1.25, ease expo** → overwrite: "auto" means a direction change mid-flight retargets cleanly instead of queueing competing tweens (without it, fast scroll reversals stack tweens and elements flicker). On small phone sections, halve the travel to ~50px.
- **Mechanism & key values:** GSAP ScrollTrigger + fromTo; source-verified (fullpage source). LIB: fromTo ±100px, 1.25s expo, overwrite auto, direction from ScrollTrigger self.direction. L2 scored it **Rel 5 / Fit 5**.
- **Tier:** CROWN — the house reveal candidate: source-verified, the strongest transferable yield in the slice (per the slice's own summary).
- **Best for:** The default section entrance for every section of trade templates.

## [BANK] Q41 · Ghost Trails / A Drift — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-1.md)
- **Reference source:** tympanus.net/Demos/ADrift

The R3F stack itself doesn't transfer to Elementor, and 3D product grids don't fit services (products ≠ services).

## [BANK] Q50 · LottieScrollTrigger — SVG renderer (GreenSock pen mdGdbwO) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md)
- **Reference source:** https://codepen.io/GreenSock/pen/mdGdbwO
- **How it looks:** A page of full-screen sections, each holding a Lottie animation in a grey (`#ccc`) container. The animation does not play on its own — it is a filmstrip tied to the scrollbar: scroll and the vector drawing animates, stop scrolling and it freezes on the exact frame.
- **Frame by frame:** A section scrolls to the top and pins → continued scrolling scrubs the Lottie playhead from frame 0 to the last frame, linearly, over the pinned distance → the section unpins and the next one takes over. Three sections run the same system with different start points.
- **Mechanism & key values:** GSAP + ScrollTrigger + lottie-web, SVG renderer, one reusable `LottieScrollTrigger` helper (~45 lines). Tweened playhead object `{frame: 0}` with `ease: "none"`, `onUpdate` → `goToAndStop(frame, true)`; scrub 1 on all three instances; pin distance set by a speed map — slow `+=2000`, medium `+=1000`, fast `+=500`; `preserveAspectRatio: 'xMidYMid slice'`; below the 749px breakpoint the starts change (`"center 45%"` vs `"center center"` / `"center 55%"`); tween is created only after the Lottie's `DOMLoaded`, then `ScrollTrigger.sort()` + `refresh()`. No reduced-motion handling in the pen.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Scroll-scrubbed illustrated process sections (a roof/anatomy drawing that builds as you scroll), hero storytelling. Keep Lottie files low-path-count on mobile; three pinned sections add ~3,000px of scroll travel.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md (entry Q50). **Code:** code-source/50-lottiescrolltrigger-svg/

The transferable trick is the global `path{stroke:<brand>}` recolour of Lottie SVGs.
