## [BANK] Q53 · How to Animate SVG Shapes on Scroll — OnScrollPathAnimations (Codrops) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2022/06/08/how-to-animate-svg-shapes-on-scroll/
- **How it looks:** Sections divided by a wide, shallow wave edge (150px tall) filled with the page background colour, so the wave reads as the shaped bottom edge of the full-bleed image above it. In the second form, a portrait photograph is clipped inside an organic blob outline instead of a rectangle.
- **Frame by frame:** As the separator SVG crosses the viewport (start "top bottom" → end "bottom top"), the wave's control points sink from a flat line into a deep curve — the edge visibly sags and reshapes continuously with scroll, then settles. The clipped photograph's blob edge morphs the same way while the photo itself stays still. No pinning, no extra scroll length.
- **Mechanism & key values:** GSAP ScrollTrigger tweening the SVG `d` attribute (`attr:{d: pathTo}`, ease 'none', scrub true) — start shape in `d`, end shape in `data-path-to`, and both paths must share identical command/point structure (design the complex shape first, derive the flat one). Separator spec: `viewBox 0 0 100 10`, `preserveAspectRatio="none"`, height 150px, z-index 1000, `vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"`. Clip variant worked example: 500×750 clip path pair printed in full in the entry. Lenis smooth scroll at lerp 0.1 (2022 manual-rAF wiring).
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Section separators and image reveals on content sites — the cheapest entry in its batch: GSAP core only, no pin, no WebGL, near-zero phone cost. Add a reduced-motion gate that sets the final path (none in the article).

## [BANK] Q54 · Responsive Scroll-Triggered Curved Path Animations (Codrops / betawaxx) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2025/12/17/building-responsive-scroll-triggered-curved-path-animations-with-gsap/ (working configurator pen: https://codepen.io/betawaxx/pen/JoGZQLZ; the effect originates from a hero built for Lando Norris's site)
- **How it looks:** A tall hero section with three empty anchor spots arranged down the page. A single image (the "traveller") floats above the layout and, as you scroll, glides down an invisible S-curve from the first spot to the second to the third, growing and shrinking to match each spot's size as it arrives.
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll starts → the traveller leaves anchor 1 heading mostly downward (80% vertical pull) → curves in to land exactly centred on anchor 2 at the scroll's midpoint, resizing from anchor 1's box to anchor 2's box → leaves with a small capped dip → swings in from the upper-left to settle on anchor 3 at its size. Resizing the window rebuilds the whole curve from the re-measured boxes within 200ms, keeping the traveller's scroll progress.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Vanilla JS + GSAP MotionPathPlugin; the path is a generated string, not a DOM path: two cubic segments through three measured anchor centres, control points from four multipliers (0.8 / 0.3 / 0.6 / 0.2) with caps min(800px) on the approach pull and min(80px) on the exit dip. ScrollTrigger trigger = section, start 'top top', end 'bottom bottom', scrub true, invalidateOnRefresh true; tween duration 1.5, ease 'none', autoRotate false; traveller centred with xPercent/yPercent −50; size lerp split at progress 0.5 (×2 normalisation per half). The pen's dev configurator (draggable control points, `#ff0040` path overlay, copy-values export) is fully specified in the entry; production hard-codes the exported points and deletes the overlay. Reduced-motion pattern given: `gsap.matchMedia()` jump straight to the final anchor.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Heroes where one product image journeys between layout positions; process/story sections. The most portable deep read in its batch — no pin, one tween, adapts to any viewport because the curve is computed from measured boxes.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md (entry Q54). **Code:** the configurator pen above (pen JS captured verbatim in the entry).

## [BANK] Q55 · 3D Scroll-Driven Text Animations with CSS and GSAP — Cylinder (Codrops) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2025/11/04/creating-3d-scroll-driven-text-animations-with-css-and-gsap/ (demo: https://tympanus.net/Tutorials/3DTextScroll/; repo: https://github.com/davidfaure/3d-text-animation-codrops/)
- **How it looks:** A full-screen section of huge bold words (5vw type) standing on the front face of an invisible rotating drum — words arc over the top and under the bottom like text printed on a spinning can, the ones near the edges tilting away in 3D. Two bonus variants in the same entry: two flat circles of words counter-rotating like twin carousels, and a horizontal tube of words rolling sideways.
- **Frame by frame:** The section pins → scrolling rotates the drum a 350° sweep (rotateX −80° → 270°) across 20 viewport-heights of pinned scroll, with a heavy 2-second scrub lag so the drum glides after the scrollbar → words continuously rise over the crown and sink under the base, backfaces hidden so nothing reads mirrored. The Double Circle variant needs no pin: a half-rotation plays out as the section crosses the viewport, left ring turning one way, right ring the other, with a 180° flip keeping the counter-rotating side's text upright.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Pure CSS 3D — no Three.js/WebGL. Stage `perspective: 70vw` (≤768px: 400px); items placed with `radius = 0.4 × min(vw, vh)`, spacing 180°/N on the visible half only, `backface-visibility: hidden` (load-bearing); ScrollTrigger start "center center", end "+=2000svh", pin, scrub 2, ease "none"; font 5vw (132px fixed ≥2560px, 1.6rem ≤768px); ScrollSmoother `smooth: 1` app-wide (optional — works on native scroll). Tube variant: spacing 360°/N, rotateY 0→360, same trigger. Circle variant: spacing π/N, direction ±1, progress ×0.5, scrub 1, unpinned.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Services/word-list showcase sections, big statement dividers. The most Elementor-portable 3D effect in the bank (one list + ~60 lines of JS, zero assets) — but cut the pinned end to ~600–800svh on mobile; the article's 20-screen scroll-jack is the phone warning.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md (entry Q55). **Code:** code-source/55-3d-text-scroll/ (demo shell only — parameters are article-stated, cross-checked against the repo).

- **Tier:** STRONG (partial record — reveal grammar and scroll config are fully mined; the WebGL layer is not).
- **Best for:** A reveal-grammar reference: entrance window, duration cluster and stagger values for fast, agency-style page motion.

The resize pattern is the point of the demo: `progress()` → `revert()` → rebuild → `.progress(saved)`. Path: `viewBox="-20 0 557 190"`, `vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke`; container capped square by `max-width: 90vh; max-height: 90vw`; follower sized 20% × 20% of the container; caption hides below 350px. No reduced-motion handling in the pen.

Two master curves cover the whole set: `cubic-bezier(0.7,0,0.3,1)` (×8, the sweep) and `cubic-bezier(0.2,1,0.3,1)` (×8, the spring); dominant durations transform 0.5s (×7) and 0.4s (×3), colour 0.5s; staged second-layer delay 0.3s. Named sets: `TEXT-HOVER-CURVES = {sweep: (0.7,0,0.3,1), spring: (0.2,1,0.3,1), durMain: 0.5, durFast: 0.4, stageDelay: 0.3}`, `KUKURI = {barH: 16, wipeDur: 0.4, wipeDelay: 0.3, weight: 900, lh: 0.75}`. Breakpoints at 50em/42em shrink display sizes. No reduced-motion handling.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — hover does not exist on touch; treat as progressive enhancement (tap navigates).
- **Best for:** Navigation links, text CTAs and footer links on desktop-led pages — the most portable entry in its batch: each effect is one copy-paste CSS class plus a `data-letters` attribute where the effect needs one.

- **Frame by frame:** Drag or wheel → the track slides with momentum (velocity decays frame-rate-independently), cards wrapping endlessly in both directions via modulo → each frame, a card's rotation, depth, scale and blur are computed from its signed distance to centre → when the centre card changes, the background gradients tween to its palette over 0.45s (power2.out) and the background loop runs at 60fps for 800ms before idling at ~30fps. On entry, visible cards stagger in from scale 0.92 / +40px / transparent over 0.6s (power3.out, 0.05 per index) after a compositing warm-up pass, with input locked until it finishes.

Palette extraction: image downscaled to max 48px, 36×5 hue/saturation histogram, weight `a·s²·(1−|l−0.5|·0.6)`, saturation boost ×1.15 clamped [0.45, 1], secondary only if ≥25° hue away and ≥0.6× primary weight. Gradient blobs: alphas 0.85/0.70, radii 0.75/0.65 × max dimension, slow orbital drift. Correction to the L2 record: MIN_SCALE measures **0.92** in the deployed script, not 0.8. Reduced motion is partial (CSS kills card transitions; the JS loops are not gated).
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Project, testimonial and before/after galleries — the cheapest rich effect in its batch (own JS 27 KB + ~5 KB CSS; touch drag via Pointer Events). Scope the wheel handler to the stage or the desktop page cannot scroll.

## [BANK] Q89 · Animating SVG Text on a Path (Codrops) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2020/02/26/animating-svg-text-on-a-path/ (source of record: article-linked repo github.com/codrops/AnimateSVGTextPath — the demo URL is 404 today)
- **How it looks:** Huge display text (19vw in the demo) bent along an invisible curved path. As the page scrolls, the words slide along the curve; scroll fast and the letters smear — six of the demo's eight instances blur with speed, two warp through a displacement filter — then sharpen again as scrolling settles.
- **Frame by frame:** An SVG enters the viewport → its text begins sliding along the path, travelling 1.5 path-lengths over the full bottom-to-top transit, the applied offset easing toward the target each frame (lerp 0.22) → a fast scroll flick widens the gap between smoothed and actual scroll (second lerp, 0.17) and the blur/warp amount grows with that gap → scrolling slows, the gap closes, the text sharpens and keeps gliding → the SVG leaves the viewport and its updates stop (IntersectionObserver gate).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Vanilla JS, no GSAP. `<textPath>` `startOffset` mapped `[viewportHeight → 0] ↦ [pathLength → −pathLength/2]`, set every rAF while visible. `TEXTPATH-SCROLL = {lerpPos: 0.22, lerpScroll: 0.17, blurMap: distance 0–400 → stdDeviation 0–10 (demo also runs 30), distortMap: distance 0–200 → scale 0–100 (demo runs 50 and 100), gate: IntersectionObserver ratio > 0}`. Firefox guard: the filter attribute is stripped entirely in Firefox (animated SVG filters are pathologically slow there — bugs cited in the entry). No reduced-motion handling.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — the startOffset/dual-lerp core is cheap (~3 KB hand-ported); per-frame SVG filters are the expensive part and are stripped in Firefox.
- **Best for:** Headline bands and statement sections where a curved, scroll-coupled line of text carries the design.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md (entry Q89). **Code:** none recorded (repo above).

## [BANK] Q90 · Organic Shape Animations with SVG clipPath (Codrops) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2017/06/28/organic-shape-animations-with-svg-clippath/ (source of record: article-linked repo github.com/codrops/OrganicShapeAnimations — the demo URL is 404 today)
- **How it looks:** A grid of photo cards (500×500 SVGs), each photograph clipped inside a soft organic blob instead of a rectangle, with a decorative outline shape floating at the same spot. Hovering (or tapping) makes the blob morph into a second, different blob shape with an elastic wobble, while the photo inside counter-moves and the decoration lags behind — three layers moving at three different speeds. The card's title rolls away and back in two quick steps; the subtitle follows a beat later.
- **Frame by frame:** Pointer rests on a card for 75ms (debounce, so pass-throughs don't flicker) → clip path, image and deco tweens start together: the blob morphs and scales/rotates elastically, the photo counter-scales (≥1.1 so clip edges never show), the deco drifts slower → title translates −50% then rolls 50%→0% (200ms + 200ms, easeOutQuad) with opacity, subtitle enters at a 250ms delay → pointer leaves and everything reverses, except the subtitle, which collapses in 1ms (staged-in, instant-out).
- **Mechanism & key values:** anime.js (11 KB) + per-item `data-*` attributes carrying the morph target and every timing, so the system is fully data-driven. `ORGANIC-CLIP` defaults: path {1500ms, easeOutElastic, elasticity 400}, image {2000ms, easeOutElastic, 400, scale 1.1}, deco {2500ms, easeOutQuad, 400, scale 0.9}; tuned demo set: path {800, easeInOutCubic, 300, scaleX 0.8 / scaleY 1.1, translateY 30, rotate 5}, image {800, easeInOutQuart, 300, scale 1.2, translate −20/−45, rotate −5}, deco {1300, easeOutQuad, 300}; `anime.remove(target)` before every re-tween so reversals interrupt cleanly; path pairs must share command structure. Touch: touchstart/touchend mapped to the same handlers. No reduced-motion handling. Ports 1:1 to GSAP (`attr:{d}` + transforms; elasticity maps to the `elastic.out` family) — keep the three-layer duration ladder, the deco lag is what reads as "organic".
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Service cards, project cards, team cards — any grid where the image container itself should feel alive.

## [BANK] Q91 · Animated SVG Icons with Snap.svg (Codrops) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2013/11/05/animated-svg-icons-with-snap-svg/ (live demo survives: https://tympanus.net/Development/AnimatedSVGIcons/; repo: github.com/codrops/AnimatedSVGIcons)
- **How it looks:** A wall of 42 line icons on a 64×64 canvas that come alive on click: a clock's minute hand spins 630° while its hour hand moves 80°, sound arcs ripple out from a speaker in a staggered wave, a hamburger's outer lines morph into an X while the middle line vanishes, a play triangle morphs into a stop square, an hourglass flips 180° and then swaps its sand to the other bulb.
- **Frame by frame:** Click (or touchstart on touch devices) → each icon's configured steps run: instant "before" attributes apply → each element animates to its "to" attributes at the global speed, its start delayed by `delayFactor × speed` (the volume arcs use 0.5 / 0.25 / 0, producing the ripple) → "after" attributes and optional chained second animations fire on completion (the hourglass sand swap). A second click toggles back. The hover set runs larger (128×128) on mouseover with a back-in ease; the elastic set (hamburgerCross, trash, clock, maximize, contract, glass) pops over 600ms.
- **Mechanism & key values:** The portable asset is the config format, not the library: 24 named configs of `{el, from-attrs, to-attrs, delayFactor}` steps + one global `{speed, easing}`; attribute values are Snap transform strings (`r` rotate w/ centre, `t` translate, `s` scale) or full path `d` strings for morphs. `ICON-TOGGLE = {speed: 200ms, elasticSpeed: 600ms, easings: {default: mina.linear, pop: mina.backin, elastic: mina.elastic}, canvas: 64, hoverSize: 128}`. Do NOT ship Snap.svg (71.6 KB, unmaintained) — re-implemented on GSAP's attr plugin in ~40 lines, the whole 24-icon library costs GSAP core only. No reduced-motion handling (2013 source).
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — the config pattern is strong; the original library is dead tech.
- **Best for:** Service-icon rows (wrench/fan/thermostat icons that animate on tap) — bind click/tap, never hover-only.

- **How it looks:** A wall of nine photographs arranged on an invisible 1522×1238 design tile, repeated seamlessly in every direction — wheel or drag and the wall drifts forever, each photo moving at its own slightly different rate, the photo inside each frame counter-shifting against the drift, and pressing the mouse subtly zooms every photo. Under each photo, a caption whose lines wipe in one by one.
- **Frame by frame:** On load, the on-screen photos start stacked at the viewport centre and explode outward to their grid positions over 2s (expo.inOut, 0.05 stagger, reversed DOM order) → wheel/drag input moves a scroll target (wheel deltas × 0.4, page scroll fully hijacked) while the rendered position lerps after it at 0.06 per frame → items crossing an edge wrap by a doubled tile size, direction-aware → a caption entering view triggers its lines: a 2s custom-bezier wipe per line, each delayed 0.15s more than the last. Resize rebuilds the whole grid and re-anchors scroll.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Hand-rolled lerp engine — despite the title, no ScrollTrigger and no scroll library; GSAP does only the intro and SplitText caption splitting. `INFINITE-GRID = {tile: 1522×1238, reps: 2×2 (36 DOM items), scrollEase: 0.06, lerpAux: 0.04 (delta/mouse/press), wheel: 0.4, itemEase: random [0.5, 1.0] re-rolled per rebuild, parallax: 5×delta + 0.6×rect mouse, img: base scale 1.2, press +0.2, counter-move 10%}`; `INTRO-EXPLODE = {2s, expo.inOut, stagger 0.05, from viewport centre}`; `CAPTION-LINES = {transition 2s, cubic-bezier(0.6,0.14,0,1), delay 0.15s/line, gate: IntersectionObserver .visible}`. No touch handlers in source (mouse only — on phones the grid is effectively static) and no reduced-motion handling.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — the wheel preventDefault makes it a page-level scroll trap anywhere except a dedicated full-screen section; the intro and caption systems lift out cleanly for normal pages.
- **Best for:** Full-screen gallery walls; separately, the centre-out intro for a photo wall and the SplitText-lines caption reveal anywhere.

## [BANK] Q93 · Elastic Grid Scroll with GSAP ScrollSmoother (Codrops) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2025/06/03/elastic-grid-scroll-creating-lag-based-layout-animations-with-gsap-scrollsmoother/ (demo: https://tympanus.net/Tutorials/ElasticGridScroll/ + index2/3/4 variants; repo: github.com/codrops/ElasticGridScroll)
- **How it looks:** A plain grid of portrait photos (128/160 aspect). Scroll and the columns chase the page at different rates — the grid stretches and relaxes like elastic as you speed up and slow down. In the second demo the photos also squash and stretch with scroll velocity, elongating up to 1.7× vertically when you flick hard, then settling back to shape.
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll begins → each column lags behind the scroll position by an amount set by its column index, so columns separate and trail → scrolling steadies and the trailing columns catch up, the grid re-knitting itself → in demo 2, a fast flick past 700px/s additionally squashes items (scaleX down to 0.7, scaleY up to 1.7, transform-origin flipping with scroll direction) until velocity drops back under the dead-zone. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` none of this happens: smoothing is forced to 0 and the grid is a plain static grid.
- **Mechanism & key values:** GSAP ScrollSmoother `{smooth: 1, effects: true, normalizeScroll: true}`; JS reads the computed `grid-template-columns`, wraps each column, and applies `smoother.effects(el, {speed: 1, lag})` per item. Four lag distributions over one scaffold — centre: `lag = 0.5 + |i − mid| × 0.1`; velocity-squash variant: base 0.5, scale 0.13, squash thresholds above; linear wave: `lag = 0.2 + (i + 1) × 0.3`; inverted: `lag = 0.3 + (maxDistance − distance + 1) × 0.15` (centre lags most). Grid: 3 columns base → 5/7/9 at min-width 65em, gaps 5vw base → 5px/0, `--column-size: 80px`. Effects rebuild on resize only when the column count changes. ScrollSmoother is a Club plugin (licence note in the entry); a free fallback (per-column quickTo offsets) approximates demos 1/3/4 but not the squash.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Work/project gallery grids that should feel physical without any per-item animation code. Keep grid images ≤ ~60 KB each or the lag reads as jank on mid-range Android.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md (entry Q93). **Code:** code-source/93-elastic-grid-scroll/

## [BANK] Q94 · Sticky Grid Scroll (Codrops, Theo Plawinski) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2026/03/02/sticky-grid-scroll-building-a-scroll-driven-animated-grid/ (demo: https://tympanus.net/Tutorials/StickyGridScroll/; repo: github.com/theoplawinski/codrops-sticky-grid-scroll)
- **How it looks:** A tall (425vh) section with a sticky stage holding a neat 3-column grid of twelve square photos. Scrolling first rains the columns in from alternating directions, then the whole grid zooms toward you to 2.05× and splits open down the middle — side columns sliding out ±40%, centre photos parting up and down — and in the opened gap a title, a paragraph and a button settle into place.
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll progress 0–45% → columns reveal, alternating from top and bottom, items staggered 0.06 apart (power1.inOut) → 45–90% → the zoom sub-timeline runs (power3.inOut): grid scales to 2.05, side columns shift xPercent ∓40, centre-column items split yPercent ±40 over 0.5s → 90–95% → a direction-aware call fades/slides the title (0.7s power2.inOut, from a measured centre offset), description and button (0.4s) in — and reverses them out when scrolling back up. Side pieces: the wrapper parallaxes in from yPercent −100 on entry, and a title fade plays at start "top 57%".
- **Mechanism & key values:** GSAP + ScrollTrigger + Lenis `{lerp: 0.08, wheelMultiplier: 1.4}` wired via `lenis.on("scroll", ScrollTrigger.update)` + GSAP ticker with `lagSmoothing(0)`. Main timeline ST: trigger = the 425vh block, start "top 25%", end "bottom bottom", scrub true. The portability key is fluid rem: `html {font-size: calc(100vw / 1440)}` with the gallery 736rem wide, column-gap 32rem, row-gap 40rem — the whole composition scales proportionally at any width; below 768px the effect simply doesn't run. **Gap:** the shipped CSS has no `prefers-reduced-motion` rules — a rebuild must gate the zoom timeline behind matchMedia.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Gallery→message reveal sections: a photo grid that opens to deliver the pitch. Free plugins only (GSAP + ScrollTrigger + Lenis); in Elementor the 425vh block must be a plain section using the demo's own position:sticky, not Elementor's sticky.

## [BANK] Q95 · Masked Heading (React Bits) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md)
- **Reference source:** https://reactbits.dev/text-animations/masked-heading (source from the site's own registry endpoint reactbits.dev/r/MaskedHeading-JS-CSS, read in full)
- **How it looks:** A giant heading whose letters are windows: a photograph or video shows only inside the letterforms, drifting slowly and shifting against the pointer like the text is a cut-out stencil over a living image. Optionally a soft spotlight disc follows the mouse (or wanders on its own), inside which the letters pick up colour/saturation treatment, and a thin outline copy of the glyphs can sit on top.
- **Frame by frame:** Heading enters view (IntersectionObserver threshold 0.25, plays once) → one of five reveals runs: **rise** — glyphs climb from 1.15em below, word by word (power4.out, 1.1s, 0.09 stagger per word); **scale** — glyphs grow from scale 0 (expo.out); **blur** — glyphs slide in from a 0.22 offset as a 0.3em blur clears; **wipe** — a clip inset opens left-to-right (power3.inOut); or **fade** — the layer fades from scale 1.08. After the reveal, the media inside keeps a slow idle drift (sin/cos cycles) and parallaxes toward the pointer with exponential smoothing, clamped so its overscan never exposes an edge. Under reduced motion the reveal is forced straight to the settled state, video pauses, and the loop stops.
- **Mechanism & key values:** React + GSAP 3.13 only — the mask is an SVG `<clipPath>` of per-glyph `<text>` elements positioned from Range-rect measurements (glyph centre-y = baseline − fontPx × 0.36); per-glyph transforms move glyphs around their own centres. The 29 props are the parameter set; defaults: fillScale 1.25, parallax 26, drift 18 (drift dx = sin(t×0.21)×drift, dy = cos(t×0.17)×drift×0.6; smoothing `1 − exp(−dt/0.18)`, zoom `1 − exp(−dt/0.35)`), textScale 0.115 with font clamp 20–200px, tracking −0.03, lineHeight 1.06, reveal "rise", duration 1.1, stagger 0.09. Spotlight: radius 160, smootherstep falloff `u³(u(6u−15)+10)`, follow tau 0.12s hover / 0.6s idle, tone layer #808080 at `mix-blend-mode: saturation`, shade black at 0.55. ResizeObserver + `document.fonts.ready` re-measure; the rAF loop is IO-gated.
- **Tier:** STRONG — the entry calls it one of the cheapest "wow" headings in the bank (framework-free rebuild ≈ 250 lines; the heading stays real DOM text, so SEO/a11y survive).
- **Best for:** Hero headings and section titles over imagery. Avoid video media on mobile (poster image instead).
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md (entry Q95). **Code:** code-source/95-masked-heading/

## [BANK] Q98 · Silo — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md)
- **Reference source:** https://www.silosilosilo.com/
- **How it looks:** A one-page shop for a modular stacking storage product. Three material columns stand side by side — Aluminum, Brass, Titanium (waitlist) — each a neat stack of parts. Scrolling pulls every stack apart piece by piece like an exploded diagram; each separated piece gets its own quantity stepper, and a sticky bar at the bottom keeps a running total that turns into a Shopify checkout link.
- **Frame by frame:** The shop section scrolls into place and the page parks exactly at it (a momentum clamp) → further scrolling hands the wheel to the shop's own scroll surface → the three stacks explode apart together over a run of 1 timeline unit plus a 1.15 hold, pieces parting until their steppers become clickable (controls stay pointer-dead until the pieces part) → scroll back and the stacks close with a magnetic snap — within 0.3 of shut they snap fully closed, past 35% open they snap fully open; the surface never parks half-open → steppers change quantities, complete 5-piece sets collapse into the single stack variant in the bar (aluminum stack $100 vs $145 parts ≈ 31% off; brass $299 vs $445 ≈ 33%), and checkout is built from that one collapsed state.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Webflow shell + GSAP 3.12.2 + Lenis 1.2.3, all logic in hand-written inline scripts. Explode engine: paused timelines driven by a proxy tween (not scrub) — opening duration max(OPEN_LAG 0.35, |Δp| / OPEN_RATE 1) power2.out, closing 0.6s expo.out, CLOSE_MAGNET 0.3, OFFER_GONE 0.35, snap {min 0.2, max 0.45, delay 0.2, power1.inOut}, wheel deltas capped at MAX_WHEEL_DELTA 100, desktop handoff at ≥992px. Cart discipline (the entry's headline): one CartManager config map {id: price, variant}; every stepper writes to the product's cart row; displayed prices are *derived* from that state (a past overcharge bug is documented in the code comments — change Shopify first, then match here); checkout = Shopify cart permalink built from the collapsed list + attribution params (UTM + Meta click id) captured on landing. Full price map in the entry (aluminum Cap $9 → 90 $49, inserts $19; brass Cap $29 → 90 $149; titanium $1,000 waitlist via mailto). No reduced-motion handling (gap — freeze the explode open in a rebuild).
- **Tier:** STRONG — the heaviest entry in its batch, but its pattern is the bank's closest analogue to a quote-builder.
- **Best for:** Configurator/quote-builder sections for trades: options as steppers, one state object, a derived live total, and a final CTA (prefilled enquiry/booking link) built from the same collapsed state. The explode engine ports in ~60 lines; the dual-Lenis handoff is only needed if the configurator is its own scroll surface.

## [BANK] Q106 · Design Embraced (Anthony Goodwin) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md)
- **Reference source:** https://designembraced.com (Codrops case study: https://tympanus.net/codrops/2024/03/21/case-study-design-embraced-portfolio-2024/ — Awwwards SOTD 18 Mar 2024, article-stated)
- **How it looks:** A freelance designer's portfolio with a minimal text surface ("Available For Freelance"; services: Web Design / UI UX / Branding / Typeface Design / Motion Design). The homepage slider's photographs are not flat — each image is a WebGL plane that bends in 3D, curling cylindrically as it travels, and page changes ripple through the image before it unbends into the next.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger a slide/page change → a ripple fires 0→1 over 800ms (easeOutQuart) → the plane's curviness tweens to 0 and its transition uniform to 1 (800ms easeOutSine, overlapping at −0.6) → scaleProgress runs to 1 (900ms easeInOutExpo at −0.7) and the offset scale/position tweens run 1000ms easeInOutExpo (at −1) → UI elements toggle at −0.85 and incoming components replay their entrances at −0.9 → on complete, offsets zero and interaction re-locks. The site's base UI beat is 1500ms (×12 in the duration census).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Custom component framework + anime.js timelines + a hand-rolled WebGL engine (no three.js). The bend is ~15 lines of GLSL: `angle = −planeSize.y × 1.5 + y × (−π)`; `bentCoords.y = sin(angle) × radius − planeSize.y × 0.5`; `bentCoords.z = cos(angle) × radius`; flat and bent coords mixed by a curviness uniform and rotated around the plane centre; a full simplex-noise implementation is compiled into the same shader for ripple/displacement. Vertex uniforms: time, scaleProgress, ripple, fadeOut, fadeOutDir, progress, curviness, transition, planeSize, planeCenter, imageSize, mousePos, screenSize, backFace, scrolling, bendMult. IntersectionObserver (×4) drives component enter/leave with lock semantics. No reduced-motion gating in the shipped bundle (the case study documents keyboard-navigation work; motion reduction is a rebuild requirement).
- **Tier:** STRONG — as a scoped rebuild (one plane shader + GSAP core ≈ 45 KB); do not import the whole custom engine (150 KB JS).
- **Best for:** Hero sliders needing one signature move. In GSAP terms the same uniforms are driven with identical durations/eases/offsets (anime offsets map to GSAP position parameters). Keep it a self-contained canvas section, out of Elementor's DOM transforms; cap plane segments (~32×32) on low-power phones.

Four hinge directions, each with its own geometry: left (origin `0 50%`, rotateY −15°→−40°), right (`100% 50%`, 15°→40°), bottom (`50% 0`, rotateX 15°→40° with a 0.045em drop), top (`50% 100%`, −15°→−40°); shadow formulas per direction are tabled in full in the entry.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Pure CSS3 — no JavaScript in the effect (Modernizr is only a feature-test shim). Direction class on the `<li>` (`ot-letter-left/top/right/bottom`), glyph duplicated via `content: attr(data-letter)`; base span carries `perspective: 550px`, `transform-style: preserve-3d`, and the cut-out illusion from an inset text-shadow stack (`1px 4px 6px <tile colour>, 0 0 0 hsla(0,0%,0%,.3), 1px 4px 6px <tile colour>`); both pseudos transition `all .3s` (default ease); grid cells `calc(100%/6)`, max-height 290px. No reduced-motion handling (2013 demo — gate the transition when rebuilding).
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — hover-only as shipped; trigger the open state on tap/`:active` or an IntersectionObserver class on touch.
- **Best for:** Playful display-type moments — still the cheapest "3D type" effect in the bank: ~15 lines of CSS per direction, 0 JS, ~1 KB per direction set.

## [BANK] Q123 · Refraction Cursor over Video (CodePen, jhnsnc) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md)
- **Reference source:** https://codepen.io/jhnsnc/pen/ByoEmoq
- **How it looks:** A fullscreen video (an ocean clip in the demo) with an invisible elongated glass capsule riding at the cursor: inside the capsule the video bends as if seen through a lens, a bright specular edge glints on one side of the glass, and the picture seems to bleed light just past its own frame edges. Along the bottom, a thin progress bar drawn inside the same distorted space — so the lens bends the bar too — fills with a shifting rainbow cos-palette colour.
- **Frame by frame:** The cursor moves (raw mousemove, no smoothing — the glass tracks 1:1 and all softness comes from the falloff shape) → pixels near the capsule are displaced along the direction away from it, strongest at its edge (an exponential-impulse falloff), so the video warps around the glass as it passes → the specular band (a ±0.002 smoothstep ring weighted by a fake centre light, intensity 5.0) brightens on the lit side → clicking on the bar (within |y−0.85| < 0.05) seeks the video; clicking near the vertical centre toggles play/pause. Startup polls the video every 300ms (up to 50 attempts) before the first frame, with a click-to-start fallback.
- **Mechanism & key values:** regl, one fullscreen triangle, one fragment shader, hidden `<video>` re-uploaded as a texture every frame; PIXEL_DENSITY 2. `#define` set: VIDEO_GLOW_AMOUNT 1.5, VIDEO_GLOW_DIM 0.8, MOUSE_SIZE 0.042, MOUSE_WIDTH 0.8, MOUSE_EDGE 0.02, MOUSE_DISPLACEMENT_DIST 0.03, MOUSE_BASE_ALBEDO vec3(.4), MOUSE_BASE_ALPHA 0.15, MOUSE_SPECULAR_INTENSITY 5.0; displacement = `normalize(mouse − p) × expImpulse(−d/MOUSE_EDGE, k=4, cut=0.175)` (commented sharper variant k=8, cut=0.085); contain-fit video lookup in GLSL with glow falloff; progress bar segment x 0.1–0.9 at y 0.85, thickness 0.004, fill = `currentTime/duration`. The author's own comments list what is NOT done: no fresnel, no blur, no tinting.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — a fullscreen fragment shader sampling a video texture at DPR 2 is a battery/GPU load no trade homepage should carry as decoration; run at DPR 1, pause off-screen and under reduced motion.
- **Best for:** The transferable kernel: the impulse-displacement lens over a *static* image — a cheap product-photo magnifier. The shader is ~150 lines and ports to any fullscreen-quad setup (Three.js ShaderMaterial or raw WebGL); regl is incidental.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md (entry Q123). **Code:** code-source/123-refraction-cursor/

## [BANK] Q125 · Mouse-Following Square Lens Effect with Three.js and GLSL (Codrops) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2026/08/25/building-a-mouse-following-square-lens-effect-with-three-js-and-glsl/ (demo: https://tympanus.net/Tutorials/PointerSquareLensDistortion)
- **How it looks:** A fullscreen photograph shown in grayscale, quietly alive with a slow sine wave and film-grain shimmer. Following the pointer is a hard-edged square window; inside the square the same photograph appears in colour, bulged through a lens, its red and blue channels splitting radially toward the square's edges. The square's edge is deliberately aliased — a graphic, un-feathered cut between the two worlds.
- **Frame by frame:** The pointer moves → the square eases after it (~10% per frame, lerp 0.1) → inside, the colour image is sampled through the CC-lens remap (pulled inward = bulge) with RGB fetches offset along the centre-out direction (R +0.01 / G 0 / B −0.01) → outside, the grayscale copy keeps waving (`sin(uv.y × 10 + time × 1) × 0.01`) and shimmering with a hash-random term. No render targets, no post-processing — one fragment shader does everything.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Three.js + TypeScript, one fullscreen 1×1 plane, camera distance computed so the plane exactly fills the view. Deployed defaults (verified in the bundle): `squareSize: 0.4` (the half-side in −1..1 space — the tutorial text says 0.3; the deployed 0.4 governs), `lensDistortion: 1.5, rgbShiftR: .01, rgbShiftG: 0, rgbShiftB: −.01, waveFrequency: 10, waveStrength: .01, waveSpeed: 1, randomFrequency: 1, randomStrength: .02, randomSpeed: .2, pointerEase: .1`. Square mask = four multiplied `step()` tests in an aspect-corrected, pointer-centred coordinate system; CC-lens scale = `1 + distortion·radius²` (or `1/(1 − distortion·radius²)` for negative distortion), inverse-mapped; both textures cover-fitted independently in GLSL. Full GUI ranges are tabled in the entry. No touch fallback for lens position and no reduced-motion handling in the demo.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — pointer-only as shipped; add an auto-path/deviceorientation fallback and DPR cap on touch, and gate the wave/random terms under reduced motion.
- **Best for:** Colour-reveal and before/after hero interactions. The fragment shader is ~120 lines and self-contained (cover-UV + mask + CC-lens + shift + wave compose in that order); needs two same-size images (colour + pre-desaturated copy).
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md (entry Q125). **Code:** none recorded (deployed demo bundle mined; shader described in full in the entry).

## [BANK] Q126 · Building an Endless Procedural Snake with Three.js and WebGL (Codrops, Sujen Phea) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2026/02/10/building-an-endless-procedural-snake-with-three-js-and-webgl/ (demo: https://tympanus.net/Tutorials/WebGLSnakeAnimation/)
- **How it looks:** A spotted, glossy snake that swims endlessly through empty space — no head texture or model: the whole animal is generated, its body thick through the middle, pinching at the neck and swelling into a head, belly lighter than its back, an FBM spot pattern moving over scales that catch an anisotropic highlight and a fresnel rim as it coils, seeks and wanders.
- **Frame by frame:** Each new path segment, a steering blend picks a direction — seek the target when far (beyond 1.5× the orbit radius), orbit it tangentially with a radial correction, coil vertically while orbiting, wander by noise — and a turn-rate cap (π/6 per segment) forces the direction to swing gradually, which is what makes it read as animal rather than mechanical → the segment becomes a G1-continuous cubic Bézier whose handle length grows with turn sharpness → every frame the whole path window slides forward: new segments generate ahead, old ones trim behind, the body remaps → the spine is sampled into two float DataTextures and thousands of flattened octahedron instances rebuild the body in the vertex shader, radius following the profile: ramp 0→0.74 (tail), full 0.74–0.85 (body), pinch 0.85–0.95 (neck), bulge and close 0.95–1.0 (head), with a 3-radian twist along the spine and an elliptical 0.5:0.8 cross-section.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Three.js (511 KB bundle). Steering kit {orbitRadius 8, seek threshold ×1.5, radial gain 0.1, turn cap π/6, coilAmplitude 3, coilFrequency 0.25, wanderStrength π/24, tiltStrength π/48}; Bézier handle rule `length × (0.33 + 0.34 × turnFactor)`, segments 4–8 units; parallel-transport frames propagated by quaternion (early-out at dot > 0.9999); texturePoints 100 (presets 50/75), radialSegments 8; scale material: spots {scale 5, threshold 0.6, smoothness 0.1, intensity 0.8, octaves 2}, specular power 27 / intensity 0.5, fresnel power 3.5 / intensity 0.3, belly width 0.5, light dir (0.5, 1, 0.3); speed default 2. No reduced-motion handling (fallback: freeze the distance — a static curved pose).
- **Tier:** NOT-FOR-TRADES — a study piece at desktop-demo weight (511 KB Three.js + per-frame CPU spine sampling); its value is the reusable steering→Bézier→sliding-window curve engine (~200 lines, no rendering) for "creature/trail follows the pointer" jobs.
- **Best for:** Reference for procedural-creature and trail work; on mobile use texturePoints 50, radialSegments 6, DPR 1. Embed only as a standalone canvas section.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md (entry Q126). **Code:** none recorded (deployed demo bundles mined).

## [BANK] Q127 · Creating an Infinite Circular Gallery using WebGL with OGL and GLSL Shaders (Codrops) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2021/02/23/creating-an-infinite-circular-gallery-using-webgl-with-ogl-and-glsl-shaders/ (demo: http://tympanus.net/Tutorials/InfiniteCircularGallery/; based on Lions Good News 2020 by SHIFTBRAIN)
- **How it looks:** A horizontal gallery of twelve tall cards (700×900) that do not run on a straight line — they ride a shallow invisible circle, dipping 75 world units at the extremes and rotating tangent to the arc, so the row feels like the top of a giant wheel. Each card's surface ripples faintly like paper, its title is rendered inside the WebGL itself under the image, and behind everything fifty pale blocks drift slowly upward at individual speeds for depth.
- **Frame by frame:** Wheel adds to a scroll target (gain 0.005), drag adds at 0.01 → the current position lerps after the target at 0.05 per frame → each card is placed at `x − current × 0.1`, wrapped by a full widthTotal when it passes a full viewport beyond the edge → its height and rotation follow its x: `y = cos((x/widthTotal) × π) × 75 − 75`, `rotation.z` mapped [−widthTotal, widthTotal] → [π, −π] → the paper bend runs continuously in the vertex shader (time stepping 0.04/frame) → release or a 200ms-debounced wheel-end snaps the target to the nearest card.
- **Mechanism & key values:** OGL (minimal WebGL), constants cross-verified in the deployed bundle. Camera fov 45, z 20; planes sized in "design pixels": 700×900 at a 1500px reference screen height, padding 2, `widthTotal = (scale.x + 2) × count`; 12 images duplicated to 24 medias for wide-screen headroom; dense plane geometry (100×50 segments) for the bend `z = sin(4x + t)·1.5 + cos(2y + t)·1.5`; clear colour (0.796, 0.792, 0.741). MSDF titles: size 0.08, letterSpacing −0.05, offset −0.085 below the plane, colour #545050, median-of-3 decode. Background: 50 blocks (#c4c3b6), scale (1.6, 0.9) × random(0.75, 1), own parallax speed each, upward drift 0.05 × speed. No reduced-motion handling; L2 logged user comments reporting mobile breakage (the drag path is wheel-tuned; halve plane segments on phones).
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — desktop-led showcase piece; the MSDF title system is a build step most productions should replace with DOM titles over the canvas.
- **Best for:** Gallery centrepieces. The gallery core (calibration, layout, scroll model, wrap, arc, snap) is ~150 lines with OGL or ~200 with Three.js.

## [BANK] Q128 · Creative WebGL Image Transitions (Codrops, Yuriy Artyukh / akella) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2019/11/05/creative-webgl-image-transitions/ (demos: https://tympanus.net/Development/webGLImageTransitions/ — index.html … index8.html, all eight mined)
- **How it looks:** A fullscreen image viewer where clicking swaps the photograph through a shader effect rather than a fade: a noisy edge wipes across; one image zooms in as the other zooms out on a diagonal; a circle grows out of the centre swallowing the old photo; the picture smears sideways in fifty thin strips; or the two images slide against each other by their own brightness. Eight distinct transitions, one shared engine.
- **Frame by frame:** Click → a guard blocks re-entry → a GSAP tween runs a single `progress` uniform 0 → 1 over 1s (Power2.easeInOut) → every frame, each pixel's sample position is remapped by that demo's function of progress (below) and the two textures are mixed → at completion the second texture becomes the first, progress resets to 0, and the loop's `time` keeps stepping 0.05/frame for the noise-based variants. Per-demo math: **1 noise-mask wipe** — Perlin-noise mask over a left-to-right front, `dt = parabola(progress, 1)`, edge smoothstep width 0.01; **2 diagonal zoom crossfade** — `x = smoothstep(0,1, progress·2 + y − 1)`, images counter-zoomed by x; **3 circle grow** — radius 0.9, width 0.35, `prog = progress·0.66 + noise·0.04`, both textures counter-scaled; **4 pow-wipe** — `prog = progress·0.8 − 0.05 + noise·0.06`, interpolation raised to the 10th power; **5 luminance shift** — each image displaced vertically by the *other's* mean brightness × intensity 0.3; **6 rotated displacement** — displacement texture applied along ±45° rotations × progress; **7 "planetary" strips** — `fract(uv × vec2(50, 1))` strips displaced 0.1 along a 45° rotation in opposite phases; **8 noisy vertical split** — the images shear apart vertically by hash noise (÷5).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Three.js fullscreen plane + a reusable `Sketch` class (5,933 B) shared by all eight demos; camera fov computed to fit a 1-unit plane at distance 2; cover-fit via the standard `resolution` vec4 correction every shader starts from. Base uniforms: time, progress, border, intensity, scaleX 40, scaleY 40, transition 40, swipe, width, radius, texture1, texture2, displacement, resolution; dat.GUI auto-built from uniform min/max in debug. Transition engine {duration 1s, Power2.easeInOut, time += 0.05}; clear colour 0xeeeeee; pixelRatio uncapped in the demo (cap it in production). No reduced-motion handling — fall back to the plain `mix` fade under `prefers-reduced-motion`. The entry's core lesson: every effect is just a remapping of the sample UV by a function of progress ∈ [0,1].
- **Tier:** STRONG — the entry (confirming L2's call) rates it the most production-adjacent in its batch: engine + any one fragment ≈ a complete transition in ~250 lines of single-HTML.
- **Best for:** Hero image crossfades and before/after reveals — demos 7 (strips) and 3 (circle grow) are the two worth shipping. One fullscreen pass, 2–3 texture fetches: cheap on phones if DPR is capped and the loop pauses off-screen.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md (entry Q128). **Code:** none recorded (all eight demo files hand-refetched and mined; integrity note in the slug's values-raw.txt).

## [BANK] Q129 · Shader Based Reveal Effect with React Three Fiber & GLSL (Codrops) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/Tutorials/R3FImageReveal/ (article: https://tympanus.net/codrops/2024/12/02/how-to-code-a-shader-based-reveal-effect-with-react-three-fiber-glsl/ · repo: https://github.com/colindmg/r3f-image-reveal-effect)
- **How it looks:** A photograph on a WebGL plane that is not simply faded in — a living noise field eats across it: the image materialises through a swirling Perlin-noise mask whose edge keeps boiling, strongest at the centre and dissolving outward, while the plane itself ripples like a flag that flattens as the reveal completes. A button toggles the reveal on and off; a second toggle blows the image up to fill the whole viewport.
- **Frame by frame:** Click → over 1.5 s (easeInOut) the progress value runs 0→1 → near the centre the noise mask first crosses its threshold and patches of image appear → the revealed region spreads outward as a radial gradient term (−7.0 × progress) drags the noise field down → the vertex ripple (amplitude ∝ 1 − progress) subsides → end state: full image, flat plane. The noise keeps drifting slowly the whole time (time rates 0.1 / 0.2), so even the settled edge is alive.
- **Mechanism & key values:** React Three Fiber + drei shaderMaterial; plane geometry [1, 1, 32, 32] scaled by drei useAspect(texW, texH, 0.2). Fragment: mask computed on raw vUv — displacedUv = vUv + cnoise(vec3(vUv×5.0, uTime×0.1)); strength = cnoise(vec3(displacedUv×5.0, uTime×0.2)) (Ashima 3D Perlin); radialGradient = distance(vUv, 0.5)×12.5 − 7.0×uProgress; alpha = (1 − clamp(strength + radialGradient, 0, 1)) × smoothstep(0.0, 0.7, uProgress); texture sampled at CoverUV cover-fit. Vertex: position.z += (1 − uProgress) × sin(distance(uv, 0.5)×20.0 − uProgress×5.0). Drive: a Motion MotionValue animated over 1.5 s easeInOut; useFrame copies clock time → uTime and the value → uProgress (no React state in the loop). Stack: three ^0.169.0, @react-three/fiber ^8.17.10, motion ^11.11.17, Vite ^5.4.8.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Hero image reveals and before/after-style image moments on trade sites (a finished-roof photo burning in through noise). Vanilla-Three rebuild is direct: same shader pair, drive uProgress with a GSAP tween on a plain object. No-WebGL fallback must be a plain <img> with a CSS reveal — the material is transparent, so visibility must never depend on the canvas.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry Q129). **Code:** code-source/shader-reveal-r3f/ (values.txt carries the correction note).

## [BANK] Q131 · WebGL Rotating Image Gallery using OGL and GLSL (Codrops) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/Tutorials/RotatingSlideshow/ (article: https://tympanus.net/codrops/2024/12/03/how-to-create-a-webgl-rotating-image-gallery-using-ogl-and-glsl-shaders/ · repo: https://github.com/oluwadareseyi/webgl-rotating-image-gallery)
- **How it looks:** A vertical column of ten photographs that never ends. As you scroll (or drag), the column drifts with a heavy, slow ease; each photo is flat while it sits near the centre of the screen, but as it travels toward the top or bottom edge it curls away around an invisible cylinder, bending along its width like a page wrapping a drum.
- **Frame by frame:** Wheel/drag input feeds a scroll target → the actual scroll position lerps toward it at only 0.01 per frame, so the column glides and overshoots softly → each plane's position in the column is remapped (viewport −H→+H becomes 5→15) and drives its bend: angle = quinticInOut(local progress) × π applied as a rotation around the Y axis varying along the plane's width → planes leaving one end wrap seamlessly to the other via a direction-aware modulo offset.
- **Mechanism & key values:** OGL ^1.0.8 + normalize-wheel; no GSAP, no Three. Renderer alpha + antialias, DPR = min(devicePixelRatio, 2); camera fov 45, z = 20. All 10 planes share one Plane geometry with widthSegments 100, heightSegments 1 (segments exist purely so the vertex shader can bend); a 320×300 px design box maps into world units, vertical padding factor 0.8. Vertex: offset = (dot(vec3(1,1,0), position) + 0.25)/0.5; localprogress = clamp((fract(uPosition×0.05) − 0.01×uDistortion×offset) / (1 − 0.01×uDistortion), 0, 2) with uDistortion = 3; Rodrigues rotation around (0,1,0). quinticInOut GLSL: t<0.5 ? 16t⁵ : −0.5|2t−2|⁵+1 — the entry warns not to substitute a cubic. depthTest/depthWrite/cullFace all false; textures generateMipmaps false; fragment does cover-fit cropping only. Scroll lerp 0.01; wheel scale 0.005; drag scale 0.1.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Infinite project-photo columns / gallery sections (roofing or remodeling portfolios) where images should feel physical. Ports 1:1 to Three (PlaneGeometry(1,1,100,1) + ShaderMaterial + renderOrder).
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry Q131). **Code:** code-source/rotating-gallery-ogl/

## [BANK] Q132 · Interactive WebGL Hover Effects (Codrops / Yuri Artiukh) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/Tutorials/webgl-mouseover-effects/step3.html (article: https://tympanus.net/codrops/2020/04/14/interactive-webgl-hover-effects/ · repo: https://github.com/akella/webgl-mouseover-effects)
- **How it looks:** An ordinary image list on the page — except the photos live on a WebGL canvas that mirrors the DOM exactly. Move the mouse fast and the whole rendered scene warps around the cursor: in one mode the colour channels split apart into an RGB smear, in another the image melts and zooms into the pointer, in a third it dissolves into grainy noise displacement. Stop moving and everything settles back to a clean page — the distortion is a brief impulse tied to cursor speed, zero at rest.
- **Frame by frame:** DOM <img> elements are measured, hidden (visibility:hidden) and replaced by pixel-calibrated planes → mouse moves → a smoothed follower lerps toward the cursor at 0.1/frame while cursor speed is measured, lerped and capped (uVelo = min(speed, 0.05), decaying ×0.999/frame) → the single fullscreen post-process pass warps the entire canvas around the cursor by that velocity → cursor stops → velocity decays → image returns to rest. Effect type (0 RGB split / 1 zoom-melt / 2 random) switches live.
- **Mechanism & key values:** three + @johh/three-effectcomposer; EffectComposer = RenderPass + one custom ShaderPass — the effect is a post-process over everything rendered, not per-image. Camera px-calibrated: PerspectiveCamera(70, aspect, 100, 1000) at distance 400, fov recomputed on resize so 1 world unit = 1 px; renderer setPixelRatio(1) deliberately. Per-mesh cover-fit in the fragment (resolution = vec4(w, h, a1, a2)). Post shader verbatim values: circle(uv, c, r, border) with aspect correction; Type 0: channel offsets c×uVelo×0.5 / 0.525 / 0.55 (accumulating +=); Type 1: c = circle(uv, mouse, 0.0, 0.1 + uVelo×2)×40×uVelo, warpedUV = mix(vUv, uMouse, c×0.99); Type 2: hash12(vUv×10) noise, c = circle(..., 0.1 + uVelo×0.01)×10×uVelo. IntersectionObserver (thresholds 0, .3–.9, 1) toggles mesh visibility; scroll translates the scene in world units so planes track their DOM boxes.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Cursor-reactive photo sections and portfolio indexes. Cost is one fullscreen pass regardless of image count; the trade-off is that everything in the canvas warps — keep real text in the DOM.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry Q132). **Code:** code-source/webgl-hover-effects/

## [BANK] Q133 · Gooey Image Hover Effects with Three.js (Codrops) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/Tutorials/GooeyImageHoverEffects/ (article: https://tympanus.net/codrops/2019/10/23/making-gooey-image-hover-effects-with-three-js/ · repo: https://github.com/Aqro/gooey-hover-codrops)
- **How it looks:** Photo tiles with a second, hidden photo inside each one. Hover a tile and a soft blob grows out from under the cursor — its edge doesn't stay round: it boils, wobbles and drips like liquid — and inside the blob the second photo shows through. The blob swells and shrinks with the hover; move away and it melts back, leaving the first photo.
- **Frame by frame:** Hover → a progress value tweens 0→1 over 0.5 s (0.8 s on two of the five shipped tiles), Power2.easeInOut → a disc centred on the cursor grows (radius driven by progress) → a 3D noise field is added to the disc and its amplitude is itself gated by the hover progress, so the edge starts smooth and gets more turbulent as the blob grows → the mask (smoothstep over noise + disc) cross-fades photo 1 into photo 2 → the tile also tilts toward the cursor (rotation.x = −mouse.y×0.3, rotation.y = mouse.x×π/6) and its base image zooms slightly (1 − 0.2×progress). The shipped demo runs five tiles with five different shader flavours (trippy, shape, gooey, wave, reveal).
- **Mechanism & key values:** three ^0.109.0, GSAP ^2.1.3 TweenMax, smooth-scrollbar; canvas fixed behind content; camera px-calibrated (perspective 800, z = 800). Gooey shader (shipped): c = circle(cpos, 0.04×progressHover + progress×0.8, 2.0)×50; nc = snoise3(vec3(offX, offY, time×0.5)×8.0) × progressHover; c2 = smoothstep(0.1, 0.8, c2×5 + nc×3 − 1); hover UV zoom 1 − 0.1×progressHover; hover tinted toward deep blue (0.0314, 0.0314, 0.2235) by 0.8×(1−progress); mix factor clamp(c2 + progress, 0, 1). Article version: mask = smoothstep(0.4, 0.5, snoise3 field + pow(circle, 2.0)). Generalisable idiom per the entry: mask = smoothstep(lo, hi, noiseField + shapeField) — swap the circle for any SDF.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Before/after and hover-swap photo tiles (project galleries, material swaps). Prefer the shipped progress-gated version in production: only hovered tiles pay the noise cost and the goo doesn't boil permanently.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry Q133). **Code:** code-source/gooey-hover/

## [BANK] Q136 · WebGL Shader Techniques for Dynamic Image Transitions (Codrops / Arlind Aliu) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/Tutorials/ShaderImageReveal (article: https://tympanus.net/codrops/2025/01/22/webgl-shader-techniques-for-dynamic-image-transitions/ · repo: https://github.com/Arrlindii/Shader-Image-Transition)
- **How it looks:** Scrolling down a stack of large images, each one is born as a single clean circular blob at its centre that splits and merges into rings of smaller blobs — one centre blob plus rings of 3, 3 and 5 circles — the blobs' edges getting wigglier as they grow, until the merged field covers the whole frame and the photograph stands fully revealed. The whole transition is one growing threshold swept across a soft-min SDF field.
- **Frame by frame:** A section enters → GSAP tweens that mesh's uProgress → 1 over 3.0 s → t = pow(uProgress, 2.5) accelerates the radius growth → rad = t × (width/2) grows → the field (central blob + three rings, soft-min merged with k = 50/width, noise multiplied by rad so blobs start clean and get wigglier as they grow) is thresholded by mask = step(field, rad) → where the field passes, texture replaces transparent black → end state: full image. Camera lerps toward −scrollY at 0.1/frame; sections are one viewport apart.
- **Mechanism & key values:** three ^0.166.1, GSAP ^3.12.5, Vite 5; camera PerspectiveCamera(35) at z = 1600; four meshes (1000×667, 450×581, 553×600, 600×600), PlaneGeometry(w, h, 128, 128). circleSDF returns length(pos) + noise(pos)×rad×amt with amt = 0.5 + sin(uProgress×0.2)×0.25; noise is cheap trig noise with angle = atan(y,x) + uProgress×π. radialCircles uses a sector fold (s = round(atan(p)/sectorAngle)) so one circleSDF evaluation yields a whole ring — O(1) per pixel instead of the article's 4-layer × 12-item loop. Rings at 0.20×w (count 3), 0.25×w (count 3), 0.45×w (count 5), inner radius 15.0; softMin(a,b,k) = −log(exp(−ka) + exp(−kb))/k. uProgress is the ONLY animated uniform — the shipped code re-parameterises the article's free-running clock as progress, which makes the reveal scrubbable and scroll-safe.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Scroll-triggered image reveals in gallery/work sections; works as a standalone fragment shader on any fullscreen quad, and the entry notes it can run as a small Three snippet behind a hero image in WordPress/Elementor contexts.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry Q136). **Code:** code-source/shader-image-transitions/

## [BANK] Q137 · Animated Heat Distortion Effects with WebGL (Codrops / Lucas Bebber) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/Tutorials/HeatDistortionEffect/ (article: https://tympanus.net/codrops/2016/05/03/animated-heat-distortion-effects-webgl/ · repo: https://github.com/lbebber/HeatDistortionEffect)
- **How it looks:** Still photographs — a desert, a cooking pan, a flight scene, water — with heat shimmering off them: in the masked hot zones the image wobbles and ripples upward like air over a stove, while the rest of the frame stays perfectly clean. Moving the mouse slides the scene's depth layers against each other slightly, and even the big SVG title text shimmers — though less than the photo behind it. A fine film grain crawls over everything.
- **Frame by frame:** Continuous loop (no trigger): a sine wave (in the shipped desert shader, wave(pos.y, 190.0, 0.35) and wave(pos.x, 100.0, 0.4), scaled by pixel-size offsets vec2(2.0, 1.0)) displaces the texture sample, multiplied by a painted mask channel so only hot areas distort → mouse move adds parallax = mouse × depth-map value (d = −pow(maps.r, 1.0), offset vec2(0.004)×mouse×d), the mouse itself normalised −1..1 and shaped by curve(v) = sign(v)×|v|^0.8 → per-frame random grain offsets add (1 − colour)×0.1×noise. Article walkthrough values: frequency 100.0, amplitude 0.003, speed 0.03, x-only offset, parallax mouse × 0.005.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Raw WebGL, no library — one fullscreen-quad program per demo (4 demos: desert, cooking, flight, water). One packed maps texture carries both maps: depthMap = maps.r, distortionMap = maps.g (shipped desert uses maps.b as the haze mask). Frame clock: incr = delta/(1000/60) clamped to 1.5, time wraps at 1000 loops. Title text: an SVG rasterised to a 2D canvas texture, positioned from the placeholder element's getBoundingClientRect; title UVs waved at 30% blend, alpha gated by maps.g. Cooking variant: 5-wave turbulence (55/−0.48, 66/−0.33 on x−0.7y; 50/0.21, 66/0.45, 45/0.25 on y), masked by maps.g, intensity 0.3×pixel(). Touch uses devicemotion (accel/10, 6-sample smoothing).
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — a one-texture trick with a narrow subject fit; the reusable core (masked sine offset + channel-packed depth parallax) is small and portable, the heat subject itself rarely suits trade imagery.
- **Best for:** Atmospheric hero stills where heat/energy is literally the subject (solar, HVAC-adjacent imagery), and as the bank's smallest complete example of mask-gated distortion + packed-channel parallax.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry Q137). **Code:** code-source/heat-distortion/

## [BANK] Q138 · Interactive Wave Propagation Cube Grid with Three.js (Codrops / Franky Hung) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** https://projects.arkon.digital/threejs/wavy-cubes/ (article: https://tympanus.net/codrops/2026/07/09/building-an-interactive-wave-propagation-cube-grid-with-three-js/ · repo: https://github.com/franky-adl/3d-wave-grid)
- **How it looks:** A field of 1,600 white cubes standing on end in a tight grid, lit with soft shadows. Drag the pointer across them and a ripple races outward from the cursor's path: a Gaussian ring of cubes rises and falls as the wavefront expands, cresting blue (#0055ff) at its highest and settling back to white; move slowly and the wave is weak, flick fast and it surges. Leave it alone for 3 seconds and the field starts rippling on its own with random ghost waves. The camera tilts gently toward the mouse throughout.
- **Frame by frame:** Pointer moves ≥ 0.1 world units → a trail point (x, z, age, speed-delta) is recorded into a 128-texel DataTexture → in the vertex shader each cube measures its distance to every trail point: window = exp(−relDist²/width²) centred on the expanding wavefront (wavefront = speed 6.0 × age), fade = exp(−age/2.0), attenuation 1/(1 + dist×0.1), weight includes the pointer's speed delta → waveHeight += weight × cos(1.2 × relDist), normalised as a weighted average so overlapping waves blend instead of spiking → displacement clamped to ±0.4 lifts the cube's top vertices; the identical deformation is applied to the depth material so shadows stay attached → height drives the white→blue colour mix.
- **Mechanism & key values:** three ^0.184.0, GSAP ^3.15.0 (peripheral); InstancedMesh of BoxGeometry(0.8, 3, 0.8), gridSize 40 → 1,600 instances in ONE draw call (article walkthrough builds 20×20 = 400); gap 0.01, footprint ≈ 32.4 world units. Injection via MeshPhongMaterial.onBeforeCompile, top vertices only (position.y > 0 — ~50% vertex saving); per-instance aOffset attribute doubles as ID, with hash jitter uJitter 0.2. Defaults: uWaveSpeed 6.0, uWaveFreq 1.2, uWaveWidth 3.0, uAmplitude 0.4, uMaxHeight 0.4, uFadeTime 2.0; trail texture 128×1 RGBA float (cut from 200 for cost), points expire at age > 8 s. Lights: ambient 0.5, directional 4.0 (shadow 1024², radius 6) + 1.0. Post: VignetteRGBShift pass, shiftAmount 0.005, vignette darken 1 − factor×0.5. Camera PerspectiveCamera(40) on a mouse-tilted sphere (α range π×0.03, β range π×0.05, lerp 0.04/frame). Idle mode: random trail points after 3.0 s idle, one every 1.5 s at strength 0.8.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Interactive hero fields and playful section backgrounds; the entry's production lessons are the payload — pointer history as a DataTexture (zero per-frame JS math per instance), weighted-average wave superposition, speed-gated wave strength, depth-material parity, and the idle random-point mode as the mobile answer for cursor-driven heroes.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry Q138). **Code:** code-source/wave-cube-grid/

## [BANK] Q140 · Color Customizer App for a 3D Model with Three.js (Codrops) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/Tutorials/3DModelCustomizer/ (article: https://tympanus.net/codrops/2019/09/17/how-to-build-a-color-customizer-app-for-a-3d-model-with-three-js/)
- **How it looks:** A single 3D armchair floating in a light-grey void — the floor is the same colour as the background, so the chair seems to hover over nothing, with only its soft shadow grounding it. On load the chair spins one full turn, then a "drag to rotate" notice appears. Down the side: rows of parts (back, base, cushions, legs, supports) and a strip of swatches — wood and denim textures plus plain colours. Click a part, click a swatch, and that part of the chair instantly re-skins while the rest stays put.
- **Frame by frame:** Page load → CSS loader overlay (a 50×50 px red square flipping on a 1 s loop) covers the screen → model loads → loader removed, chair appears at scale (2,2,2) → intro spin adds π/60 to rotation.y for the first 120 frames (a full 360° in ~2 s) → drag orbits with damped inertia (dampingFactor 0.1), polar angle clamped [π/3, π/2], no panning → swatch click builds a brand-new material and swaps it onto every mesh tagged with the selected part name.
- **Mechanism & key values:** three r108 global build + GLTFLoader + OrbitControls via script tags; no bundler, no shaders — scene-graph/material management. Model chair.glb (~1 MB), parts as separate named Blender objects. initColor traverses the model; any mesh whose name INCLUDES the part string gets the material and a nameID tag (substring matching absorbs Blender's .001/.002 suffixes). Swatches: [{texture wood.jpg, size [2,2,2], shininess 60}, {texture denim.jpg, size [3,3,3], shininess 0}, {color '66533C'}, {'173A2F'}, {'153944'}, {'27548D'}, {'438AAC'}]; texture entries use TextureLoader with repeat.set(size) + RepeatWrapping; shininess defaults to 10. Scene: background 0xf1f1f1 with matching Fog(0xf1f1f1, 20, 100); camera PerspectiveCamera(50) at z = 5; HemisphereLight(0xffffff, 0xffffff, 0.61), DirectionalLight(0xffffff, 0.54) at (−8,12,8) with 1024² shadow; floor PlaneGeometry(5000,5000) MeshPhongMaterial(0xeeeeee, shininess 0) hand-tuned to match the background so the ground vanishes.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Product configurators — the entry names it the template and direct ancestor of trade demos like door/roof configurators. Pattern: name model objects by part, tag once with nameID, and a swatch click is just build-material → traverse → swap. MeshStandard/PhysicalMaterial drops into the same architecture as an upgrade.
