## [BANK] Q141 · Underwater-Style Navigation Using PixiJS (Codrops) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/Tutorials/underwater-navigation/ (article: https://tympanus.net/codrops/2019/04/24/how-to-build-an-underwater-style-navigation-using-pixijs/ · repo: https://github.com/liamegan/underwater-navigation)
- **How it looks:** A row of big serif menu words (80 px Abril Fatface) floating on a pale background, the whole scene gently warping as if seen through water — the distortion bends most strongly around the mouse. Hover one word and an orange animated water-pattern blooms inside the letters themselves, visible only within the glyph shapes, swirling like caustics. Underneath the effect, the real HTML nav still exists: keyboard and screen-reader users get ordinary links.
- **Frame by frame:** Page load → nav titles are rasterised to 2D canvases and rebuilt as Pixi sprites in a centred row → every frame a fullscreen screen filter warps the stage: a polar squash centred on the normalised mouse plus an animated value-noise offset, edges fading out → pointer enters a word (or its DOM anchor receives focus — same path) → a per-sprite hover filter runs a double-domain-warped FBM pattern (3 octaves), the pattern squared and scaled ×1.2, mixed from vec4(0.81, 0.33, 0, 1) to white by smoothstep → the pattern shows only where glyph alpha exists → pointer leaves / blur → filter removed. A press held over 300 ms counts as a drag, not a click.
- **Mechanism & key values:** PixiJS v5, vanilla JS classes, WebFont gating init on 'Abril Fatface'. PIXI.Application({backgroundColor 0xF9F9F9, resolution: 2}); maskpadding default 100 so displacement doesn't tear at sprite edges. Rasterisation: canvas width = measureText + 50, height 120, fillStyle rgba(40,50,60,1), baseline at height − 16. ScreenFilter uniforms time (+= 0.01/frame), mouse, u_resolution, ratio; vertical squash textureCoord.y *= 1 − abs(uvm.x×1.5)×0.3; noise offset × smoothstep(0.15, 2.0, abs(uvm.x)) × 0.6; a 7-tap Gaussian blur is defined but its two-pass call is COMMENTED OUT in the shipped code. Accessibility shape: DOM checkbox-hack nav + <ul> of anchors is the source of truth; canvas is aria-hidden="true", tab-index="-1"; focus drives the same hover filter as the pointer.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — a novelty navigation treatment; the entry records that this demo class can freeze low-end phones, so the fullscreen filter needs a device gate when ported. The accessibility architecture (DOM nav as truth, decorative aria-hidden canvas, focus parity) is the durable lesson.
- **Best for:** Statement navigation on showpiece pages only — not trade homepages. Copy the accessibility shape for any WebGL menu.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry Q141). **Code:** code-source/underwater-nav-pixi/ (note: the repo README's demo link is dead; the live demo is the Tutorials path above).

## [BANK] Q143 · Liquid Distortion Effects (Codrops) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/Development/LiquidDistortion/ (article: https://tympanus.net/codrops/2017/10/10/liquid-distortion-effects/)
- **How it looks:** A fullscreen slideshow whose photos are never quite still — a slow liquid crawl keeps the image surface gently swimming. Click next and the picture melts: distortion ramps up hard for a second, the old photo dissolves into the new one right at the peak of the wobble, then the surface settles — but not to zero: it keeps a subtle permanent ripple. In the interactive variant, hovering stirs the surface and pressing down kicks it violently before it calms.
- **Frame by frame:** Idle → the Ticker slides the displacement MAP sprite (x += 10×delta, y += 3×delta) under a fixed DisplacementFilter, so the image crawls without any image motion → transition starts → filter scale tweens to (200, 200) over 1.0 s (distortion ramps FIRST) → current slide alpha → 0 over 0.5 s → next slide alpha → 1 over 0.5 s (the crossfade hides at peak distortion) → scale settles to (20, 20) over 1.0 s. Total 3.0 s. Interactive: pointerover tweens scale by (sin(mouseX)×100, cos(mouseY)×100) over 1 s and starts the map spinning (rotation += 0.001/frame); pointerdown kicks (sin×1200, cos×200); pointerout/up tween back to (0, 0) over 1 s.
- **Mechanism & key values:** PixiJS v4-era API + GSAP TimelineMax; no custom GLSL — Pixi's built-in DisplacementFilter driven by a displacement-map sprite over the whole stage; filter offsets pixels by the map's channels × filter.scale (px). DOM slides (.slide-item img + title) are scraped into Pixi sprites (wrapper set display:none); optional PIXI.Text per slide (fill #ffffff, wordWrapWidth 400, anchor 0.5). Component options: sprites[], texts[], displacementImage, autoPlay, autoPlaySpeed [10, 3], displaceScale [200, 70] (the walkthrough timeline uses 200/200), fullScreen, stageWidth 800 / stageHeight 600, navElement, displaceAutoFit. Displacement map should be power-of-2 sized (8…2048) — its dimensions change the look. Porting caveats recorded: Pixi v5+ renames the v4 APIs (pin the major or update calls); needs a server context for texture loading. All values are article-Measured — the demo fetch landed on the Codrops frame page, so no bundle parameters were recoverable.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Hero slideshows and gallery transitions on trade sites — the borrowable core is the timing shape (ramp 20→200 in 1 s, crossfade 0.5 + 0.5 s at the peak, settle 1 s), which makes any slideshow transition feel liquid regardless of the filter underneath.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry Q143). **Code:** code-source/liquid-distortion/

## [BANK] Q144 · Reactive Depth: Scroll-Driven 3D Image Tube with React Three Fiber (Codrops) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/Tutorials/3DImageTubeR3F/ (article: https://tympanus.net/codrops/2026/02/17/reactive-depth-building-a-scroll-driven-3d-image-tube-with-react-three-fiber/ · repo: https://github.com/matdn/helmet)
- **How it looks:** You are inside a slowly rotating tunnel of photographs — five rows of twelve image tiles wrapped around a cylinder of radius 4, rows staggered, endlessly wrapping — floating over a black procedural grid floor that bulges at its edges and swells under the pointer. The tube never stops turning (base speed 0.25), but flick the scroll wheel and it surges with borrowed energy, then the energy bleeds away and it settles back to its cruise. Hover a photo and time itself slows to 0.35× for the whole scene while inertia stays coherent.
- **Frame by frame:** Every frame: scrollCurrent chases scrollTarget at 0.12 → spin velocity decays frame-rate-independently (×0.92^(dt×60), clamped ±2.0) → a global time-scale lerps toward its target at 0.12 (1 normally, 0.35 while hovering) → angle += (0.25 × direction + spinVelocity) × scaled dt. Wheel input adds ENERGY, never position: spinVelocity += deltaY × 0.004. When |scrollCurrent| passes half the loop height (13.5/2), BOTH current and target shift by ∓loopHeight — shifting only current would snap the chase. The background grid's vertex shader displaces z by edge/centre masks (pointer UV lerped at 0.08/frame); a DOM tooltip chases the pointer at lerp 0.18 and a custom cursor at 0.14 on a standalone rAF.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Next.js 16 + React 19 + three ^0.182.0, @react-three/fiber ^9.4.2, drei ^10.7.7; ALL state in useRef, zero React state in the loop. Canvas camera [0,0,6.5] fov 50; drei Environment preset "studio" blur 10.5 (a glass helmet shares the tube's rotation). Tube: rows 5 × cols 12, tile planes 0.72×1.0, ySpacing 2.7, loopHeight 13.5, repeatCount 3 → 15 rendered rows; theta = ((col + rowOffset)/cols)×2π, rotationY = −(theta + π/2) (faces outward). Grid: plane 18×18 with 512×512 segments; uniforms uGridScale 28.0, uLineWidth 0.5, uEdgeWidth 0.14, uEdgeAmp 1.35, uCenterRadius 0.22, uCenterAmp 0.9, uScrollSpeed 0.01; grid lines drawn with fwidth anti-aliasing, vec3(0.1) on black. Repo also ships a sphere variant (radius 4.25, y squashed ×0.92).
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Immersive gallery/showcase sections. The portable asset is the signal graph, not the tube: one velocity fed by wheel delta (×0.004), exponentially damped (0.92^(dt·60)), clamped (±2.0), plus a global time-scale lerp (hover → 0.35×) — reusable under any infinite scroller; the wrap rule (shift target WITH current) applies to all of them.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry Q144). **Code:** code-source/reactive-depth-tube/

## [BANK] Q145 · WebGL Distortion Hover Effects (Codrops) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/Development/DistortionHoverEffect/ (article: https://tympanus.net/codrops/2018/04/10/webgl-distortion-hover-effects/ · library repo: https://github.com/robin-dela/hover-effect)
- **How it looks:** A page of photo figures, each secretly two photos laminated together by a grayscale displacement map. Hover one and the first photo melts through the second along the map's shapes — highlights push one way, shadows the other — over about a second and a half; move off and it melts back. Eleven demo instances run different intensities (some negative, so the melt runs backwards) and different maps, so each figure warps with a different personality.
- **Frame by frame:** Init (gated by imagesLoaded) → each figure's two images + data-displacement map upload as textures on a PlaneBufferGeometry(w, h, 1, 1) under an exactly-fitted OrthographicCamera — the mesh never deforms; all distortion is in the fragment shader → hover → GSAP TweenMax tweens dispFactor 0→1 over speedIn (default 1.6 s, Expo.easeOut) → image 1 is sampled at uv.x + dispFactor × (disp.r × intensity), image 2 at uv.x − (1 − dispFactor) × (disp.r × intensity), cross-faded by mix(tex1, tex2, dispFactor) → leave → tween back over speedOut (default 1.2 s). On touch, enter/leave become touchstart/touchend; next()/previous() expose the same tween programmatically.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Three.js single-quad shader per element + TweenMax + the hover-effect library (hover.js, 7,130 B, read in full). Only the displacement texture's RED channel is sampled. Defaults: intensity 1, speedIn 1.6 s, speedOut 1.2 s, easing Expo.easeOut. Displacement texture: RepeatWrapping, LinearFilter; image textures get max anisotropy; renderer antialias false. Demo's 11 instances: intensity −0.8, −0.65, −0.4, −0.1, 0.2 (×2), 0.4, 0.6 (×2), 0.7, 0.9 (negative = reversed melt); per-instance speed pairs across 0.3–1.6 s; easing overrides Sine.easeOut, Circ.easeOut, Power2.easeOut, power2.easeInOut.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Portfolio and project-card hover swaps (before/after, day/night, material changes). Any grayscale texture works as the map; blobby high-contrast maps give the classic liquid look. Keep |intensity| ≈ 0.2–0.9 for tasteful use, and cap concurrent instances — one canvas per hover target.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry Q145). **Code:** animation/code-source/ in the packs (slug: webgl-distortion-hover-effects).

## [BANK] Q146 · On-Scroll Morphing Background Shapes (Codrops) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/Development/MorphingBackgroundShapes/ (repo: https://github.com/codrops/MorphingBackgroundShapes)
- **How it looks:** One giant soft blob in a single brand colour (#282faf) floats fixed behind the whole page, so big its edges never show. Scroll into a new section and the blob heaves into a completely different posture — stretched tall, squashed wide, spun −20° — geometry and whole-SVG transform moving together so it reads as one organic creature re-settling. When it lands, it never sits still: it breathes in a slow endless loop between its shape and a variant. Foreground images and titles drift against the mouse with elastic returns.
- **Frame by frame:** scrollMonitor (offset −300) fires as a section enters/exits → anime.js morphs the path's d to that section's geometry (2000–3000 ms, mostly easeOutElastic elasticity 600; one shape + footer use easeOutQuad) WHILE tweening the SVG's scale/rotate/translate (2000–3000 ms elastic/expo) and the fill colour (500 ms linear) → morph completes → initShapeLoop() starts an infinite alternate loop path → pathAlt (3500 ms) → path (3500 ms), linear → the blob breathes forever until the next section takes over. Foreground TiltObj: image layer translates {x: −10, y: −10}, title {x: 25, y: 25} with the mouse; mouseleave returns over 1500 ms easeOutElastic elasticity 400.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Anime.js + scrollMonitor + imagesLoaded; one fixed SVG (viewBox 0 0 1400 770) in a fixed .morph-wrap. Six shape states (5 sections + footer), each a path + pathAlt + SVG transform. Extremes: shape 1 scaleX 1.2, tx −30, ty −300; shape 2 scaleX 0.4, scaleY 1.4, ty −100; shape 3 scale 0.7/1.1, rotate −20, tx 200, ty 200; shape 5 scale 1.8/1.5, tx 250, ty 50; footer scale 2.5/2; all states fill #282faf. Shape 1 path: "M -71.09,102.028 C 12.704,91.818 73.489,25.238 161,14 C 259.86,1.298 338.87,41.516 387.78,104.03 C 436.69,166.53 368.83,211.02 272,213 C 175.17,215 90.36,217.213 -71.09,102.028 Z" (all six path/pathAlt pairs verbatim in the entry / demo1.js). Hard rule from the entry: all morph targets must share identical path command structure (M + 4 cubic segments + Z) or the d interpolation breaks. A CodePen mirror uses scrollMonitor offset −350; demo1.js (−300) governs.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Long scrolling pages that need one continuous identity behind changing sections (services → process → areas). Vary geometry/transform per section, keep one brand fill throughout.

## [BANK] Q147 · Shape Hover Effect with SVG (Codrops) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** http://tympanus.net/Tutorials/ShapeHoverEffectSVG/ (article: https://tympanus.net/codrops/2014/01/07/shape-hover-effect-with-svg/ · repo: https://github.com/codrops/ShapeHoverEffectSVG)
- **How it looks:** A grid of photo cards, each with a white shape — a diagonal slash, a wave, a chevron — covering the photo's lower part, the caption text parked invisibly below it. Hover a card and the white shape snaps upward and retracts, uncovering more photo, while the caption rises 50 px into the vacated space. Move off and the shape drops back down over the photo.
- **Frame by frame:** mouseenter → Snap.svg animates the path's d from its inline state to the anchor's data-path-hover state (demo 1: 250 ms mina.easeinout; demos 2–3: 330/300 ms mina.backout, so the shape overshoots playfully) → simultaneously the caption transitions translateY(50px) → 0 over 0.3 s CSS → mouseleave reverses both.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Snap.svg path morphing + CSS grid; one inline SVG per card, viewBox "0 0 180 320", preserveAspectRatio "none" (one shape stretches over any card aspect), absolute top −1px, fill #fff. Demo 1: from "M 180,160 0,218 0,0 180,0 z" → to "m 180,34.57627 -180,0 L 0,0 180,0 z". Demo 3 (chevron): from "M 0 0 L 0 182 L 90 126.5 L 180 182 L 180 0 L 0 0 z" → to "M 0,0 0,38 90,58 180.5,38 180,0 z". Demo 2's wave pair is printed in full in the entry. Grid: figures at 33.333% width, breakpoint 58em. Both path states must share identical command counts for Snap to interpolate. A 2014 technique that still ports 1:1 to GSAP attr:{d}.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Card grids everywhere — project cards, service cards, team cards. backout at 300–330 ms reads playful; easeinout at 250 ms reads sober. Near-zero cost, no WebGL.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry Q147). **Code:** animation/code-source/ in the packs (slug: shape-hover-effect-svg).

## [BANK] Q148 · Superhero Animation Effect with SVG Filters (Codrops) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2021/08/09/superhero-animation-effect-with-svg-filters/ (no hosted demo or repo exists — the article's code blocks are the source)
- **How it looks:** A comic-style portrait built from stacked image layers inside one SVG. A liquid, wavy-edged wipe sweeps down the picture and wherever the edge has passed, the character is transformed (the article's Mystique morph) — the reveal boundary itself ripples like water because the mask doing the revealing is being seen through a distortion filter. As it goes, the scene's background colour flips from blue #4a5eb2 to yellow #ffd11b. In the interactive version there is no autoplay: your cursor's height IS the wipe position — wipe the transformation up and down by hand.
- **Frame by frame:** The transformed layer is hidden by a mask whose white rect is parked at y = −100% → GSAP animates the mask rect's translateY 0→100% (296 px) over 3 s → the distortion filter is applied to a <g> WRAPPING the mask rect, so the filter stays fixed in space while the mask moves through it and the reveal edge comes out wavy → at '<+=1' the background rect's fill tweens #4a5eb2 → #ffd11b over 2 s → autoplay variant: timeline repeat −1, yoyo true → interactive variant: timeline paused with ease 'none', mousemove (lodash.throttle 60 ms) maps relative cursor Y to tl.progress(relPos).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Inline SVG viewBox "0 0 196 296"; filter #distort = feTurbulence type="turbulence" baseFrequency 0.08, numOctaves 2 → feDisplacementMap in="SourceGraphic" in2="turbulence" scale 50. Page CSS: body radial-gradient(at top, #5e4082, #3a124d); .picture height 80vh. Author's own warning (recorded in the entry): animated SVG filters are Chrome-best and can slow pages — keep the filter on the small mask group only, never the artwork; scale 50 is strong, 20–35 reads subtler; prefer WebGL for heavy production use.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — a striking before/after reveal mechanism with a real browser-performance caveat attached by its own author.
- **Best for:** Before/after reveals (old site → new site hero, old roof → new roof) where the wavy liquid boundary is the point. Single small filtered group only.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry Q148). **Code:** animation/code-source/ in the packs (slug: superhero-svg-filters) — article code blocks are the code of record.

## [BANK] Q149 · Building an Infinite Marquee Along an SVG Path with React & Motion (Codrops / Daniel Petho) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2025/06/17/building-an-infinite-marquee-along-an-svg-path-with-react-motion/ (no public repo and no separate demo — the article's 26 code blocks are the source)
- **How it looks:** Cards (or words) riding an invisible roller-coaster track: they flow along a looping hand-drawn curve drawn as a faint SVG guide, tilting automatically to the path's slope, stacking correctly where the track crosses over itself, and fading at the curve's extremes. Hover and the whole train glides down to 30% speed; flick the page scroll and the train surges or even reverses, driven by scroll velocity.
- **Frame by frame:** One MotionValue baseOffset is the single clock; useAnimationFrame advances it by baseVelocity × delta/1000 (% of path length per second — 20 in the single-item demo, 5 in the final 5 cards × repeat 4 = 20 items) → each item derives its own offsetDistance = wrap(0, 100, clock + itemIndex × 100/totalItems) — perfectly even spacing, seamless wrap → CSS Motion Path (offset-path / offset-distance / offset-rotate) places and auto-rotates each item; zIndex = floor(zIndexBase + progress%) stacks overlaps; per-item edge fade opacity = (1 − |2p − 1|^10)^2 → hover flips a factor target to 0.3, spring-smoothed (stiffness 100, damping 20) → scroll velocity is sprung, mapped [0, 1000] → [0, 5], its sign sets direction, its magnitude boosts speed.
- **Mechanism & key values:** React + Motion (useMotionValue, useTransform, useAnimationFrame, useScroll, useVelocity, useSpring) + D3 (scaleLinear, line/curveBasis, getTotalLength/getPointAtLength). Demo path: "M0 186.219C138.5 186.219 305.5 194.719 305.5 49.7188C305.5 -113.652 -75 186.219 484.5 186.219H587.5", viewBox "0 0 588 187". Responsiveness: offset-path percentages live in the path's own coordinate space, so on resize the path is re-derived at container pixel size — D3 samples ≤100 points via getPointAtLength, rescales, regenerates a smooth curveBasis path. Not printed in the article (stated honestly in the entry): the scroll spring's numeric springConfig and the zIndexBase value — referenced by name only.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Curved testimonial/logo trains and statement tickers that should feel designed rather than taped on. Keep children × repeat high enough that item spacing < item width or a gap shows at the wrap point; the D3 resampling step is the part most reimplementations skip — without it the marquee drifts off the drawn curve on resize.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry Q149). **Code:** animation/code-source/infinite-marquee-svg-path/ (manifest pick, roofing pack — article code is the code of record).

## [BANK] Q150 · Dynamic Shape Overlays with SVG (Codrops) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/Development/ShapeOverlays/ (article: https://tympanus.net/codrops/2017/10/17/dynamic-shape-overlays-with-svg/ · original technique repo: https://github.com/ykob/shape-overlays)
- **How it looks:** Click the menu button and a full-screen curtain pours over the page — except the curtain's leading edge is not straight: it ripples like a wave, each point of the edge arriving at a different moment, and two or three coloured layers chase each other across so the wipe has depth. Click again and the layers pour back in reverse order. The ripple is re-randomised every single toggle, so the curtain never moves exactly the same way twice.
- **Frame by frame:** Toggle → the class precomputes a per-point delay wave (range = 4×random + 6; delay[i] = (sin(−radian) + sin(−radian×range) + 2)/4 × delayPointsMax over 18 points in demo 1) → each rAF frame, every point's Y = cubicInOut(clamp((time − delay[i])/duration, 0, 1)) × 100 and the path string is rebuilt (start M 0 0 V {p0}, one cubic segment per point with control X at the midpoint, closing V 0 H 0 / V 100 H 0) → layers start delayPerPath apart; closing reverses the layer order → the loop stops at duration + delayPerPath×(paths−1) + delayPointsMax; an isAnimating flag guards re-entry.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Vanilla JS ShapeOverlays class + rAF (no animation library); inline SVG viewBox "0 0 100 100" preserveAspectRatio "none" with stacked same-geometry paths; easings hand-ported from glsl-easings. Demo 1: numPoints 18, duration 600 ms, delayPointsMax 300 ms, delayPerPath 100 ms; fills #413f46 / #e6e5ea / #cccccc. Demo 2: numPoints 4, duration 800, delayPointsMax 180, delayPerPath 70 (delay formula over 2π with random range). Demo 3: numPoints 2, duration 600, delayPointsMax 0, delayPerPath 200, with per-path easing swaps between cubicOut and cubicInOut for opening vs closing.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Full-screen menu and page-transition curtains. Demo 1 config (18 points, 600 ms, 300 ms wave) = liquid; demo 3 (2 points, 200 ms stagger) = snappy wipe. Randomising range per toggle is what stops it feeling canned.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry Q150). **Code:** animation/code-source/dynamic-shape-overlays/ (manifest pick, roofing + hvac packs).

## [BANK] Q151 · Elastic SVG Elements (Codrops) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** http://tympanus.net/Development/ElasticSVGElements/ (article: https://tympanus.net/codrops/2014/12/15/elastic-svg-elements/ · repo: https://github.com/codrops/ElasticSVGElements)
- **How it looks:** UI furniture made of jelly: a sidebar whose inner edge bulges out like a bubble when the menu opens and snaps back with a wobble; a draggable element that stretches toward your pull and boings home; buttons that overshoot their pressed shape and settle. The signature is always two-stage — a quick plain jump INTO an exaggerated shape, then a long elastic release back to rest.
- **Frame by frame:** Interaction → Snap.svg animates the path's d to the exaggerated open/active state fast (50–350 ms, plain easing) → the content state (menu open class) flips 250 ms AFTER the shape starts, so the shape visibly leads the content → the path releases back to its reset state over 600–800 ms with mina.elastic or mina.bounce. Sidebar numbers: toggle 350 ms mina.easeout to open/close, then 800 ms mina.elastic back to reset. Drag demo per-item pairs {reset/active speed, easing}: {100/100, easeinout/easeinout}, {800/100, elastic/easeinout}, {600/50, bounce/easeout}. Button demo: {800/150, elastic/easein}, {650/650, elastic/elastic}.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Snap.svg path morphs with mina easings + classie.js + Draggabilly (drag demo). Every component keeps 2–3 states of one path topology: reset (the inline d), open/active and close stored as data-morph-* attributes. Sidebar: .morph-shape width 240 px, height 100%; svg viewBox "0 0 600 800", preserveAspectRatio "none"; path stroke #5f656f, stroke-width 5. Reset d "M300-10c0,0,0,164,0,410c0,232,0,410,0,410"; data-morph-open "M300-10c0,0,295,164,295,410c0,232-295,410-295,410"; data-morph-close "M300-10C300-10,5,154,5,400c0,232,295,410,295,410". Six further variant pages (hamburger, circlemenu, collapseexpand, dropdown, inputs, pullupmenu) run the same pattern.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — micro-interaction seasoning, not page furniture, per the entry's own rebuild note.
- **Best for:** Menu buttons, toggles, checkbox/tick shapes. Port = GSAP attr:{d} with an elastic ease on the RETURN leg only; keep the out-leg short and plain. All states must share identical path command structure.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry Q151). **Code:** animation/code-source/ in the packs (slug: elastic-svg-elements).

## [BANK] Q152 · GSAP getScrollLookup() helper — fake horizontal scrolling (GreenSock pen) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** https://codepen.io/GreenSock/pen/zYeZmVw
- **How it looks:** A horizontal-scroll website — panels sliding sideways as you scroll down — whose nav actually works: click a link naming a panel buried deep in the sideways strip and the page scrolls vertically by exactly the right amount, the strip scrubbing sideways in sync, until the target panel lands centred. Without the helper those anchors are meaningless, because a panel inside a horizontal strip has no document scroll position.
- **Frame by frame:** The container pins and a horizontal x tween scrubs over a long vertical distance (2000 px per panel) → getScrollLookup pre-creates one ScrollTrigger per target measured in container-animation space (refreshPriority −10 so they measure after the main pin) → the lookup converts: targetPos = mainST.start + (targetStart / containerDuration) × (mainST.end − mainST.start) → nav click → ScrollToPlugin tweens the window scroll to that position over 1 s → the scrubbed horizontal tween follows and the target panel lands centred. Misses log "target not found"; an isParent flag resolves parentNode targets.
- **Mechanism & key values:** GSAP + ScrollTrigger + ScrollToPlugin. Horizontal tween: x: () => −(panelContainer.scrollWidth − window.innerWidth − 50), ease "none"; ScrollTrigger pin true, scrub 1, end "+=" + panels.length × 2000. Lookup built as getScrollLookup(".section", { start: "center center", containerAnimation: scrollHorizontalTween }); helper start default "top top", refreshPriority −10. Nav scroll: duration 1, overwrite "auto". A Level-2-seen variant (start "top 125px", pinSpacing false) is a usage variant; the pen's values govern.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Any horizontal-scroll section or site with in-page navigation — process galleries, project strips. Create the lookup AFTER the container tween exists and keep refreshPriority −10.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry Q152). **Code:** animation/code-source/ in the packs (slug: gsap-getscrolllookup).

## [BANK] Q153 · GSAP Pin Sidebar (akapowl pen) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** https://codepen.io/akapowl/pen/poRdoLV/9b99361db3839f1169cdc0f278746ee5 (the hash-suffixed URL is required — bare /pen/poRdoLV 404s; a "- 2" fork JjEOwoP and a GreenSock variant NWprdPM exist as variants only)
- **How it looks:** A full-screen section that stays pinned while a sequence of "points" — each an image beside an article — cross-fades through it in place: the current point's image fades in as its text rises from below, holds, then slides up and out as the next rises in. Down the left edge a slim vertical rail of segments lights orange one by one, marking where you are in the sequence. All motion is transform/opacity — nothing on the page ever reflows.
- **Frame by frame:** Section pins for exactly +100% of scroll (separate pinner timeline) → the points timeline scrubs over 100% of viewport height per point → at each point's position: its indicator segment tweens to orange (0.25 s), its image fades in from autoAlpha 0, its article rises from y 100 with autoAlpha → at +0.75 the point exits upward (y −100, fade out) and the indicator dims to #adadad — except the last point, which stays.
- **Mechanism & key values:** GSAP + ScrollTrigger; two scrubbed timelines on one pinned section; all points absolutely stacked at top 0. Points timeline: duration = points.length; ScrollTrigger trigger ".philosophie", start "top bottom", end "+=" + (100 × points.length) + "%", scrub true, id "points". Pinner: trigger ".philosophie.wrapper", start "top top", end "+=100%", scrub true, pinSpacing true, id "pinning" (markers true in the pen — remove for production). CSS: .indicators absolute left 2rem, margin 10vh 0, height 80vh, width 3px, flex column space-between, display none until JS sets flex; .point height 100vh, padding 4rem; article flex-basis 60%; img flex-basis 25%, max-width 25vw. The entry's rebuild note: keep the pin timeline separate from the content timeline — pin distance = one viewport, content distance = 100% × point count.
- **Tier:** STRONG — the bank entry itself calls it a "strong pattern for services/process sections on trade sites."
- **Best for:** Services and process sections: a pinned step-by-step (inspect → quote → build → guarantee) with a progress rail, on any trade homepage.

## [BANK] Q156 · Motion Hover Effect for a Background Image Grid (Codrops) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** http://tympanus.net/Tutorials/ImageGridMotionEffect/ (article: https://tympanus.net/codrops/2020/06/10/how-to-create-a-motion-hover-effect-for-a-background-image-grid/ · repo: https://github.com/codrops/ImageGridMotionEffect)
- **How it looks:** Behind the hero's text, a wall of small photos — a grid 10% larger than the screen on every side. It is alive: the whole field drifts and shears slowly around your cursor, tiles on one side sliding one way and tiles on the other side the opposite way, each tile with its own random drift range so the field feels organic rather than mechanical. On load the tiles bloom in from the centre — small and transparent, swelling to full size in a centre-out wave.
- **Frame by frame:** Init → each GridItem draws its own random roam amplitude (15–60 px, separately for x and y) → entrance: items from scale 0.7 / opacity 0 → scale 1 over 2 s, Expo.easeOut, centre-out grid stagger (amount 0.6 s) → a single rAF loop maps cursor position to a per-item target translation (−amp…+amp across the window) and lerps current toward target at 0.07/frame (~99% of target in ~1 s — that lag is the floaty feel; 0.12 tightens it) applied with gsap.set → opposite sides of the grid drift in opposite directions, shearing the field around the pointer.
- **Mechanism & key values:** GSAP (gsap.set in the loop; Expo.easeOut intro) + vanilla Grid/GridItem classes. .grid: position absolute, width 110%, height 110%, top −5%, left −5%, grid-template-columns/rows: repeat(50, 2%), pointer-events none (essential — the layer is decorative). GridItem.move(): xstart/ystart = getRandomNumber(15, 60); tx = lerp(tx, map(mousepos.x, 0, winsize.width, −xstart, xstart), 0.07), same for ty. Bundle-verified: lerp 0.07, stagger amount 0.6, Expo.easeOut all present in the shipped demo bundle.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Living hero backdrops on trade homepages — works with any tile content (project photos, logos, icons) behind a headline.

## [BANK] Q157 · Push Animation on Grid Items (Codrops) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** http://tympanus.net/Development/PushGridItems/ (article: https://tympanus.net/codrops/2024/06/05/push-animation-on-grid-items/ · repo: https://github.com/codrops/PushGridItems)
- **How it looks:** A 7×7 collage of photos in a strict grid. Click one photo and it swells to fullscreen while every other photo is physically shoved to the grid's edges — the ones above it fly to the top row, the ones below to the bottom, left and right likewise — as if the expanding image pushed them out of its way. Click again and everything slides back into the collage. Variants: one where the pushed photos tumble with random ±50° rotations, and one where the clicked item's declared direction pushes ALL items the same way.
- **Frame by frame:** Click → Flip.getState captures every item's rect → the clicked image is reparented into a separate .fullscreen element (its grid item gets zIndex 99) → every other item is classified against the clicked rect (bottom < clicked.top → north; top > clicked.bottom → south; right < clicked.left → west; left > clicked.right → east) and only its row or column class toggles to the edge (1 or 7) → Flip.from replays all items from captured rects to their new positions (scale: true, prune: true) → click again → classes toggle off, image reparents back, Flip returns everything.
- **Mechanism & key values:** GSAP + Flip plugin + CSS Grid with explicit per-item grid-area placements — the layout IS the animation data; no coordinate math at all. Grid vars: --rows 7, --columns 7 (one breakpoint raises columns to 8); placement example .pos-9 { grid-area: 3 / 5 / 4 / 6; }; push classes override one axis only: .pos-north { grid-row: 1; } .pos-south { grid-row: var(--rows); } .pos-west { grid-column: 1; } .pos-east { grid-column: var(--columns); }. Demo 1: duration 0.9, ease 'expo', Flip.from {scale: true, prune: true}. Demo 2: duration 1, ease 'expo.inOut', getState props 'borderRadius', pushed items rotation = random(−50, 50) entering fullscreen, 0 leaving. Demo 3: duration 0.6, ease 'expo', direction from the clicked item's data-direction-items. imagesloaded preload gate.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Project galleries and portfolio grids — click-to-expand with a physical push. Demo 3's uniform data-direction push suits directional page transitions and gallery openers.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry Q157). **Code:** animation/code-source/ in the packs (slug: push-grid-items).

## [BANK] Q158 · The Never Ending Story: Seamless Infinite Scroll with GSAP & Lenis (Codrops / Joe Ben Taylor) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2026/05/28/the-never-ending-story-building-a-seamless-infinite-scroll-experience-with-gsap-lenis/ (demo: https://tympanus.net/Tutorials/InfiniteScrollParallax/ · repo: https://github.com/joebentaylor1995/infinite-scroll-with-parallax)
- **How it looks:** A page of three fullscreen photo heroes (Founder/Creator, Producer/Executive, Psychic/Celebrity) that never ends: scroll down past the last one and you are simply back at the first — no jump, no seam, no scrollbar reset. Each hero settles flush at the top of the screen with a snap, and inside each frame the photograph drifts slower than the scroll (its picture slides from −50% to +50% as the section crosses), so the stills feel deep. In the shipped repo version, curved SVG marquees ride inside the heroes, shrinking from 1.5× to 0.5× as their section passes.
- **Frame by frame:** The window never scrolls — a nested Lenis instance scrolls .content inside a clipped 100svh wrapper with infinite: true → when the scroll wraps, it lands on a 4th section that is an exact duplicate of the first (aria-hidden), so the wrap is invisible → lenis-snap (mandatory, debounce 500 ms, duration 0.9 s, easeOutQuart 1−(1−t)⁴) settles every hero flush at top → ScrollTrigger is bridged to the non-window scroller via scrollerProxy with pinType 'transform', driven on one clock (lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update); gsap.ticker.add(t => lenis.raf(t × 1000)); lagSmoothing(0)) → each hero's picture tweens yPercent −50 → 50, ease 'none', start 'top bottom', end 'bottom top', scrub true.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Vanilla JS + GSAP 3.12.5 + ScrollTrigger + Lenis 1.3.23 + lenis-snap; syncTouch: true in the shipped repo. Sections: 100svh each, 3 + 1 duplicate, each overflow: clip; pictures position absolute inset 0, z-index −1, img object-fit cover. The entry's three load-bearing decisions: (1) scroll inside a clipped 100svh wrapper, not the window; (2) duplicate the first section — Lenis infinite mode does the wrap, the duplicate makes it seamless; (3) scrollerProxy with pinType 'transform' is mandatory or ScrollTrigger measures the wrong scroll. Drop the snap and it still loops; drop the duplicate and it visibly jumps. Chrome CSS: header/footer fixed z-index 12, padding 1.2rem; link hover transition opacity 0.4s cubic-bezier(0.430, 0.195, 0.020, 1); mobile breakpoint 700 px; root font-size 62.5%.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Looping showcase pages and fullscreen section stories where an endless reel is the concept. Heavier machinery than a normal trade homepage wants — take the parallax/snap values even if the infinite wrap stays unused.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry Q158). **Code:** code-source/infinite-scroll-parallax/

## [BANK] Q161 · GSAP Marquee Text (GreenSock pen) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** https://codepen.io/GreenSock/pen/wvZMwez (full JS recovered via the embed preview route — direct pen asset URLs were Cloudflare-blocked and the pen page yielded CSS + HTML only; the embed source is the Measured source of record)
- **How it looks:** A dark footer band carrying six huge uppercase words (186 px, "Komt goed bro.") sliding sideways in an endless, perfectly even train — no gap, no jump, no speed difference between items of different widths. It can run backwards forever just as seamlessly, and it exposes next()/previous()/toIndex() controls that glide the train to any item.
- **Frame by frame:** document.fonts.ready resolves first (so item widths are final) → horizontalLoop converts each item's x into xPercent with integer snapping, measures totalWidth (last item's offsetLeft + its xPercent share + scaled width − startX + paddingRight) → per item, two tweens on one timeline with ease "none": a `to` carrying it to its loop point, then a fromTo (immediateRender: false) restarting it one full totalWidth ahead and carrying it home → durations are distance ÷ pixelsPerSecond, so every item moves at identical velocity → the timeline pre-renders (progress(1, true).progress(0, true)), labels mark each item's start, and a modifiers time-wrap loops the playhead itself; onReverseComplete jumps totalTime forward by duration × 100 for endless reverse.
- **Mechanism & key values:** GSAP core only — the seamlessLoop/horizontalLoop helper is fully self-contained, no plugins. Config: { repeat: -1, paused: false, speed: 5, paddingRight: 100 } → pixelsPerSecond = (speed || 1) × 100 = 500 px/s. Markup: .marquee-container display flex, flex-wrap nowrap, white-space nowrap, gap 100 px (mirrors paddingRight 100); 6 items at font-size 186 px, uppercase, line-height 1 (item text as authored in the pen, including a prefixed "1" on the first item and a stray "L" on the last). Snap: gsap.utils.snap(config.snap || 1) — xPercent snapped to integers unless snap: false. The entry's two classic failure warnings: measuring before fonts load (widths shift, seam jumps) and forgetting immediateRender: false on the wrap tween (items flash at their wrapped position on load).
- **Tier:** CROWN — the bank entry's own verdict: "This helper is the canonical GSAP seamless marquee — lift it whole."
- **Best for:** Every marquee on every trade build — services tickers, review trains, town lists. This is the default implementation; reach for the fancier path/curved variants (Q149, Q169) only when the geometry demands them.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry Q161). **Code:** animation/code-source/gsap-marquee-text-codepen/ (manifest pick, roofing + hvac packs).

## [BANK] Q162 · How to Code the K72 Marquee Hover Animation (Codrops) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2021/06/30/how-to-code-the-k72-marquee-hover-animation/ (demo: http://tympanus.net/Tutorials/MarqueeMenu/ · repo: https://github.com/codrops/MarqueeMenu; recreates the menu hover from Locomotive's k72.ca)
- **How it looks:** A list of huge menu rows (6vw uppercase links). Run your pointer into a row — from whichever edge you crossed, top or bottom — and a black band wipes over the row carrying a white marquee that is already scrolling sideways (text and pill-shaped photos streaming past). The strange, polished part: the band visibly slides in, but the marquee text inside it does NOT slide vertically at all — it is simply revealed, already in place and already moving sideways. Leave from the bottom and the band wipes out downward.
- **Frame by frame:** mouseenter on the link → closestEdge() compares squared distance to the top-centre vs bottom-centre point of the row → one GSAP timeline (duration 0.6, ease 'expo'): .set parks the .marquee overlay at −101% or +101% on the entry edge and the inner wrap at the OPPOSITE offset → .to slides both to 0% together — the two translations cancel, so the content reads as revealed, not slid → the pure-CSS marquee inside (animation: marquee 15s linear infinite, translate3d(−50%, 0, 0) loop over exactly 2× duplicated content) runs independently the whole time, including mid-wipe → mouseleave mirrors: set both to 0%, tween both out toward the exit edge.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Vanilla ES modules + GSAP 3, plain CSS. .marquee: position absolute, inset 0, overflow hidden, pointer-events none, parked at translate3d(0, 101%, 0); .marquee__inner-wrap counter-parked at translate3d(0, −101%); .marquee__inner flex, width fit-content, will-change transform. Type: 6vw, line-height 1.2, uppercase, nowrap, padding 1vh 1vw 0; link weight 600, marquee spans 400. Marquee images: width 15vw, height 70%, margin 0 2vw, border-radius 5vw, background-size cover. Colours: --marquee-bg #000, --marquee-text #fff, --menu-focus #775e41. closestEdge helper credited in-source to John Stewart's CodePen (zxYJZP). The entry's rebuild note: the nested counter-translation is the whole trick — a single sliding layer looks like sliding text; keep the marquee on CSS, not GSAP, so it costs nothing and never pauses during wipes.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Full-screen menu hovers and big list-row hovers (services index, project index). Top/bottom edge detection only — correct for full-width rows.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry Q162). **Code:** code-source/k72-marquee-menu/

## [BANK] Q163 · The Architecture Behind Trionn: Coordinating GSAP, Three.js, Lenis, and Web Audio (Codrops case study) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2026/07/15/the-architecture-behind-trionn-coordinating-gsap-three-js-lenis-and-web-audio/ (case study of trionn.com; no single demo/repo — the article is itself the architecture document and every value is quoted from its code excerpts)
- **How it looks:** An agency site where everything moves to one heartbeat: a glassy 3D hero symbol that idles, drifts on magnetic hover with light flashing across its panels, crackles with weld sparks when you trace its guide lines, and explodes apart the longer you hold a press; headlines that un-blur letter by letter in random order over a difference-blend canvas; a services section that plays a 371-frame image sequence as you scroll, then bursts into particle glyphs and six arc-flying cards; a 3D helix gallery; a footer whose wire logo strings can be plucked like an instrument while fog rolls behind it, the fog itself swelling with the music's energy.
- **Frame by frame:** One master clock: GSAP's ticker drives Lenis (rafed from the ticker), the Three.js scenes and ScrollTrigger off the same scroll state — nothing runs its own rAF. A shared transitionReady flag gates every hero animation until the loader clears (headline delay 1.2 s); non-critical work (the 371-frame services preload, chunks of 20 in requestIdleCallback) defers to idle. Sections consume ONE shared scrollProgressRef (0–1) remapped per section — the flagship Services sequence uses no ScrollTrigger at all: a stripe-wipe holdT pattern (clamp of progress past a hold start) scrubs a paused timeline plus the next section's yPercent slide, reused across Services/Vision/About/Gallery. Cross-section talk is decoupled: a shared "atmosphere" context exposes only pulseSmoke() and getSmokeAnalyser(); the About lion fires a CustomEvent plus a dataset flag so late-mounting components still catch it.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Next.js + React + Tailwind; GSAP + @gsap/react (useGSAP owns lifecycle); vanilla Three.js deliberately NOT React Three Fiber (one shared render loop, per-panel meshes); Lenis; Swiper; Web Audio (synthesised sounds, gesture-triggered only — the article documents no AudioContext.resume() routine, an absence the entry labels honestly); SplitText behind a reusable BlurTextReveal; gsap.matchMedia() splits desktop/mobile logic. Key numbers — BlurTextReveal: chars set autoAlpha 0 + blur(12px); container to blur(0) over 0.5 s; chars duration 0.8, stagger {each: 0.08, from: "random"}, ease power2.out; text in mix-blend-mode: difference. Hero symbol: idle rotY += 0.0042/frame (0.0015 under prefers-reduced-motion — reduced, not removed); rotation lerp 0.06 toward target + mouse×0.22; magnetic raycast gated on scrollProgress < 0.08; flash decays ×0.92/frame; envMapIntensity = 3.0 + f×1.6; hold-to-blast: charge < 0.5 s, clickBurst +0.02/frame to 1.0, panel offset = max(0, explodeAmt − panel.delay) × 5.5. Services: 371 WebP frames on one <img>, EXPLODE_START 0.35, EXPLODE_END 0.53, CARDS_START 0.56; frame index lerp 0.12; DrawSVG icon draws duration 1.5, stagger 0.04, once per card. Helix gallery: 9 cards on a parametric helix with a Gaussian dip; vertex-deformed per column per frame (scalar math, zero Vector3 allocations); SDF rounded-corner fragment (alpha = 1 − smoothstep(−0.5, 0.5, dist)); warmUp ritual = show all → compile → render → restore → clear, at init and after textures load. Footer: string cycles 2.2, wave rebuilt per frame with 26 segments, invisible hit-clones at strokeWidth max(12, strokeWidth×18); pluck synth = 3 sine oscillators at f/2f/3f, 4.9 Hz vibrato, delay 0.14, feedback 0.32 + intensity×0.12; fog = one fullscreen FBM shader (3 octaves, rise T×0.07, domain warp 1.4×fbm) made audio-reactive via an AnalyserNode (morphOffset += (4.0 + freqEnergy×16.0 + hoverBoost×2.8)×dt). Lion reveal: depth-map displacement amount (0.03 + 0.012×breathing)×uHover, RGB split ±0.16×disp, cursor eased 0.07/frame. Curtain: per-strip spring sp = −offY×0.12, vel = (vel + sp)×0.65, neighbour coupling ×0.22/×0.62. Scatter gallery: 11 photos, pinned scrub 0.6, item tweens 1.2 at index×0.34, dominant colour extracted from a 72×72 downsample.
- **Tier:** STRONG — as an architecture reference. The author's closing lesson is the takeaway the entry underlines: build a shared canvasManager from day one; hand-juggling multiple canvases was the project's biggest friction. Individual showpieces (371-frame sequence, vertex-deformed helix) are agency-scale — the coordination patterns are what transfer to trade builds.
- **Best for:** The blueprint for any page coordinating scroll + 3D + shaders: (1) one ticker to rule everything; (2) one shared progress ref per page instead of dozens of ScrollTriggers; (3) a single transitionReady gate above the fold; (4) idle-chunked preloads (20 at a time) for image sequences; (5) cross-section talk only through tiny named functions/events.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry Q163). **Code:** code-source/trionn-architecture/ (manifest pick, roofing + remodeling packs).

## [BANK] Q164 · Circular Text (React Bits) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** https://reactbits.dev/text-animations/circular-text (canonical source: DavidHDev/react-bits repo, src/content/TextAnimations/CircularText/CircularText.jsx + .css)
- **How it looks:** A ring of letters — "FULLY LICENSED • SINCE 1995 •" style — spinning slowly and continuously like a coin rotating in place. Speed it up 4× by hovering, or in "goBonkers" mode 20× while the whole ring shrinks to 0.8 scale; grab it and drag it around, then fling it and watch it spin with thrown momentum, decaying until it settles back to cruise speed. It only spins while actually on screen, and it sits still entirely for reduced-motion visitors.
- **Frame by frame:** Letters are DOM spans (NOT SVG textPath) positioned around the ring centre — in fill mode evenly stepped (360/letters, offset by startAngle, ×repeat copies); in non-fill mode each glyph gets an arc proportional to its measured real width → a Motion frame.update loop advances the ring angle by the current speed (delta clamped 100 ms); cruise velocity = 360/spinDuration °/s (default spin 20 s), sign flipped for counterclockwise → hover multiplies the speed (slowDown 0.5, speedUp 4, pause 0, goBonkers 20) through a spring (stiffness 60, damping 18) so changes glide → drag samples pointer angle (dead radius 6% of size, 100 ms sample window); release within 80 ms of the last sample flings at up to ±1440 °/s, decaying fling *= exp(−dt/0.7), zeroing below 1 °/s → scale (300/20 spring) and pointer tilt (150/18 springs) ride on top; perspective = size × 2.5.
- **Mechanism & key values:** React + Motion (motion values, springs, frame.update, reduced-motion hook). Defaults: spinDuration 20, onHover 'speedUp', direction 'clockwise', size 200, fontSize 24, fontWeight 900, letterSpacing 0, startAngle 0, fill true, repeat 1, tilt 0, hoverTilt 0, draggable false. Non-fill glyph estimates before fonts measure: space = fontSize×0.3, other = fontSize×0.6, plus letterSpacing×fontSize. Ring line option: inset 1.3em, borderWidth max(1, fontSize/16). CSS transitions: plane transform 0.7 s cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); settled letters 0.5 s cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0, 1). Root role="img" with aria-label = text; IntersectionObserver gates the spin; reduced motion zeroes cruise speed and disables fling/tilt. The entry's rebuild note: the DOM-span ring (vs SVG textPath) is what makes drag/fling and per-letter springs trivial — copy that choice.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Rotating badge/stamp motifs — around a logo, a CTA, a hero corner ("GET A FREE QUOTE •" rings). Fully portable to vanilla JS with one rAF loop.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry Q164). **Code:** code-source/circular-text/

## [BANK] Q165 · Depth Text (React Bits) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** https://reactbits.dev/text-animations/depth-text (canonical source: DavidHDev/react-bits repo, src/content/TextAnimations/DepthText/DepthText.jsx + .css)
- **How it looks:** A headline with real physical depth — the word rendered 35 times in a stack, each copy pushed a few pixels further back in 3D space and shaded progressively darker toward a violet depth colour, so the letters look extruded like a solid sign. On load the extrusion grows out of the flat face over 1.2 seconds. Move the pointer and the whole sign tilts toward you in 3D; press it and it sinks backward on a spring. Leave it alone and it slowly orbits by itself.
- **Frame by frame:** Intro: a grow factor runs 0→1 over 1200 ms with cubic-out easing, scaling every layer's Z offset — the depth literally grows → pointer tracked over 0.8× the element rect: target rotation = base tilt (−tilt×0.32 X, +tilt×0.42 Y) adjusted ±tilt, current rotation lerping by smoothing 0.14/frame → no pointer: auto-orbit takes over with sinusoidal targets at orbitSpeed 0.35 (amplitude factor 0.18 on pointer-capable devices, 0.55 otherwise) → hover/press runs a push spring (stiffness 260, damping 17; press adds 0.25) whose sink value pushes the stage back by sink × total extent and shrinks the grow → the rAF loop stops itself when everything settles; reduced motion renders the static base pose with the intro completed.
- **Mechanism & key values:** React + plain CSS 3D — no WebGL, no animation library. Face span at translateZ(0.6px) + N aria-hidden layer spans in a preserve-3d stage, layer i at translateZ(−i × depth px) via a --depth-text-grow custom property; total extent = layers × depth (default 34 × 2.4 = 81.6 px). Layer shading: color-mix with eased progress p² — (1−p²)×72+4 % face colour into depth colour, then 92% toward black; gradientDepth mode fades alpha instead, reach = (1 − (i−0.5)/total)^1.6. Defaults: text 'Elevate', layers 34 (clamp 2–64), depth 2.4 (0–12), depthColor '#7c3aed', tilt 7.5 (0–12), smoothing 0.14, perspective 900, fontSize 'clamp(3rem, 12vw, 7rem)', fontWeight 900, line-height 0.86, letter-spacing −0.065em. Float option: rotX cos(t×1.19)×2×drift, rotY sin(t×0.86+2.1)×4×drift, lift sin(t×1.43)×fontSizePx×0.045×drift.
- **Tier:** STRONG — the entry calls it the cheapest possible "3D headline": 35 DOM nodes, zero libraries, works in WordPress/Elementor with a small JS shim. Watch DOM cost at layers 64 on low-end phones.
- **Best for:** Hero and section headlines that need dimension without WebGL weight.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry Q165). **Code:** code-source/depth-text/

## [BANK] Q166 · Particle Text (React Bits) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** https://reactbits.dev/text-animations/particle-text (canonical source: DavidHDev/react-bits repo, src/content/TextAnimations/ParticleText/ParticleText.jsx + .css)
- **How it looks:** A headline made of up to ~5,000 tiny dots. On load they gather — swirling in from a scattered circle (or raining from above, spiralling in, or revealed by a scanning light line, depending on the intro mode) — and lock into the letterforms. After that the word is alive: push the pointer through it and particles scatter away from your cursor, glowing orange-hot exactly where they've been displaced, then spring home and cool back to the base colour. Click and a burst explodes outward from the click point.
- **Frame by frame:** Text is rasterised to an offscreen canvas (shrunk so width ≤ 0.92 × container), alpha-sampled on a grid (step = density 4, alpha > 40 kept), capped at clamp(floor(w×h/90), 900, 5200) particles with deterministic seeds (no Math.random — resizes are stable) → per-particle intro with delay = seed × stagger 420 ms: gather = easeOutCubic from a circle over 1600 ms; rain = easeInFall t^1.7 from above; spiral = easeInOutCubic with swirl (1.5 + 2.6×(1 − r/reach)); scan = a 1.5 px sweep line with a 9-stop gradient → per frame (frame-rate normalised, dt clamped 0.05): positions follow targets at 1 − 0.78^frames, pointer smoothed at 1 − 0.82^frames, particles inside repelRadius 120 are pushed by (1 − d/radius)² × pointerRepel 40 → heat = clamp((distance-from-target − 3)/36, 0, 1) shifts displaced particles toward the highlight colour (#ff5a36) — the signature: the headline visibly lights up where it is disturbed → click burst: radius = 90 + 70×√strength + repelRadius×0.25, power = 950×strength×(0.2 + 0.8×falloff²)×(0.65 + depth×0.45), offsets spring home (BURST_SPRING 18 / BURST_DAMPING 7.5).
- **Mechanism & key values:** React + Canvas 2D (no WebGL). Rendering batched into 96 draw groups (12 tone steps × 8 alpha fades) to avoid per-particle fillStyle changes; hot tones (tone ≥ 1) composited through an offscreen glow layer with shadowBlur (3 + particleSize×1.5)×dpr; DPR capped at 2; the rAF loop sleeps when nothing is busy. Defaults: particleSize 2, density 4, highlightMode 'motion', intro 'gather', scatter 180, gatherDuration 1600, stagger 420, burstStrength 1, pointerRepel 40, repelRadius 120, idleDrift 0.7, fontSize 'clamp(3rem, 12vw, 8rem)', fontWeight 800. Idle drift adds sin/cos wobble scaled by idleDrift × per-particle depth (0.45…1.35). Reduced motion snaps particles to targets; an sr-only span carries the text.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** One hero headline moment per page — the heat-from-displacement colour system is what lifts it above a generic particle demo. The two transferable tricks per the entry: bucketed colour batching and deterministic seeds.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry Q166). **Code:** code-source/particle-text/

## [BANK] Q167 · Stroke Text (React Bits) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** https://reactbits.dev/text-animations/stroke-text (canonical source: DavidHDev/react-bits repo, src/content/TextAnimations/StrokeText/StrokeText.jsx + .css)
- **How it looks:** A headline that draws itself: each letter's outline is traced stroke by stroke, left to right, like an invisible pen writing — then, once the outlines finish, colour floods in with a wipe from one side while a soft drop shadow lifts in behind the word. It can run once on scroll, replay on hover, or loop forever; the strokes can be solid, dashed, dotted, or even marching-ants animated.
- **Frame by frame:** Every char is a <tspan> in two SVG <text> layers (stroke, fill) inside a viewBox measured from the real glyph bbox (getBBox, padded by max(strokeWidth, fontSize×0.1)) → each char's dash is set to max(fontSize×7, 200) — deliberately far longer than any glyph path — with dashoffset = dash (fully hidden) → draw-on: all chars' strokeDashoffset tween to 0 over drawDuration 1.6 s, staggered 0.05, ease power2.out — because the dash exceeds every path length, each letter reads as genuinely drawn, never faded → after drawDuration + fillDelay 0.2, over max(0.4, drawDuration×0.5): either a clipPath rect wipes the fill across (power2.inOut) or per-char fill tspans fade in (power2.out) → optional shadow: feDropShadow dx/dy 0 → fontSize×0.06, flood-opacity 0 → 0.5, over fillDuration×1.4, power3.out.
- **Mechanism & key values:** React + GSAP + ScrollTrigger. Defaults: text 'Draw Attention', strokeColor '#A78BFA', fillColor 'currentColor', strokeWidth 1.4, drawDuration 1.6, fillDelay 0.2, stagger 0.05, ease 'power2.out', trigger 'mount', fillMode 'wipe', wipeFrom 'left', fontSize 128, fontWeight 800, letterSpacing −4, dashLength 10. Triggers: mount immediate; scroll = ScrollTrigger start 'top 82%', once; hover replays from the finished state; loop = repeat −1, repeatDelay 0.9, yoyo; hoverRedraw fades strokes out in 0.2 s and redraws at 0.8× duration. Patterned strokes: dashed (on = max(dashLength − strokeWidth, 0.5), off = dashLength×0.6 + strokeWidth) or dotted (0 ${gap}, gap = max(dashLength, strokeWidth×1.8), round caps) drawn through a mask + feMorphology erode filter (radius strokeWidth/2 + 0.75) so the reveal consumes the pattern cleanly; marching mode animates dashoffset 0 → −period with duration = period/(fontSize×0.22), linear, infinite. Shadow stdDeviation = fontSize×0.016, SHADOW_OPACITY 0.5. Re-measure on document.fonts.ready and ResizeObserver (0.5 px hysteresis); SVG hidden until measured; reduced motion sets the end state instantly.
- **Tier:** STRONG — the entry's distinction notes: the dash = fontSize×7 rule and the directional clip wipe are the two details that separate this from every "SVG text draw" tutorial; the erode-mask trick for dashed/dotted reveals is unique in the bank.
- **Best for:** Section headlines and hero words that should arrive as an event. One headline per page — the draw takes 1.6 s of attention.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry Q167). **Code:** code-source/stroke-text/

## [BANK] Q169 · Text Loop (React Bits) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** https://reactbits.dev/text-animations/text-loop (canonical source: DavidHDev/react-bits repo, src/content/TextAnimations/TextLoop/TextLoop.jsx + .css — despite the name it is NOT a phrase cycler: the component page describes "a seamless text marquee that flows along curved SVG paths")
- **How it looks:** A ribbon of text — "React ✦ Bits" by default — flowing forever along a shaped track: a sine wave, a circle, an infinity loop, an arch, or a straight line. The text rides a coloured tape band (default #5227FF, 86 px wide) that follows the same path underneath it. Drag it and fling it; scroll the page fast and it surges (with the scrollBoost module); hover and it eases to a stop. A cross mode adds a second tape counter-scrolling at an angle through the first.
- **Frame by frame:** The path is generated per shape inside viewBox 1200×520 (wave: amplitude a = min(curviness×2.2, room×2), built from T steps of 320; circle: r = min(90 + curviness×0.95, room); infinity: r = 150 + curviness×1.4; arch: rise = min(120 + curviness×1.1, room×2)) → pathLength via getTotalLength(), one text unit via getComputedTextLength(); the rendered text carries textLength = pathLength with lengthAdjust 'spacing' — the browser stretches letter-spacing so one repetition always equals the full path length exactly → two <textPath> copies sit exactly one path-length apart (head startOffset = wrap(travel, L), tail = startOffset − L) and tile the path seamlessly forever → GSAP ticker (dt clamped 0.05) advances travel at v = base×hoverScale + fling + boost → drag fling decays exp(−dt/0.55), clamped ±2600; scrollBoost approaches its ±1600-capped target at 1 − exp(−dt/0.18); pauseOnHover tweens hover scale to 0 over 0.6 s power2.out, back over 0.9 s power2.inOut.
- **Mechanism & key values:** React + GSAP (ticker only, as the frame clock). Defaults: text 'React ✦ Bits', shape 'wave', speed 90 (path units/sec), separator '✦', curviness 90, tilt 0, fontSize 46, fontWeight 800, letterSpacing 2, ribbon true, ribbonColor '#5227FF', ribbonWidth 86, edgeFade 0, pauseOnHover true, cross false, crossAngle 16, scrollBoost 0. Constants: MAX_FLING 2600, MAX_BOOST 1600, FADE_STEPS 8, smootherstep t³(t(6t−15)+10); edgeFade builds an 8-stop smootherstep gradient mask over min(1, edgeFade)×0.3 of the path; cross-mode tape colour = tint(ribbonColor, 0.62), ink by sRGB luminance threshold 0.2. IntersectionObserver starts/stops the ticker; reduced motion sets base speed 0 and never starts it. The entry's load-bearing trick: textLength + lengthAdjust 'spacing' makes the two-copy wrap exact on any path shape without manual letter counting; the scrollBoost recipe (EMA velocity → ±1600 cap → 0.18 s approach) is a drop-in "marquee reacts to page scroll" module for any marquee in the bank.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Curved statement ribbons and tape-style marquee dividers — the shaped-track alternative to Q161's straight canonical marquee and Q149's CSS-motion-path train.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry Q169). **Code:** code-source/text-loop/

## [BANK] Q170 · Text Type (React Bits) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md)
- **Reference source:** https://reactbits.dev/text-animations/text-type (canonical source: DavidHDev/react-bits repo, src/content/TextAnimations/TextType/TextType.jsx + .css)
- **How it looks:** A typewriter that behaves like a person: sentences type out grapheme by grapheme at 50 ms a character while a cursor GLIDES to each new caret position (instead of jumping) and stays solid while moving, blinking only at rest. Occasionally — if you turn mistakes on — it types a wrong neighbouring key, dwells a beat, deletes it, pauses, and carries on correctly. At the end of a sentence it pauses 2 seconds, deletes (backspace-style, or by growing a selection highlight and clearing instantly), and types the next.
- **Frame by frame:** Type: one grapheme per tick (typingSpeed 50, or a uniform random delay in [min, max] with variableSpeed); text split grapheme-aware via Intl.Segmenter → cursor: an absolutely positioned element tracked to a zero-width caret span; with cursorGlide it tweens to each caret over clamp(pace×0.0016, 0.06, 0.18) s, power3.out; blink is a GSAP timeline repeat −1 (hold = blink×0.7, fades at blink×0.45 each, sine.inOut, extra gap blink×0.4), paused and snapped solid on every caret move, restarted after a 0.12 s delayedCall → per-char entrances (optional, WAAPI): fade 360 ms cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1); blur 520 ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) with blur(0.3em→0); rise 480 ms cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.4, 0.64, 1) → mistakes: each char has probability min(1, mistakes)×0.16 of a typo (never the first char, never the same index twice running; QWERTY NEIGHBORS map in source): wrong neighbour typed at typing speed (40% chance the following char too), dwell 260 + rand×320 ms, delete at max(45, deletingSpeed), pause 90 + rand×140 ms → sentence end: pause pauseDuration 2000 → delete at deletingSpeed 30 (backspace) or select-mode highlight growing one char per tick, wait max(160, deletingSpeed×8), clear instantly → next sentence; loop or stop.
- **Mechanism & key values:** React + GSAP (cursor glide + blink only); typing is a setTimeout state machine with an onSentenceComplete callback. Defaults: typingSpeed 50, initialDelay 0, pauseDuration 2000, deletingSpeed 30, deleteMode 'backspace', loop true, cursorStyle 'character', cursorCharacter '|', cursorBlinkDuration 0.5, cursorGlide true, typeEffect 'none', mistakes 0, startOnVisible false (when true: IntersectionObserver threshold 0.1, one-shot). Cursor shapes: bar max(2px, 0.07em) × 1.1em; block 0.56em × 1.1em; underscore 0.56em × max(2px, 0.075em); selected-char background color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 25%, transparent). An sr-only span holds the prefix + all sentences for screen readers; reduced motion resolves typing/deleting instantly. The entry's rebuild note: the realism lives in the mistakes system and caret physics, not the typing speed — steal those two layers onto any simpler typewriter; grapheme-aware splitting is mandatory if strings ever contain emoji or combining accents.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Best for:** Hero sub-lines and rotating service phrases where a human typing feel is the point ("We replace roofs… / We repair siding… / We fit windows…"). Use sparingly — one typing element per page.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry Q170). **Code:** code-source/text-type/

## [BANK] Variable Proximity (React Bits) — deep-read (reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md, all four packs)
- **Reference source:** https://reactbits.dev/text-animations/variable-proximity
- **How it looks:** A line of text set in the Roboto Flex variable font. At rest every letter sits light and narrow (weight 400, optical size 9). Letters near the visitor's cursor swell — up to weight 1000 and optical size 40 right under the pointer — so a soft bulge of heavy type follows the mouse across the headline while distant letters stay thin.
- **Frame by frame:** Pointer moves over or near the text → every frame, each letter's target is set by its distance from the pointer (falloff inside the radius, default 50 px) and its weight/optical size ease toward that target with frame-rate-independent damping, snapping when within 0.002 → pointer leaves and nothing is near for 500 ms → if the idle wave is enabled, a wave rolls through the text (period 3.2 s, peak strength 0.7) mixing in over ~600 ms → everything settles and the animation loop stops entirely (zero idle cost). Optional extras per letter: colour mixing toward a "near" colour, and lift/scale transforms. The wave is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion and paused off-screen.
- **Mechanism & key values:** React component, no animation library — hand-rolled rAF writing `font-variation-settings` per letter (write-cached). Falloff curves: linear `1 − d/r`; exponential `(1 − d/r)²`; gaussian `(e^(−2(d/r)²) − e⁻²)/(1 − e⁻²)`; hard 0 at d ≥ radius. Damping: `level += (target − level) × (1 − exp(−Δt/(smoothing × 400)))`, smoothing default 0.2, Δt clamped to 64 ms. Defaults: from `'wght' 400, 'opsz' 9` → to `'wght' 1000, 'opsz' 40`; radius 50 px; falloff 'linear'; idleWave off by default; wave span `max(220, 0.85 × text width)`.
- **Best for:** Hero headlines and interactive section titles. Trade fit: use at headline scale — the deep read advises radius ≈ 0.8–1.2× font-size (the 50 px default suits body text). Vanilla-JS port is ~120 lines; no GSAP needed.
- **Deep read:** reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md (entry 171). **Code:** none in packs.

House CustomEase 'eleos' = cubic-bezier(0.625, 0.05, 0, 1); loader ease = (0.3589, 0.5033, 0, 0.9972). Inline duration palette across the page: 0.15 / 0.2 / 0.25 / 0.4 / 0.5 / 0.7 / 0.725 / 0.8 / 1 / 1.2 s.

## [BANK] Collapsing Logo Effect (Codrops) — deep-read (reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md, all four packs)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/Development/CollapsingLogo/ (article: https://tympanus.net/codrops/2018/06/05/collapsing-logo-effect/)
- **How it looks:** A fullscreen intro that is secretly just the site logo: the small logo box is pre-scaled to fill the whole viewport, so the "intro screen" is the stretched logo itself. Clicking "enter" collapses the whole screen — width first, then height — down into the small logo at its real position, while slideshow images settle in behind it and the logo's arrow icon hops and spins into place. Clicking the collapsed logo blows it back up to fullscreen.
- **Frame by frame:** Close (click enter): box scaleX → 1 in 300 ms easeOutQuad, then scaleY → 1 in 700 ms easeOutExpo delayed 300 ms (total ~1 s — the two-axis asymmetry is the signature); other intro elements exit in 150 ms easeOutQuad (translateX −30%, opacity 0); arrow icon hops translateY −400% (300 ms easeOutQuad) then 200% → 0% (700 ms easeOutExpo) plus rotation 90 → 0 over 1300 ms easeOutElastic; slideshow images settle scale 1.5 → 1, translateY 10% → 0 over 1000 ms easeOutCubic, delay i×60. Open (click logo): mirror — scaleX out 700 ms easeOutExpo delayed 300, scaleY out 300 ms easeOutQuad; content returns over 1200 ms easeOutExpo, delay 350 + i×30, with a 400 ms linear opacity track.
- **Mechanism & key values:** anime.js + a vanilla `Panel` class + CSS custom properties/grid; no GSAP. Scale factors computed from the box's own getBoundingClientRect at load and recomputed on resize (debounced 10 ms); `isAnimating` lock both directions. GSAP equivalents map 1:1 (easeOutQuad ≈ power2.out, easeOutExpo ≈ expo.out, easeOutCubic ≈ power3.out, easeOutElastic ≈ elastic.out(1, 0.5)-class).
- **Best for:** Intro/enter screens, logo-reveal loaders, and page transitions (run close on link click, navigate, run open reversed). In Elementor: fixed header logo as the box + a fullscreen intro section, ~80 lines of JS.
- **Deep read:** reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md (entry 196). **Code:** none in packs.

## [BANK] Decorative Letter Animations (Codrops) — deep-read (reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md, all four packs)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/Development/DecorativeLetterAnimations/ (article: https://tympanus.net/codrops/2018/01/10/decorative-letter-animations/)
- **How it looks:** One display word on a fullscreen SVG stage. When the word shows, each letter pops in while a burst of small coloured shapes — circles, rectangles, triangles — explodes outward from that letter's own outline and fades away. The demo cycles 5 words as a slideshow, each with its own burst personality (one elastic-rising with confetti drops, one ring of blue outline circles expanding from the word's centre).
- **Frame by frame:** show() → letters animate in (article's canonical config: 400 ms, delay i×60, easeInExpo, scale and opacity 0 → 1); synchronised per letter, its 10 shapes fly out over 700 ms, delay i×40, easeOutExpo — translateX random(−20, 20), translateY random(−400, 400), scale random(0.2–0.6)², rotate random(−16, 16) — with opacity popping to 1 in 1 ms then fading over 700 ms easeOutQuad. Effect 1: letters 800 ms easeOutElastic rising translateY 100% → 0%; shapes 300 ms easeOutQuad, translateY random(−15, 15) → random(−200, 200). Effect 2 (stroke-only circles, colour #0671e6): letters 800 ms easeOutElastic with centre-out delay |total/2 − i|×60; shapes 700 ms easeOutExpo; on hide the shapes fly up −random(400–800) px. hide() reverses and resets letter transforms to none.
- **Mechanism & key values:** anime.js + Charming letter splitter + a hand-written `Word` class. One viewport-sized SVG per word; shapes generated from each letter's measured rect (circle r = 0.5 × letter width at its centre; rect w/h = random(0.05–0.5) × letter w/h; triangle polygon across the rect), transform-origin at the letter centre, all starting at opacity 0. Defaults: 10 shapes/letter; palette #e07272, #0805b5, #49c6ff, #8bc34a, #1e1e21, #e24e81, #e0cd24; shapeFill true; strokeWidth 1. Randoms must be re-rolled per run (functions, not values) or every letter bursts identically; cap total shapes ≈ 120 for performance.
- **Best for:** Hero word reveals and section-title moments — e.g. a trade word bursting shapes when scrolled into view (trigger show() with IntersectionObserver). Port is ~200 lines.

## [BANK] Grid Layout with Motion Hover Effect and Content Preview (Codrops) — deep-read (reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md, all four packs)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/Development/GridLayoutMotion/ (article: https://tympanus.net/codrops/2018/05/23/grid-layout-with-motion-hover/)
- **How it looks:** A CSS-Grid of editorial boxes, each a stack of absolutely-positioned layers — photo, title, text, a decorative frame, a shadow, content. Moving the pointer across a box leans all its layers at different amplitudes, like a paper collage tilting in depth. Clicking a box sweeps a full-width panel across the screen, the other boxes explode outward off the grid and fade, and the chosen box's layers fly into a preview arrangement.
- **Frame by frame:** Hover (after a 40 ms arming delay so passing glances don't trigger): the pointer's position inside the item maps linearly onto per-layer ranges — image (−10, −10) px, title (20, 10), text (20, 50, rotZ −20), deco (−20, 0, rotZ 3), shadow (30, 20, rotZ −2), content (5, 3) — every layer chasing with a 1.5 s Power1.easeOut tween → mouseleave: all layers return to 0 over 1.5 s Power2.easeOut (shadow: 2 s Back.easeOut) → click: revealer panel sweeps x −100% → 0% in 0.5 s Power1.easeInOut, body scroll locks, panel sweeps out 0.5 s Power3.easeOut at delay 0.2 while the item's layers fly to preview positions (duration distance-mapped 0.8–1.2 s across viewport width, Expo.easeOut, from offsets up to x 800 px, y ±100 px, rotZ 5–30°) and every other item explodes outward (direction by vertical third, distance mapped 20–600 px, 700 in the middle band, 0.4 s Power3.easeOut, delay mapped 0–0.3 s, rotZ random ±10°, opacity → 0) → close: revealer sweeps back, layers restore over 0.6 s Expo.easeOut at delay 0.55 + 0–0.2 mapped, tilt re-enabled.
- **Mechanism & key values:** TweenMax (GSAP 1.x-era API) + imagesLoaded + CSS Grid; the core is one shared pointer→range mapper (lineEq) driving per-layer tweens. Modern port: GSAP 3 `quickTo` per layer (1.5 s power1 chase), fixed overlay for the preview. Keep ≤ 6 layers/item and ≤ 12 items; the demo has no touch path — gate tilt behind `(hover: hover)`.
- **Best for:** Work/project galleries — box layers map to photo, title, "view project" text, deco frame, shadow, with the revealer-sweep preview on click.
