## [BANK] On-Scroll Text Motion (Codrops) — deep-read (reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md, all four packs)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/Development/ScrollTextMotion/
- **How it looks:** A black page of giant white text blocks — up to clamp(2rem, 20vw, 15rem) in the 'lores-12' display face with 'forma-djr-mono' secondary text. As you scroll, each block flies from its home layout position to an alternate position and back again, its width, opacity and blur shifting as it travels; and every time a block passes through the viewport it re-types itself in a scramble of upper/lowercase characters before settling.
- **Frame by frame:** Smooth scroll runs throughout (ScrollSmoother, smooth: 1, normalizeScroll: true) → for each text element, a two-pass scrubbed Flip loop: Flip.to from start clamp(bottom bottom−10%) to end clamp(center center), then Flip.from from clamp(center center) to clamp(top top), both scrubbed, ease expo.inOut by default (per-element override), interpolating opacity, filter and width → a separate ScrollTrigger (top bottom → bottom top) fires a ScrambleText re-type of the element's own text on enter and on enter-back, duration 1 s default (per-element override), chars 'upperAndLowerCase', starting from an empty scramble state; the logo scrambles once on load with revealDelay 0.5 → entering the footer zone (top center+=25%) fades the logo out (0.7 s expo) and staggers related-demo cards in from xPercent 100, scale 0, opacity 0 (0.7 s expo, stagger 0.1); leaving reverses it (0.5 s power3.in, stagger 0.05). Resize fully re-initialises the system.
- **Mechanism & key values:** GSAP core + ScrollTrigger, ScrollSmoother, Flip, ScrambleTextPlugin (Club plugins — the live demo is the current modernised build; the deep read notes Club GSAP is now free via npm since the Webflow acquisition, terms to verify before commercial shipping). Flip state captured with props 'opacity, filter, width' after swapping each element to its `data-alt-pos` class. Type scale: display clamp(2rem, 20vw, 15rem), secondary clamp(2rem, 10vw, 4rem).
- **Best for:** A giant word-stream section (e.g. "ROOFING — REPAIRS — REPLACEMENTS") whose words swap grid positions and re-scramble through the viewport centre. Keep word count modest (≈10–14 blocks as in the demo); Flip with filter interpolation is GPU-heavy on low-end phones — drop `filter` from props for production.

## [BANK] Creating a Smooth Horizontal Parallax Gallery: From DOM to WebGL (Codrops) — deep-read (reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md, all four packs)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2026/02/19/creating-a-smooth-horizontal-parallax-gallery-from-dom-to-webgl/
- **How it looks:** A full-screen horizontal gallery of 10 images (frames 60vh tall, 4/3 aspect, 2rem gaps) that never actually scrolls the page — wheel input glides the strip sideways while each photograph drifts inside its own frame against the direction of travel: images at screen centre sit neutral, images at the edges lean furthest. In the second phase the identical gallery renders in WebGL on one fixed canvas, the parallax done inside the shader, with the DOM images kept in layout as the source of truth and the no-WebGL fallback.
- **Frame by frame:** Wheel event → `scroll.target += deltaY` (passive), clamped to [0, container width − wrapper width] → each frame `scroll.current` lerps toward target at 0.07 and the container moves by translateX(−current px) → per image: t = (element centre − viewport centre) / viewport centre, clamped −1..1; shift = −t × MAX_SHIFT applied to the oversized inner image (width 125%, left −12.5%) — MAX_SHIFT 10 is the arithmetic ceiling (12.5% spare ÷ 125% image width); guide values 4 subtle / 8 medium / 10 max-safe → WebGL phase: per visible element, uParallax = distance × parallaxIntensity (0.4; guide 0.2 subtle / 0.6 dramatic) feeds the fragment shader after cover-UV mapping, with UV pre-scaled ×0.85 so the shift never exposes an edge.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Hand-rolled scroll engine — no GSAP. Vite + TypeScript, three@^0.170.0. WebGL sync: renderer antialias + alpha, pixelRatio min(devicePixelRatio, 2); camera calibrated so 1 CSS px = 1 world unit — fov = 2·atan(screenHeight/2/100) in degrees, camera z = 100, near 0.01, far 1000; one shared PlaneGeometry(1, 1, 32, 32); mesh position x = bounds.left − scroll − vw/2 + w/2, y = −bounds.top + vh/2 − h/2; `coverUv()` GLSL reproduces object-fit: cover; fragment order: coverUv → uv.x += uParallax × uShaderMultiplier (1.0) → recentre → uv ×= uUvScale (0.85) → sample. Tuning surface is three knobs only (lil-gui). Touch/drag support is an unimplemented exercise in the article — as shipped, the gallery is wheel-only.
- **Best for:** Horizontal work galleries. The DOM phase alone (~80 lines of vanilla JS) is a complete dependency-free pattern and the version to bank for client work; the WebGL phase pays off only at dozens of images or when shader effects stack on top. Keep the two buffer systems consistent: DOM 125% / MAX_SHIFT 10 pairs with uUvScale 0.85 at intensity 0.4; raising intensity toward 0.6 means dropping uUvScale toward 0.8.

## [BANK] Interlude: A Starter for Custom Page Transitions in Astro (Codrops) — deep-read (reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md, all four packs)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2026/10/07/interlude-astro-page-transitions/
- **How it looks:** An Astro starter where clicking a link covers the current page before the swap: covers sweep in (a curtain, a wipe, a growing circle, columns, or a typewriter that types a phrase across a grid then erases it); other transitions move the old page itself away — peel like a turning page, tear along a rough line, a cube face turning, a stack, a frame, a corner; a third family dissolves through WebGL (a swaying red velvet stage curtain, old-TV channel static, dither dot-squares in 3 sizes, particles). The catalogue is 21 transitions: 5 covers / 9 page-moving / 7 WebGL.
- **Frame by frame:** The one transition printed in full, slide-up: LEAVE — panel yPercent 100 → 0, duration 0.8, ease power2.inOut (the cover accelerates away committed) → the router swaps the page while covered → ENTER — panel yPercent 0 → −100, duration 0.8, ease power2.out (fast start, gentle landing). Around that, the engine: locks the page while covered → waits for fonts + on-screen images → after swap, moves focus to the new content → remembers which transition played so back/forward replays it → if a new navigation interrupts mid-transition, it picks up from the current visual state instead of snapping. Transition modules lazy-load on link hover/focus — zero cost for transitions never approached.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Astro's own `<ClientRouter />` (not Barba/Swup) + GSAP; Three.js (TSL shaders) only for the WebGL family. Payload budget per page (article-stated): router ≈ 5 kB, engine ≈ 4 kB, GSAP ≈ 28 kB; Three.js ≈ 240 kB loads ONLY when a WebGL transition is about to trigger. The engine listens to astro:before-preparation / before-swap / after-swap / page-load — confirmed in the mined demo bundles, not just prose. Links opt in with `data-transition="slide-up"`.
- **Best for:** An architecture pattern, not a transplant (WordPress/Elementor has no client router). Transferable assets: (a) the contract — cover → lock → wait → swap → move focus → replay-on-back → interruption pickup — as the checklist any PJAX/Barba-style layer must satisfy; (b) lazy-load-on-hover/focus for transition code; (c) the slide-up parameter pair as a default page-cover preset on any stack (fixed overlay + the two tweens ≈ 30 lines). Full Interlude needs Astro — bank it for a future Astro rebuild, where it drops in as-is.

## [BANK] Progressively Enhanced WebGL Lens Refraction (Codrops) — deep-read (reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md, all four packs)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2023/10/10/progressively-enhanced-webgl-lens-refraction/ (by David Lindkvist, 14islands; companion repo github.com/14islands/codrops-scroll-rig-tutorial; library `@14islands/r3f-scroll-rig`; Lens component by Paul Henschel)
- **How it looks:** A real semantic HTML page first. On desktop with smooth scroll active, each photograph lifts into a fixed WebGL canvas exactly over its DOM box: it enters grey, blooms into full colour as it becomes fully visible, and slowly pushes in across its whole transit through the viewport. Headline text gets a distorted WebGL twin rendered over the real text — the DOM text itself only turns transparent, staying selectable, findable and readable by assistive tech. A lens element refracts the WebGL background rendered behind everything. On touch devices, none of this exists: the plain DOM page simply is the page.
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll (Lenis-backed main-thread smooth scroll — the only way to perfectly sync a fixed canvas with DOM boxes) → for each tracked element, per frame: `grayscale = clamp(1 − visibility³, 0, 1)` (colour cubed-eases in), `zoom = 1 + progress × 0.66` (slow push-in over the full transit), `opacity = clamp(viewport × 3, 0, 1)` (fades in over the first third of approach) — where visibility runs 0 entering → 1 fully visible, progress 0 entering → 1 exited, viewport 0 entering → 1 at top of screen → the WebGL text twin distorts with MeshDistortMaterial speed 1.4, distort 0.14, glyphGeometryDetail 16. If the rig is off (touch / below breakpoint), the hidden-when-smooth and transparent-when-smooth classes deactivate, DOM content reappears untouched, and no WebGL meshes render at all.
- **Mechanism & key values:** React + react-three-fiber + Drei on the r3f-scroll-rig architecture: one fixed GlobalCanvas, Lenis SmoothScrollbar, `UseCanvas` tunnels portal per-component WebGL into the global canvas; `<ScrollScene track={el}>` measures one DOM element per frame and passes scale (exact DOM dimensions), scrollState and inViewport. Textures reuse the already-loaded DOM image via `useImageAsTexture` (resolves `currentSrc`, prefers ImageBitmapLoader for off-main-thread GPU upload). WebGLText computes size/spacing/leading/colour/alignment from getComputedStyle (Troika underneath; font must be .woff). The Lens needs a persistent WebGL background rendered behind the canvas children to refract. Honesty label from the source: the Lens's internal shader parameters are NOT in the article and are not claimed — only its integration contract is measured. The touch alternative — hijacking touch scroll via Lenis `syncTouch: true` — is used in the demo only to showcase it; the article explicitly says native scroll feels better on touch. HMR caveat: define ScrollScene children as top-level components.
- **Best for:** The swap discipline transfers to ANY stack: WebGL replaces media only while the enhancement is provably active, and text is made transparent, never hidden — an SEO/a11y-safe enhancement contract. The three scrollState formulas are stack-agnostic and reusable in GSAP ScrollTrigger onUpdate handlers. The rig itself is React/R3F-only (installable as-is if a rebuild goes React/Astro); it does not port to WordPress/Elementor as code.
- **Deep read:** reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md (entry 249). **Code:** none in packs.

- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2015/11/12/animating-svg-menu-icon-segment/
- **How it looks:** A 34×34 px burger button whose bars never morph shape. Each outer bar is one long invisible trajectory that traces the bar, curls around, and ends as one diagonal of the X; the animation simply slides a fixed-length window of visible stroke (24 units, never changing) along that path, so the bar travels and lands as the diagonal with an elastic overshoot. - **Frame by frame:** Burger → X (~1.0 s total): outer paths first slide linearly — draw("80% − 24", "80%"), 0.3 s, delay 0.1 — then land with draw("100% − 54.5", "100% − 30.5"), 0.6 s, elastic-out(1, 0.3); middle bar stretches draw(2, 38) in 0.1 s, then collapses to its centre point draw(20, 20) in 0.3 s, bounce-out(1, 0.3). X → burger (~1.1 s): outer paths pull back 0.1 s elastic-in(1, 0.3), pass an intermediate stop 0.3 s linear, settle 0.7 s elastic-out(1, 0.3); middle bar restores draw(8, 32) over 0.7 s, delay 0.1, elastic-out(2, 0.4) — a stronger amplitude for the "pop back".
- **Mechanism & key values:** Segment.js (< 2 kB, zero dependencies) animating stroke-dasharray/dashoffset windows; positions accept absolute units or % notation ("80% − 24"). Cross-browser fix (the famous detail): getTotalLength differs slightly between Firefox and Chrome at small sizes, enough to desync the choreography — so author the SVG at 1000×1000, scale down with CSS `transform: scale(0.1)`, multiply all JS segment values ×10, scale stroke-width accordingly. Init windows: Segment(A, 8, 32), (C, 8, 32), (B, 8, 32) in 100-unit space. Presentation: wrapper pointer-events none with the trigger button pointer-events auto (the SVG overscans the hit area). Full path data for all three trajectories is printed in the deep read.
- **Best for:** Menu buttons and any two-state icon morph in a single HTML file or Elementor HTML widget (~60 lines to reimplement draw() with dasharray math). The transferable gold: (a) the trajectory-path design method — one path containing both icon states; (b) the constant-length invariant; (c) the 10×-authoring fix, which applies to ANY getTotalLength-based animation. For a service-site header, halve the elastic tails.

## [BANK] Page Loading Effects (Codrops) — deep-read (reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md, all four packs)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/Development/PageLoadingEffects/ (demo) · repo: github.com/codrops/PageLoadingEffects
- **How it looks:** A roster of 13 full-screen page covers: Lazy Stretch, Circle, Spill, Frame it, Windscreen wiper, Jammed blind, Parallelogram, Tilted, Lateral Swipe, Wave, Origami, Curtain (and one further variant slot). A brand-coloured SVG shape stretches or morphs in steps to cover the whole viewport while the next page loads, then morphs back away. The loading spinner state appears only after the cover has completely closed — never behind an unfinished cover.
- **Frame by frame:** Lazy Stretch (verified in the live page source): a 4-point polygon inside a viewBox 0 0 80 60 morphs through 4 opening steps — `M20,15 50,30 50,30 30,30 Z` → `M0,0 80,0 50,30 20,45 Z` → `M0,0 80,0 60,45 0,60 Z` → `M0,0 80,0 80,60 0,60 Z` — at speedIn 100 ms per step, stretched to any viewport (preserveAspectRatio "none"; the distortion is the aesthetic); closing runs 4 steps back and ends collapsed to a point `M30,30 …`. Circle: a single-Bézier circle path grows from a collapsed point, speedIn 300, easing mina.easeinout (≈ cubic-bezier(0.42, 0, 0.58, 1), Derived mapping), preserveAspectRatio "xMidYMid slice" so the shape stays true. Class order (repo-sourced): `.show` added immediately → morph runs → `.pageload-loading` added only after the morph completes; on hide, if no closing sequence is defined, it animates back to the initial path.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Vanilla JS `SVGLoader` class + Snap.svg + classie.js; each variant is a static page carrying its own inline SVG overlay + config; morph targets live in markup as `data-opening` / `data-closing` attributes holding semicolon-separated path sequences. The live demo's svgLoader.js URL returns the host's 404 page today (measured and logged in the source) — loader internals above are labelled repo-sourced where used. The bank's standing verdict, adopted in the deep read: reimplement CSS-only; do not resurrect the Snap.svg dependency (all Lazy Stretch steps are 4-point polygons with the same command structure, so CSS `d: path("…")` transitions interpolate natively in Chromium; cross-browser, a ~20-line JS interpolator or GSAP AttrPlugin on `d` covers it).
- **Best for:** Page-cover loaders/transitions — the same cover family as Interlude (entry 248). In WordPress: a fixed overlay div + a click interceptor on internal links gives a credible cover on brochure sites; keep speedIn totals ≤ ~400 ms per direction or the cover becomes the wait.

- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2015/11/24/shazam-like-morphing-button-effect/ · demo http://tympanus.net/Tutorials/ShazamButtonEffect/
- **How it looks:** A music-identification button (one SVG component in a 300×500 viewBox space) that morphs through three shapes: a start button, a "listening" form with a double pulsing ripple ring behind it while musical notes drift outward in random directions at a constant speed, and a player panel. Each state's content slides and fades in on its own bezier as the outline reshapes — the first morph squashes with an overshoot bezier that dips below zero.
- **Frame by frame:** Click → morph to listen: 400 ms, cubic-bezier(0.8, −0.6, 0.2, 1) (the anticipation "squash") → listening simulation runs 6500 ms: notes spawn on a 60 ms cascade, each note's transition duration = 4.5 × its euclidean distance in px (constant velocity ≈ 222 px/s), transition `transform <speed>ms ease-in, opacity 0.8s`, rotation random −30°…+30°, recycling on transitionend while listening; the ripple ring pulses 1.2 s ease-out infinite (scale3d(3,3,1) opacity 0 → scale3d(1,1,1) opacity 1 at 50% → opacity 0) with the ::after ring repeating at 0.6 s delay → morph to player: 450 ms, cubic-bezier(0.7, 0, 0.3, 1), fired after a 250 ms delay → close back to start: 400 ms, cubic-bezier(0.4, 1, 0.3, 1). Content panels swap at 0.4 s transform/opacity: start-content enters on cubic-bezier(0.8, −0.6, 0.2, 1) from translate3d(0, −25px, 0); listen-content on cubic-bezier(0.8, 0, 0.2, 1) from translate3d(0, 25px, 0); button opacity 0.3 s; player panel opacity 0.5 s (hidden state 0.2 s).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Snap.svg path morphing between three same-point-count paths stored as strings in `data-path-start` / `data-path-listen` / `data-path-player` attributes (shared point counts let Snap interpolate `d` directly); timing functions are mina easings or raw 4-point cubic-bezier arrays. totalNotes = 50. Stack: Snap.svg + custom Modernizr (csstransitions test) + classie.js + icon font; no GSAP.
- **Best for:** Multi-state CTA buttons (e.g. a quote button stepping through form states). Port: replace Snap with GSAP's `attr: { d: … }` tween (works when point counts match) or the native `d: path("…")` CSS property in Chromium; ~40 lines in an Elementor HTML widget. Keep the constant-velocity particle rule (duration = factor × distance) — it is what makes particles feel physical instead of metronomic.

## [BANK] SVG Filter Effects: Outline Text with feMorphology (Codrops, Sara Soueidan) — deep-read (reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md, all four packs)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2019/01/22/svg-filter-effects-outline-text-with-femorphology/
- **How it looks:** Display text wearing a thick flat-colour outline grown evenly around the glyphs (demo: 85 px, weight 700 type with a cyan #32DFEC ring), or a hollow "knockout" version where only the ring remains, the letter middles transparent — and because the ring is cut from the text itself, it takes whatever colour the text's CSS `fill` is set to (demo: Bangers at 150 px). The same primitives roughen a photograph's edges into a painterly silhouette.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. Zero JS, zero CSS animation; the effect is a filter chain applied to the text.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Pure SVG filter primitives. Coloured outline: `feMorphology in="SourceAlpha" operator="dilate" radius="4"` → `feFlood flood-color="#32DFEC"` → `feComposite operator="in"` (flood clipped to the dilated silhouette) → `feMerge` with the outline under SourceGraphic (demo svg 900×200, viewBox "100 0 900 200"). Knockout outline: `feMorphology operator="dilate" radius="8" in="SourceGraphic"` → `feComposite operator="out"` subtracts the original glyph, leaving only the ring in the text's own fill colour (demo letter-spacing 13 px in the governing CSS version). Rule of thumb (Derived in the source): outline thickness ≈ radius in user units per side; use radius 8 for knockout because the ring loses its inner half to the subtraction. Image paint effect: erode or dilate at radius 3. Caveat to carry: Safari historically renders feMorphology on HTML elements poorly — apply to SVG-internal text only.
- **Best for:** Display headlines, logo-type treatments, sticker/badge text. Copy-paste library-grade: define the filter once in a hidden inline SVG, apply with `filter: url(#id)` on SVG `<text>`; the text stays real, selectable SVG text.
- **Deep read:** reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md (entry 256). **Code:** none in packs.

## [BANK] Fancy SVG Letter Animation (Codrops) — deep-read (reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md, all four packs)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2016/09/13/fancy-svg-letter-animation/ · demo http://tympanus.net/Development/FancyLetterAnimation/
- **How it looks:** A hand-lettered word (viewBox 0 0 320 180) whose letters rise in elastically while their strokes draw themselves on. Every stroke exists in 3 stacked layers of slightly increasing width and different colours, so as the widest layer draws on top, the thinner coloured layers peek out at the edges as fringes. Variant effects change the width recipe — one is a reverse taper: a thin bright core line riding on a thick dark body.
- **Frame by frame:** Per letter: entrance translateY [−30, 0] over 900 ms easeOutElastic (elasticity 600) with opacity [0, 1] over 500 ms linear, delay increasing 40 ms per letter → each path draws (stroke-dashoffset from its full getTotalLength to 0) over 800 ms easeOutQuint, delay = pathIndex × 200 + letterIndex × 40 → at the end, the non-final layers fade out (200 ms, starting at delay + duration − 0.1×duration) → exit: translateY [0, 15] + opacity [1, 0], 250 ms easeInOutQuad.
- **Mechanism & key values:** anime.js (v1-era API) + hand-drawn single-stroke SVG paths, each triplicated into 3 identical layers. Effect 1 layer widths 9 px / 9.5 px / 10 px; palette #dea521, #f84242, #3758a7, #f79c8c, #84b5bd, #feefde; stroke-linecap butt, linejoin bevel, miterlimit 3, fill none. Variant stacks from the shipped CSS: effect-2 1/4/10 px; effect-3 10/6/8 px; effect-4 10 px #00966c / 4 px #27272d / 1 px #fcec9b (the reverse taper). Container min-height 400 px / max-height 70vh; the demo's index.html contains 165 `letter__layer` paths (measured count).
- **Best for:** Logo/wordmark reveals and hero lettering for artisan brands. The recipe is font-independent: trace any wordmark as single-stroke paths (or convert a single-line/engraving font to paths), triplicate, run the two tween sets. The manual dasharray technique here is the free equivalent of GSAP's Club DrawSVG. Total JS ≈ 120 lines in one HTML widget.
- **Deep read:** reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md (entry 258). **Code:** animation/code-source/fancy-svg-letter-animation/ (roofing, remodeling packs).

## [BANK] Page Preloading Effect (Codrops) — deep-read (reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md, all four packs)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2014/08/05/page-preloading-effect/ · demo http://tympanus.net/Tutorials/PagePreloadingEffect/
- **How it looks:** A fixed pale header (#f1f1f1, min-height 480 px) covers the screen, holding a pink (#ef6e7e) outlined logo and a small 60 px circular progress ring beneath it. The ring's stroke fills as loading progresses. At 100% the logo drops down, shrinks and turns white; the ring shrinks away; the whole header slides up off the top of the screen; and the page content rises in beneath it — every moving element on one shared easing, so the whole exit reads as a single gesture. The header then flips from fixed to absolute and the page becomes scrollable.
- **Frame by frame:** Load start → header keyframes in from translate3d(0, 800px, 0), opacity 0, 1 s, the loader element delayed 0.2 s; during load a scroll listener forces scrollTo(0, 0) → progress updates set the ring's stroke-dashoffset = L × (1 − val), smoothed by a 0.2 s CSS transition on stroke-dashoffset (the shipped demo simulates progress: +random × 0.1 every 80 ms, ≈ 20 ticks ≈ 1.6 s total, Derived; a real build hooks the same callback to asset-load events) → at 100% (+200 ms completion callback) class `.loaded` fires: logo 1 s forwards to translate3d(0, 100%, 0) + translate3d(0, 50px, 0) + scale3d(0.65, 0.65, 1), its path fill transitioning to #fff (all 0.5s ease, delay 0.3 s); ring 0.5 s forwards to opacity 0, translate3d(0, −100%, 0), scale3d(0.3, 0.3, 1); header 1 s forwards to translate3d(0, −100%, 0); content items rise from translate3d(0, 200px, 0), opacity 0, 1 s, with delays 0.1 / 0.15 / 0.2 s → body gets `.layout-switch` (header fixed → absolute). EVERY keyframe uses cubic-bezier(0.7, 0, 0.3, 1).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Vanilla JS `PathLoader` class + Modernizr (cssanimations) + classie.js; no animation library — CSS keyframes driven by two class flips. Ring: SVG 60 px, viewBox 0 0 80 80, stroke-width 6, track #ddd, progress #ef6e7e. Logo SVG viewBox 0 0 300 160, preserveAspectRatio "xMidYMin meet", width 25% (min 320 px / max 480 px). Breakpoint @media (max-width: 45em).
- **Best for:** Preloaders and intro reveals on preview/brochure pages — the lesson is the unified easing: five different elements read as one motion because they share cubic-bezier(0.7, 0, 0.3, 1). Gate the `.loaded` flip on window.load in real builds and keep the total wait ≤ ~1.6 s. The ring math transfers to any SVG progress ring.
- **Deep read:** reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md (entry 259). **Code:** none in packs.

## [BANK] Pin 2 (kokoruz, CodePen) — deep-read (reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md, all four packs)
- **Reference source:** https://codepen.io/kokoruz/pen/QwjMGBg
- **How it looks:** One page running three independent pinned scroll systems. First, a section pins while a list of words cycles through it — each word slides/fades up into place, then slides out upward, except the last, which dwells. Second, a giant headline starts off-screen right and travels horizontally across its pinned section. Third, a video grows from quarter-size to full-bleed as you scroll, then holds at full size while side texts converge from both edges and a dark overlay deepens over it to 75% black.
- **Frame by frame:** System 1 (word rotator): JS sets the section's bottom margin to (words − 1) × 50vh to manufacture scroll room; pinned timeline (start "top top", end "+=" + words×50 + "%", scrub, pin, pinSpacing FALSE — the margin does the spacing) steps each word in (y 20% → 0%, opacity 0 → 1, duration 1) then out (y −20%, opacity 0, duration 1; skipped for the last word), with a trailing empty tween of duration 2 as dwell → System 2 (headline): set x = section width; tween x → −headline width, ease "none", ScrollTrigger start "top top", end = "+=" + (headline.scrollWidth − section.clientWidth), scrub 2, anticipatePin 1, invalidateOnRefresh → System 3 (video): scale 0.25 → 1 (ease "none") across scaleScroll = (1 − 0.25) × innerWidth, with the total end stretched ×1.5 (holdRatio 0.5) to create the hold phase; side texts from xPercent −100 / +100 → 0 (power1.out) and overlay backgroundColor rgba(0,0,0,0) → rgba(0,0,0,0.75) run in parallel at position 0; a hold tween (duration 0.5) sits at position 1. Extras in the pen: boxes spinning in from scale 0 / rotate 360 (one plain with delay 1, one through a "top 60%" → "top 30%" trigger zone).
- **Mechanism & key values:** GSAP + ScrollTrigger (versions not visible in the pen's JS panel). Defect found in the source (Measured): the resize handler calls an undefined function `getPinEnd()` — the pen throws on window resize; a rebuild must recompute distances via invalidateOnRefresh + functional end values, as systems 2–3 already do. HTML/CSS panels were not exposed by the pen-page fetch — the JS carried all animation parameters, which are this entry's subject.
- **Best for:** Pinned word rotators, horizontal headlines, and product-video scale-then-hold reveals. System 3's formula — scroll distance × (1 + holdRatio) — is the prize; system 1's pinSpacing:false + JS-margin trick suits pinned elements that must overlay following content. All three are single HTML-widget builds; set markers: false in production.
- **Deep read:** reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md (entry 268). **Code:** none in packs.

## [BANK] scroll horizontal Gsap (charlyta, CodePen) — deep-read (reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md, all four packs)
- **Reference source:** https://codepen.io/charlyta/pen/YzjEqyP
- **How it looks:** A smooth-scrolling page where one section pins and its inner strip travels sideways by exactly its overflow width, while a decorative element spins five full turns alongside the travel. As each inner section crosses the centre band of the viewport it gains an "active" class — the theming hook (the L2 log records data-bgcolor / data-textcolor section theming with a 0.3 s body transition in the pen's HTML/CSS: Seen via L2, not re-verified, as the pen-page fetch didn't expose those panels).
- **Frame by frame:** Locomotive Scroll (smooth: true) owns scrolling on the container; `scroller.on("scroll", ScrollTrigger.update)` keeps ScrollTrigger in sync → all pin setup deferred to window load so widths are final → the pinned timeline (defaults ease 'none', scrub) tweens `.pin-wrap` x → −(pinWrapWidth − window.innerWidth) across an end equal to the raw pinWrapWidth in px (note: a raw number, not a "+=" string) → in parallel at position 0, `.anuncio1` rotates 360 × 5 = 1800° → three ScrollTrigger.create instances with containerAnimation toggle "active" on the inner sections between start "center 70%" and end "center 31%" → on ScrollTrigger refresh, `scroller.update()` runs, then ScrollTrigger.refresh().
- **Mechanism & key values:** GSAP + ScrollTrigger + Locomotive Scroll wired through scrollerProxy — the reusable asset, verbatim in the deep read: scrollTop getter/setter delegates to `scroller.scroll.instance.scroll.y` / `scroller.scrollTo(value, 0, 0)`; getBoundingClientRect returns the fixed viewport rect; pinType = "transform" if the container already has a transform, else "fixed". Defects found in the source (Measured): all three creates share id: "3" (duplicate ScrollTrigger ids — later lookups collide), and pinBoxes / twoWidth / horizontalTwoLength are computed and never used. Production fix for the end value: prefer `end: "+=" + horizontalScrollLength` so scroll distance matches travel 1:1 (here end = full wrap width makes horizontal travel slightly slower than 1:1 — copy knowingly).
- **Best for:** The canonical GSAP × Locomotive integration recipe. On WordPress, apply Locomotive to a wrapper section, not body (it hijacks page scroll), or skip Locomotive entirely — the pin timeline works unchanged with the default scroller.
- **Deep read:** reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md (entry 269). **Code:** none in packs.

## [BANK] ScrollTrigger horizontal scroll with pagination (akapowl, CodePen) — deep-read (reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md, all four packs)
- **Reference source:** https://codepen.io/akapowl/embed/preview/qBXqKZM/ba638948806ca4adca9dae41178f29c1
- **How it looks:** On a deep-green page (#2d4026), a horizontal strip of 5 large photos (each 60vw × 60vh, centred in its panel) travels sideways under a pinned scroll. Below, a fixed row of 50 px outlined circle dots tracks progress: the dot for the panel currently crossing the centre morphs from a circle into a square. There is no snap and no click navigation — the dots are pure indicators, and that circle→square morph is the pagination's entire visual language.
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll → the wrapper tweens x → −(scrollWidth − clientWidth) px, ease "none", scrubbed, pinned with pinSpacing: true, invalidateOnRefresh → per panel, a dummy tween's ScrollTrigger (start "left center", end "right center", containerAnimation = the main tween) toggles the matching dot's `active` class, and `.active` sets border-radius: 0 → the strip itself is built with a layout trick: the wrapper is `display: flex; flex-direction: column; flex-wrap: wrap; height: 80vh`, and the five items at height 100% overflow the column and wrap into successive columns — a horizontal strip with zero horizontal-flow CSS. Page details: section padding 10 rem 0; item padding 2rem 0; dots fixed at bottom 5rem, border 1px solid #fff, border-radius 50px; body overflow-x: hidden.
- **Mechanism & key values:** GSAP + ScrollTrigger, SCSS; no smooth-scroll library, no pin-spacing tricks. Defect flagged in the source (Measured inconsistency): `end` uses container.offsetWidth (≈ one panel width — the wrapper's layout width is one column) while the actual travel is scrollWidth − clientWidth (≈ four panels), so the pin releases after ~¼ of the implied scroll distance and the horizontal motion runs ~4× faster than the page scroll; a rebuild should set `end: () => "+=" + (container.scrollWidth − document.documentElement.clientWidth)` to match travel 1:1.
- **Best for:** Horizontal galleries with progress pagination. Two steals: (a) the column-wrap strip — useful inside Elementor where a flex row with overflow is fiddly; (b) circle→square active dots via containerAnimation + toggleClass — ~15 lines for pagination on any horizontal build, no state management. Single-HTML transfer is direct.
- **Deep read:** reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md (entry 270). **Code:** animation/code-source/scrolltrigger-horizontal-pagination/ (roofing, siding-windows-doors, remodeling packs).

## [BANK] A Practical Introduction to Scroll-Driven Animations with CSS scroll() and view() (Codrops, Adam Argyle) — deep-read (reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md, all four packs)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2024/01/17/a-practical-introduction-to-scroll-driven-animations-with-css-scroll-and-view/
- **How it looks:** A set of zero-JavaScript demos where ordinary keyframe animations are driven by scroll itself: an element spinning five full turns as the page scrolls; elements scaling up from half-size as they cross the middle band of the viewport; a snap carousel whose prev/next buttons and dots highlight themselves with no observers or JS; and a whole colour palette that hue-rotates as you scroll horizontally, every oklch colour slot turning together.
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll position becomes the animation's currentTime, scrubbed in both directions → spin: `@keyframes spin { to { transform: rotateY(5turn) } }` (time version: spin 5s ease infinite) attached as `animation: spin linear both; animation-timeline: scroll();` → view() reveals: `animation-timeline: view(); animation-range: contain;` (default range is cover); the gentle scale pattern uses keyframes from scale .5 with `animation-range: 25vh 75vh` → carousel: sections own named view timelines (`--section-1` … `--section-7`), `timeline-scope` on the ancestor lets fixed chrome animate against whichever section is passing: toggle-control keyframes are just `50% { opacity: 0 }` (buttons fade mid-range), dot-selected keyframes run 0%,100% scale .75 → 50% scale 1 with a background swap → hue cycle: `@property --hue` (syntax '<angle>', initial 0turn) animates 0turn → 1turn on `animation-timeline: scroll(x)` at :root, and the palette slots (surfaces oklch 40%/50% and 50%/40%, text 98%/10% and 95%/20%, link 99%/10%, focus 80%/90% lightness/chroma) follow; keyframe selectors can also be named ranges (entry 0% / entry 100% / exit 0% / exit 100%).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Pure CSS scroll-driven animations — `animation-timeline: scroll() / view()`, named view timelines, `@property`. Zero JS. Everything gated behind `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` + `@supports (animation-timeline: scroll())`, with the static end-state as the no-support fallback (fill `both`). Chromium-only at publication (Jan 2024); the deep read notes Firefox shipped SDA in 2025 (Inferred — verify before relying). No-@property fallback hue: 275. SDA has no pinning — keep GSAP for anything that needs a pin.
- **Best for:** Scroll progress indicators, hue-cycle accents (~6 lines, no JS, no ScrollTrigger) and the named-timeline carousel chrome. Drops into an Elementor Custom CSS field or HTML widget unchanged.
- **Deep read:** reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md (entry 271). **Code:** none in packs.

## [BANK] Building a Scrollable and Draggable Timeline with GSAP (Codrops, Michelle Barker) — deep-read (reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md, all four packs)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2022/01/03/building-a-scrollable-and-draggable-timeline-with-gsap/ · final pen https://codepen.io/michellebarker/pen/QWqdqZV
- **How it looks:** A fixed top nav holds an over-wide track of year links (nav height 6 rem, a fixed 1 rem marker dot at top 1.75 rem / left 4 rem) that slides sideways as you scroll the page — and you can also grab the track and throw it with inertia; both inputs stay in perfect sync because drag offsets are converted back into page scroll positions. Below, full-height sections — each tinted by its index, `hsl(calc(var(--i) × 30) 75% 50%)` — reveal with an elastic image swing and a rising heading; a second per-section timeline lights the nav link (`is-active`) for the section in view, and keyboard Tab navigation scrolls to the focused link's section (these two from the pen, labelled Seen in the source).
- **Frame by frame:** Page scroll → the master timeline's single tween moves the track x → −getDraggableWidth() with ease 'none' (mandatory — any easing desyncs the drag↔scroll mapping), bound by ScrollTrigger.create({ animation, scrub: 0 }) across the full page scroll; getDraggableWidth() = track.offsetWidth × 0.5 − lastItemWidth (the 0.5 exists because the track's right padding ≈ 100% of its content width) → drag: Draggable type 'x', inertia true, bounds { minX: 0, maxX: −width }, edgeResistance 1; onDragStart disables the ScrollTrigger, onDragEnd re-enables it; every drag/throw update maps the track's pixel offset back — `y = gsap.utils.mapRange(0, width, 0, docHeight − innerHeight, −trackLeft)` — and calls `st.scroll(y)` → section enters (ScrollTrigger start 'top center', end '+=' + window.innerHeight, toggleActions 'play reverse play reverse'): image from opacity 0 / rotateY 15 to opacity 1 / rotateY −5 (deliberate overshoot past 0) over 6 s ease 'elastic'; heading from y 50 to 0 over 2 s at position 0.5.
- **Mechanism & key values:** GSAP + ScrollTrigger + Draggable + InertiaPlugin (Club plugin — the licensing fact matters: a free rebuild substitutes Draggable with inertia: false + a manual throw from onDragEnd velocity, or keeps the native-scroll-only half, which needs no Club plugins). Track sizing: min-width max(200rem, 200%), padding 1.5rem max(100rem, 100%) 0 0; links min-width 8 rem; marker z-index 2000, translate3d(−50%, 0, 0). Reduced motion: a matchMedia early-return guards the SECTION animations — the drag/scroll sync itself is NOT guarded (a gap worth fixing in rebuilds). Evidence limits from the source: the article's closing "Navigating on click" tail was not read in the deep-read session — click navigation beyond "native anchors" is unverified there; the pen itself was not separately opened (article + search excerpt carry the full JS).
- **Best for:** Timeline/history sections for established firms (years-in-business stories) and any scrubbed timeline that should also be draggable — the bidirectional sync (drag → mapRange → st.scroll) is the transferable mechanism: one source of truth (scroll position), two input modes. In WordPress/Elementor this is a page-level build (the fixed nav conflicts with theme headers — plan on a canvas template).
- **Deep read:** reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md (entry 275). **Code:** none in packs.

## [BANK] Blur Text (React Bits) — deep-read (reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md, all four packs)
- **Reference source:** https://reactbits.dev/text-animations/blur-text · source: registry https://reactbits.dev/r/BlurText-JS-CSS
- **How it looks:** A headline whose words (or letters) arrive through fog: each piece starts blurred at 10 px, invisible and dropped 50 px, passes a half-sharp midpoint where it overshoots slightly downward, then lands crisp — the vertical motion feels springy while the blur and opacity run on a plain linear clock. Other presets: zoom (pieces scale from 1.4, settle through 0.97), tilt (pieces rotate in from 55° in 3D to flat), focus, and drift (pieces slide in with a 28° skew). Hovering can dim the sibling words while one stays sharp.
- **Frame by frame:** Default 'blur' preset, per piece: keyframes at times [0, 0.5, 1] — from { filter: blur(10px), opacity: 0, y: −50 } → step { blur(5px), opacity: 0.5, y: +5 } → rest { blur(0), opacity: 1, y: 0 }; filter/opacity run as a plain tween (ease 'linear') over totalDuration = stepDuration 0.35 × 2 steps = 0.7 s, while the transform keys are peeled off into a spring (visualDuration = 0.35 s, bounce 0.35) — the hybrid is what makes it feel soft-but-snappy → pieces stagger by delay 200 ms in a computed order (start / end / center / deterministic-random via an FNV-1a hash of the text — same text, same order every render) → trigger: IntersectionObserver at threshold 0.1 ('view' default) → exit snapshot { blur(10px), opacity: 0, y: +30 } over 0.455 s with exit stagger 0.4 × stagger and ease EASE_IN [0.55, 0, 0.9, 0.45]; optional loop (loopDelay 2 s); focus-on-hover dims siblings to blur clamp(blur × 0.3, 2, 6) px / opacity 0.3 over 0.45 s cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1). Other presets (measured): zoom — from blur ×1.2, scale 1.4, offset 0.35d; mid blur ×0.2, opacity .9, scale 0.97, overshoot −0.03d; times [0, .6, 1]; bounce 0.25. tilt — rotate 55° (rotateX/Y by axis, transformPerspective 600), mid −8°, times [0, .6, 1], bounce 0.3, settle 0.8, origin pinned to the entry edge. focus — from blur ×1.4, opacity 0.32, scale 1.12, mid at time 0.72, NO spring (pure tween), EASE_IN_OUT [0.65, 0, 0.35, 1]. drift — from x offset 1.6d, skewX 28°, mid overshoot −0.06d / −7°, times [0, .62, 1], bounce 0.3. Defaults: delay 200, blur 10, distance 50, animateBy 'words', direction 'top', staggerFrom 'start', threshold 0.1.
- **Mechanism & key values:** React + `motion` v12 (`motion/react`) — note the current shipped source is substantially richer than the widely-copied 2024 original (which used framer-motion with a simple blur(10px)→0 word stagger); values above are measured from the current registry source (BlurText.jsx, 12,715 B). Letter mode regroups pieces inside per-word inline-flex wrappers so words never break mid-word; spaces become \u00A0 suffixes; an SR-only span carries the full text; MotionConfig reducedMotion="user". Completion clock: inTotal = totalDuration × max(1, settle × 2.2) + maxRank × stagger. Easings: EASE_OUT [0.33, 1, 0.68, 1] · EASE_IN_OUT [0.65, 0, 0.35, 1] · EASE_IN [0.55, 0, 0.9, 0.45].
- **Best for:** Hero and section headline reveals. Vanilla/GSAP transfer of the default look: split words into spans; tween filter + opacity linearly over 0.7 s (blur 10 → 5 → 0, opacity 0 → .5 → 1, keyframe split at 50%) while y runs a springy ease (GSAP back.out(1.4) approximates visualDuration 0.35 / bounce 0.35); stagger 200 ms/word; trigger at 10% visibility, once. For React builds, copy the registry source as-is (MIT + Commons Clause — fine for client sites, not for resale as a library).

## [BANK] Count Up (React Bits) — deep-read (reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md, all four packs)
- **Reference source:** https://reactbits.dev/text-animations/count-up · source: registry https://reactbits.dev/r/CountUp-JS-CSS
- **How it looks:** A stat number that counts up from its start value the first time it scrolls into view, in tabular numerals — or, in roll mode, an odometer: digit columns rolling vertically through 1.2 em windows, right-hand columns starting later, lower-significance places spinning extra turns, and a faint vertical motion blur on any column only while that column is actually moving fast, gone the moment it settles. Thousands separators, decimals, compact K/M/B/T units and prefix/suffix are formatted in; a negative sign fades/slides in roll mode.
- **Frame by frame:** Count mode: a master `animate(0, total)` clock with a LINEAR ease drives a render function that maps elapsed t through the chosen easing curve and writes `formatValue(from + (to − from) × ease(t/total))` directly to the node's textContent (no React re-render per frame); trigger = useInView, once: true, margin '0px' — fires at first pixel intersection, once → roll mode: from/to decompose into per-place digit columns rendered as 4-cell vertical strips (offsets −1..+2) in 1.2 em windows; each column's travel = the mod-10 shortest distance plus whole extra turns (capped at 3 − rank, fewer for higher places); columns stagger 0.07 s each, capped so stagger never eats more than 40% of duration; per-column motion blur via an SVG feGaussianBlur with sigma = min(cell × 0.05, speed × cell / 600), applied only when sigma > 0.2; digit columns and sign/separator marks fade/collapse with smoothstep windows — enter over u ∈ [0, 0.45], leave over [0.55, 1] (marks: [0, 0.3] / [0.7, 1]); roll-mode per-column overshoot = clamp(0.35 / max(1, |delta|), 0.01, 0.12) → under prefers-reduced-motion, the number finishes instantly at the end value.
- **Mechanism & key values:** React + `motion` v12 (animate, cubicBezier, useInView from motion/react); wrapper sets fontVariantNumeric: tabular-nums; an SR-only span carries the final formatted value. Prop defaults: from 0, direction 'up', delay 0, duration 2 s, separator '' (none by default), mode 'count', easing 'easeOut', format 'standard', trigger 'view'; decimals default = max(decimal places of from, to). Easings: easeOut = cubicBezier(0.33, 1, 0.68, 1); expo = normalised 1 − 2^(−10t); linear; and spring = makeSpring(0.06) — an analytic damped-spring easing whose damping ratio ζ is derived from 6% overshoot (ζ = −ln(0.06) / √(π² + ln²(0.06))), damped frequency π / 0.52, plus a cubic residual term so the curve lands EXACTLY on 1 at t = 1. Compact units: 1 decimal under 100 of the unit.
- **Best for:** Stat bands on trade/service sites (review counts, years, project totals). Count mode is a ~20-line vanilla equivalent: IntersectionObserver once → rAF clock 2 s → easeOut cubic-bezier(0.33, 1, 0.68, 1); or reuse makeSpring(0.06) for a spring-settled number with a guaranteed exact landing — the residual-correction trick (add (1 − raw(1)) × t³) forces ANY spring easing to hit exactly 1 at t = 1. Roll mode is worth copying wholesale for hero stats; its blur cap (5% of cell height) and sigma > 0.2 gate keep it cheap. GSAP transfer: tween an object {v: from} with onUpdate formatting.

Single-file rebuild: SVG textPath + duplicated string, CSS animation with duration derived from speed.

## [BANK] 348 · How to Create a Circular Progress Button (2014) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-5.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2014/04/09/how-to-create-a-circular-progress-button/ (concept: Colin Garven; dash technique after Jake Archibald)
- **How it looks:** A wide pill button (250×70px, Montserrat) that, when clicked, shrinks into a circle while an SVG ring draws around it in green; on success the ring completes and a checkmark draws itself in white; on error a cross draws instead.
- **Frame by frame:** Idle pill → hover fill → click: the label fades out (opacity transition 0.15s) → the button morphs to a 70px circle (border-width 5px, border-color #ddd, transparent background) → the ring stroke draws as progress reports → stop(status): success fills border/background #1ECD97 and the checkmark path draws (stroke #fff, stroke-width 4, linecap round, opacity transition 0.1s), error draws the cross → returning to default fades the label back over 0.3s with a 0.1s delay. An elastic variant exists with its own CSS transitions.
- **Mechanism & key values:** CSS + vanilla JS. A `UIProgressButton` class with an SVGEl helper that caches each path and its strokeDasharray/strokeDashoffset length; click adds `loading`, `transitionend` fires the callback, `stop(status)` resolves to success/error and resets the ring. Measured (article code + the deep reader's own direct read): SVG sized 2r + border = 70 → **r = 32.5**, circle cx/cy 35 converted to a path · ring stroke **#1ECD97, stroke-width 5** · final-state transition override: background-color 0.3s, width 0.3s, border-width 0.3s · svg positioned absolute, left 50%, translateX(-50%), pointer-events none; paths opacity 0 / fill none until drawn.
- **Tier:** CROWN — the slice names it "the bank's form-feedback standard for quote forms"; L2 log (chunk 12) KEEP with the same values.
- **Best for:** Quote-form submit buttons — wire the morph + ring + drawn check/cross to the real submit state. Pairs with entry 317's quote form. Mobile / reduced motion not addressed in the article.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-5.md (entry 348). **Code:** none in the packs (full values measured from the article code).

## [BANK] 349 · SVG Filter Effects: Creating Texture with feTurbulence (2019, Sara Soueidan — series part 6) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-5.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2019/02/19/svg-filter-effects-creating-texture-with-feturbulence/
- **How it looks:** Surfaces gain real texture: rough paper grain lit from an angle, wavy liquid distortion across text and images, and a button whose edges boil with noise when clicked.
- **Frame by frame:** Most recipes are static filters. Two animate: a displacement demo whose horizontal-noise baseFrequency is animated **0.01 0.4 → 0 0.2**; and an animated button recreation — on click, GSAP tweens baseFrequency from "0 0.000001" to **0 0.2** and back, warping the button through an feDisplacementMap. The squiggly-text technique cycles several filter copies via @keyframes swapping filter:url().
- **Mechanism & key values:** feTurbulence generates Perlin noise filling the filter region, then the noise is (a) used raw as texture, (b) lit via feDiffuseLighting/feSpecularLighting (the alpha channel acts as a bump map; surfaceScale is the z-multiplier; light sources feDistantLight / fePointLight / feSpotLight), or (c) fed as in2 to feDisplacementMap to distort the SourceGraphic. Measured (article code + the deep reader's own direct read): the 5 attributes — type / baseFrequency / numOctaves / seed / stitchTiles · baseFrequency **0.001 = large patterns, 0.5+ = small**; the article's useful working range is **0.02–0.2** · type 'turbulence' (ripples/liquid) vs 'fractalNoise' (cloudy/smooth) · numOctaves default 1, past ~5 the extra detail is practically unnoticeable · stitchTiles default 'noStitch'. **Rough-paper recipe:** feTurbulence fractalNoise, baseFrequency **0.04**, numOctaves **5** → feDiffuseLighting (lighting-color white, **surfaceScale 2**, feDistantLight **azimuth 45, elevation 60**). Displacement demo: filter region 0%/100%; feDisplacementMap scale is the distortion intensity (a large value in the demo). Animated button: baseFrequency **"0 0.000001"**, numOctaves **2** → feDisplacementMap in SourceGraphic, scale ~30 (value truncated in the readable view — flagged, not asserted). Applied via CSS `filter:url(#noise)`; inline SVG defs needed (Elementor has no filter-primitive controls — HTML block). Demo noted working in Chrome/Firefox, buggy in Safari but degrading to a normal element.
- **Tier:** STRONG — L2 log (chunk 12) KEEP, recording the same working range and the mobile warning below.
- **Best for:** Paper/grain texture overlays, distorted display text, texture on hero panels. Caution from the sources: the squiggly-text variant is resource-intensive — the L2 ruling is avoid on mobile; reduced motion not addressed.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-5.md (entry 349). **Code:** none in the packs (recipes measured verbatim from the article code).

## [BANK] 351 · SVG Filter Effects: Poster Image Effect with feComponentTransfer (2019, Soueidan — series part 3) — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-5.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2019/01/29/svg-filter-effects-poster-image-effect-with-fecomponenttransfer/
- **How it looks:** A photograph flattened into a screen-print poster — each colour channel quantised into five stepped levels, with blacks lifted so the shadows stay open rather than crushing to pure black.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion; the filter applies instantly.
- **Mechanism & key values:** feComponentTransfer remaps each channel independently via feFuncR/G/B/A; function types: identity | table | discrete | linear (slope/intercept) | gamma. `discrete` divides [0,1] into n equal ranges mapped to the n tableValues — that quantisation IS the posterize. Measured verbatim from the article code: demo SVG 500×335 · posterize: feFuncR/G/B each type **"discrete"** with tableValues **".25 .4 .5 .75 1"** (5 levels per channel, floor 0.25) · alpha demo: feFuncA type "table" tableValues **"0 0.5"** → flat 0.5 opacity. Worked example in the article: 3 values [0, 0.5, 1] map ranges [0,0.33]→0, [0.33,0.66]→0.5, [0.66,1]→1. Rebuild: inline SVG, filter id "posterize", the discrete values above on R/G/B; Elementor: HTML block. The article's CodePen demos were embedded but not readable in the browser view — the values here are from the article code itself.
- **Tier:** STRONG — L2 log (chunk 12) KEEP, recording the same tableValues.
- **Best for:** Duotone/poster treatments of project photos, before/after panels, texture passes. Mobile / reduced motion not addressed (static effect).
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-5.md (entry 351). **Code:** none in the packs.

## [BANK] 352 · SVG Filters 101 — Codrops (Sara Soueidan) — deep-read (hvac/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-6.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2019/01/15/svg-filters-101/
- **How it looks:** Not a page design — the visual output is filtered imagery: a soft coloured drop shadow sitting under any graphic, built entirely from SVG filter primitives rather than CSS box-shadow. The shadow can be offset, tinted and halved in opacity while the original graphic stays crisp on top.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. The "sequence" is the primitive chain: blur the alpha silhouette → flood with colour → clip the colour inside the blur → halve its alpha → merge it under the original.
- **Mechanism & key values:** SVG filter primitives chained by named `result`s. The bank's drop-shadow recipe (Measured, verbatim from the article): filter region `x="-10%" y="-10%" width="120%" height="120%"`; `feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="10" result="DROP"`; `feFlood flood-color="#000"`; `feComposite operator="in"` (DROP × COLOR = SHADOW1); `feComponentTransfer` with `feFuncA type="table" tableValues="0 0.5"` to halve alpha; `feMerge` shadow first, SourceGraphic second (order = paint order). Variant: `feOffset dx="20" dy="20"` before compositing; alpha can also be scaled via `feColorMatrix` row 4. Article's convention: name results in CAPS.
- **Tier:** STRONG — the SVG-library foundation entry; the recipe is quoted verbatim and library-ready.
- **Best for:** Custom shadows under badges, cards, stickers and SVG artwork anywhere; the base knowledge for every other SVG-filter effect in the bank.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/hvac/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-6.md (entry 352). **Code:** none (no separate demo file — the article itself, 109 code blocks read in full, is the source).

Call config: `{ paused: false, speed: 2, draggable: true, center: true, repeat: -1, paddingRight: 150, onChange }`. `pixelsPerSecond = speed × 100` → speed 2 = 200 px/s; two tweens per item on one timeline with `ease: "none"`; `gsap.utils.snap(config.snap || 1)`; API: `next()`, `previous()`, `toIndex(i)` (shortest wrap direction), `current()`, `closestIndex()`. Reduced-motion: 0 occurrences (2012) — wrap in a no-preference media query when reusing.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — small utility recipes, not page designs; the mismatched-period trick is the durable idea.

## [BANK] 364 · CSS-Only Marquee Effect — Codrops — deep-read (hvac/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-6.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2020/03/31/css-only-marquee-effect/ (live demo: tympanus.net/Development/CSSMarqueeMenu/)
- **How it looks:** In the demo, a menu where hovering an item starts a giant (10vw type) marquee scrolling behind it. The mechanism is general: a track of repeated content sliding sideways in a perfect loop, with a word already partially visible at rest instead of an empty gap. A film-grain overlay textures the page.
- **Frame by frame:** At rest the track sits paused and (in the demo) transparent, offset so a word peeks in → on hover of the menu item the track fades in over 0.4s and the marquee starts, translating from −25%+offset to −50%+offset of the track width — exactly one copy-width — then wraps seamlessly, linear, forever → hover off and it pauses/fades back.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Pure CSS, variables drive everything (Measured from base.css): `--marquee-width: 100vw; --offset: 20vw; --move-initial: calc(-25% + var(--offset)); --move-final: calc(-50% + var(--offset)); --item-font-size: 10vw`. Track holds 4 copies; loop distance = 25% of track (one copy); `.marquee__inner { width: fit-content; display: flex; animation: marquee 5s linear infinite; animation-play-state: paused; }`, started by `.menu__item-link:hover ~ .marquee .marquee__inner { animation-play-state: running; opacity: 1; transition-duration: 0.4s; }`. The 20vw offset is the subtle part: starting at −25%+20vw keeps a word partially visible at rest. Grain: `@keyframes grain 8s steps(10) infinite`. General recipe: track = N identical copies, start at minus one copy, end at minus two copies, linear infinite; duration by eye (5s at 10vw font is fast — a logo strip wants 20–40s, cf. entry 374). Reduced-motion: 0 occurrences — an always-on marquee must ship with a pause when reused.
- **Tier:** STRONG — the bank's CSS-only marquee reference; zero JS, fully portable.
- **Best for:** Logo strips, review tickers, big-word section dividers; hover-gated background marquees behind menus or lists.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/hvac/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-6.md (entry 364). **Code:** the live Codrops demo directory above (no pack code-source slug named in the entry).

## [BANK] 372 · Glare Hover — React Bits — deep-read (hvac/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-6.md)
- **Reference source:** https://reactbits.dev/animations/glare-hover (full source: https://reactbits.dev/r/GlareHover-TS-TW.json)
- **How it looks:** A card or button with a soft diagonal sheen of light across it: a hot bright core with a wide faint skirt (or two streaks, or a broad sheen, depending on variant) that sweeps across on hover — with a quick flash along the card's rim as it passes. Modes let it follow the pointer, loop on its own every few seconds, or fire on click.
- **Frame by frame:** Hover (default mode) → the pre-generated gradient layer rotates/slides into its swept position over 650ms → the rim-glint mask flashes the edges as the streak crosses → on leave it sweeps back. In `loop` mode the sweep repeats every `interval` (default 3s); `follow` tracks the pointer continuously; an optional intro plays once on mount.
- **Mechanism & key values:** No canvas, no gradient-tracking divs (Measured from the full component source, 11,287 chars TSX — this supersedes the Level 2 props-table record). The glare is a 33-stop linear-gradient generated from an analytic brightness profile: easing kernel `smootherstep(t) = t³(t(6t−15)+10)`; `bump(t, center, half) = smootherstep(1 − |t−center|/half)` inside the half-width. Profiles: streak = `bump(t,.5,.06+.16·softness) + 0.32·bump(t,.5,.5)`; twin = bumps at .36 and .70 (weights 1 / .85) + .26 skirt; sheen = `.55·bump(t,.5,.25+.25·softness) + .3` skirt. Stops sampled at `index/32`, emitted as `color-mix(in srgb, <color> <alpha>%, transparent)` — one static gradient layer whose position/rotation animates (650ms transition), not a per-frame repaint. Defaults: `glareColor '#ffffff'`, `glareOpacity 0.5`, `glareAngle -45`, `glareSize 30`, `softness 0.6`, `variant 'streak'`, `mode 'hover'`, `blendMode 'screen'`, `rimGlint true`, `transitionDuration 650`, `interval 3`, `borderRadius '10px'`. Reduced-motion: implemented in source via `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` — one of only two entries in this slice with it in the actual code. Vanilla translation (bank's): precompute the same 33-stop gradient in CSS (softness .6 → core half-width .156), rotate −45°, blend screen, sweep background-position on hover over .65s.
- **Tier:** STRONG — complete analytic recipe; the profile math is all a single-file build needs.
- **Best for:** Card/button hover sheen — pricing cards, service cards, CTA buttons, before/after tiles.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/hvac/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-6.md (entry 372). **Code:** the React Bits registry source above (no pack code-source slug named in the entry).

- **Reference source:** https://reactbits.dev/animations/logo-loop (full source: https://reactbits.dev/r/LogoLoop-TS-TW.json)
- **How it looks:** A logo strip that glides sideways at a perfectly constant speed, fading out at both edges, pausing when hovered. It can also bend — logos following a wave, an arc or an orbit instead of a straight line — be dragged and flung, magnify under the pointer like a lens, or advance one logo at a time in steps.
- **Frame by frame:** On load an intro plays (0.7s, staggered 0.45) → the strip translates at constant px/s, offset wrapping modulo one copy width so the seam never shows → hover eases the speed to 0 (velocity approaches smoothly, it doesn't stop dead) → a drag grabs the strip; on release it flings (capped at 4000 px/s) and glides back to base speed → in step mode it holds, eases one item forward, holds again.

Defaults: `speed 120` (px/s), `direction 'left'`, `logoHeight 28`, `gap 32`, `fadeOutWidth 0.12` (fraction of width, each edge), `pauseOnHover` (via `hoverSpeed`), `layout 'line'` (line|wave|arc|orbit), `draggable` on, `intro` on. (Level 2's Customize-panel values — speed 100, height 48, gap 56 — are the site's demo settings, not defaults.) Engine constants: velocity smoothing `SMOOTH_TAU 0.25`, glide `GLIDE_TAU 0.8` (exponential approach `v += (target−v)(1−e^(−dt/τ))`), `DRAG_THRESHOLD 6`px, `MAX_FLING 4000` px/s, `INTRO_TIME 0.7`s, `INTRO_STAGGER 0.45`; magnify lens eases τ 0.12 in / 0.25 out, pointer tracking τ 0.06. Reduced-motion: implemented — `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` disables step/magnify behaviour. Bank use: as a React component it's a dependency; the transferable pattern is duplicate-the-strip + constant px/s + wrap modulo one copy + fade outer 12% at both edges + pause on hover; the τ-smoothing numbers (0.25s velocity approach, 0.8s post-fling glide) are the upgrade worth stealing for drag-enabled strips.
- **Tier:** STRONG — the engineered end of the marquee family (cf. CSS-only 364, Swiper ticker 413 in this slice).
- **Best for:** Logo/brand strips and review tickers on trade sites; draggable galleries where the fling feel matters.

Below: a brands row of 17 logos with its own Pause button, 4 featured case films, a 4-step Approach, an All-work gallery with a GRID / INDEX toggle, career chapters, and a footer with Reduce motion and Sound toggles.
- **Frame by frame:** The conversation state changes → the orb's shader uniforms tween to the named preset for that state (ripple speed, intensity, wave frequency, glow, rotation and pulse all retarget together) → the orb settles into the new behaviour and keeps animating there. Page motion runs on an expo-like bezier; the brands row scrolls until the visitor presses its Pause button.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Custom WebGL shader with uniforms `uRippleSpeed, uRippleIntensity, uWaveFreq, uGlow, uRotation, uPulse` and named state presets (Measured from the main bundle): **listening** {rippleSpeed 3.5, rippleIntensity 1.3, waveFreq 7, glow 1.1, rotation .2, pulse .3}; **processing** {1.2 / intensity in the same band / waveFreq 10, glow 1.4, rotation .8, pulse 1}; **speaking** {3 / 1.8 / 6 / 1.7 / .45 / 1.2}; a fourth set {waveFreq 3, glow .8, rotation .25, pulse .5} (the default-ish state's first value was cut in the minified source — recorded as such in the bank). The mechanism to bank: one shader, N named uniform presets, tween between presets on state change. CSS layer (Measured): beziers `cubic-bezier(.76,0,.24,1)` ×2, `(.2,.7,.2,1)`, `(.16,1,.3,1)`; keyframes `ask-in, ask-bar, ask-pulse, nether-rise, link-sweep, consent-in`; font Söhne; `prefers-reduced-motion` ×2 in CSS plus the visible Reduce motion button.
- **Tier:** STRONG — the shader-preset state machine, the pauseable logo row and user-controlled motion are all directly copyable patterns.
- **Best for:** GRID / INDEX toggle for project galleries; pause controls on moving strips; a hero that needs modes (e.g. emergency vs planned-service states).

- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2018/02/21/animated-fragment-slideshow/ (live demo: tympanus.net/Tutorials/PiecesSlider/)
- **How it looks:** A full-screen slideshow where each slide — photo, a coloured text block and a big number — shatters into dozens of angled strips that scatter across the screen and then reassemble into the next slide. The slide numbers keep slowly rotating forever while idle.

- **Mechanism & key values:** Pieces.js (canvas fragmentation) + anime.js (Measured from demo.js, pieces.min.js, anime.min.js). Per-layer config: **Image** `angle: 45`, `extraSpacing {extraX:100, extraY:200}`, `piecesWidth: () => random(50,200)`, `ty: () => random(-400,400)`. **Text** colour white on `backgroundColor '#5104ab'`, `fontSize: width>720 ? 50 : 30`, `padding '15 20 10 20'`, `angle: -45`, `piecesSpacing: 2`, `extraSpacing {0, 300}`, translate by breakpoint: >1120px {200,200}, >720 {0,200}, else {0,100}. **Number** `fontSize: >720 ? 60 : 20`, `angle: 0`, `piecesWidth: 35`, translate >1120 {−340,−180}, >720 {−240,−180}, else {−140,−100}. Global: `piecesSpacing: 1`, `animation: { duration: () => random(1000, 2000), easing: 'easeOutQuint' }`, canvas 100vw×100vh, image max-width shrinks at ≤720px. Reduced-motion: 0 occurrences (2018).
- **Tier:** STRONG — a complete, exact recipe; heavy for a whole page, perfect for one hero.
- **Best for:** Hero/gallery transitions for before→after sliders: split into random 50–200px strips at ±45°, scatter ty ±400, reassemble with easeOutQuint over a randomised 1–2s.

## [BANK] 406 · Dot Navigation Styles — Codrops — deep-read (hvac/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-6.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2014/01/21/dot-navigation-styles/ (live demo: tympanus.net/Development/DotNavigationStyles/)
- **How it looks:** A row of small dots (16px, 18px for one style) marking position in a slideshow or page — with ~10 personalities: one fills up from the bottom inside its ring, one draws its own circle outline, one scales up, one hops, one flips, one grows a tooltip. The current dot is unmistakable in every style.
- **Frame by frame:** Click a dot (dots.js only moves the `.current` class; everything else is CSS) → the newly-current dot animates over 0.3s ease: FillUp's inner `::after` circle grows height 0→100% inside an inset box-shadow ring; DrawCircle's inline SVG ring strokes itself in (`stroke-dashoffset 39→0`); the others scale, stroke, flip or grow per their recipe → the previous dot reverses. Link text is `text-indent: -999em` — visually hidden but retained for screen readers, so dots are never empty anchors.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Pure CSS transitions + inline SVG, zero framework (Measured from component.css 12.7K + dots.js). One timing rules the whole set: `0.3s ease` on box-shadow, opacity, transform, background, height. DrawCircle: `stroke-dasharray 39 39` (≈ 2πr for r≈6.2), `stroke-dashoffset 39→0` over 0.3s, stroke-width 3, round line-caps. Reduced-motion: 0 occurrences (2014). Bank's trade note: 16px is small for thumbs — scale to ≥24px tap targets on phone layouts.
- **Tier:** STRONG — drops straight into an Elementor HTML widget or single-file build with no dependencies.
- **Best for:** Section/slide dot navigation for galleries, testimonial sliders and multi-step forms.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/hvac/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-6.md (entry 406). **Code:** the live Codrops demo above (component.css + dots.js fetched and mined; no pack code-source slug named in the entry).

## [BANK] 407 · Infinite Tubes with Three.js — Codrops — deep-read (hvac/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-6.md)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2017/05/09/infinite-tubes-with-three-js/ (live demo 1: tympanus.net/Development/InfiniteTubes/)
- **How it looks:** You fly endlessly through a textured stone tube (six variants exist: brick tunnel, low-poly particles, hyperspace, blood vessel, triangular tube, device-orientation). The tunnel rushes past continuously and flexes gently toward your cursor — the walls bend instead of the camera jumping — while the camera rolls and drifts slightly with the mouse.
- **Frame by frame:** Every frame the texture offset advances (`map.offset.x += 0.02`) so the world appears to rush past while no geometry moves → the mouse (normalised −1…1) lerps by /30 per frame toward its target → the spline's control points shift by mouse × 0.1, the curve is rebuilt, and every tube vertex lerps /10 per frame toward its bent position — the tube visibly flexes rather than snapping → camera: `rotation.z = mouse.x·0.2`, `rotation.y = π − mouse.x·0.06`, `position.x = mouse.x·0.015`, `position.y = −mouse.y·0.015`.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Three.js (Measured from demo1.js, read line-by-line). Curve: `CatmullRomCurve3` through 5 points on the Z axis, `points[i] = (0, 0, 2.5·(i/4))`, `points[4].y = -0.06`. Tube: `TubeGeometry(curve, 70 tubular segments, 0.02 radius, 50 radial segments, open)`, `MeshStandardMaterial { side: BackSide, map + bumpMap (stone), bumpScale: 0.0003 }`; lights HemisphereLight(0xffffbb, 0x887979, 0.9) + DirectionalLight(0xffffff, 0.8). (Radius quoted exactly as written in the source.) Travel = texture, not geometry: both maps `RepeatWrapping`, `repeat.set(30, 6)`, offset += 0.02/frame (`this.speed = 0.02`) — the cheapest infinite-travel illusion in the bank, one uniform update per frame. Steering as above (mouse lerp /30, vertex lerp /10, ring index `floor(i/50)`); morph targets always computed from a pristine clone of the original geometry, never accumulated. Mobile: variant 6 uses device orientation (article Stated). Reduced-motion: 0 occurrences.
- **Tier:** STRONG — banked in the 3D library; the texture-offset travel trick and the /30 + /10 smoothing constants are reusable anywhere.
- **Best for:** "Journey" hero backgrounds (a van-route / through-the-pipe visual for a trade hero) at near-zero GPU cost; reusable smoothing constants for any cursor-steered scene.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/hvac/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-6.md (entry 407). **Code:** the live Codrops demo above (demo1.js + three.min.js fetched and read; no pack code-source slug named in the entry).

## [BANK] 421 · MA Studio Speculative Software — FH Potsdam — deep-read (hvac/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-6.md)
- **Reference source:** interface.fh-potsdam.de/ma-speculative-software
- **How it looks:** A university microsite where the whole page reacts to the pointer: elements drift and scale at their own rates as the cursor crosses, elements that shrink toward you sharpen while elements that grow blur, and the key-visual type literally stretches — its variable-font width axis widening and narrowing with cursor position. Hovering one project dims all its siblings. On touch devices the same depth comes from scroll instead: three key-visual lines slide at different speeds and blur at different rates. A scroll progress bar appears only after 600px of scroll.
- **Frame by frame:** Pointer moves → mouse normalises to (−.5…+.5) → per frame each element translates `x = mouseX·tx·100`, `y = mouseY·ty·100` and scales `1 + mouseX·sx + mouseY·sy` via `translate3d(x, y, 0) scale(s)`, with coupled blur `blur = max(0, 10·(1 − scale))` → the smoothed mouse (lerp 0.08/frame) drives the variable font: `wdth = min + (smoothX + 0.5)·(max − min)`, written as `fontVariationSettings: "wght" 100, "wdth" <wdth>` in the key-visual lines (`"wght" 70` elsewhere) — the 0.08 lerp makes it feel liquid rather than tracked → hover a `.project` → siblings get `--unfocused`, it gets `--focused` → scroll past 600px → the progress bar appears, width = scroll fraction ×100%. Touch gate: the pointer field is desktop-only (`matchMedia("(pointer: coarse)")` blocks it); the scroll parallax runs only when the pointer IS coarse.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Hand-written vanilla JS, no libraries — one 5K script runs the whole interaction system (Measured from application.js, fetched directly after the miner's subpath-resolution fault saved a 404 page as application.js — fault logged in the bank). All parameters live in markup: `data-tx / data-ty` (×53 / ×31 in the HTML) and `data-sx / data-sy` per element; `.vf` elements carry `data-min / data-max` (×40 each; defaults 400/600). Touch scroll parallax: scroll lerped `current += (target − current)·0.1`; three key-visual lines translate at −0.2 / −0.3 / −0.4 × scrollY with blur at 0.02 / 0.01 / 0.005 × scrollY (background blurs at 0.01). Reduced-motion: none in the script — gate the rAF loop when reusing.
- **Tier:** STRONG — called in the bank the most portable cursor system in the slice: no library, per-element factors in the HTML, blur coupled to scale; the variable-font drive is a complete headline-effect recipe for any variable font.
- **Best for:** Cursor-parallax hero fields, variable-font headline effects, dim-the-rest project/student lists, scroll progress bars.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/hvac/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-6.md (entry 421). **Code:** none named (application.js fetched directly from the site; no pack code-source slug recorded in the entry).

## [BANK] 492 · Patio — deep-read (roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-8.md)
- **Reference source:** https://patio.so
- **How it looks:** A Next.js product site with frosted panels (backdrop-filter ×5) and a Dashboard/Storefront tab pair as product proof (Seen at Level 2). Reveals fade/slide in and out on a single enter/exit keyframe pair as sections cross the viewport — everything on the classic three-curve material easing system, nothing else. Its standout is invisible: reduced-motion handling is systematic, a single token layer referenced everywhere rather than one-off rules.
- **Frame by frame:** An element crosses an IntersectionObserver threshold → the `enter` keyframes run with `cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1)` → it settles; on exit the `exit` keyframes reverse the feel with the decelerate/accelerate pair. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the token layer suppresses the motion site-wide.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Next.js, no GSAP/ScrollTrigger at all — motion is CSS + observer-driven (Measured from the full 1.8M JS / 68K CSS same-host capture). IntersectionObserver ×12, rAF ×13. CSS holds exactly 2 @keyframes (enter, exit); beziers: `cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1)` ×3 (material standard), `(0,0,.2,1)` ×2 (decelerate), `(.4,0,1,1)` ×2 (accelerate). Fonts: Doto + EB Garamond + Inter. Reduced-motion: JS ×29, HTML(inline) ×108 — the strongest reduced-motion implementation in this slice (Measured counts). Limits: IO threshold values not extractable from the minified bundle; durations in the bundle are component-internal (the 9/8/11/12 hits are not tween durations — do not bank them).
- **Tier:** STRONG — the reduced-motion token-layer pattern is the copyable system; the slice's RM runner-up benchmark (after 538).
- **Best for:** Any build that needs a disciplined reduced-motion layer; IO-reveal sites that want one easing system and no animation library.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-8.md (entry 492). **Code:** code-source/patio/

Observer vocabulary: thresholds 0 / .1 / .5; rootMargins "5%", "50px", "200px", "30% 30% 30% 30%", "100% 100% 100% 100%". CSS variables: `--scroll-state-duration: .6s`, `--scroll-state-easing: cubic-bezier(.41,.19,.13,.95)`; `--fade-out-duration: .52s` / `cubic-bezier(.25,.46,.45,.94)`; slide chain `--slide-duration: .6s`, `--slide-easing: cubic-bezier(.72,.16,.19,.96)` (slide keyframe starts at translateX(-898px)); lines `--lines-duration: 3s` / loading variant 6s. Overshoot signature `cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1)` (×5; cloud-card transform .4s). 14 @keyframes total (emoji-rise, orbit-path, stagger-fade-in, media-entrance, nav-item-in — 1s `cubic-bezier(.13,.46,.15,.92)` from translateY(-100%), timeline-start, line-fade 4s, opacityPulse 2s infinite, search-loading-rotate 3s linear + stroke 1.5s). 9 `prefers-reduced-motion` blocks — the most complete reduced-motion implementation in its slice (kills orbital animation, view transitions, flattens modals).
