## [BANK] fancy-svg-letter-animation — code-source demo (roofing pack: animation/code-source/fancy-svg-letter-animation/; also in remodeling)
- **Reference source:** http://tympanus.net/Development/FancyLetterAnimation/ (Codrops "Fancy SVG Letter Animation"; MANIFEST records the article: https://tympanus.net/codrops/2016/09/13/fancy-svg-letter-animation/)
- **How it looks:** A single word set as huge hand-drawn lettering (SVG viewBox 0 0 320 180, container min-height 400px / max 70vh). Each letter is drawn three times in stacked stroke layers of slightly different widths and colours, so as the strokes draw themselves on, the thinner coloured under-layers peek out at the edges as fringes. Four effect variants ship in the CSS (different width stacks and palettes — 165 `letter__layer` paths in the demo page). A replay button fades the word out and runs it again.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger (load, or click to replay): existing letters drop 15px and fade out in 250ms → each letter rises from −30px with an elastic settle (900ms) while fading in (500ms), letters staggered 40ms apart → simultaneously each letter's stroke layers draw on via stroke-dashoffset (800ms easeOutQuint, delay = pathIndex × 200ms + letterIndex × 40ms) → at the end, the non-final layers fade out over 200ms so only the top stroke remains crisp.
- **Mechanism & key values:** anime.js (v1-era API) + hand-drawn single-stroke SVG paths, no GSAP. Each path's dasharray/dashoffset is set from `getTotalLength()` in JS — the free equivalent of DrawSVG. Layer geometry (Effect 1): stroke widths 9 / 9.5 / 10px, `stroke-linecap: butt`, linejoin bevel, miterlimit 3, fill none; palette #dea521, #f84242, #3758a7, #f79c8c, #84b5bd, #feefde. Entrance: translateY [−30, 0], 900ms easeOutElastic, elasticity 600; opacity 500ms linear. Draw: 800ms easeOutQuint. Exit: translateY [0, 15], opacity [1, 0], 250ms easeInOutQuad. Variant stacks in the shipped CSS: effect-2 = 1/4/10px; effect-3 = 10/6/8px; effect-4 = 10px #00966c / 4px #27272d / 1px #fcec9b (reverse taper — thin bright core on a thick dark body). Capture note: main.js (5,715 B) and component.css in the folder are verified real files (hand-refetched after the bank's first pass hit 404 stubs).
- **Tier:** STRONG — trade-fit basis: a complete, font-independent wordmark recipe with every parameter measured from the shipped source.
- **Best for:** Hero wordmarks and section-title lettering — a trade name or one big word that draws itself on. Trade fit: strong for a hero or a divider moment; it needs the word traced as single-stroke paths (or a single-line font converted to paths).
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md (entry 258). **Code:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/animation/code-source/fancy-svg-letter-animation/

## [BANK] scrolltrigger-horizontal-pagination — code-source demo (roofing pack: animation/code-source/scrolltrigger-horizontal-pagination/; also in remodeling, siding-windows-doors)
- **Reference source:** https://codepen.io/akapowl/embed/preview/qBXqKZM/ba638948806ca4adca9dae41178f29c1?&default-tabs=html%2Cresult (pen by Paul Slawik / akapowl, forked from a Cotton Ltd pen)
- **How it looks:** A deep-green (#2d4026) gallery section holding five large captioned images ("Bedroom 1", "Bedroom 2", …) that travel sideways as you scroll, with a fixed row of five numbered dots (50×50px circles, white outline) floating at bottom centre. The dot for the panel currently centred is a square; the rest are circles. Capture state: full — the capture is the CodePen embed page, which contains the pen's complete HTML/SCSS/JS panels verbatim (values-raw.txt is an empty mine because the embed page has no linked bundles; the source is in index.html itself).
- **Frame by frame:** The section pins → vertical scroll drives the strip's x from 0 to −(scrollWidth − viewport width), scrubbed 1:1 with ease "none" → each panel crossing the centre flips its dot from circle (border-radius 50px) to square (border-radius 0) via toggleClass, and back as it leaves → the pin releases and normal vertical scroll resumes. Dots are pure indicators — no snap, no click navigation.
- **Mechanism & key values:** GSAP 3 + ScrollTrigger. The layout trick: `.carousel_wrapper { display:flex; flex-direction:column; flex-wrap:wrap; height:80vh }` — five `.image_item` children at height 100% wrap into successive columns, manufacturing a horizontal strip with no horizontal-flow CSS. Panels: padding 2rem 0; inner image wrapper 60vw × 60vh centred. Main tween: `x: () => -(container.scrollWidth - document.documentElement.clientWidth) + "px"`, ease "none", ScrollTrigger { trigger: container, scrub: true, pin: true, pinSpacing: true, invalidateOnRefresh: true, end: () => "+=" + container.offsetWidth }. Per-panel dummy tweens use `containerAnimation` with start "left center" / end "right center" and toggleClass on `.dot[data-panel="<id>"]`. Dots: fixed, bottom 5rem, 50×50px, border 1px solid #fff. **Defect flagged in the deep read (measured):** `end` uses offsetWidth (≈ one panel) while actual travel is ≈ four panels, so the pin releases after ~¼ of the implied distance and the horizontal motion runs ~4× faster than page scroll — a rebuild should set `end: () => "+=" + (container.scrollWidth - document.documentElement.clientWidth)`.
- **Tier:** STRONG — trade-fit basis: two portable steals (column-wrap strip; circle→square pagination) with one recorded defect to fix on rebuild.
- **Best for:** Work/gallery sections — a pinned horizontal run of project panels with numbered pagination. Trade fit: strong for before/after or project galleries; apply the `end` fix so travel matches scroll 1:1.

## [BANK] count-up-reactbits — code-source demo (roofing pack: animation/code-source/count-up-reactbits/; in all four packs)
- **Reference source:** https://reactbits.dev/text-animations/count-up
- **How it looks:** A number that counts up when it scrolls into view — e.g. a stat in a proof band ticking from 0 to its final value with tabular, non-jittering digits. In its second mode it is an odometer: each digit is a rolling column (slot-machine style) with a visible motion blur while the column spins fast, columns settling right-to-left into the final number, with thousands separators, decimals, K/M/B/T compact units and prefix/suffix (a $, a +, a %) all supported. Capture is full and includes the actual component source: CountUp.jsx (15,407 B) + the React Bits registry JSON.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger = first pixel in view (motion `useInView`, once, margin 0px) or on load → count mode: a linear master clock maps elapsed time through the chosen easing and writes the formatted value straight to the DOM each frame (no React re-render) → roll mode: each digit column rolls through its computed travel (shortest mod-10 distance plus up to 3 extra full turns, fewer for higher places), columns staggered (0.07s, capped so stagger never exceeds 40% of duration), blur σ rising with column speed and clearing as it settles, entering/leaving digit columns and sign/separator marks fading and collapsing width in smoothstep windows → ends exactly on the final formatted value; the final value also sits in a screen-reader-only span from the start. `prefers-reduced-motion` finishes instantly.
- **Mechanism & key values:** React + motion v12 (`animate`, `cubicBezier`, `useInView` from motion/react). Defaults (measured from CountUp.jsx): from 0, duration 2s, delay 0, easing 'easeOut' = cubicBezier(0.33, 1, 0.68, 1); 'expo' = normalised 1 − 2^(−10t); 'spring' = an analytic damped spring built from 6% overshoot (ζ = −ln(0.06) / √(π² + ln²(0.06)), damped frequency π / 0.52, plus a cubic residual so it lands exactly on 1). Roll internals: CELL = 1.2em slot height; STAGGER = 0.07s; strips render 4 cells (offsets −1..+2) inside overflow-hidden slots; blur σ = min(cell × 0.05, speed × cell / 600), applied only when σ > 0.2 via an SVG feGaussianBlur (vertical only); enter window u ∈ [0, 0.45], leave [0.55, 1]; per-column spring overshoot clamped 0.01–0.12. Compact format: 1 decimal under 100 of the unit. `fontVariantNumeric: tabular-nums` on the wrapper; optional replayOnHover (roll mode re-spins in place).
- **Tier:** STRONG — trade-fit basis: the bank's complete measured count-up component; proof-band numbers are a standard trade-homepage element.
- **Best for:** Proof/reviews bands and stat strips — years trading, roofs done, review counts, rating numbers. Trade fit: direct; the roll mode is the premium version for a hero stat. In a single-file HTML build the mechanism ports to a small JS tween writing textContent (count mode) — the JSX is the measured reference, not a dependency.

## [BANK] pen-40-direction-reveals — code-source demo (roofing pack: animation/code-source/pen-40-direction-reveals/; in all four packs)
- **Reference source:** None recorded (the bank records only the pen id pojzxwZ — GreenSock on CodePen; the captured page's own canonical link is https://codepen.io/GreenSock/pen/pojzxwZ and its title is "Reveal animations based on scroll direction - ScrollTrigger")
- **How it looks:** A features page: a centred hero heading, then four full-height feature rows alternating left/right — a square photo card (aspect-ratio 1/1, 8px radius) beside a title and a four-line description. Nothing is visible until it is revealed: each block slides in from the side or below and fades up, and — the point — blocks re-enter from the opposite direction when you scroll back up. Capture state: fullpage-only — the folder holds one file, fullpage.html (11,373 B), the CodePen fullpage view whose srcdoc contains the pen's complete CSS + JS, curled and verified by the bank on 26 Oct.
- **Frame by frame:** An element's ScrollTrigger fires onEnter → the element animates from 100px below (or ∓100px from the side for fromLeft/fromRight blocks) and autoAlpha 0 to place over 1.25s on an expo ease → scroll it out and it hides instantly (autoAlpha 0) → scroll back and onEnterBack replays the entrance mirrored (direction −1: from −100px above) → fast direction changes mid-flight retarget cleanly instead of queueing, because the tween uses overwrite "auto".
- **Mechanism & key values:** GSAP + ScrollTrigger; every `.gs_reveal` element starts at opacity 0 / visibility hidden (`will-change: transform, opacity`). `animateFrom(elem, direction)`: y = direction × 100 by default; x = −100 (fromLeft) or +100 (fromRight) with y = 0; `gsap.fromTo(elem, {x, y, autoAlpha: 0}, { duration: 1.25, x: 0, y: 0, autoAlpha: 1, ease: "expo", overwrite: "auto" })`. ScrollTrigger.create per element: onEnter → animateFrom(elem); onEnterBack → animateFrom(elem, −1); onLeave → hide (gsap.set autoAlpha 0). Layout values from the pen CSS: content max-width 1240px, hero 40vh, feature rows 100vh with 3rem gaps, title 1.8em, description line-height 1.6. Deep read's cautions: overwrite:"auto" is the load-bearing detail (without it, scroll reversals stack competing tweens and elements flicker); ±100px travel is too much for small phone sections — halve to ~50px on mobile.
- **Tier:** STRONG — bank's own verdict basis: the deep read names it "the house reveal candidate — direction-aware entrances for every section of trade templates" (L2: Relevance 5 / Fit 5).
- **Best for:** The default entrance for every section of a trade homepage — services, proof, process, towns — one reveal system used consistently. Trade fit: direct and universal; it is a foundation pattern, not a garnish.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-1.md (entry 40). **Code:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/animation/code-source/pen-40-direction-reveals/

## [BANK] 125-square-lens — code-source demo (siding-windows-doors pack: animation/code-source/125-square-lens/)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/Tutorials/PointerSquareLensDistortion (Codrops, Tomoyuki Nakata / baqemono; article: https://tympanus.net/codrops/2026/08/25/building-a-mouse-following-square-lens-effect-with-three-js-and-glsl/)
- **How it looks:** One full-viewport photograph on a dark page (#232121). Outside the lens the image is grayscale and alive — a slow wave wobble and fine noise shimmer run through it. A hard-edged square follows the pointer with a slight lag; inside the square the same photograph appears in full colour, bulged by a lens distortion, with the colour channels split radially (red pushed +0.01, blue −0.01 at the edges). The square's edge is deliberately aliased — a graphic, poster-like cut, not a soft mask. Capture is full: index.html + the real deployed Astro/Three.js bundle (538,912 B; 46 vertex + 46 fragment shaders, 123 uniform declarations in the mine).
- **Frame by frame:** Pointer moves → the eased mouse position lerps ~10% per frame toward it (pointerEase 0.1), so the square trails and settles → inside the square, the image bulges (CC lens scale = 1 + distortion × radius²) and the RGB split grows from 0 at the square's centre to full at its corners → outside, the grayscale image continuously undulates (sin wave on Y) and shimmers (hash-random noise) with time → the square itself never rotates or scales; only its position and the internal warp change.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Three.js + one fullscreen 1×1 plane and a single fragment shader — no render targets, no post-processing. Both textures (colour inside, grayscale outside) are cover-fit independently in GLSL; a square coordinate system (uv × 2 − 1, aspect-corrected, centred on the eased mouse) feeds four step() tests multiplied into a hard mask; colour = mix(outside, inside, mask). Deployed defaults, verified in the bundle: squareSize 0.4 (half-side; the article text says 0.3 — the bundle wins), lensDistortion 1.5, rgbShift R +0.01 / G 0 / B −0.01, pointerEase 0.1. Ambient terms: waveFrequency 10, waveStrength 0.01, waveSpeed 1; randomFrequency 1, randomStrength 0.02, randomSpeed 0.2. GUI ranges in the deep read (squareSize 0–5, distortion −5–5, shifts ±0.05). Phone honesty from the deep read: no touch fallback for lens position (the square would sit at the last mouse position/centre) — add a slow auto-path or deviceorientation on touch, cap DPR at 1.5–2, pause off-screen; no reduced-motion handling in the demo.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — trade-fit basis: a single-image WebGL garnish with no touch story as shipped; powerful on one hero photograph, wrong as a page-wide system.
- **Best for:** A hero or a single showcase photograph (a flagship project shot) where the visitor "develops" the colour image by moving the lens. Trade fit: one hero moment on desktop-led portfolio pages; budget the touch fallback before shipping.

- **Reference source:** http://tympanus.net/Tutorials/ShazamButtonEffect/ (Codrops "Shazam-Like Morphing Button Effect", 24 Nov 2015)
- **How it looks:** A single SVG shape on a plain page that is three things in turn: a wide "Listen" button; on click it squashes and morphs into a circle that pulses with double ripple rings while 50 small music-note glyphs stream in from off-screen and spiral into it; after a simulated 6.5-second "listening" period it morphs again into a wide audio-player panel; closing the player morphs the shape back into the original button. Capture is full: index.html + verified real sources (main.js 11,917 B, snap.svg-min.js, component.css — hand-refetched by the bank after its first pass hit 404 stubs).
- **Frame by frame:** Click → the shape morphs button → circle in 400ms on an overshoot bezier [0.8, −0.6, 0.2, 1] (it dips below its start size first — the squash anticipation) → ripple rings start (1.2s ease-out infinite: scale 3→1 with opacity 0→1 at 50%→0; a second ring repeats offset by 0.6s) → 50 notes spawn at random positions outside the viewport (rotation −30°…+30°), fade in, and fly to the button, each note's flight duration = 4.5 × its distance in px so the whole stream moves at one constant velocity; notes recycle on transitionend for as long as it is "listening" → at 6,500ms the notes stop, and after a 250ms beat the circle morphs into the player panel in 450ms on [0.7, 0, 0.3, 1] while the button fades out → close: player hides, shape morphs back in 400ms on [0.4, 1, 0.3, 1], button content returns after 50ms.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Snap.svg path morphing + CSS transitions/keyframes; no GSAP. The transferable core: three same-point-count SVG paths stored as strings in `data-path-start` / `data-path-listen` / `data-path-player` attributes; `animatePath(el, path, duration, bezierArray, callback)` interpolates `d` directly (Snap/mina accepts a raw 4-point cubic-bezier array, solver included in main.js). State values: morph durations 400 / 450 / 400ms with the three beziers above; totalNotes 50 (6 glyph variants); notesSpeedFactor 4.5; per-note transition `transform <speed>ms ease-in, opacity 0.8s`, spawn cascade 60ms; simulateTime 6500ms. Content swaps: transform/opacity 0.4s (start content enters on [0.8, −0.6, 0.2, 1] from translateY(−25px); listen content on [0.8, 0, 0.2, 1] from translateY(25px)); button opacity 0.3s; player panel opacity 0.5s (0.2s hiding). Modern rebuild (deep read): GSAP `attr: { d: … }` tweens `d` when point counts match, or Chromium's native `d: path("…")`.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — trade-fit basis: the morphing-container pattern is genuinely reusable, but the demo's music-listening theatre is not a trade pattern; steal the mechanism, not the scene.
- **Best for:** A call/CTA or quote button that morphs into its form/panel in place (button → form → confirmation as one continuous shape). Trade fit: situational — one morph moment per page, on the primary CTA.

## [BANK] infinite-marquee-svg-path — code-source demo (roofing pack: animation/code-source/infinite-marquee-svg-path/)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/codrops/2025/06/17/building-an-infinite-marquee-along-an-svg-path-with-react-motion/ (Codrops, Daniel Petho — "Building an Infinite Marquee Along an SVG Path with React & Motion")
- **How it looks:** Cards (five in the final demo) travelling endlessly along a drawn, looping S-curve path — the path visibly crosses over itself, and the cards stack correctly where they overlap, each card rotating to stay tangent to the curve and fading out as it reaches the path's ends and back in as it re-enters. Hovering glides the whole stream down to 30% speed; scrolling the page speeds the stream up, and scrolling the other way reverses its direction. Capture state: **values-only** — the folder holds only values.txt (3,997 B). There is no public repo and no hosted demo (the bank checked the author's repos); every parameter below is measured from the article's 26 code blocks, which values.txt extracts in full.
- **Frame by frame:** Every animation frame, one shared clock (a MotionValue, baseOffset) advances by baseVelocity × delta/1000 — percent of path length per second (20 for the single-item demo, 5 for the final card marquee) → each item's offset-distance = wrap(0, 100, clock + itemIndex × 100 / totalItems), so items stay evenly spaced and wrap seamlessly → the browser's CSS motion-path engine places and auto-rotates each item along the path → on hover, a spring (stiffness 100, damping 20) eases the speed factor toward 0.3 → page-scroll velocity (sprung, mapped 0–1000 px/s → 0–5×) adds to the speed, its sign flipping direction → each item's opacity follows (1 − |2 × progress − 1|^10)², dissolving at the path ends.
- **Mechanism & key values:** React + Motion ("motion/react": useMotionValue, useTransform, useAnimationFrame, useScroll, useVelocity, useSpring) + CSS Motion Path (offset-path / offset-distance / offset-rotate: "auto" — no SVG animateMotion) + D3 for responsive path rescaling. Demo path: viewBox 0 0 588 187, `M0 186.219C138.5 186.219 305.5 194.719 305.5 49.7188C305.5 -113.652 -75 186.219 484.5 186.219H587.5`. Distribution: 5 cards × repeat 4 = 20 items; duplicates aria-hidden; zIndex = floor(zIndexBase + progress%) so overlaps stack correctly (zIndexBase's numeric value is not printed in the article — recorded as a gap). Scroll spring config values likewise not printed in the article excerpts. Responsive fix: on resize the path is re-derived at container pixel size — sample the original with getPointAtLength (max 100 samples), rescale with d3.scaleLinear, regenerate smooth with d3.line().curve(curveBasis). Rebuild note from values.txt: keep totalItems high enough that spacing < item width or gaps open at the wrap point; wrap() is plain modulo arithmetic.
- **Tier:** STRONG — trade-fit basis: complete article-measured parameters for a distinctive marquee variant; the mechanism (one clock + CSS motion path) ports to vanilla JS without React.
- **Best for:** Logo/proof marquees and testimonial streams that should not look like every straight-line marquee — a curved path across a section, cards riding it. Trade fit: strong for a reviews or brands band with real design ambition; heavier than a CSS-translate marquee, so one per page.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry 149). **Code:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/animation/code-source/infinite-marquee-svg-path/ (values.txt only — no demo code exists to capture; the Codrops article's code blocks are the source)

## [BANK] 98-silo — code-source demo (animation/code-source/98-silo/, packs: all four)
- **Reference source:** https://www.silosilosilo.com/ (values-raw.txt SOURCE PASS line)
- **How it looks:** "Silo" — a Webflow shop for modular storage containers in three materials (Aluminum 6061-T6, Brass C360, Titanium waitlist), sold as lids/caps/inserts in 15/30/60/90 MM sizes. The page is three material columns under a sticky cart bar; each product is drawn as a stack of pieces (lid, body, inserts) that pulls apart — "explodes" — as you scroll, with prices ($9–$100 items in the captured price map) and a quantity stepper appearing once the stack is open. Capture is full: index.html (185,554 B) + six inline scripts holding the real shop/animation code.
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll (desktop ≥992px, three columns side by side on one scroll surface; mobile gives each material its own screen) → the sticky frame parks directly under the measured sticky header (--head-h) → the stack's pieces part from the bottom up (each lower piece travels further, so upper pieces never close on lower ones), driven by a paused GSAP timeline whose progress is carried by a 0.35s "catch-up" tween (OFFER_GONE = 0.35 — what scrub used to do, applied per column) → the price offer fades out early (power1.out, duration EXPAND_RUN × 0.3, at EXPAND_RUN × 0.05) → the quantity stepper rises after the pieces have parted → scroll continues into a held stretch where the open stack just stays open (OPEN_HOLD), then the frame releases with a power2.in ramp at half the release distance. Scrolling back up runs the expand backwards — the stack re-nests. Separately: responsive Swiper carousels initialise/destroy at the 991/992px breakpoint, and the cart strip opening never resizes the layout because its height (7.2rem) is reserved from the start via --bar-room.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Webflow + GSAP 3.12.2 + ScrollTrigger (CDN, per assets.txt) + Lenis 1.2.3 driven from gsap.ticker (lenis.raf inside the ticker, lagSmoothing(0)); a second Lenis instance runs the columns' own scroller. EXPAND_RUN = 1 (share of scroll range spent opening), OPEN_HOLD = 1.15 (held stretch at the cap, in timeline units), EXPAND_END = EXPAND_RUN/(EXPAND_RUN+OPEN_HOLD); column stagger = EXPAND_RUN × 0.06; stacked-below cut at (0.77 × EXPAND_RUN)/T. Hand-driven explode: openDur = max(OPEN_LAG 0.35, |target − p| / OPEN_RATE 1); closing duration 0.6, ease expo.out closing / power2.out opening. Wheel speed limit: MAX_WHEEL_DELTA = 100, lead capped at 0.3 × viewport height so the surface never outruns the hand. Offer close: power3.inOut, duration EXPAND_RUN × 0.82. Bar sizing measured live into --bar-h / --bar-room / --head-h CSS variables. Swiper 8/10 bundles loaded; the responsive-Swiper factory keys instances per component with bullets pagination + arrow navigation.
- **Tier:** STRONG — basis: the bank deep-read (slice-2 entry 98) exists for this exact mechanism and the capture carries the full production code; trade fit is as a product/configurator scroll story rather than a whole-page template.
- **Best for:** Product explainer sections where a thing pulls apart as you scroll (roof build-up layers, window cross-section, unit teardown), configurator-style shops, sticky cart/CTA bars that must not shift layout. The wheel-speed cap + lead cap is a reusable pattern for any scroll-driven product story.
- **Deep read:** reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md (entry 98). **Code:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/animation/code-source/98-silo/ (full capture + inline-0.js…inline-5.js + assets/tracking.js)

Pin scene: duration "1200%", 12 scenes, scene width = document height / 12. Sun path values are viewport-relative: entry to (width/3.5, −height/2.5); mid continues to (width/1.1, height/2.5) via (width/2.3 height point); sun scenes start at offset 150 with durations of one scene width (entry), scene8Offset − 350 (mid), one scene width (exit). 118 ScrollMagic scenes are constructed in the captured inline script in total (sun, clouds, and per-panel element scenes, many with duration 200 or sceneWidth − 100). Rebuilt on window resize (initScrollMagic re-runs).

- **Reference source:** https://reactbits.dev/text-animations/masked-heading (values-raw.txt SOURCE PASS line)
- **How it looks:** A React Bits component demo page whose centrepiece is a huge heading (default text "Designed in the details") where the letters themselves are windows: a photo or video plays *inside* the glyph shapes, slightly larger than the text and drifting with the mouse, while the surrounding page stays plain. After reveal, moving the mouse parallaxes the inner media (default parallax 26px, idle drift 18px), clamped so the oversized fill (fillScale 1.25) never shows an edge; optional hoverZoom. prefers-reduced-motion settles everything instantly with no reveal.
- **Mechanism & key values:** React component (MaskedHeading.jsx, 18,833 B, read in full) + MaskedHeading.css. Technique: the heading is measured with a transparent copy; each glyph becomes an SVG clipPath; the media layer (img/video, object-fit cover) is clipped by those glyph paths and transformed as one plane — no background-clip:text. Defaults from the source: fillScale 1.25, parallax 26, drift 18, hoverZoom 0, brightness 1, saturation 1, spotlightRadius 160 (spot mask = 9-stop radial-gradient with a smootherstep alpha curve), outlineWidth 1, reveal 'rise', duration 1.1, stagger 0.09, weight 700, tracking −0.03, lineHeight 1.06, textScale 0.115. Tint layer uses mix-blend-mode: color; spot tone layer #808080 at mix-blend saturation, shade layer black at opacity 0.55. GSAP drives glyph state objects; rendering writes transform/filter only when changed.
- **Tier:** STRONG — basis: trade fit (hero headlines are the highest-value slot on a trade homepage) + full component source in the capture + bank deep read.
- **Best for:** Hero headlines with imagery inside the type (roof texture in "ROOFING", kitchen photo in a remodel headline), section-title treatments for Work/gallery intros. Heavy machinery for one heading — budget it as the hero's one big trick.

## [BANK] dynamic-shape-overlays — code-source demo (animation/code-source/dynamic-shape-overlays/, packs: hvac, roofing)
- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/Development/ShapeOverlays/ (values-raw.txt SOURCE PASS line; values.txt records the article https://tympanus.net/codrops/2017/10/17/dynamic-shape-overlays-with-svg/ and the original technique repo github.com/ykob/shape-overlays)
- **How it looks:** The classic Codrops full-screen curtain: click the hamburger and two-to-four solid colour sheets sweep across the whole screen one after another, their leading edge not straight but a living, rippling wave — dark grey (#413f46), light grey (#e6e5ea), mid grey (#cccccc) in demo 1 — covering the page before the menu (or next page state) is revealed; click again and the sheets peel back in reverse order. The capture holds all three demo variants (same class, different configs) with full JS (demo1/2/3.js + easings.js, read via values.txt's measured extraction).
- **Frame by frame:** Click toggle → the class precomputes a per-point delay wave (sine composite with a randomised range, re-rolled every toggle so it never feels canned) → a requestAnimationFrame loop rebuilds the SVG path string every frame: each of the 19 points' Y = cubicInOut(progress delayed by its wave value) × 100 → the top edge is a smooth curve swept across a full-bleed rect → layer 2 follows 100ms behind, layer 3 another 100ms (delayPerPath) → on close, the layer order reverses → loop ends after duration + delayPerPath × (paths − 1) + delayPointsMax; an isAnimating flag blocks re-entry mid-sweep.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Vanilla JS ShapeOverlays class + inline SVG (viewBox 0 0 100 100, preserveAspectRatio="none") with stacked <path> layers; hand-ported glsl-easings (cubicInOut(t) = t<.5 ? 4t³ : 0.5(2t−2)³+1, plus exponential/sine/circular/quartic set). Demo 1 (liquid): numPoints 18, duration 600ms, delayPointsMax 300ms, delayPerPath 100ms; delay field range = 4×random+6 (6–10), delay[i] = (sin(−radian) + sin(−radian×range) + 2)/4 × delayPointsMax. Demo 2: numPoints 4, duration 800, delayPointsMax 180, delayPerPath 70, delay from a 2π sine with random phase. Demo 3 (snappy wipe): numPoints 2, duration 600, delayPointsMax 0, delayPerPath 200, easing alternates cubicOut/cubicInOut per path and swaps on close. Path built with midpoint control points (cp halfway between point X positions) for a smooth curve.

## [BANK] trionn-architecture — code-source demo, **values-only** (animation/code-source/trionn-architecture/, packs: remodeling, roofing)
- **Reference source:** Codrops article 2026/07/15 "The Architecture Behind Trionn — Coordinating GSAP, Three.js, Lenis and Web Audio", https://tympanus.net/codrops/2026/07/15/the-architecture-behind-trionn-coordinating-gsap-three-js-lenis-and-web-audio/ (values.txt: the article IS the code source; the site itself is trionn.com). **Capture state: values.txt ONLY (10,583 B) — no demo files exist; every value below is quoted from the article's code excerpts as recorded in values.txt.**
- **How it looks:** Trionn — an award-style agency site built over 4 months: a hero with a rotating 3D symbol made of panels that drift, flash on hover and can be held down until they blast apart; a Services sequence where a product assembles/explodes across 371 image frames as you scroll; a helix gallery of cards winding through 3D space; an About section with a lion image that distorts around the cursor and a draggable curtain; a scatter gallery of photos flying in; a footer whose wire-outline logo strings can be plucked like guitar strings (with synthesised sound and fog reacting).
- **Frame by frame:** Per the article excerpts: page load → hero layers stay gated until a shared transitionReady flag clears (headline delay 1.2s) → headline chars un-blur in random order (blur 12px → 0) → the hero symbol idles (rotY += 0.0042/frame) and leans toward the mouse (lerp 0.06, mouse × 0.22) → hover a panel: it flashes (flash decays ×0.92/frame; envMapIntensity 3.0 + flash × 1.6) and beeps once → press and hold: vibration builds (< 0.5s charge), then panels blast outward along explode directions (offset = max(0, explodeAmt − panel.delay) × 5.5) with weld sparks when lines complete → scroll: the Services frame sequence scrubs (explode window at progress 0.35–0.53, cards 0.56–1.0), the helix gallery pins and winds, the scatter gallery's 11 photos fly in scrubbed at 0.6 → footer: hover a logo string and it plucks (amp/speed tween to 0 over 0.9s expo.out) while fog pulses.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Next.js + React + Tailwind; GSAP + @gsap/react at the centre; vanilla Three.js (deliberately not R3F) on ONE shared render loop; Lenis driven from gsap.ticker (single master clock); Swiper for carousels; Web Audio — all hero/footer sounds synthesised at runtime. BlurTextReveal: SplitText "chars, words, lines", chars duration 0.8, stagger {each: 0.08, from: "random"}, ease power2.out, container blur over 0.5. Panel drift: 3 arms at 120° phases, driftX = sin(t×0.4 + phase) × 0.012 etc., all × (1 − explodeAmt). Services: 371 WebP frames on one <img>, frame index eased videoIdx += (target − videoIdx) × 0.12, preloaded in requestIdleCallback chunks of 20. Helix: 9 cards, ScrollTrigger pin start "top top", hover scale target 1.12, rounded corners via fragment-shader SDF. Footer strings: 26 segments rebuilt per frame, hit-clones with strokeWidth = max(12, strokeWidth × 18). Pluck synth: 3 sine oscillators (f, 2f, 3f), 4.9 Hz vibrato LFO, delay 0.14s, feedback 0.32 + intensity × 0.12. Fog: FBM 3 octaves, domain warp 1.4 × fbm. Lion: depth-map displacement amount (0.03 + 0.012 × breathing) × uHover, RGB split ±0.16 × disp, cursor eased 0.07/frame. Curtain: per-strip springs (sp = −offY × 0.12, vel = (vel + sp) × 0.65; neighbour coupling 0.22 / 0.62). The article's own closing lesson, recorded in values.txt: build a shared canvasManager from the start.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — basis: capture state + portability. No code on disk (article excerpts only) and the stack is a 4-month Next.js production; what transfers is the architecture discipline (one master clock, one shared scroll-progress ref, transition-ready gating, idle-time preload chunks) and individual parameter sets, not a liftable demo.
- **Best for:** Reference architecture for any heavy build: hero gating, scroll-driven frame sequences (a roof/unit assembling frame by frame), helix or scatter galleries, sound-free adaptations of the pluck/fog ideas. Read before attempting multiple WebGL sections on one page.
- **Deep read:** reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry 163). **Code:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/animation/code-source/trionn-architecture/ (values.txt only — no demo code captured)

- **Reference source:** https://tympanus.net/Tutorials/StickyGridScroll/ (values-raw.txt SOURCE PASS line; article recorded in the MANIFEST pick: https://tympanus.net/codrops/2026/03/02/sticky-grid-scroll-building-a-scroll-driven-animated-grid/, by Theo Plawinski)
- **How it looks:** A Codrops scroll experiment: a centred title block ("Sticky Grid Scroll — a structured scroll-driven image grid where movement unfolds progressively within a sticky layout") surrounded by a 3-column grid of images. As you scroll, the columns pour in from above and below, then the whole grid zooms in ×2.05 while the outer columns split sideways and the middle column's images split up/down — the grid "explodes" open around the title, which then slides to centre and its description + button fade in. A fixed corner frame holds credits/tags throughout; the page opens behind a thin line loader (100px line scaling across, 1.5s ease-in-out alternate). Capture note: the mined asset files are stubs, but the folder also holds the real bundle as index-CbAMiMj5.js.real (141,359 B) and index-AjrfVRK8.css.real (4,020 B) — the values below are read from those real files.
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll (Lenis smooth scroll, lerp 0.08, wheelMultiplier 1.4, driven by gsap.ticker) → the section wrapper parallaxes in (from yPercent −100, scrubbed, "top bottom" → "top top") → title fades in at "top 57%" (from opacity 0, 0.7s, power1.out, toggleActions play none none reset) → master scrubbed timeline ("top 25%" → "bottom bottom"): (1) grid reveal — each of the 3 columns slides in from y = ±(viewport-derived offset), even columns from one side, odd from the other, items staggered 0.06 each from start or end alternately, ease power1.inOut; (2) at −0.6 overlap, the zoom: grid scales to 2.05 (duration 1, power3.inOut), column 1 → xPercent −40, column 3 → xPercent +40, middle column's items split yPercent ±40 by half (duration 0.5, power1.inOut, at −0.5); (3) at −0.32, content toggles: title moves yPercent → 0 (0.7s power2.inOut) and description + button fade in (0.4s power1.inOut).
- **Mechanism & key values:** GSAP + ScrollTrigger + Lenis, bundled (Vite). Items grouped into 3 columns by index % 3. Reveal offset r = vh − (vh − gridHeight)/2, applied ± by column parity. gridZoomTimeline defaults: duration 1, ease power3.inOut; scale 2.05; splits ±40 xPercent / ±40 yPercent — these match the deep read's extracted values (2.05 zoom / ±40 splits). Title vertical centring is computed: titleOffsetY = (contentH − titleH)/2 / contentH × 100, applied as yPercent. CSS: base font-size calc(100vw / 14); loader keyframes loaderAnim 1.5s ease-in-out infinite alternate (scaleX 0→1 with origin flip at 50.1%). Fonts Arial / Times (demo styling).
- **Tier:** STRONG — basis: bank deep read with matching extracted parameters + full working bundle in the capture; direct gallery-section fit.
- **Best for:** Work/gallery sections that open with drama: a photo grid that assembles then explodes around a centred heading + CTA. Also a clean study of scrubbed multi-stage timelines with labelled overlaps ("-=0.6", "-=0.32").

## [BANK] gsap-pin-sidebar — code-source demo, **values-only** (animation/code-source/gsap-pin-sidebar/, packs: hvac, roofing)
- **Reference source:** https://codepen.io/akapowl/pen/poRdoLV/9b99361db3839f1169cdc0f278746ee5 (values.txt — the hash-suffixed URL is required; the bare /pen/poRdoLV 404s). **Capture state: values.txt ONLY (2,701 B) — the pen's full HTML/CSS/JS was captured into that measured extraction; no separate demo files exist.**
- **How it looks:** A "philosophie" section: a full-height stage where numbered points (an image beside a text article) are stacked exactly on top of each other, with a slim vertical indicator rail down the left side (one segment per point, grey #adadad, the active one orange). Scrolling doesn't move the page — the stage stays pinned while the points crossfade/slide through one by one, the rail lighting up in step. It reads as a scroll-driven carousel with a progress rail.
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll → the section wrapper pins for exactly +100% of viewport height (pin timeline, scrub) → simultaneously the points timeline scrubs across 100% of viewport height *per point*: at each point's turn its indicator lights orange (0.25 duration), its image fades in (from autoAlpha 0) and its article rises in (from autoAlpha 0, y +100) → at 75% through the point's unit, the article exits upward (y −100, autoAlpha 0), the image fades out and the indicator dims back to #adadad → next point takes over. Because points are absolutely stacked, there is no layout shift at any point.
- **Mechanism & key values:** GSAP + ScrollTrigger, vanilla CSS layout, **two separate scrubbed timelines** (values.txt's rebuild note: keep the pin timeline separate from the content timeline — pin distance = one viewport, content distance = 100% × number of points). Points timeline: duration = points.length (1 unit per point), trigger ".philosophie", start "top bottom", end "+=" + (100 × points.length) + "%", scrub true. Pinner: trigger ".philosophie.wrapper", start "top top", end "+=100%", pin true, pinSpacing true (markers: true left on in the pen — remove for production). CSS measured: indicators rail position absolute, left 2rem, margin 10vh 0, height 80vh, width 3px, flex column, space-between, display none until JS enables it; .point height 100vh, padding 4rem, flex; article flex-basis 60%; img flex-basis 25%, max-width 25vw.
- **Tier:** STRONG — basis: trade fit (this is a ready-made process/why-us stepper) + the bank's measured extraction is complete enough to rebuild from without the pen.
- **Best for:** Process sections (4–5 steps with photo + text), "how we work" / philosophy blocks, before-you-call checklists. One pinned viewport, zero layout shift, works with any number of points.
- **Deep read:** reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry 153). **Code:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/animation/code-source/gsap-pin-sidebar/ (values.txt only — measured pen extraction)

## [BANK] gsap-marquee-text-codepen — code-source demo, **values-only** (animation/code-source/gsap-marquee-text-codepen/, packs: hvac, roofing)
- **Reference source:** codepen.io/GreenSock/pen/wvZMwez (values.txt: GreenSock's official pen; full JS recovered via the embed-preview route — direct .js/.css asset URLs are Cloudflare-blocked). **Capture state: values.txt ONLY (2,676 B).**
- **How it looks:** A footer marquee: a single row of huge uppercase text items (186px, line-height 1, white-space nowrap) streaming sideways forever with no visible seam — in the pen the repeated item text is the placeholder phrase "Komt goed bro." across 6 identical items, separated by 100px gaps. It never pauses, jumps or changes speed.
- **Frame by frame:** On load (deferred until document.fonts.ready so item widths are final) → every item slides left at a constant 500 px/s (speed 5 × 100) → as an item's turn ends it teleports exactly one total loop width ahead — inside a fromTo tween with immediateRender: false, so the jump happens off-screen and the stream looks endless → the playhead itself wraps (pre-rendered with progress(1, true).progress(0, true)), and the loop exposes next()/previous()/toIndex()/current() controls that travel the shortest wrap-aware direction.
- **Mechanism & key values:** GSAP core only — the horizontalLoop() helper is fully self-contained in the pen (no plugins); page furniture is Tailwind CDN classes. Invocation measured: horizontalLoop(".marquee__item", { repeat: −1, paused: false, speed: 5, paddingRight: 100 }). pixelsPerSecond = (speed || 1) × 100; timeline ease "none"; item x converted to xPercent with integer snapping by default (gsap.utils.snap, snap: false disables); totalWidth = last.offsetLeft + (xPercent/100) × lastWidth − startX + last.offsetWidth × lastScaleX + paddingRight; per item two tweens (out-going and wrap-around) with distance-based durations so all items share one velocity regardless of width; markup gap: 100px in CSS mirrors paddingRight 100.
- **Tier:** STRONG — basis: this is the canonical GSAP seamless-loop pattern (values.txt's own reading), GreenSock-official source, and marquees are a standard hero/footer device on trade sites.
- **Best for:** Marquee bands anywhere: service lists ("ROOFING • GUTTERS • SIDING…"), review-score tickers, town-name strips, footer sign-offs. Copy the helper wholesale; set speed in hundreds of px/s and match the CSS gap to paddingRight.
- **Deep read:** reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry 161). **Code:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/animation/code-source/gsap-marquee-text-codepen/ (values.txt only — full JS described from the embed-preview recovery)

## [BANK] P01 · Masked word reveal — library (animation/animation-parameter-library.md, seed table row 1)
- **Reference source:** Nick Ho Motorsports (seen at).
- **How it looks:** A headline whose words rise one after another from behind an invisible horizontal mask — each word starts hidden below its line and slides up into place, so the line assembles word by word.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: element enters (ScrollTrigger onEnter) → each word starts 64–70px under its clipped mask → words translate up to place in quick succession → end state: full line readable, masks removed by the split structure.
- **Mechanism & key values:** GSAP SplitText mask wrappers; duration 0.6s; ease expo.out; stagger 0.04–0.06; property y.
- **Best for:** Hero headlines, section headings. Trade fit: core headline recipe for any trade homepage.
- **Tier:** STRONG (trade fit).
- **Deep read:** animation/animation-parameter-library.md (seed table). **Code:** none.

## [BANK] P02 · Slide-up text reveal — library (animation/animation-parameter-library.md, seed table row 2)
- **Reference source:** Heron AI (seen at).
- **How it looks:** Blocks of text fade and rise gently into view as you scroll — the workhorse reveal across a whole page; one recipe drives 40 of 41 triggers on the source site.

- **Mechanism & key values:** Duration 0.8s (median 0.82); ease power2.out (40/41 triggers); stagger 0.02; mostly unscrubbed; properties autoAlpha + yPercent, then clearProps.
- **Best for:** Every text block — intro copy, proof, process, towns. Trade fit: the default reveal for trade pages.
- **Tier:** STRONG (trade fit).
- **Deep read:** animation/animation-parameter-library.md (seed table). **Code:** none.

## [BANK] P04 · Parallax layers — library (animation/animation-parameter-library.md, seed table row 4)
- **Reference source:** Nick Ho Motorsports (seen at).
- **How it looks:** Stacked image/type layers drift at different speeds while scrolling, so the composition has depth instead of moving as one flat sheet.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: continuous scroll, top bottom → bottom top → each layer translates yPercent/y at its own scrub rate → layers never lockstep → end state: offsets fully travelled at section exit.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Linear ease; scrub values mixed per layer, 1.9–4.3; properties yPercent / y. Mixed scrub is the point — it stops lockstep motion.
- **Best for:** Hero backgrounds, full-bleed photo sections, work galleries. Trade fit: standard depth device for trade heroes.
- **Tier:** STRONG (trade fit).
- **Deep read:** animation/animation-parameter-library.md (seed table). **Code:** none.

- **How it looks:** A grid of images whose columns lag behind the scroll like elastic — the further a column sits from the centre column, the more it trails, then catches up.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: smoothed scroll (ScrollSmoother) → grid regrouped into column wrappers → each column's lag scales with distance from the centre column → on release/scroll-stop columns settle back → rebuild on resize if column count changes.
- **Mechanism & key values:** ScrollSmoother smooth 1, effects true; lag ∝ distance from centre column.
- **Best for:** Work/gallery grids. Trade fit: lively gallery motion; needs ScrollSmoother (club plugin route).
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL (trade fit).
- **Deep read:** animation/animation-parameter-library.md (L2 Chunk 4). **Code:** none in packs.

## [BANK] P38 · Infinite parallax grid — library (animation/animation-parameter-library.md, L2 Chunk 4 row 3)
- **Reference source:** Codrops InfiniteLayersGrid (seen at).
- **How it looks:** A tile grid that tiles seamlessly forever (tiles duplicated 2×2), introduced by a 2-second expo.inOut tween with a 0.05 stagger.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: load → intro tween runs 2s expo.inOut, stagger 0.05 → grid then scrolls/parallaxes endlessly over the duplicated tiles → IntersectionObserver toggles a visibility class for off-screen economy.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Tiles duplicated 2×2 for seamless tiling; intro duration 2, expo.inOut, stagger 0.05; IntersectionObserver visibility class.
- **Best for:** Background grids, gallery walls. Trade fit: backdrop device.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL (trade fit).
- **Deep read:** animation/animation-parameter-library.md (L2 Chunk 4). **Code:** none in packs.

> Note (not counted as items): the file's "Cross-site rules" section records verified cross-site laws — scrubbed motion = linear ease; triggered motion = expo/power2/power3 out; reveals run 0.4–0.8s; staggers live in 0.02–0.12s; Lenis feeds its rAF into the GSAP ticker (one clock); clearProps after reveals; touch/coarse pointers get a separate simpler path; attribute-driven (data-*) animation keeps a 97-trigger page maintainable.

Idle wave: period 3.2s, peak 0.7, phase (x + 0.6y)/span − t/T, shape ((1+cos)/2)^2.2, span max(220, 0.85 × width), engage after 500ms idle, mix time-constant 600ms. Shadow softness stdDeviation = fontSize·0.016, SHADOW_OPACITY 0.5. CSS: svg max-width var(--stroke-text-width, 600px), overflow visible. Same mechanism as Q167.

# PART 1 — UI/UX PATTERN LIBRARY (58 items)

## [BANK] Smooth scroll — Lenis is the class default — pattern (structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md, roofing pack copy)
- **Reference source:** None recorded (bank-internal cross-site measurement; 24 opened sites).
- **How it looks:** The whole page glides with eased, inertial scrolling instead of the browser's stepped native scroll; scroll-linked animation stays in sync because Lenis is wired to the GSAP ticker.
- **Frame by frame:** Continuous — scroll input → Lenis eases the page toward the target position on its raf loop → GSAP ScrollTrigger reads the same clock.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Lenis found on 14 of 24 opened sites (Measured) — "it is the default of this class of site." Rule: wire Lenis raf to the GSAP ticker. (Trade-top reality check in the anatomy, F17: Lenis appears at only two of 20 GC shortlist homepages — this is the award-class default, not the trade default.)
- **Best for:** Any immersive portfolio/preview build as the scroll foundation. Trade fit: fine under content; never let it turn the page into a non-scrolling scene page (see the anti-pattern item below).
- **Tier:** STRONG (trade fit — measured class default, but not a conversion device by itself).
- **Deep read:** structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md (Cross-site facts). **Code:** none.

## [BANK] Stacks census — what this class of site is built on — pattern (structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md, roofing pack copy)
- **Reference source:** None recorded (bank-internal measurement, 24 opened sites).
- **How it looks:** Not a visual pattern — a build-stack fact: Next.js 5 sites, Nuxt 6, Webflow 4, WordPress 1 of the 24 opened.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Measured stack counts: Next.js 5 · Nuxt 6 · Webflow 4 · WordPress 1. Recorded proof point: LPAS won an Awwwards SOTD on WordPress — "proof our stack is not the ceiling."
- **Best for:** Stack decisions on trade builds — removes "we need a fancier stack" as an excuse; the WordPress/Elementor stack can reach award level.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL (trade fit — background fact, not a design pattern).
- **Deep read:** structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md (Cross-site facts). **Code:** none.

## [BANK] Page length — service sites cluster at 8–12 screens — pattern (structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md, roofing pack copy)
- **Reference source:** None recorded (bank-internal measurement; sites named: Neutomni, Belgrade Arbor, FORMAT, Nick Ho, LPAS, Odyssee, ESR, Signal-A).
- **How it looks:** A service/trade page runs roughly 8–12 viewport-heights of content; agency/studio pages run far longer (up to ~24 screens).
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion (a length/structure rule).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Measured page lengths in screens: Neutomni 23.8 · Belgrade Arbor 23.3 · FORMAT 20.9 · Nick Ho 14.1 · LPAS 11.8 · Odyssee 10.8 · ESR 8.5 · Signal-A 7.3. Rule drawn: service sites cluster ~8–12 screens.
- **Best for:** Scoping any trade homepage — enough room for hero, proof, services, process, work, towns, CTA without agency-length sprawl.
- **Tier:** STRONG (trade fit — direct measured guidance for our page class).
- **Deep read:** structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md (Cross-site facts). **Code:** none.

## [BANK] Anti-pattern — scene pages and gate loaders on lead pages — pattern (structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md, roofing pack copy)
- **Reference source:** None recorded (bank-internal measurement, 24 opened sites).
- **How it looks:** What NOT to build: a page that doesn't scroll normally (a fixed "scene" the visitor steps through), or a page that opens behind a gate or a long loader before any content or phone number appears.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion (a prohibition, recorded so it is indexed, not lost).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Measured: 8/24 opened sites are scene pages that don't scroll normally; 5/24 open with a gate or long loader. File's verdict, verbatim sense: both = DO NOT USE where the job is phone calls.
- **Best for:** A veto check on every trade lead page design — if a version gates content or breaks normal scroll, it fails regardless of craft.
- **Tier:** NOT-FOR-TRADES (bank verdict — the file bans both patterns for lead pages).
- **Deep read:** structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md (Cross-site facts, "Anti-patterns for a lead page (Measured)"). **Code:** none.

## [BANK] Reduced-motion support as a quality edge — pattern (structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md, roofing pack copy)
- **Reference source:** None recorded (bank-internal measurement; style-checked sites named: Forge, Interaction Library).
- **How it looks:** Visitors who set prefers-reduced-motion get a calm, static-but-complete version of the page instead of full animation; almost no competitor site bothers, so shipping it reads as craft.
- **Frame by frame:** Static fallback — with reduced motion on, animated reveals/transitions are suppressed and content is simply present.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Measured gap: reduced-motion rules found in only 2 of 15 style-checked sites (Forge 7 rules, Interaction Library 5). File's position: "Our builds ship reduced-motion support — that is a quality edge, not a chore."
- **Best for:** Every build, as a standing rule — pairs with the motion-effects toggle and kill-switch patterns in the harvest blocks ([203], [222]).
- **Tier:** STRONG (bank stance — adopted as a standing build rule in the file itself).
- **Deep read:** structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md (Cross-site facts, "Accessibility gap"). **Code:** none.

## [BANK] Cursor — small follower, system cursor kept usable — pattern (structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md, roofing pack copy)
- **Reference source:** None recorded (bank-internal measurement; sites named: PixelVault, Neutomni).
- **How it looks:** A small follower element trails the pointer and changes reaction per background/element, while the visitor's real system cursor stays visible and usable — unlike top-end sites that hide the system cursor entirely.
- **Frame by frame:** Continuous — pointer moves → the small follower tracks it (elsewhere in the bank the CSS-transition follower runs 0.2s transform + left/top, no rAF lerp, [222]) → follower state changes over interactive/different-background zones.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Measured: hiding the system cursor is common at the top end (PixelVault 239 elements, Neutomni 171 — element counts as recorded). Our pattern per the file: small follower that reacts per background, system cursor kept usable — labelled a standing build rule.
- **Best for:** Portfolio/preview builds needing a custom-cursor signature without the usability risk of cursor-hiding; the user-facing build brief requires the cursor to react differently per element/section.
- **Tier:** STRONG (bank stance — recorded as our standing build rule).
- **Deep read:** structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md (Cross-site facts, "Cursor"). **Code:** none.

## [BANK] Seamless infinite scroll with iOS fixes — pattern (structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md, roofing pack copy)
- **Reference source:** Codrops "Never Ending Story" (Level-2 entry 158, as recorded in the file; exact parameters in harvest block [158]).

## [BANK] Harvest [8] — velocity→uniform feed (scroll velocity drives skew) — pattern (structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md, roofing pack copy)
- **Reference source:** Deep-read queue entry 8 — Roman Jean-Elie (romanjeanelie.com, per MAP slice-1 list).
- **How it looks:** Content skews/leans in proportion to how fast the visitor is scrolling — flick fast and the page visibly leans; stop and it settles upright.
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll → scroll velocity is sampled (getVelocity) → fed to a skew uniform → elements skew with speed → velocity decays → skew returns to zero.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Named only in this file: "velocity→uniform feed (getVelocity → skew uniform)" (slice 1). No numeric parameters printed in this block.
- **Best for:** Portfolio/preview pages — a felt sense of speed in galleries and lists; keep off dense lead content.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL (trade fit — signature-feel mechanism, not a conversion device).
- **Deep read:** structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md (DEEP-READ HARVEST, block [8]); substance: reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-1.md (entry 8). **Code:** code-source/roman-jean-elie/ (named in slice 1; pack presence per MAP caveat).

## [BANK] Harvest [31] — single-master-uniform pattern; mount-once/swap-textures rule — pattern (structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md, roofing pack copy)
- **Reference source:** Deep-read queue entry 31 — Thibault Guignand (thibaultguignand.com, per MAP slice-1 list).

- **Mechanism & key values:** Named rules only in this file: "single-master-uniform pattern; mount-once/swap-textures rule" (slice 1). No numeric parameters printed in this block.
- **Best for:** WebGL galleries/heroes on portfolio builds — an architecture rule that prevents jank from scene rebuilds.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL (trade fit — build-architecture rule for WebGL work, not a page pattern).

## [BANK] Harvest [125] — square-lens kit + ambient distortion set — pattern (structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md, roofing pack copy)
- **Reference source:** Deep-read queue entry 125 — Mouse-Following Square Lens, Codrops (Three.js/GLSL; article on tympanus.net, per MAP slice-2 list).
- **How it looks:** A square lens follows the pointer over an image; inside the lens the image is distorted and RGB-split, and a gentle ambient distortion runs underneath even at rest.
- **Frame by frame:** Pointer moves → lens follows with pointerEase .1 → inside the square, radial RGB channels offset (.01 / 0 / −.01) and the lens distortion (1.5) warps the image → ambient wave keeps moving slowly behind it.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Lens kit {squareSize .4 (half-side, −1..1 space), lensDistortion 1.5, RGB radial .01/0/−.01, pointerEase .1}; ambient distortion {wave 10 / .01 / 1, random 1 / .02 / .2}; CC-lens scale formula (both sign branches, in the entry).
- **Best for:** Interactive image moments on portfolio builds (work/gallery hover); heavy for lead pages.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL (trade fit — a signature WebGL effect with full values; portfolio-side).
- **Deep read:** structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md (DEEP-READ HARVEST, block [125]); substance: reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md (entry 125). **Code:** animation/code-source/125-square-lens/ (per MAP manifest pick, siding pack).

## [BANK] Harvest [126] — procedural snake steering kit + radius profile — pattern (structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md, roofing pack copy)
- **Reference source:** Deep-read queue entry 126 — Endless Procedural Snake, Codrops (Three.js/WebGL; article on tympanus.net, per MAP slice-2 list).
- **How it looks:** A continuous procedural "snake" form steers itself endlessly through 3D space, coiling and wandering without a authored path.
- **Frame by frame:** Continuous — the head steers by orbit/seek forces → the body follows through Bézier handles → coil and wander perturbations keep the motion organic.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Steering kit {orbit 8, seek ×1.5, radial gain 0.1, turn cap π/6, coil 3 × 0.25, wander π/24 / tilt π/48}; Bézier handle rule {0.33 + 0.34 × turnFactor}; radius-profile landmarks {0 / .74 / .85 / .95 / 1}; scale-material uniform set (in the entry).
- **Best for:** Ambient WebGL background creatures on portfolio builds only.
- **Tier:** NOT-FOR-TRADES (trade fit — no trade-page use; recorded as a portfolio-side mechanism with its full parameter kit).
- **Deep read:** structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md (DEEP-READ HARVEST, block [126]); substance: reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-2.md (entry 126). **Code:** none recorded in this block.

- **Mechanism & key values:** Ui-ux values as recorded: motion-effects toggle with persisted flag + prefers-reduced-motion check ("accessibility as a feature"); time-of-day greeting (Good Morning/Afternoon/Evening by local hour) as hero micro-personalisation; named-methodology explainer section ("Anatomy of …").
- **Best for:** Portfolio/preview builds (motion toggle), any homepage hero (greeting), and process/method sections for firms with a named system (pairs with anatomy F4).
- **Tier:** STRONG (trade fit — three small, honest, reusable devices).
- **Deep read:** structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md (DEEP-READ HARVEST, block [203]); substance: reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-4.md (entry 203). **Code:** none recorded in this block.

## [BANK] Harvest II [149] — infinite marquee along an SVG path (exact parameters) — pattern (structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md, roofing pack copy)
- **Reference source:** Slice-3 entry 149 — Codrops, Building an Infinite Marquee Along an SVG Path with React & Motion (tympanus.net).
- **How it looks:** Cards travel endlessly along a curved SVG path — a marquee that follows a drawn curve instead of a straight line, speeding/slowing with scroll and easing on hover.
- **Frame by frame:** Continuous loop → items advance along the path at baseVelocity → hover applies factor 0.3 through a spring (stiffness 100, damping 20) → items keep wrapping seamlessly.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Demo path "M0 186.219C138.5 186.219 305.5 194.719 305.5 49.7188C305.5 -113.652 -75 186.219 484.5 186.219H587.5"; viewBox "0 0 588 187". baseVelocity 20 (single-item demo), 5 (final: 5 cards × repeat 4 = 20 items). Hover factor 0.3; hover spring stiffness 100, damping 20. wrap() = ((((v − min) % range) + range) % range) + min. parsePathToPoints maxSamples default 100. Honestly not in the article (as recorded): the numeric springConfig for the scroll spring and the zIndexBase value — referenced by name only.
- **Best for:** Logo/proof marquees and gallery ribbons on portfolio builds — a curved upgrade on the straight marquee (anatomy F17 records the trade ceiling's one marquee at 60s linear infinite).
- **Tier:** STRONG (trade fit — full measured values and an honest gap note; portfolio-side weight).
- **Deep read:** structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md (DEEP-READ HARVEST II, block [149]); substance: reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry 149). **Code:** animation/code-source/infinite-marquee-svg-path/ (per MAP manifest pick, roofing pack).

## [BANK] Harvest II [150] — dynamic shape overlays (exact parameters, 3 demos) — pattern (structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md, roofing pack copy)
- **Reference source:** Slice-3 entry 150 — Codrops, Dynamic Shape Overlays (tympanus.net/Development/ShapeOverlays/).
- **How it looks:** A full-screen SVG shape overlay sweeps across the page as a transition curtain — multiple path layers chase each other with staggered point delays, in muted fill colours.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger → path points animate with per-point delay (sin-based spread) → layers follow at delayPerPath intervals → overlay covers, then reveals.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Demo 1: numPoints 18, duration 600ms, delayPointsMax 300ms, delayPerPath 100ms; fills #413f46 / #e6e5ea / #cccccc. Demo 2: numPoints 4, duration 800, delayPointsMax 180, delayPerPath 70; delay formula (sin(radian + range) + 1)/2 × max, radian over 2π, range = random × 2π. Demo 3: numPoints 2, duration 600, delayPointsMax 0, delayPerPath 200; per-path easing swap — opening (i==1 ? cubicOut : cubicInOut), closing (i==1 ? cubicInOut : cubicOut).
- **Best for:** Page/section transitions on portfolio builds — a curtain with fully tuned stagger math.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL (trade fit — transition showpiece; keep off lead pages per the loader/scene cautions).
- **Deep read:** structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md (DEEP-READ HARVEST II, block [150]); substance: reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry 150). **Code:** animation/code-source/dynamic-shape-overlays/ (per MAP manifest pick, roofing + hvac packs).

## [BANK] Harvest II [152] — horizontal scroll section + scroll-lookup navigation (exact parameters) — pattern (structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md, roofing pack copy)
- **Reference source:** Slice-3 entry 152 (pen; the horizontal-scroll lookup pattern).
- **How it looks:** Panels scroll horizontally under a pin while the page scrolls vertically; navigation links jump to the right panel by looking up positions inside the horizontal tween rather than the document.
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll → container pins, scrub 1 → panels translate x by −(scrollWidth − innerWidth − 50) → nav click animates scroll (duration 1, overwrite "auto") to the panel's looked-up start.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Horizontal tween: x: () => -(panelContainer.scrollWidth - window.innerWidth - 50), ease "none"; ScrollTrigger pin true, scrub 1, end "+=" + panels.length * 2000. Lookup: getScrollLookup(".section", { start: "center center", containerAnimation: scrollHorizontalTween }); helper start default "top top", refreshPriority −10. Nav scroll: duration 1, overwrite "auto". Usage variant seen in Level 2 (start "top 125px", pinSpacing false) — the block rules: pen values govern.
- **Best for:** Horizontal sector/process panels (pairs with the LPAS sector-panels item) that still need working anchor navigation.
- **Tier:** STRONG (trade fit — the navigation wiring is what makes horizontal sections usable, and it is fully measured).
- **Deep read:** structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md (DEEP-READ HARVEST II, block [152]); substance: reverse-engineering/deep-reads-slice-3.md (entry 152). **Code:** none recorded in this block.

## [BANK] Harvest II [158] — seamless infinite scroll (exact parameters) — pattern (structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md, roofing pack copy)
- **Reference source:** Slice-3 entry 158 — Codrops "Never Ending Story" (the parameter record behind the Part 1 infinite-scroll item).
- **How it looks:** Full-screen sections (100svh) loop seamlessly; inside them, content parallaxes and a marquee shrinks as it travels; fixed header/footer chrome floats above at z-index 12.
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll → sections snap (mandatory, 500ms debounce, 0.9s, easeOutQuart) → parallax layers move yPercent −50→50 linearly across each section traversal → marquee scales 1.5→0.5 → the duplicated first section continues the loop.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Sections: 100svh each, 3 + 1 duplicate. Snap: mandatory, debounce 500ms, duration 0.9s, easeOutQuart 1−(1−t)^4. Parallax: yPercent −50→50, linear, full section traversal. Marquee scale 1.5→0.5. Chrome CSS: header/footer fixed, z-index 12, padding 1.2rem; link hover opacity 0.5 with transition opacity 0.4s cubic-bezier(0.430,0.195,0.020,1); mobile breakpoint 700px; helper beziers --bezzy: cubic-bezier(0.8,0,0,1), --bezzy3: cubic-bezier(0.5,0,0,1); root font-size 62.5% (1rem = 10px).
- **Best for:** The optional loop mode for one-page sites (see Part 1 item) — this block is its build sheet.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL (bank verdict — optional mode only, per the Part 1 item).

## [BANK] Harvest II [164] — circular text spinner (exact parameters/defaults) — pattern (structure-uiux/ui-ux-patterns.md, roofing pack copy)
- **Reference source:** Slice-3 entry 164 (circular-text component as recorded in the block).
- **How it looks:** Text set on a circle spins continuously — a rotating badge of words — speeding up on hover, tiltable, draggable, with an optional ring line inside.
- **Frame by frame:** Load → the circular text rotates (default spinDuration 20, clockwise) → hover speeds it up ('speedUp' default) with spring-driven speed/scale/tilt → letters settle with a 0.5s transition when the state changes.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Defaults: text (required), spinDuration 20, onHover 'speedUp', direction 'clockwise', size 200, fontSize 24, fontWeight 900, letterSpacing 0, startAngle 0, fill true, repeat 1, ring false, tilt 0, hoverTilt 0, draggable false. Springs: speed stiffness 60 / damping 18; scale 300/20; tilt 150/18. MAX_FLING 1440°/s. Perspective = size × 2.5. Non-fill glyph arc = width × (180 / (π · max(size/2 − fontSize·0.6, 1))); span scaled by fit = min(1, 360/(span × copies)). Ring line: inset 1.3em, borderWidth max(1, fontSize/16). CSS transitions: plane transform 0.7s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); settled letters 0.5s cubic-bezier(0,0,0,1); ring opacity 0.4s ease. Root role="img", aria-label = text.
- **Best for:** Rotating badge/stamp elements (est. year, "licensed & insured", scroll hints) on heroes and footers — a small, fully-specified component.
- **Tier:** STRONG (trade fit — small footprint, complete defaults, accessible root semantics recorded).
