# PART 2 — CONVERSION ANATOMY (33 items)

Source for all Part 2 entries: `structure-uiux/00-conversion-anatomy.md` (roofing pack copy; shared reference-core, all four packs), v0.4. Evidence levels are the file's own: OPENED = a lane personally opened the site; EXCERPT = search-result excerpts, not a direct open; SOURCE = source-verified. A pattern is a FINDING when confirmed in ≥2 trades; single-trade items stay CANDIDATE. Reference source at file level: bank-internal compilation ("none recorded" per MAP); the named sites inside each finding are its sources.

## [BANK] Anatomy §1 — Hero anatomy (F1, F2, F3, F11 + candidate) — library (structure-uiux/00-conversion-anatomy.md §1)
- **Reference source:** Hippo Roofing; Erie Home; Neil Kelly; Pacific Outdoor Living; ResinPro; Green Conception; System Pavers; BOWA; Paverston; Elbaz Construction; Richard Lusk; Murray Lampert; CQC Home (evidence levels per finding, in the entry below).
- **How it looks:** The first screen carries everything that matters: a one-line proof strip (stars + review count + licence/years/warranty) directly in or under the hero, a headline selling the outcome or the fear relieved — not company history — an interactive low-friction entry (project picker, instant estimate, zip-first form) instead of a lone button, and the licence number printed in the first screen itself, ideally linked to the regulator.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion (hero content/offer structure).
- **Mechanism & key values:** **F1** One-line hero proof strip — Hippo: ★4.8 Google · 700+ reviews · Veteran-owned since 2008 · Licensed CCC1331992 (OPENED); Erie: 4.8 / 40,000+ reviews + BBB A+ (OPENED); Neil Kelly: 80 Years / 30,000+ Projects / 5 Year Warranty / 4.6/5 from 2,200+ Reviews, repeated under hero (OPENED); present in 3 trades — "the single most consistent top-site device found so far." **F2** Hero sells outcome/fear-relief: Neil Kelly "THE EASIEST WAY TO REMODEL, HONESTLY." + "Straight talk on budget, timing, and risk."; Green Conception "See your roof price before anyone calls you"; BOWA is the recorded counter-example (emotional brand hero, no offer/proof — weaker direct response). **F3** Interactive hero entry beats a plain button: Neil Kelly project-picker (service + space + location); Hippo instant roof estimate; System Pavers zip-first form (EXCERPT); Paverston photo-estimate (EXCERPT). **F11** Licence IN the first screen, best linked to the regulator: Elbaz "Licensed, bonded & insured · CBC1265280" + "104 municipalities" (OPENED); Lusk "C-27 & C-53 · CSLB license #950714 · insured & bonded" under hero (OPENED); Murray Lampert footer "License 458038" hyperlinked to the CSLB (OPENED); 4 trades. CANDIDATE (GC only): hero-adjacent giant credential statement (Neil Kelly's stat bar ≈ the pattern library's ESR giant-type pattern).
- **Best for:** Every trade hero — this section is the hero build sheet; checklist items 1, 2, 3 and 13 derive from it.
- **Tier:** CROWN (bank verdict — F1 is the file's own "single most consistent top-site device"; F2/F3/F11 are multi-trade FINDINGS; the giant-credential candidate stays CANDIDATE inside the entry).
- **Deep read:** structure-uiux/00-conversion-anatomy.md (§1, findings F1/F2/F3/F11). **Code:** none.

## [BANK] Anatomy §2 — Proof systems (F4, F5, F6, F12, F13 + candidate) — library (structure-uiux/00-conversion-anatomy.md §2)
- **Reference source:** Hippo Roofing; One Hour; Erie Home; Service Experts; A.B. May; Pacific Outdoor Living; Jackson Design; ResinPro; KBF Design Gallery; Georgia Contractor Group; Saddlewood Builders; Green Conception; Austin Pro; LYKORA; TruGreen; CMK (evidence levels in the entry).
- **How it looks:** Proof presented as products and records, not adjectives: trademarked named systems as pillars, review VOLUME printed next to the stars, reviews tagged by project type or shown as a live feed, at least one claim the visitor can check against a public record (printed with its honest caveat), and reviews that name the operative who did the work.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion (proof content systems; live feeds update by recency, see §5).
- **Mechanism & key values:** **F4** Named/trademarked systems: HippoShield™ / DefenderRoof® (roofing); StraightForward Pricing® Guide + "Always On Time… Or You Don't Pay A Dime!®" (HVAC); Permalast Layered Install System™ + 8,000 PSI vs 4,000 PSI standard (concrete, EXCERPT); Neil Kelly "5-Year Warranty — the longest in the business." **F5** Review VOLUME displayed: One Hour 201,360 Google reviews; Erie 40,000+; Service Experts 200k 5-star claim; A.B. May 17,058; strong local level = hundreds (Hippo 700+) — rule: show the real count, however small, beside the platform name. **F6** Reviews tagged by project type beat generic sliders (Pacific Outdoor Living, EXCERPT; Jackson video "Client Success Stories" + long named reviews with project scope, OPENED; Hippo live Google feed, OPENED; Erie even shows a 4-star critical review — authenticity device). **F12** Checkable proof beats asserted proof: KBF "The Ledger" — of 13 tracked resales of KBF homes, 9 ranked top-3 ever sold on their street, 7 were #1, "Verified against Orange, Seminole & Lake County deeds", printed WITH the caveat "We don't claim our remodel caused it" — the caveat makes it believable; Austin Pro's self-reconciling arithmetic (312 mapped + "574 more documented projects counted but outside this frame" = 886 documented, same page); LYKORA marks the boundary (its render-vs-real "1:1 Realization" pairs ARE checkable; its "0% Budget Overruns" headline is an unverifiable absolute). **F13** Reviews name the OPERATIVE, not the brand (TruGreen's wall names technicians; CMK's name project managers; Jackson's name staff). CANDIDATE: "Every photo is our real work" gallery caption (ResinPro, EXCERPT).
- **Best for:** Proof/reviews sections on every trade homepage; checklist items 5, 8, 11, 14, 18 derive from it.
- **Tier:** CROWN (bank verdict — F12 is stated as an outperforming principle and F4/F5/F6 are multi-trade FINDINGS; the gallery-caption item remains CANDIDATE inside the entry).
- **Deep read:** structure-uiux/00-conversion-anatomy.md (§2, findings F4/F5/F6/F12/F13). **Code:** none.

## [BANK] Anatomy §3 — Offer / CTA systems (F7, F8, F9, F10, F14, F15, F16) — library (structure-uiux/00-conversion-anatomy.md §3)
- **Reference source:** Green Conception; Hippo; Install-It-Direct; A.B. May; Service Experts; Neil Kelly; Austin Pro; System Pavers; Paverston; DaBella; Erie; Elbaz; CMK; Richard Lusk; Harmony Basements; Phoenix Home Remodeling; Gilk; OHi; Michael Nash; PHS Renovations; Home Gyms Design; LYKORA; Coldwells Build; Augusta Lawn Care; TruGreen; Abodu (evidence levels in the entry).
- **How it looks:** The offer layer of a winning page: a price-transparency device in one of five ranked forms, an us-vs-them comparison table early, a primary offer worded as a free named next step whose consultation produces a NUMBER, financing as its own section, published money mechanics (schedules, penalties, retainers), and productised offers — named plans/designs with from-prices.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion (offer structures and copy systems).
- **Mechanism & key values:** **F7** Price transparency, forms ranked: (a) instant/no-gate quote — Green Conception: address only, NO name/email/phone, price on screen, cash/financed/monthly (OPENED); (b) published price ranges — Install-It-Direct verified on the live homepage: paver patios $21–$36, driveways $25–$40, pool decks $20–$45, turf $13–$25, gravel $3–$8 /sq ft; $25,000 minimum in the guarantee clause; (c) published plan/coupon pricing — A.B. May $14.95/$70/$80 per mo; Service Experts $0 diagnostic w/ repair, $49 tune-up; (d) pricing as top-nav + fixed-price explainer (Neil Kelly); **(e) STRONGEST — publish your own invoiced distributions (Austin Pro): 415 priced siding jobs 2022–2026, median band $10k–$15k, middle-half $5k–$20k, per-project price bands on before/after pairs, sample caveat printed on the page** — "Ranges are estimates; distributions are evidence." **F8** Comparison table early (System Pavers section #2; Green Conception's competitor-quote candour block $13,585 → $26,400 competitor final vs $13,585 in writing). **F9** Primary offer = free named next step (Free Design Consultation is the GC/remodeling standard; emergency trades use Book Online / "pick your visit time — no voicemail"). **F10** Financing as a section/nav item; strongest form: Elbaz places financing BEFORE the gallery with 4 named lenders (Service Finance, Synchrony, Ygrene, Renew Financial), "$0 down, 12–240 month terms", soft-check "Check If You Qualify" CTA. **F14** The winning consultation PRODUCES A NUMBER (Lusk: site visit → detailed scope + budget before design begins; Harmony: line-by-line pricing before you leave; Neil Kelly: home visit ends with a rough budget range). **F15** Published money mechanics: Neil Kelly retainers ($2,000 schematic credited; 5–10% design development), payment schedule 50/40/10, phase timelines 30–44 wks; Harmony **$250 paid to the client for every day late** + $5M liability + 2026 pricing per 1,000 sq ft ($53,500/$89,200/$123,500); OHi ladder (retainer = 5% of high-end ballpark, 30% deposit, final 5%); PHS warranty CLOCK ("You sign off when you are happy, not when we are finished. That signature starts your 2-year warranty"); Home Gyms price-lock in writing; LYKORA "Final 250-point inspection" handover protocol. **F16** Productised offers: Coldwells 8 named Passivhaus designs, from-prices £214k–£311k; Augusta's full published rate card (mowing $40/$50/$80 by lot size); Home Gyms per-piece list repricing live by finish (nine pieces £799–£5,990) + "Add to enquiry" cart; PHS per-service Investment + Timeline (kitchens from $44,499 / 4–8 wks; whole-home $75k–$200k+ / 3–6 mo); LYKORA numbered price sheets (LK-PR-01 Essential 9,500 MAD/m² / LK-PR-02 Premium 15,000 MAD/m² / LK-PR-03 Exclusive contact-only; add-ons KNX +65K, epoxy +30K MAD).
- **Best for:** Offer/CTA, pricing and process sections on every trade page; checklist items 6, 7, 9, 15, 16, 17, 21–24 derive from it.
- **Tier:** CROWN (bank verdict — the file ranks F7's forms with (e) as strongest, and F14/F15/F16 are multi-firm OPENED + SOURCE findings).
- **Deep read:** structure-uiux/00-conversion-anatomy.md (§3, findings F7/F8/F9/F10/F14/F15/F16). **Code:** none.

## [BANK] Anatomy §4 — Quote-form patterns — library (structure-uiux/00-conversion-anatomy.md §4)
- **Reference source:** System Pavers; Green Conception; Paverston; DaBella; Install-It-Direct; TruGreen; Hippo; Augusta (evidence levels in the entry).
- **How it looks:** The quote path starts with the lowest-friction first field that exists — a zip code, a property address with NO contact details, or a photo upload — and the same hero form repeats down the page; where price stays gated, a problem-picker quiz becomes the quote path and ends in a recommendation.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion (form/lead-path patterns; the quiz flow is step-by-step selection → recommendation in under 2 minutes, TruGreen as recorded).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Lowest-friction first field wins: zip (System Pavers, EXCERPT); address only, no contact details (Green Conception, OPENED); photo upload → estimate (Paverston, EXCERPT). Hero form repeated: DaBella's free-quote form in hero and 3× down the page (OPENED). Minimum-project qualifier published in FAQ (Install-It-Direct $25,000) — CANDIDATE for high-ticket trades, wrong for emergency trades. Problem-picker quiz (TruGreen, OPENED): pick lawn problems → plan recommendation in under 2 minutes. Resumable quote + attribution (Green Conception, SOURCE-VERIFIED): gc-lead.js stores utm + referrer class (incl. AI sources) in localStorage, attaches it to quote leads, resumes unfinished quotes — "the most stealable small-firm lead-tech pattern in the bank." Call tracking standard at the top: CallRail on Hippo and Augusta (SOURCE-VERIFIED); GTM effectively everywhere.
- **Best for:** Forms/quote sections in every trade template; pairs with the budget-radio form pattern (pattern library) and checklist items 3 and 6.
- **Tier:** STRONG (bank verdict — the resumable-quote pattern is the file's own "most stealable" call; the section is labelled "early data" and the minimum-qualifier stays CANDIDATE, hence not CROWN overall).
- **Deep read:** structure-uiux/00-conversion-anatomy.md (§4). **Code:** reverse-engineering/trade-site-sources/gc-lead.js (Green Conception's lead script, held in the roofing pack per MAP).

## [BANK] Anatomy §5 — Review systems — library (structure-uiux/00-conversion-anatomy.md §5)
- **Reference source:** Stronghold Roofing; Strike Force HVAC; Dr. Roof; Expo HVAC; Hippo; One Hour; Jackson Design (evidence levels in the entry).
- **How it looks:** Reviews run as a system: live dated feeds instead of a stale wall, platform names attached (Google dominant), and AggregateRating schema in the page source so stars appear in search results before the click.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion (data/schema systems; feeds show recency — reviews dated days ago at Hippo/One Hour).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Platforms seen: Google (dominant, live feeds), Yelp, BBB, Houzz, Angi, HomeStars (CA). Deepest non-platform system: Jackson's named+photo+project-scope testimonials (OPENED). Review schema (SOURCE-VERIFIED): JSON-LD AggregateRating in homepage source at Stronghold Roofing (4.9/500), Strike Force HVAC (4.9/194), Dr. Roof (5/372), Expo HVAC. Template rule as recorded: ship LocalBusiness + AggregateRating schema with the client's REAL numbers. Warning as recorded: a stale testimonial wall reads older than no wall.
- **Best for:** Proof/reviews sections and the SEO layer of every trade template; checklist item 18 derives from it.
- **Tier:** STRONG (bank verdict — source-verified schema rule with exact recorded ratings; section labelled "early data").
- **Deep read:** structure-uiux/00-conversion-anatomy.md (§5; builds on §2 findings F5/F6/F13). **Code:** none.

## [BANK] Anatomy §6 — Sticky-call & persistent contact — library (structure-uiux/00-conversion-anatomy.md §6)
- **Reference source:** Bone Dry Roofing; A.B. May; Neil Kelly; Jackson; Power Home Remodeling; Tecta America (OPENED, per Lane 2 notes as recorded).
- **How it looks:** A call/quote path that never leaves the screen: sticky "GET A FREE QUOTE + CALL TODAY" with the number, a mobile sticky bar (Text / Call / BOOK NOW), the phone number carried in the nav.
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll → the sticky bar/button persists through the whole page; on mobile the Text / Call / BOOK NOW bar stays thumb-reachable.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Bone Dry Roofing: sticky GET A FREE QUOTE + CALL TODAY with number. A.B. May (HVAC): mobile sticky bar Text / Call / BOOK NOW + mobile popup form. Neil Kelly: nav carries Get Started + phone number. Jackson: phone in nav/footer + consultation CTA repeated. Recorded counter-examples: nationals with NO phone/quote CTA in page text (Power Home Remodeling; Tecta America footer-only number) underperform on direct response. Section status as recorded: "[AWAITING: mobile sticky bottom bars per trade, chat widgets.]"
- **Best for:** Navigation + mobile chrome of every trade template; checklist item 10 derives from it; pairs with the pattern library's Persistent Contact button.
- **Tier:** STRONG (trade fit — consistent OPENED evidence; the file marks the section still awaiting per-trade mobile data).
- **Deep read:** structure-uiux/00-conversion-anatomy.md (§6). **Code:** none.

## [BANK] Anatomy §7 — Service-page pattern (incl. before/after slider status per trade + timed process) — library (structure-uiux/00-conversion-anatomy.md §7)
- **Reference source:** System Pavers; Neil Kelly; Bone Dry; Hippo; Jackson; Elbaz; CMK; Phoenix; CRD; Green Conception; Richard Lusk; TruGreen; Austin Pro (evidence levels in the entry).
- **How it looks:** One page per service plus genuinely local location pages (local rules, permits, climate — never city-swap), a portfolio split by type and style, a before/after drag slider where the trade expects one — in siding carrying a price band per pair — and a process whose stages carry calendar time.
- **Frame by frame:** Before/after slider: visitor drags the divider → the after image is revealed over the before image in proportion to the drag (Elbaz's are keyboard-accessible, OPENED). Other elements static.
- **Mechanism & key values:** National pattern: one page per service × location pages (Bone Dry 20-location router). Local content rule: Hippo's town pages (local insurer rules, tear-off rules) vs System Pavers' city-swap pages — flagged as the thing NOT to copy. Jackson: services split into 10 pages + portfolio by type AND style. **Slider status per trade:** REMODELING standard at the top (Elbaz draggables keyboard-accessible; CMK custom CSS slider in Bricks; Phoenix; CRD component in source). ROOFING present at Green Conception (custom-built). LANDSCAPING ABSENT at the high end — substitutes are Lusk's before/construction/finished VIDEO case study and TruGreen's labelled with/without gallery; recorded open flank: a landscaping template with a working slider beats most of that market on one feature. CONCRETE labelled galleries standard. **SIDING strongest form in the bank: Austin Pro's draggable pairs carry a per-project PRICE BAND (showcase job: siding portion $25k–$30k)**. PLUMBING: the slider is not the trade's interactive — the phone path is (§8). **Timed process:** Elbaz Week 1 → Permitting Weeks 6–12; Neil Kelly phase weeks; untimed processes scored lower everywhere.
- **Best for:** Service/location page architecture and the work/gallery interactive choice per trade; checklist items 4 and 12 relate.
- **Tier:** CROWN (bank verdict — Austin Pro's price-banded slider is the file's "strongest form in the bank," and the city-swap prohibition is a bank ruling).
- **Deep read:** structure-uiux/00-conversion-anatomy.md (§7). **Code:** none (CMK's slider is a custom CSS component in Bricks, per the entry).

## [BANK] Anatomy §7b — Tech & motion reality at the trade top tier (F17, F18) — library (structure-uiux/00-conversion-anatomy.md §7b)
- **Reference source:** Lane 2 source pass (12 sites, incl. Stronghold Roofing); Lane 5 GC source pass (5 deeps + 20-homepage census, incl. Sebby Homes, CQC Home, Hasler Homes); Lane 3; AirWorks Solutions; LYKORA; BOWA; Jackson (all SOURCE-VERIFIED as recorded).
- **How it looks:** What the winning trade sites actually run: near-zero scene animation — small CSS transitions, a carousel, maybe one marquee and video — on stacks from hand-built static to WordPress+Elementor, with page weight as the real tax.
- **Frame by frame:** The recorded trade motion family: enter/exit .15s ease · accordion .2–.28s ease-out · scale-in .18s ease-out · marquee 60s linear infinite (Stronghold's exact system, SOURCE-VERIFIED).
- **Mechanism & key values:** **F17 THE TRADE MOTION CEILING: nobody at the top of any trade runs GSAP/WebGL scene animation.** Stronghold's beziers: cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1) and (0,0,.2,1); Swiper/Slick carousels; one marquee; video. GC census (all 20 shortlist homepages): GSAP+ScrollTrigger at exactly ONE firm (Sebby Homes — deep-read 28/35 with Proof 3/CTA 3: no reviews, no licence, no pricing device); Lenis at two; Swiper at four; no animation library at the other 13 — "In GC, GSAP-grade craft and top-tier conversion have not been found in the same firm — the template opportunity is to be the first." Two v0.4 exceptions, both planned-purchase side, both Lane-5-verified: AirWorks (GSAP-architected motion with a CSS backstop, deferred-loaded) and LYKORA (GSAP ×39 on a 127KB custom build with complete conversion systems). Refined rule as recorded: dose GSAP craft at reveal level (0.15–0.3s ease-out family, carousels, one signature interactive per page) — never scene pages or loaders. **F18 Stack is not the ceiling; weight is the tax:** winners run hand-built static (Lusk ~50KB HTML; Coldwells 6 scripts/1 stylesheet), WordPress+Elementor (Hippo, Elbaz, KBF), Bricks, Next.js, franchise platforms. Cautionary weights: Expo 2.03MB HTML, Elbaz 1.14MB + 53 scripts + 8 videos, KBF 391KB, Phoenix 1.0MB; lightest deep: Murray Lampert 122KB.
- **Best for:** The motion/weight budget for every trade build — the governing constraint the portfolio craft is dosed against; checklist items 19 and 20 derive from it.
- **Tier:** CROWN (bank verdict — a source-verified, three-lane finding stated as the file's template rule).
- **Deep read:** structure-uiux/00-conversion-anatomy.md (§7b, findings F17/F18). **Code:** none.

## [BANK] Anatomy §8 — What differs per trade, and why (all eight trade rows) — library (structure-uiux/00-conversion-anatomy.md §8)
- **Reference source:** The crowned/shortlisted firms per row (named in the entry); all rows OPENED + SOURCE via their lanes and Lane 5 QA, as recorded.
- **How it looks:** Not a visual pattern — the per-trade doctrine table the templates are built from: each trade's conversion machine is different, and mixing them is the recorded failure mode.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** **Roofing:** offer+proof IN the hero (instant estimate, licence, review count); fear-killer content converts (Hippo, Green Conception). **HVAC:** guarantee trademarks + coupon carousel + membership pricing; 24/7 Book Online urgency (One Hour, Service Experts, A.B. May). Crown FINAL dual: Strike Force (emergency model) + AirWorks (planned-purchase/interactive) under Cooling Co's overall-system crown. **Concrete/paving:** before/after is the product; price anchors + visualiser/photo-estimate accelerate; dual-route transparency (System Pavers 31; Install-It-Direct 29); ownable gap: instant-price + visualisation pairing (ResinPro). **GC/design-build (COMPLETE):** the transparency trade — pricing page with tiers + % breakdown, money mechanics published, licence linked to regulator, productised range cards; the design consultation must promise a number. **Landscaping (COMPLETE):** TWO machines, never mixed — (a) RECURRING (review volume + guarantee + first-visit discount + quiz flow; photography barely matters) vs (b) PROJECT (real photography + budget-before-design + licence + case studies); the before/after slider is the open flank in both. **Remodeling (COMPLETE, crown FINAL shared-by-role):** slider is table stakes; proof-before-services order; financing sold before scoping with named lenders; timed process; per-service cost tables; Elbaz + PHS co-skeletons, Home Gyms + LYKORA pattern sources (all four 31s QA-verified). **Plumbing (COMPLETE):** converts on the PHONE, not the form — Zoom Drain's homepage carries 14 tel: links (first at 10.2% of HTML, the earliest call path in the bank), zero animation libraries; Zebra Plumbing (32, lane high): 4 USP cards ($0 call-out fee, $50 online-booking credit), lifetime labour warranty; Matt Plumbing's steals: callback-within-an-hour hero CTA, 121KB/9-script discipline, never blend per-platform review scales. **Siding-windows (COMPLETE):** two crowns by role — Austin Pro (29) documented-project transparency; Feldco (28) tooling/video model; Allied (27, first reserve) anti-pressure system. Doctrine: siding converts on the QUOTE FORM (sticky "written quote" CTA), plumbing on the phone — reverse doctrines, confirmed across both trades.
- **Best for:** Choosing which conversion machine a template implements before any design work; the first read for any new-trade build.
- **Tier:** CROWN (bank verdict — the file's completed, QA-verified per-trade conclusions, crowns included).
- **Deep read:** structure-uiux/00-conversion-anatomy.md (§8, trade table). **Code:** none.

## [BANK] Roofing industry report (roofing.md) — library / report file-level entry (roofing pack)

- **Reference source:** None recorded (bank-internal compilation; every firm's own URL is inside the report).
- **How it looks:** Not a design — a scored research report: a 21-firm scored shortlist table (0–5 × 7 dimensions, /35), five rebuild-grade DEEP teardowns, a ★ TOP 1% crown section, an 8-point template steal-stack, then wave addenda (waves 2–21) each recording crown adjudications and newly banked mechanics.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion (document).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Core scan: 109 firms logged, 107 opened and judged (2 dead). Final census after all waves: **798 distinct roofing companies opened across 21 waves** (642 with parseable scores; median 21/35; ≥30 = 17 firms; 99 shortlist firms ≥27). Scoring frame: judged as a homeowner on a phone — real work, proof everywhere, clear offer, phone/quote path in seconds; a high-tech agency look is explicitly NOT credited as trade fit. Scan closed at a final plateau after two consecutive flat waves (20 and 21).
- **Tier:** CROWN (the report's adjudication is the bank's roofing verdict of record).
- **Crown adjudication (final):** #1 Stronghold Roofing FL (33/35) — never out-scored in 21 waves. #2 small-firm crown: West London Roofing (31/35) — tied five times (Quantock, Roofline, Oslo Takmester, Moderna Tak, Complete Roofing FL) and never out-scored; every tie broke on the same line: the counted, displayed, third-party review aggregate, which no challenger matched alongside equal craft + pricing. The market law: across 798 firms on six continents, displayed review volume, published pricing, verifiable licence and interactive craft almost never coexist on one homepage.
- **Steal-stack (the report's template synthesis):** (1) hero proof strip ABOVE the headline → trademark-style claim or honesty headline → funnel step 1 or Call/WhatsApp at equal weight; (2) a NAMED free offer with a dollar value and a number, priced in writing; (3) licence linked to the official record + Verify links, review count in the page title, JSON-LD AggregateRating; (4) honesty block ("If you don't need a new roof, we'll tell you — in writing") + why-we're-cheaper FAQ; (5) real job photos captioned by town/postcode + process-story sequence + live review feed; (6) fear-killer (local firm-death/longevity stat, or insurance help proven by reviews); (7) motion budget from Stronghold's CSS (reveals .15–.28s ease-out, one 60s project marquee, before/after drag slider); (8) plumbing: call tracking + first/last-touch attribution (Green Conception's gc-lead.js pattern) feeding the CRM.
- **Best for:** the roofing template skeleton as a whole; any roofing build's section order, proof placement and offer architecture.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/structure-uiux/roofing.md (whole file). **Code:** none.

## [BANK] Stronghold Roofing — DEEP 1 (roofing.md)

- **Reference source:** https://strongholdroofing.com/
- **How it looks:** Hand-built static page, font Archivo. Top to bottom: third-party claim banner ("Rated #1 for Roofing Price in Central Florida") → a proof strip sitting ABOVE the headline (4.9★ · 500+ reviews · GAF Master Elite (Top 2%) · Licensed CCC1331698 · 4,386 Florida Roofs) → headline "A Better Roof. A Lower Quote." with the subhead "Florida's top 2% GAF roofer. Straight answers, no pressure. If you don't need a new roof, we'll tell you." → the hero is funnel step 1 ("Step 1 — Select your roof type (~60 sec)") with a phone fallback → stat repeat (4,386 Florida Roofs) → project gallery of real homes → Free Roof Plan™ value stack → "Prove it" price-match challenge → 4-step zero-surprises process → why-we're-cheaper FAQ → warranties → financing → real team photo → dual close (Call 24/7 / Call me back). County pages repeat the stack with a monthly-payment slider.
- **Frame by frame:** Motion inventory taken from its CSS (source-verified): elements enter/exit at .15s ease; accordions open over .2–.28s ease-out; scale-in at .18s ease-out; the project gallery runs as a continuous marquee, 60s linear infinite; caret-blink 1.25s; pulse 3s. No GSAP, no Lenis — CSS only, dosed like a tool, not a show.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Tailwind v4, single 210KB CSS file, hashed webp assets, GTM-TRJWWKX; easing cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1). Proof system: licence number as a hero element; JSON-LD AggregateRating 4.9/500 in source (stars also show in Google results). Offer: Free Roof Plan™ itemised value stack — $395 drone inspection + $250 written line-by-line scope + $500 insurance documentation + $150 wind-mitigation filing + 3-quote comparison + $0-down financing + Golden Pledge eligibility = "$1,295+ value → $0". Price-match issued as a dare ("already have a quote? Bring it. We'll price the exact same scope, line-by-line"). Honesty promise in writing "even if it costs us the job." Financing $0 down to 84 months, no prepayment penalty. Warranties tiered: Silver 10yr / Golden Pledge 25yr / metal 45yr. Phone 863-225-8482 ("we'll figure it out in 60 seconds").
- **Tier:** CROWN — the report's Crown 1 (overall system), 33/35, the highest score in the scan; "This is the conversion skeleton for the roofing template."
- **Best for:** hero (proof strip above headline + funnel step 1), offer/value-stack section, price-match dare, honesty block, why-we're-cheaper FAQ, motion budget for trade pages. Trade fit: exact — a real local roofer's homepage.

No animation libraries were detected in the source pass (no GSAP/Swiper/Slick/Lenis); the report's animation score of 3/5 is a text-structure inference from the slideshow mechanism, not a measured behaviour. - **Best for:** hero (exclusivity-led, no-offer hero as a deliberate contrast model), process (the named 4-step process as a homepage spine), proof/reviews (one featured project told as a full story with a name and a place, above any review grid), navigation / service-page architecture (product-type × option matrix — every service page answers style + colour + hardware + glass). First pass: 37 opened/logged (36 scored + Alure), shortlist 20, deeps 5; the 200 floor was passed at Wave 26 (202 firms); the lane closed after two consecutive null waves (W30 + W31) under the stop rule. Scoring: 0–5 each on Design craft / Animation / Proof & trust / CTA & conversion / Mobile (inferred from structure) / Speed-feel / Trade fit = /35. Funnel verdicts that recur: this trade converts on the quote form, not the phone (best first-tel: position in the deep set 3.1% of HTML, but only ×2 links; best tel: count ×5); no GSAP anywhere in the deep 5; stacks are stack-independent (Sitecore / custom / Contentful / HubSpot / WordPress — WordPress at a crowned site). **Crown adjudication, final as filed:** the original crowns (Crown 1 Feldco 28, Crown 2 Allied 27) were superseded by a ratified lead update after the waves — **Crown 1 = Austin Pro Siding, Windows & Roofing (Austin, TX), 29/35**, the documented-project transparency model (886 documented projects; 415 priced siding jobs 2022–2026 with a published $10k–$15k median band; per-project price bands; draggable before/after pairs with per-project cost; a 312-point project map; worked APR financing examples — 0%/24mo, 4.99%/60, 7.99%/120 → $181.91/mo on $15k; Hardie Elite Preferred + President's Club 2025; source pass: Sanity headless, 221KB, tel: ×7 first at 19.4%, 38 price-range mentions, no animation libraries). **Crown 2 = Feldco 28** (tooling/video template model). Allied (27) stands displaced to first reserve, devices retained as steals. West Shore's challenge: closed, not upheld. Ties recorded without displacement: Canadian Choice 28, GP General Corp 28, North Knox 28, Tulsa Renew 28 (= Feldco); Window Source of San Antonio 27, Cornerstone Renovations 27 (= Allied). 24 firms ≥26 carry source passes. **Steal-stack (the cross-deep synthesis — what Asiful ships):** Allied's trust spine (price ranges, quote validity, disqualifier, geotagged projects) + Feldco's top layer (hero video, stat counters in trade units, visualizers) + West Shore's location skeleton (one page per town, 3 local facts) + Pacific's problem-trio opening, localised + Renewal's named 4-step process and product×option page matrix. CTA doctrine: sticky "Get my written quote" with the validity period in the button's subline; financing answered on-page in Expo's honest card format (from-$149/mo, same-day approval, all-credit) — never BOGO with labour excluded in fine print, never an up-to anchor against a stale price. Proof hierarchy that recurs at the top: installer-tier manufacturer status > review count with rating and source > geotagged projects > volume counters > awards; headline review claims must match footer/schema numbers (Thompson Creek's 71,000+ headline vs 4.5★/3,300 footer is the recorded cautionary tale).
- **Tier:** CROWN (as a source document) — this report is the bank's adjudicated best-evidence base for the siding/windows/doors industry: it holds both final crowns, the steal-stack synthesis, and the only full scan (248 firms) behind them.
- **Best for:** the starting document for any siding/windows/doors build — read it to choose which DEEP (or which crowned firm, Austin Pro via the challenge filing in the waves section) to model a section on, then deep-read that write-up and visit the firm's site. Playbook use: hero (Feldco video / Pacific problem-trio / Allied validity hero / Renewal exclusivity), proof/reviews (Allied + Austin Pro transparency systems), work/gallery (product + town project naming, before/after pairs with per-project cost), towns/areas (West Shore location skeleton), forms and call/CTA (quote-form-first doctrine, validity-period sticky CTA, tel: placement data from the source pass).
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/siding-windows-doors/structure-uiux/siding-windows.md (whole file). **Code:** none (the companion scan data lives in reverse-engineering/lane4-siding-scan.csv — indexed as its own chunk; a pre-normalization backup, lane4-siding-scan.pre-normalization-backup.csv, is also on disk).
# BANK-INDEX chunk — bank-lib-reports-remodeling

Scope: the DEEP firm write-ups inside the remodeling bank's two industry reports, three
file-level entries for the source files themselves, and one entry for the Lane 5 Segment A
top-8 list. File order: general contractors first, then the remodeling report.

File-name note: the reports live on disk as `structure-uiux/general-contractors.md` (Lane 5
general contractors) and `structure-uiux/remodeling.md` (Lane 3 remodeling — the single
report holding the kitchen/bath/whole-home/addition deeps), plus
`structure-uiux/lane5-partA-top.md` (the lane-5 top-8). No separate kitchens-bathrooms.md,
home-additions.md or lane5-design-ledger-top8.md files exist in the pack.

Honesty labels: both reports state that Animation / Mobile / Speed scores are
text-structure inferences from fetched page content (fetch impressions, not device lab
tests). Where a write-up records no motion parameters, the entry says so — no durations,
easings or timeline values are invented. Motion parameters are only stated where the
write-up's source pass found them in the site's own code.

Tier basis: the reports' own adjudications. Remodeling crown is SHARED BY ROLE (26 Oct
ruling): Elbaz Construction + PHS Renovations are co-template skeletons; Home Gyms Design +
LYKORA are crowned pattern sources; KBF keeps the originality crown. General-contractor
crowns: Neil Kelly (system crown) + Georgia Contractor Group (local-model crown), Murray
Lampert first reserve. PHS, Home Gyms and LYKORA appear in the remodeling report as wave
entries, not deeps, so they are covered in that report's file-level entry below.

## [BANK] Neil Kelly — deep-read / industry report DEEP 1 (remodeling pack: structure-uiux/general-contractors.md)
- **Reference source:** https://neilkelly.com/ (URL as recorded in lane5-partA-top.md; the GC deep itself does not print one)
- **How it looks:** A conversion system, not a brochure. The hero leads with an interactive project-picker (service / space / location) — the visitor configures their project before reading anything — under the headline "THE EASIEST WAY TO REMODEL, HONESTLY." and a subhead naming the three fears: "Straight talk on budget, timing, and risk." Directly under it, a stat bar: 80 Years / 30,000+ Projects / 5 Year Warranty / 4.6/5 from 2,200+ Reviews, repeated verbatim on subpages as a rhythm device. Then a numbered process 01–05, a 9-service grid with real photos and one-line plain descriptions, a counters row (Kitchens 1,500+ / Bathrooms 1,500+ / Repairs 10,000+ / Solar 2,500+), four "Why Neil Kelly" pillars, team, a Start My Project CTA and a "Not Sure Where to Start?" free-consultation block. Project pages are full case studies (Overview / Team / Key Facts table / Challenge / Solution); location pages form a service × location matrix, each with local design-centre address, hours, local phone and local permitting FAQ.
- **Frame by frame:** Motion is restrained and theme-level. Source pass: no animation library in the homepage HTML and no GSAP/ScrollTrigger/Lenis anywhere; the block-based Gutenberg theme's process block (view.js) uses IntersectionObserver scroll reveals, and the hero's view.js carries no animation library. So: visitor scrolls → process blocks reveal on intersection (parameters not recorded in the write-up) → everything else is static structure and copy. No timeline parameters exist in the source to copy.
- **Mechanism & key values:** WordPress, custom block theme (490 wp-content refs), 26 scripts / 19 stylesheets, HTML document 329KB. The pricing page is the deepest mechanism: kitchen tiers Refresh $55K–$130K / Replace $85K–$245K / Reimagine $175K–$385K+, "Most owners spend $140K–$190K", a trade-by-trade % breakdown at $150K (Cabinetry 40%, Countertops & Tile 20%, Plumbing & Electrical 15%, Demo/Drywall 12%, Framing 8%, Plans & Permits 5%), and a 4-stage precision ladder (Online Range → Consultation Range → Design-Phase Budget → Fixed-Price Contract). Process page publishes what competitors hide: home visit 60–90 min ending in a rough budget range; Schematic Design retainer from $2,000 credited to the project; Design Development retainer 5–10% of midpoint; payment schedule 50% signing / 40% construction start / 10% "when you're satisfied"; phase timelines Design 12–16 wks, Planning 6–8 wks, Construction 12–20 wks, total 30–44 wks; warranty explained as a 5yr/2yr structure; FAQ advises a 5% contingency. Proof = review volume (2,200+ reviews, 4.6/5). One recorded gap: no licence number found on the pages opened. Scored 30/35 (Design 5 / Animation 3 / Proof 5 / CTA 5 / Mobile 4 / Speed 3 / Trade fit 5).
- **Tier:** CROWN — the GC report's TOP 1% system crown; "for Asiful's GC template, Neil Kelly is the spine."
- **Best for:** GC and remodel homepage structure wholesale — hero project-picker, repeated stat bar, the pricing-page pattern (tiers + typical spend + % breakdown + precision ladder + objection-absorbing testimonials on the pricing page itself), a process page that publishes retainers, payment schedule and phase timelines, and explaining the "dead" planning gap instead of hiding it. Trade fit: large-project GC / design-build remodel.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/remodeling/structure-uiux/general-contractors.md (DEEP 1 — Neil Kelly). **Code:** none.

## [BANK] Georgia Contractor Group — deep-read / industry report DEEP 2 (remodeling pack: structure-uiux/general-contractors.md)
- **Reference source:** None recorded (the write-up names no URL; phone recorded as 770.549.5291, Atlanta GA)
- **How it looks:** Verifiability as the design principle. Positioning line "Designer-led vision · Master-builder execution" and "We design the homes *we build.*" — then, instead of a stock hero image, a "GCG at a glance" credential table acting as the hero's proof: founder name + role, building since 1998, both licence numbers, master-builder credentials, base + area, Houzz recognition. Below: 5 featured projects, each with a 30-second video tour and case-file metadata (Location / Project / Design: GCG / Construction: GCG); a 6-step process; a limited-intake "GCG difference" section; founder section; 3 services; reviews summary; "Where We Build" (16 named areas); testimonials; a "Reputation report"; schema-style FAQ; closing CTA.
- **Frame by frame:** Bundle-mined evidence only: CoBlocks scroll-reveal (coblocks-animation.js, IntersectionObserver-based) — visitor scrolls → elements reveal on intersection (parameters not recorded). The 30-second self-hosted MP4 project tours carry the rest of the motion. No GSAP/ScrollTrigger/Lenis anywhere in the build.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Credential table contents: company licence RLCO-003492, qualifying-agent licence RLQA-003511, NAHB Graduate Master Builder + CPHB, 22× Best of Houzz / 70 five-star Houzz reviews. Testimonials are named, project-tagged, platform-tagged and DATED (Houzz Jul 2025, Angi Jun 2026…), each linking out to the original review ("Follow each link to read the full review."). The Reputation report is an explicitly labelled AI-assisted synthesis (Claude, Anthropic; reviewed 14 Oct 2026) of their Houzz/Angi reputation — the only AI-disclosed reputation summary in 202 scans. Process: 01 Conversation & property review (investment + timeline discussed) → 02 Design & 3D visualization → 03 Scope & budget alignment ("before major commitments are made" — budget as its own named step) → 04 Selections & preconstruction → 05 Construction & communication (weekly updates promised) → 06 Quality review & completion. CTA is the softest of the five deeps — "Start with a conversation" (call / email / form) with scarcity framing ("We intentionally limit the number of custom homes we accept", twice); no pricing content, no lead magnet. Tech: WordPress, custom theme (gcg-static) + Beaver Builder + CoBlocks (the first pass's 198 "elementor" strings were WordPress core block-CSS selectors, corrected in the write-up); Google Fonts Bebas Neue + Jost + Poppins + Public Sans (4 families — "one too many"); 26 scripts / 9 stylesheets; HTML 178KB, the lightest US deep after Murray Lampert. Scored 30/35 (4/3/5/5/4/4/5).
- **Tier:** CROWN — the GC report's TOP 1% local-model crown: the version of top-1% a one-metro, founder-led firm (the size of Asiful's GC leads) can actually become in one rebuild.
- **Best for:** the glance-table credential block near the top of a homepage (licences + credentials + recognition in one scannable unit); testimonials that link to their dated originals; a 30-second video tour per portfolio project with case-file metadata; budget alignment as a named, separate process step. Not the CTA model — a colder prospect template needs a harder next step on top of it.

## [BANK] KBF Design Gallery — deep-read / industry report Deep 3 (remodeling pack: structure-uiux/remodeling.md)
- **Reference source:** https://www.kbfdesigngallery.com
- **How it looks:** An editorial, place-first homepage for Orlando, FL. Instead of a generic gallery, the hero idea is "The Neighborhood Drive": pick a neighbourhood, fly in on aerial imagery, and browse only projects actually built there (Winter Park 39 verified projects, Windermere 50+, Oviedo 50+). Then "Ledger / The Record" — a resale-proof section — categorised project galleries, process/warranty (5-year craftsmanship warranty via the Studio KBF page), and a consultation CTA. Copy is editorial and specific: "The pantry takes the mess; the kitchen keeps the manners." The map itself is the CTA — exploring it IS the engagement.
- **Frame by frame:** The signature motion is the aerial fly-in map navigation: visitor picks a neighbourhood → the view flies in on aerial imagery → that area's projects are browsed in place. It is a real custom build inside Elementor (source shows id=neighborhoods, fly-hud, chapter rail — not a stock widget). Lottie animations are present (Elementor lottie config) and Swiper is loaded; the rest is a long-scroll editorial rhythm. The report labels the inventory "inferred from structure" — no motion parameters are recorded.
- **Mechanism & key values:** The Ledger is the most original proof system in the entire Lane 3 scan: it tracks resales of KBF-remodelled homes — of 13 tracked resales, 9 ranked top-3 ever sold on their street and 7 were #1 — verified against county deeds, with the printed caveat "We don't claim our remodel caused it." (the write-up notes the caveat is what makes it believable). Backed by 1,000+ projects since 2003 and 4.8 stars / 63 reviews. Tech (source-verified 26 Oct): WordPress + Elementor 4.2.4 + HubSpot + Breeze cache; the page is enormous — 391KB HTML and 50+ images — giving Speed-feel 2 and Mobile-feel 3. Scored 29/35 (Design 5 / Animation 5 / Proof 5 / CTA 4 / Mobile 3 / Speed 2 / Trade fit 5), and tied at 29 by later specialist waves without being beaten on originality.
- **Tier:** CROWN — the originality crown; the report's TOP 1% #2 and the proof layer of the template synthesis (its core device is replicable by any remodeler with 15+ local jobs, unlike prestige award walls).
- **Best for:** proof that is checkable against a public record (deeds, permits, inspection pass rates) — one verified claim beats fifty testimonials; place-first portfolio browsing; the honest caveat line next to a big claim. Not the weight: ship the map idea as a lightweight neighbourhood index with counts and links, not a 50-image fly-in, on any template that must load fast on phones.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/remodeling/structure-uiux/remodeling.md (Deep 3 — KBF Design Gallery). **Code:** none.

## [BANK] Phoenix Home Remodeling — deep-read / industry report Deep 4 (remodeling pack: structure-uiux/remodeling.md)
- **Reference source:** https://phxhomeremodeling.com/ (write-up opened the Tempe kitchen service page, parent direct — the service page is documented as the system)
- **How it looks:** A service page run as a full conversion system: problem-led headline (1970s closed galley kitchens) → the risk-removal headline "See the Finished Layout in 3D Before Any Work Starts" with bullets (3D approved before demolition · fixed price confirmed after design, not before · dedicated PM · in-house certified designer) → services grid → quote offer bundled with 4 free homeowner guides → credentials stack → cost section → a named recent project with address-level specificity → a "why us" section arguing price-after-design → four video testimonials → before/after slider section → 4-step process → service-area map → FAQ with real numbers.
- **Frame by frame:** Minimal motion — a before/after slider interaction plus video; the persuasion is informational, not motion-led. Source-verified on the homepage: Slick + a before-after library are confirmed in source, and the four testimonials are Vimeo embeds. No motion parameters are recorded in the write-up.
- **Mechanism & key values:** The price-after-design argument as a named section — price is fixed AFTER 3D design (Feasibility/Planning/Design runs 3–5 weeks, price set at the end), converting the industry's #1 fear (bait pricing) into the reason to choose them. Published numbers: kitchens $50K–$150K (page FAQ: $50K–$100K typical), primary baths $40K–$75K, kitchen construction timelines 4–7 weeks, change-order rate claimed at 2.1% vs an industry 20–32%. Proof: 4.9 stars across 200+ reviews, BBB A+, NARI + NKBA, Best of Houzz Service 2020–2026, Nextdoor Favorite 2022–2025. Process: Discovery Call → In-Home Assessment → Feasibility/Planning/Design → Construction, with BuilderTrend portal updates; 2-year warranty. Lead magnet: quote request bundled with 4 guides (Kitchen Remodel Playbook, Avoid Bathroom Pitfalls, Avoid Hiring the Wrong Contractor, Contractor Scorecard — the scorecard lets a prospect grade competitors with Phoenix's ruler). Tech (source-verified 26 Oct): WordPress 7.1.3; 1.0MB HTML; the Tempe page runs 766+ fetch lines of SEO depth. Shortlist axes: Design 3 / Animation 2 / Proof 5 / CTA 4 / Mobile 3 / Speed 3 / Trade fit 5.
- **Tier:** STRONG — a Top-5 deep whose systems (price-after-design, cost tables, guide bundle) are named steals in the report's template synthesis; design and animation craft are its weak axes.
- **Best for:** the price-after-design argument as a named section on any design-build page; per-service cost + timeline tables on every service page; the guide-bundle lead magnet with a Contractor Scorecard. Not the page length — a homepage template should carry the headline system and ONE cost table and push the rest to service pages.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/remodeling/structure-uiux/remodeling.md (Deep 4 — Phoenix Home Remodeling). **Code:** none.

## [BANK] Harmony Basements — deep-read / industry report Deep 5 (remodeling pack: structure-uiux/remodeling.md)
- **Reference source:** https://harmonybasements.ca/services/ (services page full-opened; pricing figures are from the firm's own cost page as search-captured — the evidence split is stated in the write-up)
- **How it looks:** A specialist basement firm's services page built as a drumbeat of five hard promises, repeated verbatim at every scroll depth: lifetime workmanship warranty · $250 paid to the client for every day late · $5M liability insurance · 6× HomeStars Best of Award · Vaughan design centre. The design session is sold as ending with line-by-line pricing before you leave — the consultation produces a number, not a follow-up promise. A published-pricing page and a cost calculator sit beside it, and the page closes on the lifetime warranty.
- **Frame by frame:** No motion recorded in the write-up — no animation devices are documented for this firm; the report's Animation score (3) is a text-structure inference, not a measured behaviour. Static — no motion recorded.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Contractual proof, not decorative proof. Published 2026 pricing for a 1,000 sq ft basement: $53,500 finished living space / $89,200 full renovation / $123,500 legal apartment, with a $42,000 minimum — price bands for a STANDARD unit so prospects can self-qualify. The calculator is source-verified as a real destination: /basement-cost-calculator/ is linked from the services page ("most comprehensive basement cost calculator in Canada"). Tech: WordPress. Shortlist axes: Design 4 / Animation 3 / Proof 5 / CTA 5 / Mobile 4 / Speed 4 / Trade fit 5. Recorded cautions: HomeStars is a Canadian platform (swap for Google/Houzz in the US), and the penalty must not be imported unless the client's operations can actually honour it — a broken penalty promise is worse than none.
- **Tier:** STRONG — the specialist machine's exemplar in the remodeling Top 5; its lateness penalty is named in the write-up as the single most transferable trust device in this chunk.
- **Best for:** a lateness penalty with a dollar figure (a US version can use a smaller, survivable number); published price bands for a standard unit (per 1,000 sq ft / per room); repeating guarantees verbatim at every scroll depth — repetition of promises, not of adjectives; warranty as the closing headline.

## [BANK] General Contractors industry report (Lane 5) — library / report file (remodeling pack: structure-uiux/general-contractors.md)
- **Reference source:** None recorded (bank-internal report; each deep's own source is in its entry above)
- **How it looks:** The Lane 5 general-contractors report as a whole document: a scored shortlist table of 20 firms, five full deep write-ups plus the Sebby Homes expansion deep, a source pass (F12 fingerprint table) over all 20 shortlist homepages, the cross-deep verdict, and the two crown rulings. Weight spread across the shortlist is 53× (Gilk 19,852 bytes vs CQC Home 1,062,509 bytes of HTML) — the bespoke/static builds (Sebby, Gilk, ADD, Varcon, Aspen) are all ≤130KB, "hand-built is the speed pattern at every scale." Crown adjudication: Neil Kelly (system crown) + Georgia Contractor Group (local-model crown); first reserve Murray Lampert. Segment #1s: A (US national) Murray Lampert 29/35 · B (US regional) Georgia Contractor Group 30/35 · C (UK/IE) Coldwells Build 30/35 · D (AU/NZ/CA) Varcon Group 30/35. Cross-deep verdict / steal-stack: the five deeps split into the transparency machine (Neil Kelly, Murray Lampert — numbers, timelines, fixed price), the verifiability machine (Georgia CG, Jackson — checkable proof, sourced reviews, communication systems) and the product machine (Coldwells — priced designs, fixed price by construction); a top-1% GC template needs all three — published price logic + checkable proof + a productised offer shape. Pattern across the top 20: every 29–30 pairs a named, staged process with checkable proof (a licence number, a priced project, a dated review source, a current award for a named big project).
- **Tier:** CROWN — as a source document: it holds both GC crowns and the three-machine GC template verdict.

## [BANK] Remodeling industry report (Lane 3) — library / report file (remodeling pack: structure-uiux/remodeling.md)
- **Reference source:** None recorded (bank-internal report; each deep's own source is in its entry above)
- **How it looks:** The Lane 3 remodeling report as a whole document: the trade-split analysis, a scored shortlist of 20, sixteen expansion-wave addenda, the five full deep write-ups, the crown ruling, anti-patterns proven in the scan, and a 9-point template synthesis. Its opening doctrine: the trade splits in three and you pick the machine before the design — one-day bath / productised remodel (offer clarity), design-build (process clarity + proof depth; the Asiful template model), and specialist (niche authority + published numbers); mixing machines dilutes all three.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion (a report document). Its recorded motion position: the winning remodeling sites are motion-light — Elbaz is video-led with no GSAP/WebGL, CMK and Phoenix rely on drag sliders, KBF's signature is a fly-in map; heavy animation never carried a crown in 16 waves.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Scope: 836 firms scanned in lane3-scan.csv (opened 661, excerpt 120, no 55); 16 expansion waves; a bench of 8 exhausted names (CRD, BOWA, Case, Neil Kelly, West Shore, KOHLER Reveal, Normandy, Quartersawn) full-opened and re-scored — none out-scores Elbaz (31). Lane closed on plateau: Waves 15 + 16 consecutive no-change met the stop condition; nothing in 16 waves and 1,223 lane firms scored above 31/35 for remodeling. Crown adjudication (26 Oct ruling, decided under Asiful's delegation): the crown is SHARED BY ROLE — Elbaz Construction + PHS Renovations (31/35, Wave 14 tie; per-service from-pricing + timelines, drag slider, week-stamped design artefacts, warranty clock starting at client sign-off) are co-template skeletons (US + CA generalist systems); Home Gyms Design (31/35, Wave 10 tie; vertical integration with fully published package AND per-piece pricing plus an enquiry-cart builder) + LYKORA (31/35, Wave 11 tie; two published MAD/m² tiers, 250-point defect-check handover, render-vs-real proof pairs) are crowned pattern sources; KBF keeps the originality crown. Steal-stack (the report's template synthesis): 1) hero outcome promise + licence strip (Elbaz), one video max, poster-first; 2) proof bar — years / projects / rating / warranty — before services (CMK order); 3) before/after slider, real jobs only (Elbaz/CMK/Phoenix); 4) timed process with a price mechanism inside it (Elbaz weeks + Phoenix price-after-design + Case-style paid discovery as an option); 5) financing named, with lenders and a soft-check CTA (Elbaz); 6) place-first portfolio + one checkable claim with its caveat (KBF); 7) cost table per service (Phoenix/Huffmans) + guide/scorecard lead magnet (Phoenix); 8) warranty as headline + one contractual promise the client can honour (Harmony / OakWood tiered menu); 9) CTA = consultation or cost guide, never a bare contact form.
- **Tier:** CROWN — as a source document: it holds the shared-by-role crown ruling and the remodeling template synthesis.
- **Best for:** the remodeling template blueprint — read before building any remodeling homepage; its wave addenda are the widest evidence base in the bank for pricing-transparency, qualification-form and client-portal patterns, and its anti-patterns list (stock-photo portfolios, counters rendering 0, partner-only testimonials, inconsistent numbers, franchise sameness with no local layer) is a QA checklist.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/remodeling/structure-uiux/remodeling.md (whole file). **Code:** none.
