## [BANK] BUILDER BRIEF — the practical build manual from the research bank (structure-uiux/builder-brief.md)
- **Reference source:** None recorded — internal build manual, not taken from a live site. Sources it draws on: `proven-recipes.md` (45 test-built recipes R1–R45), `animation-parameter-library.md`, `3d-and-svg-library.md`, `ui-ux-patterns.md`, `00-conversion-anatomy.md` (findings F1–F18, 24-item checklist).
- **How it looks:** A document, not a page design — the operating manual a build session reads top to bottom before assembling any prospect homepage preview, trade template, portfolio demo site or Asiful's own site. Delivery model it governs: WordPress + Elementor Canvas, full-width container, zero padding, one HTML widget, one single-file build per page; previews live at builtbyasiful.com/<client-slug>.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (It *prescribes* motion; see Mechanism & key values.)
- **Mechanism & key values:**
  - **Authority (§0):** SKILLS-CATALOG.md is the highest authority on craft (read, never install); this brief governs bank-derived recipe choice, weight and trade conversion structure; Asiful's standing standards win over both. A pattern not in proven-recipes.md is untested — usable, but labelled untested and triple-checked.
  - **The page (§1):** a preview is the homepage of a future full website, not a landing page — full menu from the start, Services mega-menu listing all services, every future-page link just `#`. Default 12-step homepage order: nav with phone + quote CTA → hero (outcome/fear-relief headline, one-line proof strip, ONE low-friction entry) → named system/guarantee pillar → services → price-transparency device → Other-vs-Us comparison table (early) → proof (reviews, before/after, project work) → numbered timed process (3–5 steps) → financing → FAQ → closing CTA → directory footer. Hero images embedded base64 in the preview file.
  - **Recipe stack (§2), with as-shipped costs:** GSAP bought once per page — 115.6 KB min / 45.7 KB gzip shared load, never inlined per recipe. Service-page layer is vanilla: 5–16 KB per recipe, little/no JS, no library.
    - Hero: default **R33 Motion-clip proof hero** (~149 KB as files, JS 0.9 KB — 3–5 short muted looping clips/poster frames of real work, poster-first); **R31 Pin + parallax hero** (119.8 KB libs inlined = shared GSAP in production; phone variant unpinned by design); **R2 Masked word reveal** headline (4.4 KB + shared GSAP, hand-rolled splitter, no SplitText licence); **R3 Blur/rise text** (5.5 KB + shared GSAP, headlines only, modest word counts — variant A animates filter: blur(), the priciest paint); **R18 Rotating headline word** (4.0 KB, one word only); **R20 Count-up trust stats** (4.8 KB, final numbers in HTML as no-JS fallback); **R32 DOM-first WebGL headline** (595.4 KB, Three.js ≈589 KB — CAP: Asiful's own portfolio hero ONLY, never a prospect preview or trade template; real HTML text stays in the DOM).
    - Entrances/services: **R5 Role-grouped 4-step choreography** (4.9 KB — eyebrow → title → body → media, beats offset 0.08–0.12s in one timeline; the house section entrance); **R1 Direction-aware reveals** (5.0 KB — ±100px by scroll direction, 1.25s expo, overwrite auto, travel halved on mobile); **R4 Zero-JS scroll-timeline reveals** (4.0 KB, JS 0, enhancement layer only); **R45 Stacking service cards** (6.0 KB, core effect zero JS — CSS sticky; the default Services treatment); **R44 Chaptered page + anchor nav** (7.1 KB, 64px scroll-margin under sticky header); **R8 Morphing SVG separator + clip edge** (128.9 KB libs inlined = shared GSAP; production fix mandatory — last separator's morph completes only ~47% desktop / ~56% mobile, give it a taller following section or shift end to "bottom bottom"; paired d/data-path-to must keep identical command/point structure); **R39 MotionPath route divider** (97–120 KB band, hidden on touch, one per page max). Card groups always animate in staggered on scroll — never static.
    - Proof: **R28 Before/after slider** (7.7 KB, touch-first, drag handle, labels, keyboard arrows); **R29 Testimonial carousel** (10.3 KB — render cards in HTML in production, auto-advance + manual, pause on hover/touch); **R30 Comparison table Other vs Us** (7.9 KB, JS 0, placed early); **R13 Horizontal gallery + pagination** (5.9 KB + shared GSAP, desktop pinned track with progress + 01/0N counter; phone = native scroll-snap strip, no pin at ≤768px); **R10 Grid-to-fullscreen gallery** (97.2 KB GSAP inlined, DOM port no WebGL, phone fade/scale); **R34 Pixel-dissolve gallery** (596.0 KB — CAPS: desktop only, ≤6 images, one shared renderer, never the phone hero, plain <img> fallback in DOM); **R35 Distortion hover** (666.8 KB — CAP: desktop-only accent, touch = plain swap, never under a conversion-critical before/after); **R16 Seamless marquee** (6.1 KB, JS 0, duplicated track −50% loop; trade winners run 60s linear); **R42 Status & scarcity bars** (5.2 KB, honest availability only, static fallback date, never fake scarcity).
    - Form/pricing: **R21 Budget-radio quote form** (5.4–7.8 KB band, JS ≤1.9 KB — budget/job-size radios are the FIRST field, form qualifies the lead itself, carries a response-promise line, FormSubmit-compatible); **R22 Floating-label form kit** (input-then-label order, error states mandatory); **R23 CSS-only FAQ accordion** (zero JS, details/summary or checkbox + grid-rows height animation); **R24 Tier-pricing configurator** (tiers update summary price live, no-JS fallback shows static tiers); **R25 Modal kit** (focus trap + Esc mandatory); **R41 Frequency-toggle pricing** (6.2 KB, animated number swap); **R36 Colour customiser** (<11 KB, library-free, CSS/SVG tint swatches).
    - Nav/footer: **R26 Menu overlays + mega-menu** (15.7 KB, JS 2.1 KB — scroll-lock must release or QA fails outright); **R27 Filter pills with counts** (8.4 KB); **R43 Knowledge hub + directory footer** (7.9 KB, works with JS off, footer licence links to the regulator); **R19 Shuffle accent word** (4.1 KB) / **R17 Marquee along SVG path** (5.6 KB, needs fit()/path-rescale on mobile); **R37 CSS 3D card ring** (<11 KB, library-free, desktop jewellery only, unbroken preserve-3d chain); **R38 Draggable inertia row** (97–120 KB band, use Mode B — inertia without the Club plugin; keyboard path required).
    - **Evidence flag:** R21–R25 are source-audited, not device-rendered (weights measured, JS parses clean) — first production use of each gets a rendered pass at 375px + keyboard + reduced-motion. R1–R5 are code-inspection verified.
  - **Form doctrine per trade (§2.4):** emergency trades (plumbing, HVAC emergency, roofing repair) phone first, form second — first tel: link early in the HTML (bank's best 10.2% of document; Matt Plumbing's steal 6.2%); sticky mobile bar Call / Text / Book. Plumbing converts on the phone, siding converts on the quote form — reverse doctrines, both verified; siding gets a sticky "written quote" CTA. Lowest-friction first field wins (postcode/zip, property address only, or photo upload); Green Conception's no-gate form asks address and NO contact details before showing a price. The primary consultation must produce a NUMBER (F14).
  - **Motion ceiling (§3, finding F17):** trade winners do not run scene animation — CSS transitions 0.15–0.28s ease-out + one carousel + ONE signature interactive per page. Reference dose (Stronghold's production system): enter/exit .15s ease · accordion .2–.28s ease-out · scale-in .18s ease-out · marquee 60s linear · beziers cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1) and (0,0,.2,1). Three tiers: Tier 1 emergency/lead-gen (default for previews — CSS-family motion, no loaders/scene pages/WebGL, no pins except the signature story); Tier 2 planned-purchase (GSAP reveal-level allowed once conversion systems are complete — the bank's two verified exceptions, AirWorks and LYKORA, both carry full pricing/proof/process underneath; AirWorks defers GSAP with a CSS backstop); Tier 3 Asiful's own portfolio only (R31, R32, R34/R35 within caps, R6 blinds mask: 30 slits, stagger 0.02, scrub ~1 on mobile; R7 grid mask: 14 cols desktop → 6 mobile).
  - **GSAP parameters (§3, from the parameter library — do not invent):** reveals 0.4–0.8s; triggered motion expo/power2/power3 out; scrubbed motion linear ease always; staggers 0.02–0.12s, never larger; masked word reveal 0.6s expo.out, stagger 0.04–0.06, words start 64–70px under the mask, clearProps after; slide-up 0.8s power2.out, stagger 0.02, autoAlpha + yPercent; blur-in 0.4s power1.out, blur 10px→0, y 15px→0 (headlines only); R5 role beats 0.08–0.12s; R1's 1.25s expo is the one deliberate exception. Lenis, where used, feeds its rAF into the GSAP ticker. Touch/coarse pointers always get a separate, simpler path.
  - **Pin rules (§4):** the signature story (leaking-roof story, adapted per client) MUST pin on mobile — House Martin's proven configuration, mobile end ~235%, release verified by full 375px scroll-through every build. Stacking cards: never a GSAP pin (R45 CSS sticky). Pinned word-cycle headline R12 allowed (margin-manufactured spacing, finite end = words × 50%). Horizontal galleries: desktop pin proven (R13); phones get native scroll-snap; never ship a pinned horizontal on a phone. R31 phone variant unpinned. Lottie scrub R11 carries a ~250 KB lottie-web tax; under 749px its start is "center 45%". Any other pin needs a written reason + recorded 375px release test.
  - **Cost lab (§5, finding F18 — weight is the ceiling, not the stack):** trade template/preview target ≤330 KB HTML, aim at the 50–150 KB class (winners run ~50–330 KB; Lusk ~50 KB hand-built static is the model; Matt Plumbing 121 KB / 9 scripts is the template speed budget); >1 MB HTML needs explicit justification; ONE hero video, poster-first (R33 ~149 KB as files is the reference; 37-video heroes are an anti-pattern); GSAP 45.7 KB gzip once per page; Three.js ≈589 KB toll Tier 3 only; Lottie ~250 KB tax; service-page layer 5–16 KB per recipe. Ship rules: prefer the pattern that cannot trap phone scrolling; CSS sticky beats a GSAP pin; NEVER hide content in CSS (hidden start-states set by JS only, inside a prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference matchMedia branch — if JS fails, the page reads complete); no-JS fallback is structural (counters show final values, configurators show static tiers); reduced motion is a shipped feature with per-recipe recorded behaviour. Dropping Lenis where unneeded saved ~30 KB in testing.
  - **Standing standards (§6):** exact client logo, never redrawn/recoloured (Rule #1); never rotate a text-bearing element (a rotating .est badge was a real shipped bug — verify by numeric angle sampling after scroll round-trips); animation quality in the first brief at reference quality or better; personalisation scrub — search the whole file for the template's trade terms, town names, licence numbers, prices, company names before showing (a live template once shipped another trade's copy in its quote-form options); one consistent number everywhere (review count, years, job count — hero, proof, schema, footer must reconcile; F12).
  - **Checklist (§7):** the conversion anatomy's 24 items condensed, each either true on the page or a named deliberate exception — hero/offer (proof strip F1; outcome headline F2; low-friction entry F3; licence in first screen F11; consultation promises a number F14; price-transparency device F7; productised layer F16; money mechanics F15), proof (named system pillar F4; reviews platform+score+count separately F5/F6; reviews name operatives + AggregateRating JSON-LD F13; one claim checkable against a public record with honest caveat F12; invoiced distributions F7e; gallery photos real work and labelled so; comparison table early F8), structure (numbered process 3–5 steps WITH calendar time; warranty CLOCK stated — starts at client sign-off; design deliverables week-stamped; financing its own section + nav item on high-ticket trades F10; sticky call/quote path; live-repricing price list / enquiry cart F16; genuinely local service/location content, never city-swap), motion/weight (ceiling F17; weight audited F18).
  - **Anti-patterns (§8, all QA fails):** brand-first page with no phone/quote CTA; inflated unverifiable claims ("50 MILLION HOMEOWNERS"); stock imagery in process/portfolio sections; placeholder testimonials/headings/licence placeholders live; counters rendering 0 without JS; inconsistent numbers on one page; gate loaders / non-scrolling scene pages on a lead page; another trade's copy in form options; hidden content with no no-JS path; a pin that does not release; a menu scroll-lock that does not release.
  - **QA (§9):** triple-check — three independent different checks (build vs brief+checklist; fresh-eyes visual audit desktop + mobile; interactive scroll both ways, click everything, form path, menu, slider), animations frame by frame; re-check the whole page after EVERY change; mobile is its own pass (375px, pin releases, sticky bar, tap targets); reduced-motion pass; badge/rotation numeric check; numbers pass. Screenshot approval gate: screenshot EACH SECTION individually, desktop + mobile 375px, present to Asiful organised by section — no upload until screenshots approved.
  - **One-page summary (§10):** default hero R33 + R2 + R20 + proof strip (R32 portfolio only); entrance R5; services R45; proof R28 + R29 (HTML cards) + R30; form R21 + R22; footer R43; menu R26.
- **Best for:** the governing manual for every build session — read first, before shortlisting recipes or sections. Homepages and service pages for all trades; its tiers decide how much motion any given page may carry.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/roofing/structure-uiux/builder-brief.md (present in all four packs; recipe-stack tables §2.1–§2.5 carry ~43 rows). **Code:** none.

## [BANK] PORTFOLIO SITE PLAN — Six "Concept" Demo Sites (structure-uiux/portfolio-site-plan.md)
- **Reference source:** None recorded — internal plan document (written 26 Oct 2026 by the CEO merge, from the closed research bank: Lane 1 design bank + Lanes 2–5 industry files + 00-conversion-anatomy.md v0.4 + proven-recipes.md). Crown firms it builds from: Stronghold Roofing, West London Roofing, The Cooling Company, Strike Force HVAC, AirWorks Solutions, Champion Air, Richard Lusk, TruGreen, Elbaz Construction, PHS Renovations, Home Gyms Design, LYKORA, KBF Design Gallery, Zebra Plumbing, Zoom Drain, Austin Pro, Feldco, Allied Exteriors.
- **How it looks:** A document specifying six complete "Concept" demo homepages — one per trade — each a homepage of a future full website (full menu + Services mega-menu) forking from one shared conversion skeleton: hero proof strip → low-friction entry → named offer/system → proof → timed process → financing where relevant → FAQ → quote/call close. Every site is labelled "Concept" in header/footer and on its contact section; all numbers are structural placeholders (crown patterns transfer, crown numbers never do).
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Motion budgets prescribed: trade dose only — CSS-family reveals 0.15–0.3s ease-out, one carousel, ONE signature interactive per page; no loaders, scene pages, scroll gates or phone-trapping pins; GSAP one shared 45.7 KB gzip load; the ~589 KB Three.js recipes R32/R34/R35 are excluded from all six demos. R21–R25 used as specified but their rendered pass remains formally owed; R3 headlines-only per caveat C1. Every demo ships the preview-page tracking beacon + Green Conception first/last-touch attribution and resumable quote state.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Six site concepts, each with crown source(s), /35 score, US lead pool, steal-stack and recipe list:
  1. **Roofing** — pool 3,692. Crowns: Stronghold Roofing FL 33/35 (overall-system skeleton) + West London Roofing UK 31/35 (small-firm co-crown). Steals: proof strip ABOVE the headline (★ · count · licence · since-year); hero IS step 1 of a ~60-second quote funnel with Call/WhatsApp at equal weight; Free Roof Plan™ named offer (itemised stack $1,295+ → $0) + price-match as a public dare; honesty block "If you don't need a new roof, we'll tell you — in writing"; licence linked to the official record + Verify link on every credential; town/postcode-captioned job photos. Recipes: R33, R20, R16 (Stronghold's own 60s marquee), R21, R28, R45, R1, R5, R23, R26, R44.
  2. **HVAC TX/FL** — pool 1,351. Crowns by role: The Cooling Company 30/35 (overall system), Strike Force 31/35 (emergency), AirWorks 31/35 + Champion Air 31/35 (planned-purchase, independently identical bundle-builder calculators). Steals: two doors never mixed — emergency door ($79-pattern priced diagnostic, symptom picker "What's going on?" as first field, response deadline with money/minutes on it, three named promises "on every job ticket", separate after-hours number) and planned door (bundle-builder calculator: system picker with published ranges, "what can change your price" factors, financing picker, savings netted into "Effective net monthly"); published ranges in FAQ with honest APR; plan with published pricing; ONE review number identical in hero/JSON-LD/footer, rounded down (AirWorks' 1,132 shown as "1,000+"). GSAP only in the AirWorks manner — deferred-loaded with CSS backstop. Recipes: R24, R21, R27, R41, R42, R20, R45, R29, R23, R1, R26.
  3. **Landscaping incl. lawn + tree, FL** — pool 1,792. Crowns: Richard Lusk 33/35 (project — highest full-open score in Lane 3) + TruGreen (recurring). Completed by Augusta (only full published rate card in the national scan), Luv-A-Lawn, Monster Tree. Steals: model picker at top routes REC vs PROJECT (the lane's central finding — two machines, two paths); recurring formula "TruGreen's system + Augusta's rate card + Luv-A-Lawn's guarantee stack" (a combination no incumbent in 387 scanned firms fields): problem-picker quiz (<2 min) → published rate card by lot size → plan tiers → guarantee stack; project path (Lusk): complimentary visit that PRODUCES A NUMBER before any design (F14), "Budget first. Then design. Then build." 3-step process, three-stage case study (before → construction → finished); tree layer: certified-arborist estimates, line-item pricing on a tablet; the deliberate open flank — a working before/after drag SLIDER (no high-end landscaping site fields one). Recipes: R27, R41, R28, R33, R10, R13, R20, R45, R29, R23, R2, R26.
  4. **Remodeling** — pool 1,005. Shared crown by role (26 Oct ruling): Elbaz Construction Miami 31/35 + PHS Renovations Winnipeg 31/35 co-skeletons; Home Gyms Design UK 31/35 + LYKORA Morocco 31/35 pattern sources; KBF Design Gallery 29/35 proof-originality crown. Steals: Elbaz scroll order (outcome hero → licence in FIRST screen → before/after draggables → timed 8-stage process with week ranges → financing BEFORE gallery → reviews/projects → consultation CTA; Elbaz's video-everywhere weight 1.14 MB HTML / 8 videos cut ~80%); PHS Investment + Timeline figure on EVERY service card (Kitchens from $44,499 / 4–8 wks pattern), 3D render before demolition, week-stamped design artefacts, warranty CLOCK headline ("You sign off when you are happy… that signature starts your 2-year warranty"); Home Gyms per-piece price list repricing live by finish + "Add to enquiry" cart; LYKORA numbered per-m² pricing sheets, calculator with honest non-binding footnote, 250-point defect-check handover protocol (NOT copied: LYKORA's uncheckable "0% Budget Overruns"); KBF place-first portfolio + one deed-verifiable claim printed WITH its caveat (F12); Harmony per-day lateness-credit promise slot. Proof-before-services order (CMK). Recipes: R28, R24, R21, R27, R33, R20, R45, R29, R23, R44, R1/R2, R26.
  5. **Plumbing** — pool 828. Crowns: Zebra Plumbing Melbourne AU 32/35 (design system, lane high score) + Zoom Drain US 31/35 (emergency conversion). Doctrine is the REVERSE of siding: plumbing converts on the PHONE — the build is ordered around a sub-3-second call path. Steals: Zebra's hero-adjacent 4-card USP band (one card per fear, bespoke SVG icons, custom icon set for all 9 services — the single most transferable design asset in the plumbing scan); Zoom's problem-first H1 + symptom-chip selector (4–6 chips); quantified response promise in step 1 ("respond within 90 minutes" pattern) + tech text-ahead with name and photo; call-density standard measured in source — first tel: link inside the first ~6–10% of HTML (Matt 6.2%, Pimlico 6.8%, Zoom 10.2%), one identical number everywhere (Pimlico carries 32; Pimlico's three different numbers are the NOT-copy); Fallon's licence hyperlinked to the regulator's check page + published Good/Better/Best block; Benjamin Franklin $5-per-minute-late slot; Matt's 121 KB / 9 scripts / zero libraries as the demo's speed budget; platform scores + counts shown separately, never blended (Matt governance). Motion: none of the top tier uses GSAP/Lenis — GSAP reveals dosed 0.4–0.8s as differentiator only, never ahead of the call path. Recipes: R27, R30, R24, R21, R42, R20, R45, R29, R23, R4, R26.
  6. **Siding & Windows** — pool 963. Crowns: Austin Pro 29/35 (Crown 1, documented-project transparency) + Feldco 28/35 (Crown 2, tooling/video); Allied Exteriors 27/35 first reserve. **Site-6 verdict:** Siding beat Concrete & Paving (pool 1,000; System Pavers 31 + Install-It-Direct 29) — concrete won only the two margin criteria (+37 leads ~4%, +3 combined crown points) and lost the four structural ones: evidence form (Austin Pro's invoiced distributions — 415 priced siding jobs 2022–2026, published median band $10k–$15k, per-project price bands, F7 form (e), the strongest in the bank — vs concrete's published $/sq ft ranges, form (b)); visual demo power (177 draggable before/after pairs each carrying a price band vs concrete's partly unverified tooling — claimed tooling appears in ~7 of 358 scanned concrete firms); template reusability incl. into the live UK book (location-page skeleton = one page per town with local cost data + permit rule + housing-stock problem; siding scan itself contains UK operators Safestyle, CR Smith, Anglian); the ownable gap (instant price + visualisation in one flow — unshipped by any crown in either trade). Concrete banked as Site 7, phase 2, built immediately after the six, its patterns folded into Site 6 meanwhile. Steals: Austin Pro transparency spine (publish own invoiced distribution with the sample caveat printed; project map reconciling 312 mapped + "574 more" = 886 documented; product-choice statistics); Feldco top layer (real-work hero video, "since 1976" date doing the trust work, count-ups in trade units — sq ft of siding, referral section, 157 KB page weight as the efficiency benchmark); THE FLAGSHIP BUILD — instant pricing + visualisation in ONE flow (upload house photo → see it re-sided/re-windowed → ballpark band from published ranges, before any contact capture; built by fusing R36 + R24); Allied anti-pressure layer (published ranges with the factors that move them, quote-validity printed IN the hero — "written quote good for 30 days", disqualifier section "Are we the right fit?", repair-over-replacement honesty, projects/reviews named "Product + Town"); financing with a WORKED example (Austin Pro: $15,000 at 7.99% over 120 months = $181.91/mo, exact to the cent); West Shore location skeleton minus its 1.17 MB weight; Pacific problem-trio opening. This trade converts on the QUOTE FORM, not the phone (reverse of plumbing): sticky element = "Get my written quote" with validity in the subline; best-in-scan tel ×7 as backup. Motion: nobody at or above 26/35 in this trade loads GSAP/ScrollTrigger/Lenis — standard reveal family only. Recipes: R33, R28 (price band per pair), R36, R24, R27, R20, R30, R21, R29, R23, R45, R1, R26.
  - **Build order:** 1 Roofing (biggest pool, highest crown 33, Stronghold skeleton becomes the shared skeleton) → 2 Siding & Windows (flagship fused flow built second so its components exist before HVAC/Remodeling need them) → 3 HVAC TX/FL → 4 Remodeling → 5 Landscaping FL → 6 Plumbing (lightest build, smallest pool, blocks nothing). Phase 2: Site 7 Concrete & Paving.
- **Best for:** the build spec for the six portfolio demo sites (and Site 7 after them); each site's steal-stack and recipe list is the starting shortlist for that trade's homepage.

## [BANK] Lane 2 — Source-level (F12) findings, 26 Oct 2026 (reverse-engineering/lane2-source-findings.md)
- **Reference source:** None recorded — internal source-mining report. Sites mined at source level (live HTML + linked CSS/JS via curl, files in ./src/): Stronghold Roofing, Hippo Roofing, Green Conception, Erie Home, Dr. Roof, Nations Roof, The Cooling Company, Strike Force HVAC, Expo Heating & Cooling, Service Experts, Fox Service, One Hour + second batch (Evergreen Home Heating, London AirCon, Chills On Wheels, Advanced Air Home Services, Alliance Climate Control) + all remaining Top-20 shortlist sites (West London Roofing, Boardman, HHH, Greater Midwest, LOA, Indy Roof, Stay Dry, Interlock, Long Home, Bone Dry, Rogers, Bonner Built, CentiMark, A.B. May, Estes, Deljo, Horizon, Fallon Solutions, AC Installation London).
- **How it looks:** A findings document: a 12-row fingerprint table (stack / motion / tracking-CRM, proven from source not appearance), five source-level lessons, a second-batch addendum, and a 19-row Top-20 completion table including a schema-vs-marketing honesty column.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Motion evidence it records: trade top-tier motion is CSS transitions + carousels — see Mechanism & key values.)
- **Mechanism & key values:**
  - **Fingerprints (source proof):** Stronghold — custom static, Tailwind v4 (tw- CSS vars), single 210KB CSS, font Archivo, hashed Vite-style assets; NO GSAP/Lenis; CSS-only motion: enter/exit .15s ease · accordion .2–.28s ease-out · scale-in .18s ease-out · marquee-x 60s linear infinite (project gallery) · caret-blink 1.25s · pulse 3s · beziers cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1) / (0,0,.2,1); GTM-TRJWWKX; JSON-LD AggregateRating 4.9 / 500 in source. Hippo — WordPress + Elementor 4.1.4 (Asiful's exact stack), reviews-feed-pro plugin (17 refs), CallRail + GTM. Green Conception — hand-built static, Open Sans + Roboto Slab, own /assets/ hashed webp + SVG, custom before-after drag slider; GTM-NSG7TFT5 + own gc-lead.js: first/last-touch attribution in localStorage (utm + referrer class incl. AI sources) attached to quote leads + resumable quote state. Erie Home — WordPress (90 wp-content refs), Swiper (42 refs) drives review/service carousels, Birdeye-fed reviews. Dr. Roof — custom + Azure-blob CMS, video poster hero, JSON-LD 5 / 372. Nations Roof — HubSpot CMS, Swiper (16 refs). The Cooling Company — Next.js + Turbopack, Montserrat, framework motion only, no GSAP; GTM-5PRLN4M. Strike Force — Next.js + Turbopack (Vercel), real /photos/ via _next/image q75, framework motion only; JSON-LD 4.9 / 194. Expo — B12 builder (17 b12.io refs), HTML weight 2.03MB (heaviest page in the deep set, speed risk); GTM-MF87CXFN; JSON-LD present. Service Experts + Fox Service — Scorpion platform (source refs ×3), Scorpion video hero (Cloudflare Stream / mainstage-video-bg). One Hour — custom franchise platform, no CMS fingerprint, stopwatch brand motion not in HTML layer, JSON-LD not in homepage HTML.
  - **Five source-level lessons:** (1) Nobody in the trade top tier uses GSAP/WebGL — best-in-trade motion = CSS transitions .15–.28s ease-out + one marquee (60s linear) + Swiper carousels; the bank's GSAP craft must be dosed at reveal/slider level for trade templates, never scene pages. (2) The two best-designed locals (Stronghold, Green Conception) are hand-built static — speed and control beat CMS; but Hippo proves WordPress + Elementor can carry a top-1% conversion system. (3) Platforms dominate HVAC (Scorpion, B12, ServiceTitan) — platform sites share the same offer machinery; differentiation comes from copy/proof, not tech. (4) Call/lead tracking is standard at the top (CallRail, GTM everywhere); Green Conception's home-grown first/last-touch attribution is the most stealable small-firm pattern — pairs with Asiful's own pixel tracker. (5) JSON-LD review schema is part of the proof system (Stronghold 4.9/500, Strike Force 4.9/194, Dr. Roof 5/372, Expo present).
  - **Addendum (second batch):** Evergreen Home Heating — no CMS fingerprint, clean custom build, craft-benchmark status. London AirCon — WordPress (95 wp-content refs). Chills On Wheels (Jacksonville FL) — WordPress + Housecall Pro booking (29 refs) + Swiper. Advanced Air Home Services (Edgewater FL — a DIFFERENT firm from Advanced Air Cedar Park TX) — WordPress + Elementor (2,725 refs, heaviest Elementor footprint in the lane) + Swiper (33). Alliance Climate Control (Sydney) — curl route FAILED (connection, two attempts); the site stands as opened via text-fetch in the FL chunk (25/30); no source fingerprint claimed.
  - **Top-20 completion, schema vs marketing:** West London Roofing — hand-built static, own cache-busted /assets/css/site.css, self-hosted Archivo variable font, NO CMS; Checkatrade ×23 refs, WhatsApp ×15. Boardman — Vite SPA shell (2.6KB HTML, Lovable-flavoured runtime), Fraunces + Inter Tight; claims inconsistency stands. HHH — WordPress + Elementor (8,070 refs, heaviest in lane) + Swiper (575); ratingValue 5. Greater Midwest — Webflow + Swiper + HubSpot forms. LOA — WordPress 7.1.3; schema 5.0 / 734 vs "1,000+ reviews" in copy — mild inflation gap. Indy Roof — WordPress + NitroPack; 4.9 / 2,330 MATCHES hero claim (2,300+) ✓. Stay Dry — WordPress 6.9.10. Interlock — custom; 4.7 / 9,108 MATCHES ✓. Long Home — WordPress; 4.6 / 5,000. Bone Dry — WordPress + Elementor (1,867) + HubSpot. Rogers — WordPress + ServiceTitan. Bonner Built — WordPress 7.1.3 + Elementor (1,377) + Swiper; 5.0 / 660. CentiMark — Joomla (Helix Ultimate). A.B. May — WordPress + Swiper + ServiceTitan; 4.8 / 17,058 MATCHES the buried count exactly ✓. Estes — custom + HubSpot; schema 4.77 / reviewCount 3 vs hero "4.9 / 6,000+" — schema-marketing mismatch (Collis pattern). Deljo — WordPress + ServiceTitan; 4.9 / 3,228 MATCHES ✓. Horizon — Next.js + ServiceTitan. Fallon Solutions — WordPress + ServiceTitan (16 refs). AC Installation London (UK) — custom; 4.9 / 547. Pattern: hand-built static (Stronghold, West London, Green Conception) + Next.js firms (Cooling Co, Strike Force, Horizon) sit at the craft top; WordPress+Elementor is the volume stack and reaches the top only with a system on it (Hippo, Bonner); schema-claim mismatches (Estes 3, Collis 8, LOA gap) are a recurring hygiene failure the template must not inherit.
- **Best for:** source-level evidence behind the motion ceiling and stack choices — read when justifying GSAP dose, stack, schema or tracking decisions on any trade homepage.

  - West Shore Home — Contentful headless (233 contentful refs, ctfassets media); tel: ×5, first at 10.5%; 1,168KB / 12 scripts; Financing ×71, Free Quote ×15, Visualizer ×4, "$20,000 off" ×2 (fine print: up-to, tied to full remodel vs 1-yr price).
  - Pacific Exteriors — HubSpot (generator meta); tel: ×2, first at 7.7%; 182KB / 25 scripts; Financing ×4 only — thinnest offer layer of the five.
  - Window World — custom/light (no CMS markers); tel: ×1, first at 47.1%; 96KB / 19 scripts; Financing ×6, Free Quote ×4, Visualizer ×2 — lightest page, latest call path.
  - Allied (checked by lead 26 Oct) — WordPress (122 wp-content refs), Swiper, tel: ×5 at 11.4%, "30 days" ×6, Hardie ×11.
  - **Headline findings:** (1) No GSAP in the checked five; stacks mixed (Sitecore/Contentful/HubSpot at the national end) — the steal is the conversion system, not the stack, and WordPress is proven at crown level here too (Allied). (2) West Shore owns the visualizer slot in siding: "Evoke™ (online 3D bath and flooring visualizer)" is a named product with its own /evoke/ path, plus LiDAR measurement + 3D visualization inside the consultation offer — a real self-serve 3D tool, not a labelled gallery (bath-led, but the same system carries window/door lines). (3) Offer aggression scales with page weight: West Shore 1.17MB / financing ×71 / $20k-off promo vs Window World 96KB / 1 tel: link at 47% — the weakest call path of the five despite its price-led brand. (4) Call paths are quote-form-first in this trade (big-ticket, considered purchase): even the best first-tel: position (RbA 3.1%) sits beside only 2 tel: links total — the form is the conversion event, the phone is backup. Template implication: sticky quote CTA > sticky call for siding/windows; reverse for plumbing.
- **Best for:** siding/windows homepage builds — the source evidence for quote-form-first doctrine, the Evoke visualizer benchmark, and page-weight vs offer-aggression discipline.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/siding-windows-doors/reverse-engineering/lane4-siding-source-pass.md. **Code:** none.

## [BANK] Lane 4 — Siding & Windows scan CSV (248 scored firms) (reverse-engineering/lane4-siding-scan.csv)
- **Reference source:** None recorded — the scan dataset itself; each row carries its own firm URL (the row entries below).
- **How it looks:** A 248-row spreadsheet: one scored firm per row. Columns: industry, name, url, country, source, opened, scores_design, scores_animation, scores_proof, scores_cta, scores_mobile, scores_speed, scores_tradefit (each /5), total_35, verdict_1line. Sources: wave1 (rows 1–98), lane5-partA-top and lane5-partB, scan-summary remaining-unscanned, chunk-sideA/B, chunk-L5A/B/C/D (incl. chunk-L5B-highend, chunk-L5C-commercial, chunk-L5D-franchises), chunk-sideA-remaining, web.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion (a data file; the animation axis scores each firm's motion 0–5).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Scoring is /35 across 7 axes (design, animation, proof, cta, mobile, speed, trade-fit). Score distribution: top Austin Pro 29; Feldco 28; Allied Siding & Windows, Joyce Factory Direct and Renewal by Andersen 27; a 26-cluster (Power Home Remodeling, Thompson Creek, West Shore Home, Statewide Remodeling, Armorvue, Alure Home Improvements); median around 16–18; long tail down to 0 (Alure Home Improvements — defunct redirect/parked domain, scored 0 in the remaining-unscanned batch after an earlier 26 elsewhere in the file; Safestyle UK — holding page, not opened, all axes 0). Two firms appear twice with different scores/batches (Alure: 26 in chunk-L5D-franchises vs 0 in scan-summary; Armorvue: 24 in lane5-partB vs 26 in wave1) — both rows are indexed as recorded. 41 rows were not opened (opened=no — placeholders, parked domains, login pages, dead sites); their verdicts record why. The CSV is the evidence base behind the siding-windows.md report's funnel (248 firms → 37 opened → 20 shortlist → 5 deeps → crowns) and behind the Site-6 verdict in the portfolio plan.
- **Best for:** siding/windows shortlisting — any firm in the scan can be pulled up by score or by the device named in its verdict (visualizer, estimator, price list, before/after slider) when a siding homepage needs a reference.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/siding-windows-doors/reverse-engineering/lane4-siding-scan.csv (248 data rows; row numbers below are CSV data-row numbers, header excluded). **Code:** none.

# Bank chunk — bench log + high-end chunk notes (top-up: MAP items 15 + 17, remodeling pack)

Covers the two Lane 3 remodeling files that fell between the reports chunk and the
brief/plan/scans chunk: the source-pass + bench-exhaustion log and the high-end
design-build scan chunk notes. Both are bank-internal evidence compilations — neither
prints firm URLs, so every entry's Reference source is "None recorded" exactly as
MAP.md records for both files.

**Itemisation statement:** the bench log holds 18 per-item records (10 source-pass
fingerprints + 8 bench-exhaustion rescoring records). The 4 strongest — Elbaz and CMK
(source-pass records carrying the crown firms' build fingerprints and a reusable
mechanism value) and West Shore and CRD (bench records carrying score changes and a
review-aggregate discrepancy) — get their own short entries below. The other 14 records
are summarised inside the file-level entry. The high-end chunk's Top 8 is summarised
inside its file-level entry (MAP indexes that file as one chunk record).

---

## [BANK] Lane 3 Source Pass + Bench Exhaustion Log — library / evidence log (remodeling pack: reverse-engineering/source-pass-and-bench-log.md)
- **Reference source:** None recorded (bank-internal compilation; MAP.md records no source URL for this file).
- **What it is:** The verification layer behind the remodeling report's crowns, dated 26 Oct 2026 under the "F12 standing order". Three sections: (1) a curl full-HTML source pass over the Top-5/crowned remodeling sites, (2) a bench-exhaustion route log that full-opened 8 bench sites and re-scored them, (3) a crown check. It records what each site is actually built with and what its page weight is — the bank's evidence that the crowned sites' claims survive contact with their own source code.
- **How it looks:** Not a design — a fingerprint table in prose. What it tells a builder about the crowned sites' real builds: the lightest homepage in the pass is a bespoke static build (Richard Lusk, 50KB HTML, no framework fingerprint, no `<video>` tag on the homepage at all); the crowned remodeling sites are heavy WordPress builds (Elbaz 1.14MB HTML with 53 scripts; Phoenix Home 1.0MB); the fastest-feeling site in the set is explained by build weight, not by any animation system.
- **Frame by frame:** No motion of its own — it is a static log. Motion evidence it verifies in other sites' source: TruGreen carries a Swiper photo-card carousel in source; KBF carries Lottie (Elementor lottie config) plus its Neighborhood Drive DOM (`id=neighborhoods`, fly-hud, wpRail chapters); CMK's before/after is a custom CSS slider component. Where a bench site's Animation score moved on rescoring, the record says so (below).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Source-pass fingerprints, all HTTP 200 via terminal curl (route 1 of the standing route order: curl full-source → browser text-fetch → live browser → Wayback → per-name search; route 1 succeeded for all 8 bench sites, routes 2–5 unused). The 10 source-pass records: Richard Lusk 50KB, bespoke static, own `/assets/site/` JS (config, faq-search, gallery.js) + single design CSS, no homepage video; TruGreen 156KB, Next.js source-verified (`/_next/static/chunks`, App Router) + Swiper + WebP/SVG; Luv-A-Lawn 393KB, WordPress + WP Rocket 3.23.5.1 + HubSpot + custom "fairway-parent" theme + Google Maps API + Masonry; Monster Tree 125KB, Scorpion platform source-verified (scorpion.co analytics + Scorpion Connect bootstrap, `/cms/` includes); Augusta 212KB, Duda source-verified (cdn-website.com / multiscreensite runtime-react) + CallRail; Elbaz and CMK — itemised below; KBF 391KB, WordPress + Elementor 4.2.4 + HubSpot + Breeze cache, Lottie present + Swiper, Neighborhood Drive DOM in source; Phoenix Home 1.0MB, WordPress 7.1.3 + Slick + before-after library; Harmony Basements 377KB, WordPress, cost calculator source-verified as linked from the services page at `/basement-cost-calculator/` (the firm's own claim: "most comprehensive basement cost calculator in Canada") — calculator existence verified, its pricing figures remain search-captured from its cost page. The 8 bench-exhaustion records (all upgraded excerpt → opened in lane3-scan.csv and re-scored): CRD and West Shore itemised below; BOWA 134KB, WP + GSAP in source, scores unchanged, total 29 (its budget-range/referral proof sits on subpages; homepage text-thin); Case 124KB, WP minimal libraries, unchanged 25; Neil Kelly 322KB, WP block theme, homepage source verifies 30,000+ projects / 2,200+ reviews / 5-Year Warranty, unchanged 28; KOHLER Reveal 107KB, Webflow + 1 video, Lifetime Limited Warranty, unchanged 27; Normandy 118KB, WP + Swiper + Slick + AOS + 1 video, Animation 2→3, total 28; Quartersawn 280KB, WP + Swiper + 2 `<video>` tags (hero video source-verified), unchanged 29. Crown check (section 3): Elbaz stands at 31 (axis scores 4/5/5/5/4/3/5); no bench site exceeds 29, so NO crown challenge; KBF (29, crowned on proof originality + replicability) ties BOWA / West Shore / Quartersawn on points but keeps the crown — BOWA's proof is unreplicable award/referral mass, West Shore is a different machine (productised bath/windows franchise, proof = review volume), Quartersawn's proof layer is thinner (no pricing/warranty evidence on homepage source).
- **Tier:** STRONG — basis: the bank's own adjudication record; this log is what ratifies the remodeling crowns (Elbaz 31 stands, KBF's originality crown stands) against full-source evidence. It crowns nothing itself.
- **Best for:** Build-session QA and honesty checks — verifying a reference firm's real stack, page weight and library set before adapting its design; the weight contrast (50KB bespoke vs 1.14MB WordPress) is the bank's concrete evidence for the builder brief's weight budgets.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/remodeling/reverse-engineering/source-pass-and-bench-log.md (whole file; §1 source pass, §2 bench exhaustion, §3 crown check). **Code:** none.

## [BANK] Elbaz Construction — source-pass verification record (remodeling pack: reverse-engineering/source-pass-and-bench-log.md §1)
- **Reference source:** None recorded (no URL printed in this file; the firm's URL is carried by the remodeling report entries, not this log).
- **What it is:** The full-source fingerprint of the remodeling co-skeleton CROWN firm, taken by curl on 26 Oct 2026. It verifies two load-bearing claims from the report deep: that Elbaz's before/after material is real and paired in source, and that its video weight is as heavy as reported.
- **How it looks:** A 1.14MB HTML homepage — the heaviest in the source pass — built on WordPress 7.1.3 + Elementor + WPML, with 53 scripts. The before/after section is not a mock-up: paired uploads named `elbaz-before-after-renovation-*-before/after.jpg` sit in source alongside a before-after library and Slick.
- **Frame by frame:** Motion is library-driven, not custom: Slick sliders plus the before/after library's drag interaction over the paired images. The log records 8 `<video>` tags and 35 mp4 references in source — the video-weight claim verified — but no per-animation timings; timings live in the report deep, not here.
- **Mechanism & key values:** WordPress 7.1.3 + Elementor + WPML (all source-verified); 1.14MB HTML; 53 scripts; 8 `<video>` tags; 35 mp4 references; before/after = paired before/after JPG uploads + before-after lib + Slick. Crown-check axis scores for the firm: 4/5/5/5/4/3/5 = 31.
- **Tier:** CROWN — basis: the remodeling bank's own adjudication (Elbaz = co-skeleton crown, TOP 1% #1 in the reports chunk); this record is its source verification and records no crown challenge.
- **Best for:** The remodeling skeleton reference — proof that the crown design's before/after and video devices exist as shipped; also the cautionary weight figure (1.14MB) a single-file adaptation must not inherit.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/remodeling/reverse-engineering/source-pass-and-bench-log.md (§1, Elbaz bullet; §3 crown check). **Code:** none.

## [BANK] Remodeling High-End Design-Build — scan chunk notes (remodeling pack: design/chunk-remodeling-highend.md)
- **Reference source:** None recorded (bank-internal compilation; MAP.md records no source URL for this file — firm links are not printed in it).
- **What it is:** One completed scan chunk (26 Oct 2026, 05:56 UTC) over high-end design-build remodelers, MERGED into lane3-scan.csv (the CSV itself is not in any pack). 50 firms scanned: 32 excerpt (search-returned full own-site page text), 18 not opened; the first 5 attempted full opens were all 429-blocked and NOT retried. Merged totals after this chunk: CSV 105 rows — opened 8, excerpt 59, no 38. It ranks a Top 8 on seven axes (Design/Anim/Proof/CTA/Mobile/Speed/TradeFit, each /5), names four near-misses, extracts five cross-firm patterns, and files an explicit crown deferral.
- **How it looks:** Not a design — an evidence-ranked shortlist. What the Top 8 look like as sites, per their records: published price ranges and fixed-price offers as headline content (CRD, Factor, Neil Kelly); a named multi-step process with the price mechanism inside it (CG&S five steps: Discovery/Concept/Final Design/Construction/Warranty, live 3D shown at the Concept step, fixed cost locked at Final Design); portfolio pages built as named projects with neighbourhood, story and full specs (Neil Kelly editorial profiles; Quartersawn homeowner-story portfolio); warranty carried as a headline, not a footer line (Neil Kelly 5-year, Case 5-year transferable, CRD 2-year).
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion of its own. Motion evidence inside the records is excerpt-level only: Quartersawn scores the set's highest Animation (4/5) with a hero video file evidenced by name (`quartersawn-hero-no-logo-1-1.mp4`); BOWA Anim 3/5; all other Top-8 firms Anim 2/5. No durations, easings or triggers are recorded anywhere in the file — and per the file's own CROWN NOTE none of the eight was full-opened at this stage, so no frame-by-frame claim is made.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Top 8 with axis scores (Design/Anim/Proof/CTA/Mobile/Speed/TradeFit) and the recorded standout facts: 1. CRD Design Build, Seattle — 4/2/5/4/4/3/5 — published 2026 ranges held since 2017 (kitchen $100–150k+, bath $50k+, addition $200–400k, whole-home $350k+), fixed price before construction, 2-year warranty, ~70 whole-home projects in 10 years, 2024 MBAKS Remodeler of the Year. 2. CG&S, Austin — 4/2/4/4/4/4/5 — five-step named process, live 3D in Concept, fixed cost locked at Final Design, same team throughout. 3. BOWA, DC — 5/3/5/4/4/3/5 — most polished luxury in the set, Guaranteed Budget Range before design, 24/7 service team, 250+ awards, 80%+ repeat/referral. 4. Case, DC — 3/2/5/4/3/3/5 — fee maths published: 1% CaseStudy fee ($2k on a $200k project), 7% deposit credited, milestone draws, 5-year transferable warranty, since 1961, dedicated Before/After page. 5. Neil Kelly, Seattle/PNW — 4/2/5/5/4/3/5 — clearest CTA net in the set, fixed-price + 5-year warranty headline, $600–800/sqft FAQ figure, editorial project profiles with full specs, since 1947. 6. Factor, Denver/Boulder — 4/2/4/4/4/3/5 — Fixed-Cost Pricing as the hero offer, "delays cost us not you", address-led portfolio. 7. NEDC, Boston — 3/2/5/5/3/3/4 — gated 19-page cost guide carrying ACTUAL project totals ($738,400; $604,650 itemised), luxury $1–5M band. 8. Quartersawn, Minneapolis — 5/4/4/4/4/3/5 — most designed in the set, hero video file evidenced, 7-step process, dedicated 3-person team, homeowner-story portfolio, 200+ renovations. Just missed: Feinmann; Four Brothers (best DC portfolio narrative); HighCraft (deadline-pay guarantee); Hawthorn (within-1%-of-budget claim). The five extracted patterns, verbatim in substance: publish real numbers or don't talk price; name the process and put the price mechanism inside it; portfolio = named project + neighbourhood + story + specs; warranty as headline; CTA = consultation or cost guide, never a generic contact form.
- **Tier:** STRONG — basis: the file's own CROWN NOTE: none of the Top 8 was full-opened (all excerpt), and crown candidates (CRD, BOWA, Quartersawn, CG&S) MUST be full-opened later before any Top-5 deep / TOP 1% claim — so the chunk itself awards no crown. (The follow-through exists: the bench log above later full-opened CRD, BOWA and Quartersawn among its 8 bench sites and its crown check left all remodeling crowns unchanged.)
- **Best for:** Remodeling shortlisting — the pricing-transparency and process-naming pattern source for hero/proof/CTA sections (published ranges, fixed-price headlines, gated cost guides with real totals), and the excerpt-stage ranking a builder reads before choosing which firms to deep-read in the remodeling reports.
- **Deep read:** ~/workspace/previews/bank-selection/remodeling/design/chunk-remodeling-highend.md (whole file — one chunk record). **Code:** none.
